### Pip & coworkers (cross-cutting)

Reviewers: `characters`, `gap6-world-reacts`.

#### Fun

> *characters:* The world reacts: one thrown chair startled 8 seated coworkers with "!" bubbles and sweat, and the coffee-corner blobs flinch (DR-04 passes on timing). The win pose (arms up, hopping, confetti, coworkers cheering) is cheerful. The comedy is held back by Pip himself. He has one face. Throwing and the slingshot release have no body animation. The sprint, the main chaos verb, skates with slower legs than walking. The alarm reaction squashes coworkers flat instead of making them recoil. The pieces that would make the chaos funny are missing: strain grit, a release flail, an overhead heave, coworkers hopping back, and coworkers falling off yanked chairs. They are small rig and geometry additions on top of a solid base.

> *gap6-world-reacts:* DR-04 timing passes in every room I tested. A thrown prop that counts as an impact puts the '!' bubble, sweat and startled face on coworkers within 4.5 m in under 0.5 s: Playground trainee (0.24 m from the bin), Lobby receptionist (chair onto the desk), Meeting (one plant startles 8 pod workers, a nice comic ripple), Lunch corridor queue (2), QFN (1), Arcade (2). Everyone is calm again by +3.5 s, with no lingering bubbles. Three rooms got no reaction from the nearest throwable: Garage and Spectrum (paper), Observatory (box). Where the system falls short: (1) reactions are tied to the damage counter, so play is billed as breakage; (2) it is a 1 s blip that faces Pip; (3) nothing reacts to the clean player, and no clean route reaches a physical or funny beat inside 30 s (Playground has only the 8.6 s plug flash, Meeting's first alarm is at 64 s, Lunch's first spark at 33.9 s); (4) the big set pieces don't fire. Meeting glass can't be smashed and slides open for free; Lunch can't be slingshot near its crowd; the Playground slingshot alarm is centred on the hand, not the whip. Lunch's bots are the one autonomous comedy source, and they interact with the cable as designed.

#### Playability

> *characters:* Pip's controls and poses are readable at the game camera thanks to the hat and the soft ring, and none of the character models blocked play. The carry placement does affect play. The crate is held at head height 1.05 m ahead and blocks Pip's head from the default rear camera, and the tilted tray reads as unstable. In the Lunch room the thick-cable dolly parks against Pip's hip, the cable runs through his body, and the reel occludes him when the camera orbits. Seated blobs aren't attached to their chairs, so the 'Grab the chair' prompt at every Meeting desk leaves a hovering coworker. That's a visual soft fail, not a play blocker. Review tooling note: in ?manual, drive.advance(s) renders once at the end with dt = 1/60, so animateRig sees the whole interval's displacement as a 1/60 s move: speed clamps to 9 and the pose jumps. Gait judgements need real-time capture (characters/rt.mjs, used for strips 30–33) or advance(1/60) loops.

> *gap6-world-reacts:* Chaos never blocked the job in my runs. Coworkers never move, have no colliders and are not rope obstacles, so they can neither block nor help. Chaos helps in one unintended way: sprinting into a Meeting glass pane slides it 1.1 m and opens a free shortcut into the boardroom. In Lunch, E grabs cable ends ahead of props in the cable-dense power room. The stepped clean-route walker in Meeting stalled at x≈8 with the 37.2 m chain (14 s at a strain alarm, then F released the plug at the pane). That walker differs from the spec's straight walk, so I didn't file it, but routing past the glass panes looks fragile. Zero console errors in every run.

#### Teaching

> *characters:* Out of scope for this dimension, apart from one point. The cable's strain colour reads correctly in Pip's haul pose (white at the reel to red at the hand, characters-16). But the over-shoulder haul ends the red section at Pip's head, so the 'hot end' looks attached to his skull rather than to the plug in his glove. Fixing the haul pose and the cable clearance keeps the strain lesson on the cable.

> *gap6-world-reacts:* Not a teaching pass. One note: plug-in sparks (the moment the loop closes) get no audience response, so the world doesn't mark the electrical 'aha' the way it marks a tossed bin.

#### Clarity

> *characters:* Pip is findable at every camera thanks to the yellow helmet and ring. His blue overalls sit close to the '#5b9cf0' coworker hue and only about 26 luma above the Meeting carpet, so with blue blobs nearby the helmet does all the work (DR-43). Alarm bubbles at 0.7 m with depthTest off pile up and become the loudest shapes in the frame after one chaos event. The face, the main expressive and clarity cue for a character, is effectively invisible at the default camera.

> *gap6-world-reacts:* At the game camera the bubbles are big and readable: about 40 px, depthTest off, and on screen even at the frame edge (Playground trainee at the bottom-right). Two clarity problems: adjacent seated coworkers' bubbles stack into a column, and the impact dust hides the startled face. The HUD damage and cost jump with no visible broken state on the prop, so the player can't tell what they 'broke'.

#### Models

> *characters:* Pip (public/models/pip.glb from tools/create_assets.py) has the right parts and colour language: yellow hard hat with a lamp, blue overalls with front straps, belt, buckle and wrench, white mitts with thumbs, ink boots. At zoom 9 he reads as a friendly chibi technician that fits the concept, and the hat lamp is a nice touch. The three ART F9 artefacts are all still present: grey plinth soles, the ridge fin, and arms like shoulder pads that form a cape. The back is blank, the face is small and fixed, and the brim covers it at the game camera. Outlines are thin and light (luma about 106). The coworker blobs are the strongest models in the game: one capsule, big eyes with glints, blush, mood mouths, and accessories (headphones, glasses, cap, mug, tie, bun, sprout, tuft) that sit correctly with no floating or clipping in any shot I checked (characters-41b, -47, -48c, -52b). The mug held by an arm nub works. The model problems are in how blobs meet the world: seated blobs pass through backrests and hover once their chair is taken, and the alarm squash detaches the sweat and bubble. The arcade's human kid still breaks the one-character language.

> *gap6-world-reacts:* The startled blob variant (a wide eye, the 'o' mouth, and the hands up via the arm capsule rotated −2.3) reads well up close (world-reacts-24 area, world-reacts-27). The pose change is mainly a squash to 0.72, which is subtle at zoom 26–36 next to the bubble. A hop or lean would carry the reaction at the game camera.

### Props (cross-cutting)

Reviewers: `gap5-toon-pipeline`, `props-gallery`.

#### Fun

> *gap5-toon-pipeline:* Not directly in scope. The oversized plug, reel and strip make the cable kit look toy-like, which suits the comedy, but it should be a declared multiplier rather than ad hoc sizes.

> *props-gallery:* For a physics-comedy game the props are pleasantly knockable. Boxes scatter when Pip sprints through the Meeting stack, chairs tip, and bins spill paper balls. The chaos bonus targets are weak, though. The Playground "bowling pins" are white traffic cones on square plates, low-contrast on the pale floor. Cuboid reels and bins can't roll, which wastes the most cable-flavoured slapstick props in the game.

#### Playability

> *gap5-toon-pipeline:* No errors: g.close() returned [] for every run (10 levels in materials.mjs, plus the ramp, scale, pip and bevel scripts). Collider-versus-model overhangs (up to 19 cm on the coolbox) are a latent overlap issue that the audit can't see.

> *props-gallery:* No prop blocks a clean route in the levels I walked: Meeting printer, lounge and coffee corner; Playground lounge and pins. Every scripted walk arrived, and every `g.close()` returned no errors. The physics side is where props let the player down. Cuboid colliders mean:
> - bins and reels slide instead of rolling;
> - round props rest on invisible corners;
> - desk leg room and the space under the ping-pong table are solid;
> - the mop bucket carries a metre of invisible wall above it;
> - handles, prongs, the printer tray and the coolbox handle stick 9–30 cm out of their colliders and clip through walls and stacked props.
> 
> `g.audit(.02)` finds start-of-level overlaps in 6 of 9 levels, 51 of them in the Meeting, all from hand-tuned y values and offsets.

#### Teaching

> *gap5-toon-pipeline:* Not in scope for this pass.

> *props-gallery:* Props are where the electrical concepts become physical, and several underplay it:
> - **Capacitor cart:** reads as paint tins, with no polarity sleeve or terminals.
> - **Power strip:** no lead and no breaker or rating plate, even though it carries the Meeting load-budget beat.
> - **Reel:** looks like an empty spool.
> - **Cable bridge:** shows no cable channel, so it doesn't say "cables pass safely under me".
> - **Coupler:** looks like a plug, not a socket adaptor.
> 
> Each of these can carry its idea in its shape (DR-37) without any text.

#### Clarity

> *gap5-toon-pipeline:* The flat ramp hurts readability most on pale props over pale floors. With 13–25 luma of form shading, separation comes only from the outline and the new rim, and the rim is missing on Pip, coworkers and the cable. The wedge, Lunch's first job item, has no outline on its slope.

> *props-gallery:* The prop silhouettes mostly read at the game camera. Prop colour is what hurts clarity. Job yellow appears on 32 Meeting mugs, a Meeting beanbag, desk lamps, and the Garage and Lunch clutter palette (yellow carts, boxes, chairs and cabinets next to the yellow wedge and bridges). That dilutes the one visual language that marks job parts. The Meeting coffee machine is the target of a bonus and of a prompt ("Borrow the coffee machine's cable"), yet it doesn't read as a coffee machine. The coupler and the player's plug are the same shape, so the coupler-first rule can't be read from the parts.

#### Models

> *gap5-toon-pipeline:* Material census, from a scene traverse in every level through a patched Object3D.onBeforeRender: every lit surface is MeshToonMaterial. The rest are MeshBasicMaterial for screens, decals and unlit floor marks, ShaderMaterial only for the lobby portals, and sprites for glow. There are zero MeshStandard, Phong, Lambert or Physical materials, and the GLB Pip is fully converted to toon. No glossy fabric or paper exists, and the only glossy wood is the lobby door leaves. Gloss otherwise covers the intended plastics: Pip's helmet, mitts and boots (#fdd161, #f6f2e5, #424b65), the cable hose, the fridge, the bots and the lamp shades, plus several metals that need a product-owner ruling. The real pipeline gaps are the ramp (the visible shading range on pale props is tiny) and the rim being lost on glosses and clones. Scale: Pip is 1.744 m, the blob 1.01 m, the desk top 0.95, the cabinet 1.6 and the door 2.26. The handheld and job parts are where scale breaks (2–4× real). Bevels: RoundedBoxGeometry parts are fine for small pieces, but big rbox bodies cap at a 2 cm bevel, and the wedge and bridge are unbevelled with no outline.

> *props-gallery:* I judged all 35 prefabs in src/props/prefabs.ts:
> - **Gallery shots:** front and back (yaw −0.5 and 2.64) next to Pip (measured at 1.76 m) and a 1.1 m blob, with magenta collider wireframes, combined into `props-gallery-10-sheet01…12`.
> - **Measurements:** I measured each prefab's visual bounds against its collider box (`mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/measure.mjs`).
> - **In-game:** I found the props at the game camera and at zoom 9 in Meeting, Playground, Arcade, Garage, Lunch, QFN, Observatory and Spectrum.
> 
> **What works well:**
> - Chair: the best prop. Padded seat, curved back, armrests, gas lift, a five-star base on casters. Reads from any angle.
> - Box: tape, flap seam and label read well.
> - Desk: panel legs and pedestal, with per-desk dressing (keyboard, mouse, pencil cup, desk lamp, cable tail).
> - Mail cart: lipped tray with parcels.
> - Mop bucket: wringer and bail.
> - Splitter: sockets plus a green power lamp.
> - Coolbox, cabinet front, dolly reel and supply cart (bolt decal, sockets, handle): all good.
> - Materials: every prop uses only `MeshToonMaterial`, with `MeshBasic` for screens and decals, which passes DR-57.
> - Scale: Pip-relative scale is on the R6 table. Desk .95, cabinet 1.6, chair seat about .5, supply 1.3; the mug at .16×.2 is in the oversized-handheld range. Every handheld is above 8 px at the game camera.
> 
> **Weak:**
> - Coffee machine: a black cube with its cup inside it.
> - Sofa: floats 12.5 cm and has a one-slab seat.
> - Coupler: the same model as the plug.
> - Beanbag, books, vending machine, lamp: the known research issues, all still open.
> - Water cooler, printer, ping-pong table, bridge, capacitor cart: thin on cues.
> - Colliders: every prop is a cuboid regardless of shape.

### Cable (cross-cutting)

Reviewers: `cable`, `gap7-snap-grab-target`.

#### Fun

> *cable:* What works:
> - Dragging the reel cable through a dense room is the best thing in the game. At the game camera the hose is fat (0.2 m), strain shows as a gradient that warms toward Pip's hand (cable-11/12, cable-62→65), and near the limit it jitters, throws twang arcs and sparks at the corner it bites (cable-22).
> - Coworkers along a taut cable pop '!' bubbles (cable-64/65), and the reel's spring physically pulls Pip back, which feels elastic and physical.
> - Wrapping a pillar and walking back to unwrap it is clean: bends are added at real corners and removed in reverse (pg5 log, cable-40..44).
> - The Playground pins can be knocked over by dragging a taut cable through them (pg4: 2 down during the sprint, 3 moved after Q).
> 
> What lets it down:
> - The slingshot, the signature moment, is weak and hard to find. The prompt appears when Q will do nothing (standing at the limit), it only works mid-sprint, and when it fires the cable and plug don't recoil: props just get kicked, with no hitstop.
> - Lunch, the third cable floor, has leads so long that strain and slingshot never come up, and none of the twang feel.
> - The meeting coupler and extension join is invisible.
> 
> Compared with Good Job's cable levels, the drag is there; the release payoff and the satisfaction of a cable that visibly runs out and joins are not.

> *gap7-snap-grab-target:* Forgiving snaps are what keep a Good Job-style game from feeling finicky. Here the clean action (walk up, F) feels fine, but the natural slapstick action (let the plug go at the socket) silently fails, and the camera can lose Pip completely in two starting corners. Fixing the release seat and the cutaway removes the two most frustrating moments seen in this pass.

#### Playability

> *cable:* Picking up, dragging and plugging in are forgiving and reliable:
> - The plug snaps from 2.2 m (game.ts:205).
> - The clean Playground route finishes in about 15 s (pg1, won at 15.1 s, A/A/A).
> - Meeting coupler then extension via F works, with a helpful 'Attach the coupler first' prompt (cable-71).
> 
> Problems:
> - The Q/slingshot prompt is false most of the time it shows (DR-19).
> - The Meeting single-reel reach sits on the snap boundary (2.24–2.29 m vs 2.2), so 'Plug in' flickers and the spec margin is about 0.05 m.
> - The cable has no physical presence for Pip: walking or jumping over it does nothing (pg5/pg6). That is acceptable, but a small step-up or stumble would sell it.
> - The automatic whip when a taut rope comes off a corner (game.ts:286) is a nice hidden reward, but nothing in the world points to it.
> - All scripts closed their browsers except pg7.mjs, which crashed on a bad evaluate before g.close(). Node exited, so Playwright should have reaped it, but leftover chrome-headless-shell processes were visible, possibly from other reviewers.

> *gap7-snap-grab-target:* Snap and grab mostly work in code, but are signposted only in text. What works: the F snap is generous (Pip within 2.2 m or the plug within 1.6 m), the Meeting strip snaps from 2.6 m (M10 confirmed), the garage stand (2.6 m) and the spectrum pad and mirror marks (Pip within 2.2/2.1 m) agree with their prompts, and the Lunch capacitor docks inline (LR9 confirmed). The reach bias for id'd props works: a mug 0.25 m nearer than the power strip doesn't steal the prompt or the reticle. The gaps all sit on the release side. The Q/let-go path never seats a plug that lies in the socket ring. The Lunch port choice uses Pip's body, not the plug in his hand. The bare reel plug gets no job bias, so the reticle and E go to a nearer mug while the pill says F plug. The biggest camera problem is a geometry bug in the shell-wall cutaway (wall centre used instead of the wall plane): at the Meeting spawn and the Spectrum storeroom, a 180° orbit fills the screen with a wall and hides Pip, the item and the target.

#### Teaching

> *cable:* The cable teaches length and routing honestly in the Playground. The spool shrinks as cable pays out (game.ts:292), and the HUD reel meter and strain bar back it up (cable-10, cable-44).
> 
> Weak spots:
> - In the Meeting the length lesson ('join a second lead') has no visual: the extension simply disappears into the cable.
> - In Lunch, length barely constrains anything, so 'cable rating' and 'route' are taught by heat, water and door rules, not by the cable's finiteness.
> - The idle route hint still flows cyan dots along an open circuit and through props (cable-54; DR-29, re-checked, still open). The only on-cable 'flowing' cue should be the current pulses on a closed loop. Those are correct: they only run when the load is on (game.ts:305, Pulses).
> - The sprint-overstretch trick is still undiscoverable (M9).

> *gap7-snap-grab-target:* Not the focus of this gap pass, but snapping affects the cable lesson. In Lunch, a thick cable meant for the feed post ends up in the fridge 1.2 m away, which muddles the rating/budget idea the room teaches. In Playground, a plug that looks seated but isn't makes the 'needs power first' switch prompt read as an order rule rather than a bad connection.

#### Clarity

> *cable:* Strain reads from the camera from yellow upward:
> - orange and red are unmistakable in the big Meeting room (cable-64/65);
> - the gold 'connected' tint plus the gold HUD bar clearly mark success (cable-67, cable-85).
> 
> At rest, the cream hose on the cream Playground concrete is the least saturated thing near Pip (measured luma 232 vs 191–212 for the floor, saturation 0.09 vs 0.17). Yellow strain on Lunch's honey wood blends in (cable-130).
> 
> The spool is readable at the start (cable-02/03), but the reel is off-screen once you are far enough for length to matter. The HUD reel meter carries that information, so it is fine.
> 
> Three separate strain threshold tables mean the HUD bar, the hose colour and the prompt don't agree.

> *gap7-snap-grab-target:* The prompt is honest about what F/E will do, but it is the only cue. The socket torus pulses the same way with or without the plug. There is no ghost, magnet or in-range colour change at any dock, and the strip, stand, pad and cart docks have no pre-release footprint at all. Lunch alone brightens its port rings while a cable is held, which is the right idea, but all of them light. The reticle, prompt and marker disagree in three repeatable cases: the junk-near-plug start, the mail cart (reticle on the reel, text says coupler) and a plug dropped near the lamp switch (pill offers the switch). The garage pickup calls the robot 'the cart'.

#### Models

> *cable:* The hose model is good: a thick glossy tube with outline, a centripetal Catmull-Rom curve, a gentle sag when slack, and a rise to the glove over the last 1.8 m. It hugs pillar corners convincingly at 0.12 m clearance (cable-42). The thick Lunch cable's ink bands make it instantly distinct from thin leads (cable-82).
> 
> The visual bugs are interpenetration:
> - through Pip's legs on every drag and in the win shot (P3 still open);
> - through any box or shelf the plug is pressed into (the plug-inside-AABB exclusion);
> - through light props and the boardroom glass corner;
> - in Lunch, through everything that isn't a wall, including its own dolly.
> 
> No floor z-fighting was seen: the tube sits at y 0.09 with radius 0.1. The cable doesn't float, except the short arc from reel to hand when less than about 1.8 m is paid out (cable-74), which reads as 'held up'.

> *gap7-snap-grab-target:* Not assessed in depth. Incidental: the floor-level grab reticle disappears under carts and stands (mail cart), the spectrum pod is carried at head height over Pip's face (sp-pad shots), and the garage robot could end up tipped on its side behind Pip after a backward approach (shot 33; not reproduced in a normal turnaround, s6).

### HUD & UI (cross-cutting)

Reviewers: `gap8-meta-settings-errors`, `hud-ui`.

#### Fun

> *gap8-meta-settings-errors:* Meta paths don't affect fun directly. The win push-in and the result card's count-up and confetti still land. The fail card's iconography (spoiled bowl, thermometer, the three-step progress chain) is clear without text. The friction is all in the retry key.

> *hud-ui:* From the HUD side, the juice is good. The plug-in hitstop and flash, the strain bar shifting white→red with the pill flipping to 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable' at strain >0.97, the win push-in keeping Pip in frame on desktop, the result rows counting up with a stamp thud, and the Lunch fail tag that swings in with steam all land well. Things that undercut the fun: bonus stars that start lit and then go out, a bench screen that feels like a spreadsheet (59–73 words), and losing a run to a stray R. On phone the result and fail cards cover the whole frame, so the win push-in is never seen there.

#### Playability

> *gap8-meta-settings-errors:* DR-80: every level id passes start, survey (Tab in and out) and a 20 s scripted walk with zero console or page errors. This was run with errors.mjs and g.close() for each level; output verbatim:
> - lobby errors []
> - playground []
> - meeting []
> - lunch []
> - arcade []
> - arcade-rush []
> - garage []
> - qfn []
> - observatory []
> - spectrum []
> 
> The walk was W, D, S, A with sprint, plus E, Q, Space and F presses. These scripts also closed with errors []:
> - the Playground win;
> - a full Arcade practice solve;
> - the Lunch spoil fail and retry;
> - the QFN send-back, CHECK, Tab and stand-up;
> - the Arcade fuse trip;
> - the fake-gamepad run;
> - the lens cycling in Meeting and at the Arcade bench.
> 
> g.audit(.02) after 0.5 s of settling returned [] for meeting, arcade and qfn. The non-zero counts in errors.mjs (meeting 1, arcade 1, arcade-rush 1, qfn 2) were taken after the walk had knocked props together, not at start.
> 
> Start-of-level draw calls, which count every render pass (src/game.ts:450):
> 
> | Level | Draw calls at start |
> |---|---|
> | lobby | 592 |
> | playground | 782 |
> | meeting | 1315 |
> | lunch | 1309 |
> | arcade | 1497 |
> | garage | 1156 |
> | qfn | 1201 |
> | observatory | 1094 |
> | spectrum | 1133 |
> 
> Fps in ?manual is not meaningful.
> 
> DR-20: bench failures are cheap. Inputs are accepted at once during an Arcade fuse trip and right after a QFN send-back. Lunch is about 1.8 s from failure to playable through Enter. R is broken on both end cards.
> 
> The main control bugs are at the meta layer:
> - R is dead on the result and fail cards.
> - The pad camera button is labelled RS but bound to Select, and LS opens an unlabelled survey.
> - At benches, F, Space and Tab fall through to floor actions.
> - C at the QFN bench doubles as a camera reset.
> 
> The C reset itself works well: it returns to the exact home view from any orbit, zoom or the survey.

> *hud-ui:* Desktop keyboard+mouse play is solid in the cable rooms: E/F/Q/Space/Tab work as labelled, Esc pauses, Esc at a bench stands up, retry is about 2.2 s and lands straight in play (DR-20 passes), and Tab/R are gated to play (L6 fixed). The serious gaps are input coverage. (1) On phone, every bench except QFN crops its bins and buttons off-screen; in the Arcade only the 100/470 Ω bins can be tapped, so the clean fixes can't be built. Touch also has no orbit, zoom or survey. (2) On a gamepad, no station job can be played at all: bench input is keyboard and mouse only. The RS label is wrong, and the Workshop picker can't be closed or used. (3) R is an instant, unconfirmed reload that also fires at most benches, right next to E/F. (4) The Arcade 'P Fuse cooling' pill makes the player switch the bench off. Smaller leaks: Space jumps Pip out of the bench chair, C resets the orbit during QFN checks, and the picker leaves the game live behind it.

#### Teaching

> *gap8-meta-settings-errors:* No teaching content in the meta screens. The fail card shows how far the tray got (oven, belt, lift) with icons only, which fits DR-40. The cause sentence lives in the world beat beforehand: groans and puffs at the fridge, per DR-28. Practice mode keeps the full grading, which is arguably good for learning, but the copy should say 'not saved' rather than 'not graded'.

> *hud-ui:* The HUD supports teaching mostly through the bench monitors and the board labels, which are good. The HUD side panel repeats what the monitor already shows instead of adding to it, which works against Mayer's redundancy principle (DR-41). The Lunch fail card shows the result (spoiled food, a hot thermometer) but not the cause, so a player who missed the fridge doesn't learn that it needed power. The Arcade toasts are full-sentence explanations ('The block across the LED limits nothing: the LED still sits straight across 5 V, so the fuse tripped.'). They are accurate, but they are a 20-word read laid over the work. Shortening them to one clause, and moving the 'why' onto the monitor, would keep the play-by-doing balance.

#### Clarity

> *gap8-meta-settings-errors:* The settings surface is small: a Sound tile and a 'View' lens tile in pause, the C button on the action bar, and a sound button on the title screen. Both settings persist in localStorage (circuit-crew-muted, circuit-crew-fov) across a reload and a lobby round-trip.
> 
> The lens setting is too subtle to notice (about 8–10%), and 'Close' doesn't bring the camera closer. One photo-camera glyph stands for three different things: reset, lens, and orbit/zoom in the controls map.
> 
> The Sound tile never changes its label. Practice mode is hard to notice during a run, because the PRACTICE tag sits under the job card. On the result card the tag is about 7 px, while a full A-stamp grade sits next to it, after the picker promised 'nothing is graded'.
> 
> At a bench, Esc stands Pip up rather than pausing (as DR-22 intends), so the lens and mute settings can only be reached there through the HUD pause button.

> *hud-ui:* What works well: the HUD vocabulary is coherent. The ink-outlined paper cards, the yellow kbd pill, duotone icons, the striped-cable motif shared by the title, Jobs and result screens, and the dots-plus-current-step job card all read as one system. In the cable rooms the start frame text is small: Playground is about 9 words (card plus pill), and the pill matches the card there. The result card shows clearly which axis earned the grade (the highlighted row with the cable feed into the stamp). Benches use diegetic labels well: A/S/D printed under the Arcade sockets, PULSE/TEST plaques in the Garage, ROUTE: PAST MOTOR in the Observatory. The problems are density and duplication at the benches (45–73 words, with the same values on the card, panel and monitor), card/pill disagreement at the Meeting and Lunch starts, key glyphs that don't match the input device (keyboard letters on phone and pad), and a few small polish issues (the HQ icon clash, 'Hq', practise/practice, unexplained bonus stars). The marker reads in the Playground but not at the lobby or garage distance.

#### Models

> *gap8-meta-settings-errors:* Not in scope for this gap-fill. No model findings beyond what the room reviewers filed. At Close zoom with the Wide lens, the objective marker becomes a large flat cone; that is already filed under the marker findings.

> *hud-ui:* Not my dimension. HUD icons (src/render/icons.ts) are on a consistent 32-unit grid with ink strokes and read well at 28–40 px. The damage (cracked mug) and cost (coins) tally icons are legible without labels. The marker cone is the one 3D HUD element, and it lacks the ink outline every other model has.

### Camera & rendering (cross-cutting)

Reviewers: `camera-render`, `gap2-quality2-retake`.

#### Fun

> *camera-render:* Camera presentation of success is uneven.
> - The Playground win push-in frames Pip and the lit lamp well, with a confetti burst (camera-render-pg-46-win-a).
> - Every station win crops Pip at the boots and frames the bench rather than the robot, cabinets or dish that came to life (P1).
> - The arcade play test, the moment that should be funny and rewarding with a kid hammering the cabinet, happens off-screen from the bench view.
> - Sprint dust and coffee steam read as snowballs, which undercuts the otherwise clean toon look.

> *gap2-quality2-retake:* Two of the three biggest success moments get worse at quality 2. The Playground lamp turns Pip into a glare blob (lamp-area pixels above 245: 18% at q2, 2.5% at q0), and the Meeting projector slide blooms white. Garage, QFN, Observatory, Spectrum and Lunch win push-ins barely change (whole-frame blown pixels ≈0% at both qualities). Their framing problems from other reviews (Pip cropped, finale out of frame) are camera issues and hold unchanged. Arcade neon banner: mean luma 146 at q2, 145 at q0, with 1.0% vs 0.8% above 230. Bloom doesn't change it, so the arcade-models '8 m glow sprite' finding holds exactly as filed. It is a geometry and opacity issue, not a bloom one.

#### Playability

> *camera-render:* The camera is the weakest part of this dimension.
> 
> What works:
> - Interior walls fade (LR7 at the Lunch kitchen/corridor wall is fixed: camera-render-lu-56).
> - The bench camera locks orbit and wheel and snaps to a fixed framing; Esc stands Pip up again.
> - Zoom clamps 9..38 as specified.
> - No room produced console or page errors in any script.
> - The host GPU holds 60 fps in real (non-manual) runs.
> 
> What fails:
> - Shell-wall cutaway: the centre-direction test leaves a full-height wall between the camera and Pip near corners and along the front half of side walls. Pip disappears completely, or the camera grazes a wall cap (P1).
> - Fade coverage: only pillars and interior walls fade, through one ray, so shelves, racks and pillar edges hide Pip (P1, known).
> - Survey: the fixed zoom 44 crops the 33 m rooms and is useless in portrait (P1).
> - Performance: draw calls are 2.6–4.7× the 500 target, and PROGRESS's 176 figure no longer holds (P1).
> 
> The quality bug matters here too. Every first-time player runs at quality 0, so adaptQuality never had a chance to matter.

> *gap2-quality2-retake:* Quality 2 is affordable on this host: 58–60 fps in all 9 rooms in real time, at DPR 1 and 1.5, with no adaptive step-down in 10 s. Forcing quality 0 on every player therefore gains nothing here. Draw calls at quality 2 are 1076 (lobby) to 2344 (arcade start), and up to 2457 in the arcade survey, against the 250 budget. About 740–765 of each total is the GTAO pass re-drawing the scene. The game.ts:70 bug is confirmed on the real player URL, not only on ?manual. A stored value overrides ?lowfx, and the step-down never recovers, with no settings UI to undo it. DR-54 floor medians are unchanged at quality 2, because AO and bloom don't touch open floor. Lobby: terrazzo 222, rug 206, wood 185. Garage: 223 / 211. QFN wood: 208 / 209. Spectrum tile: 184 / 199. q0 matched within 1. Every DR-54 brightness finding holds as filed.

#### Teaching

> *camera-render:* From the camera side, the biggest teaching cost is the bench camera. It frames only the tabletop, so the in-world consequence of a fix stays off-screen: the cabinet the kid plays, and the garage robot on its stand partly under the side card. The player learns from the monitor text instead of the world, against DR-28 and DR-47.
> 
> The Lunch storeroom lid makes the 'dark storeroom' read as a glass sheet with a lamp poking through, which weakens the 'bring light' cue.

> *gap2-quality2-retake:* The garage arc is the taught failure, and at quality 2 it hides the switch, the node and the scope for the whole visible arc. That is six 0.1 s frames, about 0.6 s, not the 'over 1 s' others reported, and still far over DR-79's 120 ms. At q2 it covers 40% of the board, against 17% at q0. The Arcade LED halo hides LED HEAT and the current bar exactly when 'too much current' is the lesson. The fixes belong in the emissive values (hot ×3, sprite opacity .6–1.0, point lights 6–16) more than in the bloom pass: tune them for quality 2, then confirm quality 0 still reads.

#### Clarity

> *camera-render:* What reads well:
> - The game camera at default zoom.
> - Outlines are genuinely dark (the darkest 2% of a Pip crop measures 54 luma, which passes DR-56).
> - No z-fighting or shimmer appeared in settled far or close frames. All diffs were animated actors and HUD (camera-render-pg-40b, camera-render-me-60c).
> - Shadows have no visible acne or peter-panning, and the shadow frustum (±20.5/±19) covers even the 33×20 rooms at 4096².
> 
> What doesn't:
> - Start frames in the observatory and spectrum waste 44–48% of the screen on void, because the follow camera doesn't clamp to the room.
> - The lobby's first frame cuts the left-wall doors.
> - The survey's corners sit under HUD cards.
> - The rim light currently has no visible effect, so it neither helps nor hurts.

> *gap2-quality2-retake:* Quality 2 hurts clarity where bloom lands on information. The Arcade bench monitor's blacks lift by about 75 luma during the Claw heat. The Garage scope caption and socket labels disappear under the arc. The Meeting projector slide (the only signal that the job worked) washes out. Everywhere else the HUD and world text are the same at both qualities, because the HUD is DOM and the shots are DPR 1 in headless Chromium. All pixel-size claims in other reviews (14 px caps, outline px, marker height) hold at quality 2. The one exception is a real HiDPI display, where quality 0 also caps DPR at 1 instead of 1.5, so in-world signs render softer for players than intended.

#### Models

> *camera-render:* Not my dimension, but camera close-ups exposed model-side rendering issues.
> - Pillar trims (base, rail, cap) aren't part of the fade, so a faded pillar becomes a glass case whose shelves cut Pip at the waist.
> - Dust particles are outlined opaque spheres.
> - Steam puffs are hard-edged discs.
> 
> Pip, props and fixtures otherwise render cleanly at zoom 9, with no near-plane clipping into props at the bench views: no mesh came within 0.6 m of any bench camera.
> 
> All review-5 screenshots taken with cap.mjs fullfx:true were actually at quality 0 (no AO, no bloom, DPR 1) because of the fresh-profile quality bug. Model and art reviewers should know that AO and bloom were never in their frames.

> *gap2-quality2-retake:* Quality 2 changes nothing about models. AO adds contact shadows under chairs, carts and cabinets, which helps grounding a little: 7–12% of pixels darker by more than 8 luma at the game camera. AO also greys Pip's overalls by about 6 luma. Pip's hat lamp blooms into a slightly larger white dot (217 vs 186 pixels above 248 at zoom 9). That is harmless and not filed. The rim light still does nothing measurable at quality 2. Rim on against ?norim at zoom 9 in the garage gives mean |Δ| 1.29 luma, 1.2% of pixels above 10 (0.54 and 0.43% at q0), so camera-render's 'rim has no effect' claim holds at both qualities.

### Progression, juice & recovery (cross-cutting)

Reviewers: `gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock`, `gap3-recheck-list`, `gap4-juice-audio`, `progression`.

#### Fun

> *gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock:* Lobbing items with a jump-throw is fun and physical, and it is exactly what a Good Job player does first. That is why the sealed closet matters: the most natural experiment in the Meeting's opening area, 5 m from the strip, ends the run silently. Once the pockets are sealed or covered by a general unreachable rule, throwing stays a safe toy.

> *gap3-recheck-list:* The title hero shot (P7) works: Pip stands in the right third beside the logo and the sparking-plug glyph. His raised arm is cropped by the right edge, a small composition miss. The Playground win sequence (confetti, Pip cheering by the lit lamp) is charming, but the result card took more than 4 s to appear in manual time.

> *gap4-juice-audio:* I logged the event-to-sound table live, by hooking WebAudio: OscillatorNode and BufferSource start, routed back to the sfx bus.
> 
> Sounds by event:
> - **Plug-in** (Playground/Meeting): plug() click-clack plus 880/1109/1319 bells, plus plugFlash (.09 s hitstop, flash, ring, stars). This is the only juicy beat.
> - **Lunch plug-in:** plug() only, with no hitstop or flash.
> - **Unplug:** pop(), the same as grabbing any prop. Meeting appliance unplug: pop plus highpass click plus 3 groans.
> - **Breaker trip** (Meeting and Lunch): 75 Hz square plus lowpass noise, small shake. Lunch water short: identical.
> - **Arcade PTC trip:** bandpass-1800 noise, 120 Hz square, groan. Garage dead-short fuse: the same.
> - **LED pop:** bandpass-2600 noise, 90 Hz square, groan, plus a flash.
> - **Block pop:** noise, pop, 150 Hz saw, alarm voice, plus debris and smoke.
> - **Lunch spoil/burn:** 120 Hz triangle at .05 plus 3 groans, identical for both.
> - **Scorch:** 60 Hz saw.
> - **Slingshot release:** 90 Hz saw at .12 plus noise plus shake, no hitstop.
> - **Prop break:** glass, clatter or thud by mass.
> - **Coworker alarm:** formant voice, rate-limited to 0.5 s.
> - **Step tick:** bell 1175.
> - **Win:** cheer(), i.e. jingle plus crowd. The result card adds a thud plus a 90 Hz triangle, and a bell if improved.
> - **Fail card:** silent.
> - **Bench sign-off, ship, log, send:** the same cheer() plus bell 1319.
> - **Send-back:** a groan only.
> - **Lobby locked door:** 140 Hz square.
> - **Lobby door enter:** a pop that the instant location.href cuts off.
> - **Footsteps:** not observable under ?manual.
> 
> What works: the plug-in beat (click, chime, hitstop, flash, ring), the strain hum and creak, coworker gibberish, and the result-card thud and count-up all feel good. The procedural palette is coherent.
> 
> What is missing: escalation and contrast. There is one celebration sound for everything, hitstop only on the plug, no flash at the win, and fault sounds shared across different faults. Failures are quieter than successes: the QFN send-back and the Lunch spoil are the quietest events in their rooms. Lunch fail even plays Pip's victory dance.

> *progression:* Moment to moment, the cable floors deliver the Good Job promise. The Meeting mid-drag shot (progression-34) has a springy cable snaking between pillars and 24 coworkers around it, and the win push-ins land with confetti, a cheer and a card that thuds in. The campaign as a whole is weaker. After job 02 the cable, strain meter and slingshot vanish for the remaining 5 jobs (6 doors). Every station follows one template: a 2–6 s carry, an objective step that is just 'press E', then button sub-jobs. No station has a chaos route or a chaos bonus, and room breakage there is graded on bench-sized scales (one chair = Cost D). Every run I finished graded A overall: Playground 5 s, Meeting 21 s, Arcade 31 s with breaks, Garage with a D in cost. Bonus stars aren't saved and the card shows no previous best, so replay motivation rests entirely on curiosity. The Workshop practice mode is the normal run without saving, which normal play already risks nothing, so it has no purpose. What works: fast transitions (door to playable room in about 1.5 s, back to HQ in about 0.5 s), the door spring and the portal peek, the rush countdown card, and the result card's count-up and axis cable.

#### Playability

> *gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock:* I tested DR-15 and DR-25 on real builds with mockups/review5/tools/stuck-softlock/*.mjs. g.close() returned [] every time, so there were no console errors (DR-80 ok).
> 
> What works:
> - **Station rooms.** The arcade tray, garage robot, QFN parts crate, observatory motor cart, spectrum pod and spectrum mirror were thrown into corners, behind shelves and over or behind benches. After advance(10) each one could be walked to and picked up with E, usually from 0.3–0.7 m. Pip pushes dynamic props (setApplyImpulsesToDynamicBodies), and the 1.65 m reach goes through clutter, so floor-level wedges behind furniture were never fatal.
> - **High respawn.** It works: the Meeting strip on the 2.3 m racks went home after 3.5 s with a clear white puff.
> - **Out of the room.** Items lobbed over the 1 m front or right lips fall into the void and come back through the y<−3 rule.
> - **Lunch cut cables.** They show a red bolt badge and 'F Repair the burned cable (costs 15)', which can be repeated, so DR-25's 'cut part is recoverable' holds in Lunch.
> - **Cable chaos.** Playground and Meeting cables can't be cut. Sprint-overstretching and letting go (Q) leaves the plug at Pip's feet, F re-grabs it, and both jobs were finished afterwards (Playground won at 22 s by the clean route, Meeting at 40 s by the coffee reel). There are no doors on those floors.
> 
> What fails:
> - **Sealed pockets.** The real hole is not 'behind furniture' but sealed pockets you can lob into: the Meeting server closet (strip, coupler, reel cart lost for good) and Lunch's dark storeroom (items can't be grabbed until the kitchen is powered).
> - **Controls note.** The brief and DR-22 say Space throws. In the build Space jumps and Q throws or lets go (src/game.ts:166, 183). The rulebook line should be corrected.

> *gap3-recheck-list:* Most re-check items hold up on real screenshots. The bigger gap I found is the camera. At the Meeting spawn corner, zoom 9 plus a low orbit puts the camera behind an uncut wall in 3 of 8 yaws, and the whole frame goes beige. The Lunch corner doesn't do this. Also, because the fade uses one ray to the hip, half-walls (kitchen front, closet) hide Pip's legs and torso at close zoom without fading. Strip snap (M10) is forgiving: dropped at 2.44 m it snapped onto the door spot with a ring burst. L5 works: Jobs from the result card goes to the lobby, and F5 lands on the title, not the Jobs board. Keys: Tab and R are inert on the title, Jobs board and result card. R on the pause card reloads the job instantly; the card advertises it, but it is still a game key acting inside a menu. All scripts closed their browsers with zero console errors.

> *gap4-juice-audio:* Mute persists across reloads and jobs (localStorage 'circuit-crew-muted'), and the icon and aria-pressed sync on load. Only the aria-label is static.
> 
> The AudioContext correctly waits for a user gesture: the first click or key starts it (audio.ts:21, game-ui.ts:45). Hitstop skips the sim step in frame() but not in ?manual, so no spec can test it. Particles update on real time in render() (game.ts:438), so a review screenshot taken with cap.mjs's 900 ms settle never shows spark or flash bursts. Juice shots must be taken immediately.
> 
> The garage drive bug (a 22 Hz beep stutter) is a real code defect, with a one-line fix (cycleT=-1 in startDrive).
> 
> No console or page errors in any run: playground, meeting, lunch ×2, arcade ×2, garage, qfn, lobby.

> *progression:* No crashes: every script's `g.close()` returned [] (lobby, playground-win, lobby-progress, arcade-flow, arcade-full, meeting-time×2, garage-chaos, lunch-fail, transition, mailcart-probe), and saving to localStorage works and survives reloads (`circuit-crew:best:v1`). Two key problems stand out. First, R wipes the whole job instantly from the arcade, garage and spectrum benches, because unbound bench keys fall through to the walking handler, while QFN and observatory use R as a bench verb. Second, R on the result and fail cards, which display an R hint, does nothing. The Workshop picker lets W move Pip under the modal, and the prompt pill stays live behind it. In the Meeting, Pip easily bumps the second reel off the mail cart, after which E offers 'Grab the cart'. The Meeting clean spec still passes on its exact timing. The lobby uses 663 draw calls and the arcade bench about 1200.

#### Teaching

> *gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock:* Out of scope for this gap-fill. One note: in Lunch, the recovery path (let the door cut the cable, then repair it at the post) teaches 'doors cut cables' by accident. A respawn for items thrown into the dark store would keep the lesson on wedging the door instead of on a costly repair loop.

> *gap3-recheck-list:* The capacitor chain (LR9) and no-recharge-while-tripped (LR10) are truthful. In the run the kick drew the cart from 12 to 6.9, it then recharged only from the live supply, and the unit test 'a capacitor recharges between lift starts only from a live supply' passes (vitest, 9/9). The cut-cable meter (LR6) no longer flashes gold: the strain card faded with no 'connected' class. The weak spots are explanation, not simulation. The bots snag a fresh plug on frame 1 with no readable cause. A door cut is called 'burned'. The cart's inline lead is a black hairline nobody will see at the game camera.

> *gap4-juice-audio:* Sound currently can't teach fault types. Overload and water short are the same cue, and every bench tier-0 verdict is the same 160 Hz buzz plus groan.
> 
> Worse, the Lunch water short plays the success plug chime and two objective-done bells. It latches 'Mop up the leak' as done while the puddle remains and the supply is tripped, so the player is told the wrong lesson.
> 
> In Meeting the social feedback is inverted: the trip is unremarked, and the correct unplug is booed. Bench placements praise every part with the success chime, including the reversed diode about to short.
> 
> The positives: the Meeting/Lunch trip has an in-world spark at the strip or supply. The arcade pops have debris, smoke and a flash at the right part. The garage reboot has stars, red eyes and an alarm voice at the robot. These follow DR-28's 'cue at the part' well, and only their sound design needs separating.

> *progression:* Taken as a curriculum, the order is the weak point. Playground (cable feel) and Meeting (length plus loads adding up on a breaker) build nicely. Then Lunch, job 02, introduces about 7 ideas at once with the game's only fail states, and a 120 s idle timer can fail a player who is just exploring. Arcade then drops back to Ohm's law, a more basic idea than Lunch's start-up kick. Garage, QFN, Observatory and Spectrum each open a new domain without reusing the previous job's idea. Spectrum isn't a circuit job at all. Suggested chain: Playground → Meeting → Arcade (resistance sets current) → Lunch (budgets, kick, capacitor) → Garage (inductive kick, reusing the kick) → Observatory (filters, reusing C and L) → QFN (decoupling and return) → Spectrum.

#### Clarity

> *gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock:* When a job item is stranded, nothing tells the player:
> - The card keeps its text and the prompt offers nearby junk ('Grab the crate', 'Grab the chair').
> - The objective marker follows the item behind walls (into the closet) or into the void beyond the arcade's right lip.
> - In the dark Lunch storeroom the item itself is invisible among the boxes, with only the marker cone showing where it is.
> 
> The respawn puff at home reads well, but there is no cue where the item vanished.

> *gap3-recheck-list:* The vending machine faces +z with its window and products toward the player (LR2 PASS). The Lunch swing leaves stay upright after shoving through and back; they only rotate on y (lunch-runtime.ts:227). Window shafts are no longer hard wedges; at the game camera and at zoom 9 they're barely visible at all. On the Meeting back wall the windows sit behind cabinet rows with boxes on top. The pins and spool exist (P4): six pins at their homes, a yellow spool by the anchor. The spool's remaining length is still unreadable at the game camera (already reported).

> *gap4-juice-audio:* Success and failure moments lack the DR-11 trio.
> 
> | Moment | Flash | Sound | Hitstop |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Cable plug-in (Playground/Meeting) | yes | yes | yes |
> | Win | confetti only | generic jingle | no |
> | Any failure | no | yes | no |
> 
> Immediate-frame captures confirm it: juice-audio-02 (win), -06 (trip), -12 (spoil) and -26 (send-back). Each frame shows at most a few specks. The Lunch fail frame keeps the camera on a cheering Pip, with the fridge far up-frame. The station sign-off instantly swaps in the next board, so the solve has no visible beat at the bench camera.

> *progression:* The lobby gets the basics right. The job card names the next door ('00 · Cable Playground', moving to '01 · Big Meeting' after a clear), a marker bounces over it, the prompt reads 'E Enter 00 · Cable Playground', and a locked door explains itself ('Locked: finish 03 · Overheating Arcade first'). Signposting of progress is faint: the wing lamp sits on the top edge of the frame, the medals are about 10 px, Pip reloads at the centre rather than the door he left, and nothing happens on return. The doors don't hint at what is behind them. The Rush lock leaks through the Jobs board and the URL, opens on a C, and then the lobby recommends Rush ahead of the next new job. The result flow switches from 'Next →' (00–02) to 'Jobs' (03+). The title still shows the unclear 'HQ' badge on Play and a faint gamepad icon (L4). Text volume in the lobby is low and the card is short, which is good. The R key hints on the result and fail cards are false.

#### Models

> *gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock:* Out of scope. One observation: interior walls show 1.35 m but collide at 2.6 m, so thrown props stop in mid-air above the visible cap (stuck-softlock-09-1).

> *gap3-recheck-list:* The bookshelf colour wrap (prefabs.ts:123-125) is fixed. All three rows have 7 coloured books in the Meeting and Playground at zoom 9, with no missing or black blocks. The palette still includes job yellow. The Lunch door leaves are solid two-part leaves with porthole windows and read well. The capacitor cart reads as 'blue cylinders on a trolley', with no gauge to show its job.

> *gap4-juice-audio:* Not in scope for this gap-fill. Note only that the win and fail beats would benefit from a slumped Pip pose (none exists, and pipRig only has a won pose) and a power-down state on devices (projector screen, oven lamp). Those are animation and state assets, not meshes.

> *progression:* Not the focus of this dimension. From the progression angle: lobby doors read well up close (progression-20), with a colour frame, number panel, name plate and medal, but they read as one repeated slab at the game camera. The wing-lamp reward is too high to see, and the medal plate is too small. The Meeting win shot still frames the projector wall and blobs without Pip (progression-36, QA 10 / M3 still open).

378 entries: 2 × P0, 158 × P1, 218 × P2. IDs are ordered P0 → P1 → P2, and within a priority by player impact (playability > teaching > fun > clarity > overlap > visual-bug > model-detail > art-style), then by how many reviewers independently found it. "Room" is `cross-cutting` when the same root cause was found in several rooms; the entry lists every room. Line numbers are as of commit 853cad2.

### R5-001

**R5-001 | P0 | global, qfn, spectrum, arcade, arcade-rush, garage, observatory | playability | Phone / touch: every bench camera crops its own controls, and bench pills print keyboard keys a touch player cannot press (QFN and Spectrum cannot be finished on a phone)**

Found by: `hud-ui#0` (P0 playability), `qfn-play#0` (P0 playability), `spectrum-play#0` (P0 playability), `arcade-play#0` (P1 playability), `arcade-rush-play#4` (P1 playability), `garage-play#10` (P1 playability), `observatory-play#10` (P1 playability), `hud-ui#11` (P1 clarity). Batch: B1 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*hud-ui* — **Phone (390×844): every bench camera crops its own controls; in the Arcade only the 100 Ω and 470 Ω bins can be tapped, so the clean fixes can't be built by touch.** At 390×844 the bench camera uses the same framing as on a 16:10 desktop, so the table runs off both sides of the portrait screen. In the Arcade the left column of block bins (47 Ω and 220 Ω) and the sign-off button on the right are off-screen. I tapped a dense grid over the whole visible bench (every 8 px, x 2–390, y 380–500). Only the 100 Ω and 470 Ω bins answered (`phoneTakeable:[100,470]`). Pinball's clean fix needs a 220 Ω block and Rhythm needs 47 ‖ 47, so on a touch-only phone those jobs can't be solved the intended way. The other benches crop the same way. Garage: the 1000 µF cap bin and the left edge of the board are cut off. Observatory: the antenna and cable-route controls on the left and the capacitor can on the right are cut off. Spectrum: the RADIO and MICRO band buttons, the 100 mW power button and SEND are cut off. Only QFN fits. There are no keys to fall back on, because a phone has no number row. This is the NEXT_STEPS open item ('check every bench at 390×844'), and it is still open. The game ships a phone layout (thumbstick, touch action buttons), so this blocks play there.

*qfn-play* — **Phone (390×844): TURN, LAYER, VIA, CHECK and SHIP are off-screen, so a touch player can't finish the job.** At the bench in portrait, the bench camera only pulls back by clamp(1.25/aspect,1,2.1) (src/game.ts:372). The 3D tool pucks sit at x=±1.58 m either side of the board (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:99-106), so only UNDO (x=-1.08) is still in frame. The board itself shrinks to about 250 px wide (s5 log: cell centres span x 70–320), so a cell is about 19 px, well under a usable touch target. CHECK and SHIP have keyboard fallbacks only (C and Enter, station.ts:27). The prompt pill reads 'Enter Ship' but can't be tapped (src/ui/objectives.ts:93 adds no handler). A phone player can place parts and draw tracks, but can never ship a board, so the room can't be completed. The phone layout CSS also hides the net list (qfn.css:9), so the board's progress is invisible on a phone. Review 3 (REVIEW_A §1) already reported that 'On QFN none of MOVE, TURN, PEN, ERASE or SHIP are visible'. It is still open.

*spectrum-play* — **Phone (390×844): the desk view crops off SEND and the RADIO/MICRO keys, and touch has no other way to send, so the job can't be finished.** At 390×844 the bench camera can't fit the 4.4 m desk. In the bench shot the band row starts at 'RMAL' (THERMAL): the RADIO and MICRO keys are past the left edge. On the right, the power keys are cut at '100 m' and the green SEND cap (table x +1.95) is entirely off-screen. In bench mode the walking controls hide (ui.css:246). There is no HTML touch fallback for band, power, hatch or send, and a phone has no keyboard for 1–5 or Enter. A touch player therefore can't pick Radio, which Delivery 1 needs, and can't press SEND at all, so the job can't be completed on a phone. The phone layout also moves the station toast to just under the panel (ui.css:255), where it covers the top of the hall map, the surface the player drags to aim. The phone joystick and the action buttons show the game is meant to be played by touch, so this blocks play there. (R3B M1 already noted 'Phone bench layout OPEN'; this is the concrete spectrum consequence.)

*arcade-play* — **Phone (touch): the bench can't be finished. The sign-off button and the 47/220 Ω bins are off-screen in portrait, and the HUD covers them in landscape.** On a phone the bench is touch-only: there are no on-screen buttons for P, F, X, A/S/D or Enter. The only input is tapping the 3D parts.

Portrait, 390×844:
- The bench camera pulls back by `clamp(1.25/aspect,1,2.1)` (src/game.ts:371). At aspect 0.46 that clamps to 2.1, which still isn't wide enough for the 4.3 m bench.
- The left column of bins (47 Ω, 220 Ω) is completely off the left edge. Only a few pixels of the 100 Ω and 470 Ω bins show.
- The sign-off stamp (POWERAT.x+.52, station.ts:209) is off the right edge.
- I made a passing setup (soakDone true), then tapped a 6 px grid over the right edge (x 330–389, y 470–530). The station index stayed 0, so the cabinet can't be signed off.
- The prompt pill reads "Enter Sign off", but a phone has no Enter key and the pill isn't tappable.
- The bench fills only the middle sixth of the screen; the lower half is empty pink rug.
- The Rhythm pad's elegant fix needs two 47 Ω blocks, which can't be reached at all.

Landscape, 844×390:
- The station panel covers the power lever, the ACROSS slot and the sign-off stamp.
- The objective card covers the 47 and 100 Ω bins.
- The panel has pointer-events:none (src/ui/ui.css:218), so blind taps may land, but the controls can't be seen.

A phone player who reaches the bench can't complete the job. A12 (phone bench layout) was OPEN in R3B; it now blocks play.

*arcade-rush-play* — **Phone (390×844): the bench is unplayable; two bins and the sign-off stamp are off-screen and there are no touch keys.** At 390×844 the bench camera keeps the desktop distance and FOV.
- The 47 Ω and 220 Ω bins are off the left edge; only slivers of the 100 and 470 bins show.
- The SIGN OFF stamp is off the right edge.
- The whole channel board is about 260 px wide, so the A/S/D pads and the ACROSS slot are about 15–20 px touch targets.
- The prompt pill shows keyboard badges ('P Power on', 'Esc Stand up') on a touch device with a virtual joystick and no keyboard.
- The toast covers the meter.

The bench's only inputs are hotkeys and 3D clicks, so a phone player can't take a 47 Ω or 220 Ω block or sign a cabinet off. No rush cabinet can be served on a phone. This is A12 / R3A M1, still open; Rush makes it worse because the mode is about speed. The RUSH panel also sits in the middle of the walking view on the phone start screen, just under Pip.

*garage-play* — **Phone 390×844: the bench is cut off at both ends, the toast covers PULSE and TEST, and keyboard prompts show on touch.** At 390×844 the bench view widens to distance × clamp(1.25/aspect, 1, 2.1), which isn't enough for the 4.3 m table. In shot 72 the 12 V battery and fuse are cut off at the left, and the parts tray at the right: TVS 33 V and 1000 µF are only partly visible and hard to tap. The 'Caught it…' toast sits over the PULSE button and half the TEST pod. The station panel collapses to its title, so the job ask isn't readable. Prompts still show keyboard keys ('1–5 Change the parts', 'Esc Stand up') on a touch device. The survey (shot 71) crops both side walls, and the dock and charging bays are only partly visible. On a phone, job 2 (which needs the TVS) and job 3 (if you try the capacitor) involve tapping half-visible tiles behind HUD. This breaks DR-21 (the survey shows the whole room on a phone) and DR-22 (controls are consistent), and NEXT_STEPS §1 / R3B A12 ('check every bench at 390×844') is still open for the garage.

*observatory-play* — **Phone portrait: the bench is cropped (no capacitor, no rods) and has no touch controls for the bench keys.** At 390×844 the bench camera keeps the desktop framing (distance 6.3, pitch .88) and the bench is about 2× wider than the screen. The capacitor bin and most of the can tray are cut off on the right; the antenna rack is cut off on the left. The capacitor is the job 1 solution, and the whip rack is job 3. The prompt says '← → Turn the knob' and 'S / H Plug it in', but there is no on-screen arrow, Enter (LOG), S or H key. The only alternative is tapping 3D targets that are ~5–10 px wide (rods, knob). In the room, the station panel sits in the middle of the screen over Pip. The survey crops the dome and the right of the gallery. A phone player can't finish job 1 if the capacitor is off-screen. Breaks DR-21 (survey fits on a phone) and DR-22 (controls work in every view).

*hud-ui* — **Bench pills on phone print keyboard keys (1–4, P, Enter, 1–3) that a touch player can't press.** At 390×844 the bench pill shows '1–4 Take a block', 'P Fuse cooling', 'Enter Sign off', 'P Pulse the motor', '1–3 Take a can' and 'E Fetch the pod'. A phone has no such keys and the pill isn't tappable (pointer-events:none, src/ui/ui.css:208). Touch players get instructions they can't follow, and the hover hint that names the bin ('1 Take a 47 Ω block') never fires on touch, because there is no hover. AGENTS 2 allows a one-line key prompt; on a phone that line has to describe a touch action.

**Fix.**

*From hud-ui:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Change the existing pull-back in src/game.ts:372 instead of adding per-station code first. Replace clamp(1.25/cam.aspect,1,2.1) with a fit to each station's table width: horizontal half-FOV = atan(tan(vfov/2)*aspect), dist = max(v.distance, (tableHalfWidth*1.08)/tan(hHalfFov)). An optional `width` on each station's `view` gives the table width, so no station needs its own camera code. At about 2.8× pull-back the monitor text gets very small on a phone, so also consider a portrait-only bench layout (bins and sign-off moved under the board). The pill-tap backstop only helps single-key prompts (see finding 11).

Reviewer's fix: Give each station's bench `view` an aspect-aware distance and FOV. When camera.aspect < 1, pull back until the table's world-space bounding box (bins and sign-off button included) fits inside 92% of the screen width: dist = (tableWidth/2) / (tan(fov/2) * aspect) * 1.08. You could also rotate the bench camera to look down the table's long axis in portrait. Put this in a shared helper in src/stations/shared.ts, `fitBench(view, tableBox, aspect)`, and call it from each station's camera update (arcade, garage, observatory, qfn, spectrum station.ts). As a backstop, make the phone bench prompt pill tappable: a tap on it performs its action (see the keyboard-glyph finding).

*From qfn-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Part 1 is wrong. A shorter camera distance (9.5 against today's 5.6×2.1≈11.8) narrows the visible width, which would push the pucks further off-screen. Part 4 can't be done as written: 13 cells × 36 px = 468 px, wider than a 390 px screen. Corrected fix: in portrait, turn the bench camera 90° (yaw offset in game.ts:372 when cam.aspect<1) so the board's 9-cell side runs across the screen (9×0.15 m). Lay the 5 pucks plus UNDO out in one or two rows below the board (rebuild on resize). Also add DOM buttons for CHECK and SHIP to the bench chip under @media (pointer:coarse), and make .prompt-pill call g.station.key(code) on pointerdown while g.atBench. Verify with a 390×844 spec that taps the SHIP control and expects station.board to advance.

Reviewer's fix: 1) Add an optional `viewPortrait` to the Station interface (src/stations/types.ts) and use it in src/game.ts:372 when cam.aspect<1. For QFN, `{distance:9.5,pitch:1.25,lookY:.2}` puts the board at the top of the frame. 2) In QfnBench.buildBench, when innerWidth&lt;innerHeight, lay the five pucks out in one row under the board (z = board near edge + 0.45, x = -1.2…1.2, 0.6 m apart) instead of at the sides, and rebuild them on resize. 3) Make the prompt pill tappable: in ObjectivesHUD, a pointerdown on .prompt-pill while g.atBench calls g.station.key(code) for the shown key (Enter→ship, C→check). 4) At aspect<1, scale S (cell size) up so a cell is ≥ 36 px.

*From spectrum-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Prefer fix (b), the HTML control strip under body[data-bench] with (pointer:coarse). Fix (a) has a problem: raising the game.ts:372 cap to 3.0 at aspect 0.46 makes the 4.4 m desk only about 390 px wide. The band keys (0.17 m) would then be about 15 px across, far below a 44 px touch target, so (a) alone leaves the controls hard to hit. A cheap extra fallback: make .prompt-pill tappable (pointerdown → the same action as its key, so 'Enter · Send' sends). Verify: a touchscreen-only Playwright run (page.touchscreen.tap, no keyboard) through all three deliveries reaches won===true.

Reviewer's fix: Pick one of two fixes:
(a) Add a per-station portrait view. Station gets an optional `portraitView:{distance,pitch,lookY}`. For spectrum use about {distance:6.1, pitch:1.25, lookY:.42} and raise the game.ts:372 clamp cap from 2.1 to about 3.0 when `cam.aspect<.6`, so the whole 4.5 m table fits.
(b) Better for touch: under `body[data-bench]` with `(pointer:coarse)`, render a compact HTML control strip from the station's clickables: five band chips, 1/10/100 mW, HATCH and a big SEND. Hide the 3D labels' reliance.
Also move the phone toast below the map (top: calc(84px + 30vh + map height)), or show it as a one-line chip at the bottom.

*From arcade-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep the reviewer's layout fix (portrait bench layout or wider pull-back, and a touch action strip). Also correct the evidence: the stamp is reachable but only as a ~4 px sliver at x≈389, and landscape sign-off works through the panel blind. The test must check that every bin, the lever and the stamp project fully inside the viewport with at least 44×44 px tap targets, not merely that a tap somewhere works. Clamping only to 2.1 in game.ts:372 isn't enough at aspect 0.46. Either raise the clamp to about 2.8 for aspect<0.6, or lay the bench out in two rows. Making the prompt pill tappable (pointer-events:auto, calling station.key(p.key) for single-key prompts) is the cheapest partial fix.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Add a portrait bench layout in src/stations/arcade/station.ts:
   - When `game.view.camera.aspect<0.8`, move `this.top`'s contents into a 2-row layout: bins in a 2×2 block above the board (`BINSAT={x:-.5,z:-.9}`), and the power lever plus sign-off stamp below the board (`POWERAT={x:.6,z:.75}`).
   - Alternatively, give the station a `view` per aspect (`view.distance` about 7.5, `lookX` 0) and scale `this.top` by 0.75 on the x axis.
2. Add a touch action strip at the bench (src/ui/objectives.ts, next to `.bench-chip`) with 4 large buttons: POWER, FLIP, SIGN OFF ✓, STAND UP. Make the prompt pill tappable: it calls `station.key(&lt;code>)` for its key.
3. In landscape, hide `.station-panel` rows while `body[data-bench]` is set and the viewport height is under 500 px, or dock the panel to the bottom-left at 50 % width.

*From arcade-rush-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Do not use distance*max(1,1.55/aspect). At aspect 0.46 that is about 3.4×, smaller than today's 2.1× cap, and it shrinks the pads to under 10 px. Keep the camera as it is and add the DOM keypad on (pointer:coarse): 4 candy bins, A/S/D, X, Flip, Power and Sign off, each at least 44 px and each calling act(). Or give the arcade a portrait-only view with lookX and a pitch closer to top-down, so the bins and the stamp move inside the frame. Hide the kbd badges in the prompt pill on touch, or make the pill tappable so it runs the prompted action.

Reviewer's fix: In `src/game.ts:370` (the bench camera), scale the bench distance by aspect: `distance=v.distance*Math.max(1,1.55/aspect)`, so all 4.3 m of the bench fits in portrait. Better still, on coarse pointers (`matchMedia('(pointer:coarse)')`), render a DOM bench keypad in the station panel:
- 4 candy buttons for 47/100/220/470 in their CANDY colours;
- A/S/D position buttons;
- an X button and a Flip button;
- a big Power toggle and a ✓ Sign off button, each at least 44 px.

Each button calls `act()`. On touch, hide the key badges in the prompt pill. Move the RUSH panel to the top edge on narrow screens.

*From garage-play:* - Add an optional portrait `view` to the station (src/stations/types.ts), e.g. {distance:6.8, pitch:1.05, lookX:0} plus a portrait clamp up to 2.6, or move the parts tray onto two rows in front of the board when cam.aspect < 1.
- In ui.css, under body[data-bench] with max-width 600px, dock the .station-toast at the top, below the card, never over the bottom 40 % of the canvas.
- In promptFor, or in the station prompt, hide the &lt;kbd> key on touch (matchMedia('(pointer:coarse)')) and show an icon instead.
- Survey: fit the zoom to the room's bounding box and the aspect instead of a fixed 44 (game.ts:366).

*From observatory-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Not 'add aspect scaling', which already exists: raise the clamp's upper bound in game.ts:372 (for example clamp(1.25/aspect,1,3)) and/or add a portrait pitch/lookX override in Station.view. Multi-key prompts like '1–4' or 'A S D' can't map to one tap and still need the bench to fit on screen (finding 0).

Make the pill clickable at a bench (pointer-events:auto), so a tap runs the prompt's action through station.act. Implement this in ObjectivesHUD.update, src/ui/objectives.ts:116-117.

### R5-002

**R5-002 | P0 | meeting | playability | Meeting: the power strip, coupler or second reel can be lobbed into the sealed server closet and lost for good (no respawn, no reach, no hint)**

Found by: `gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock#0` (P0 playability), `gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock#1` (P1 playability). Batch: B1 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock* — **The Meeting power strip can be lost for good in the sealed server closet: no respawn, no reach, no hint.** The Big Meeting server closet is a sealed box. Its walls run x −16.5…−11.775 and z −10…−5.375 with no doorway (src/levels/meeting.ts:35: closet-east and closet-front, plus the back and left shell walls). The walls look 1.35 m high but have a 2.6 m collider (src/levels/decor.ts:44-49). Pip can't hop the collider. A jump-throw (Space, then Q at about 0.36 s) still lobs a held item over it. My script did this from (−13.5, −1.25) facing −z. The required power strip landed at (−14.11, 0.04, −8.27), on the closet floor in front of the racks.

Pip can't get it back:
- Pip can't enter the closet.
- Grabbing needs a horizontal distance under 1.65 m (src/game.ts:192). From every walkable point along the closet walls ((−11.45, −6/−7.5/−9.5) and (−12.5/−14/−15.8, −5.05)), the closest Pip got was 2.84 m. E grabbed nothing, or a nearby box.
- Respawn never fires. The stuck rule only counts an id'd item above y 2.1 m (src/game.ts:341-342), and the out-of-bounds reset only fires below y −3 or outside width/2+1 (src/game.ts:339). The strip sat at y 0.04, inside the bounds, and was still there after 30 s.

The circuit can't close without the placed strip: needsStrip() and stripPlaced() (src/game.ts:246-247) gate leads[0] (src/game.ts:348). The job can't be finished. The only way out is R or Restart, and nothing tells the player that. The card keeps saying 'Fetch the power strip by the printer…'. The objective marker sits over the racks, behind the wall Pip can't pass (stuck-softlock-10). The prompt offers 'Grab the crate' instead. In the survey the strip is invisible behind the closet wall (stuck-softlock-12).

This breaks AGENTS 7 ('stuck items respawn'), DR-15 and DR-25. The throw takes two keys any curious player presses (jump, then throw), next to the job's starting area: the strip starts 5 m from the closet.

*gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock* — **The Meeting coupler and the second reel (on its mail cart) can also be lobbed into the sealed closet and lost for good.** The same sealed-closet hole takes the clean route's two parts:
- The coupler, picked at (−3.65, 5.3), landed at (−14.30, 0.09, −8.51). The nearest reachable point was 3.59 m away.
- E at the second reel's spot (−3, 5.3) picked up the mail cart. The selection picked 'mail-cart' over 'extension' (src/game.ts:192-193: both are id'd and get the same −2 bonus). After a second jump-throw the cart ended inside the closet at (−15.80, 0.25, −7.00). The nearest reachable point was 1.98 m away.

Neither respawned after 10 s, because both sit below y 2.1 (src/game.ts:342).

The clean coupler-then-reel route (routes.spec.ts:39-44, the room's intended tidy solution, DR-01) is then impossible. The game gives no hint, and the card's 'coupler first' guidance (objectives.ts:77) now points at an item that is gone. The job can still finish by the coffee-reel or single-reel sprint routes, so this is less severe than losing the strip. But it removes the room's taught solution, which breaks DR-15 and DR-25. The brief asks for any required item that can be lost for good to be filed as P0.

**Evidence.**
