### R5-012

**R5-012 | P1 | meeting | playability | Meeting closet corner: at zoom 9 and a low orbit the camera ends up inside or behind an uncut wall, so the whole screen is beige and Pip is gone**

Found by: `gap3-recheck-list#0` (P1 playability). Batch: R-meeting (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

At spawn by the server closet (about −11.3, −7.4) at zoom 9, 3 of the 8 yaws in a low-pitch sweep (orbit(0,−200), then −180 px steps) fill the whole 1440×900 frame with one flat beige wall face. Pip, the plug, the reel and the job are all invisible. Only the HUD is left, still saying 'F Pick up the plug'. The same happens at yaw steps 375, 625 and 750 in the first sweep. At the default pitch one yaw (def-3) also hides Pip behind the closet wall cap and the server racks. The same sweep in the Lunch corner (14.5, 8.4) never blanks: the walls cut away correctly there. So this is room-specific, not general. The cause is probably the cutaway test in src/game.ts:383-385. It decides per wall, using the wall group's centre (`wall.group.parent.getWorldPosition`) and `normal·toCam > .2`. When the camera sits past a corner, the vector from the centre of a long back or left wall to the camera is nearly parallel to the wall, the dot falls below 0.2, and the wall stays 3 m tall between the camera and Pip. Nothing pulls the camera in when it is inside a wall. This is the room where the player spends the first 20 s, and the corner is the spawn point. Right-dragging there is exactly what a new player does to 'look around', and the screen goes blank. This is not the known 'stub hides Pip's legs' finding from the Playground. Here the whole frame is lost.

**Evidence.**

- [recheck-list-04g-meeting-closet-pitchdown-o-750.jpg](shots/recheck-list-04g-meeting-closet-pitchdown-o-750.jpg)
- [recheck-list-04h-closet-sweep-375.jpg](shots/recheck-list-04h-closet-sweep-375.jpg)
- [recheck-list-04k-closet-sweep-contact.jpg](shots/recheck-list-04k-closet-sweep-contact.jpg)
- [recheck-list-04l-corner-sweep-meeting.jpg](shots/recheck-list-04l-corner-sweep-meeting.jpg)
- [recheck-list-04l-corner-sweep-lunch.jpg](shots/recheck-list-04l-corner-sweep-lunch.jpg) (control: no blanking)
- `src/game.ts:383-385`
- `src/game.ts:381-382` (no camera collision)
- [verify-gap3-recheck-list-08-closet-contact.jpg](shots/verify-gap3-recheck-list-08-closet-contact.jpg) (my 8-yaw contact sheet; frame 4 blank, frame 3 Pip hidden)
- [verify-gap3-recheck-list-04-meeting-closet-low.jpg](shots/verify-gap3-recheck-list-04-meeting-closet-low.jpg) (centre luma std 1.3)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap3-recheck-list/corner.mjs`
- `src/levels/decor.ts:73` (only back and side shell walls exist, so the Lunch front-right corner is not a valid control)
- `src/levels/meeting.ts:33` (width 33, depth 20: back wall z=-10, side wall x=-16.5, both centred far from the closet)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep fix (1): stub when (cam - nearestPointOnWallSegment)·normal > 0, or when the camera is past the wall plane. For (2), raycast only against the shell walls' tall upper parts, not the fading interior walls (game.occluders), so the pull-in and the fade don't fight. The Lunch control should be replaced by a corner that actually has shell walls, e.g. Lunch's back-left corner.

Reviewer's fix: In src/game.ts updateCamera:
(1) Run the cutaway test from the nearest point on each wall segment to the camera, not from the wall centre. Or use `normal·toCam > 0` together with 'the camera is on the outside half-space of the wall plane': `(cam - wallPoint)·normal > 0`.
(2) Add a camera pull-in. Raycast from the focus to the wanted camera position against the shell walls and the interior walls (or the static colliders), and clamp the distance to hit − 0.3 m.
(3) As a safety net, if the frame is filled by one non-occluder, raise the pitch to at least 0.55.

**Verify.**

- Rerun mockups/review5/tools/recheck-list/corner.mjs (meeting at −11.3, −7.4; zoom 9; 8 yaws at default and low pitch). Every frame should show Pip, with a luma std > 30 in the centre region (today's failures measure 25–34 with a flat frame). Add a playwright check that no orbit at the spawn returns a frame whose centre 400×400 crop is a single colour.

**Rules:** —

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced this. In Meeting I walked to (-11.3,-7.4), zoomed to 9, orbited (0,-200), then swept 8 yaws in -180 px steps. Frame 4 is one flat beige wall: the centre 400×400 crop has a luma std of 1.3, against 37–62 for the other frames. In frame 3 Pip is completely hidden behind the closet wall cap and the dark racks. In frame 7 he is mostly hidden behind clutter boxes. The geometry backs up the stated cause.

### R5-013

**R5-013 | P1 | global | playability | Letting go of the plug (Q) right against the socket never seats it; the plug lies in the ring, unplugged, and the prompt moves on to the switch**

Found by: `gap7-snap-grab-target#1` (P1 playability). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The forgiving snap only runs inside interact() when F is pressed (src/game.ts:205). releasePlug() (src/game.ts:259-265), the Q path and the 'F Drop the plug' path outside range, never checks the socket. In Playground I held the plug facing the socket and pressed Q with the plug end 0.46 m from the socket centre. The prompt had just said 'F Plug in' (in range). The plug dropped visibly inside the cyan target ring, touching the socket box, and stayed `connected:false, electrical:off`. The same happened in Meeting at the power strip. A player who sees the plug lying in the ring believes it is in. The lamp then stays dark, and the next prompt reads 'E Switch on (needs power first)', which suggests the order is wrong rather than the plug. Hard rule 7 says a plug that looks in snaps in. Q is also the key the game advertises for 'let go', so releasing at the socket is a natural action.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:205` (snap only in interact)
- `src/game.ts:259-265` (releasePlug: no seat test)
- [snap-grab-target-07-pg-before-Q-0p3.jpg](shots/snap-grab-target-07-pg-before-Q-0p3.jpg)
- [snap-grab-target-08-pg-after-Q-0p3.jpg](shots/snap-grab-target-08-pg-after-Q-0p3.jpg) (plug inside ring, not connected)
- [snap-grab-target-18-mt-wallplug-afterQ.jpg](shots/snap-grab-target-18-mt-wallplug-afterQ.jpg)
- s2 log: q03 plug->socket 0.46, after KeyQ connected false electrical off
- [verify-gap7-snap-grab-target-03-pg-afterQ.jpg](shots/verify-gap7-snap-grab-target-03-pg-afterQ.jpg) (plug against socket box inside ring, not seated)
- v1.mjs p log: beforeQ prompt 'FPlug in' plug->socket 0.46; afterQ connected false electrical off

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Run the seat test before calling this.rope.release(). release() returns the slingshot energy and resets the strain, so read rope.strain and evaluate the condition first. Seat only when energy<=1, so the slingshot chaos path is unchanged.

Reviewer's fix: Extract the seat test into `trySeat()` (the same condition as :205: `Math.min(dist(Pip,target)-.6, dist(plug,target))<1.6 && strain<1.12`) and call it at the top of releasePlug() when energy<=1, i.e. no slingshot, so chaos throws still fling. Also, in step(), a plug lying idle within 0.6 m of level.target for 0.3 s seats itself with the plugFlash. Use the same rule for the Lunch cable release (src/lunch-runtime.ts release()) and for the strip/robot/pod drops on Q (throw) when the item lands inside the snap radius.

**Verify.**

- New spec in tests/routes.spec.ts: 'a plug let go beside the socket seats': F, route to (5.95,-6), Q, wait .4 → expect connected (snapshot().electrical after the switch = on). Retake snap-grab-target-08 showing the plug flash.

**Rules:** AGENTS 7, DR-14

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced it in Playground. The prompt read 'F Plug in', the plug was 0.46 m from the socket centre, and I pressed Q. Afterwards connected=false and electrical=off, and the plug lies inside the cyan ring touching the socket box. releasePlug() (src/game.ts:259-265) never runs a seat test.

### R5-014

**R5-014 | P1 | garage | playability | WASD at the bench pulls fitted parts out of their sockets (A = 'take out ACROSS MOTOR')**

Found by: `garage-play#0` (P1 playability). Batch: B2 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

At the bench the station grabs the keyboard before walking does (src/game.ts:164), and the garage maps KeyA/KeyS/KeyD to the three sockets (src/stations/garage/station.ts:330-331). act('slot') with nothing held and a part already fitted removes the part (station.ts:206). So a player who has just fitted the flyback diode and reaches for WASD to walk away, which is the first thing anyone does in a third-person game, silently unfits it. I reproduced this in 02-wrong.mjs: with the diode fitted across the motor, pressing W then A gave slots {} and put the diode back in the tray (shot 49: 'Across motor —', prompt 'A Empty socket'). W does nothing, A and S remove parts, D removes the capacitor. The player then presses P, sees the 77 V reset again and believes the fix stopped working. That wrongly teaches that the diode doesn't help. It breaks DR-22 (the same key means the same verb everywhere; here A means 'walk' in the room and 'unplug' at the bench) and DR-19 (the key does something the player never asked for). It is not a soft-lock, but it quietly undoes progress and causes confusion.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:330-331`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:202-207`
- `src/game.ts:164`
- [garage-play-49-after-wasd.jpg](shots/garage-play-49-after-wasd.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/garage-play/02-wrong.mjs` (log: 'after W,A' slots {})
- [verify-garage-play-06-after-W-A.jpg](shots/verify-garage-play-06-after-W-A.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-garage-play/01-verify.mjs` log: fitted {fly:diode} → after W same → after A {}
- `src/stations/arcade/station.ts:353` (KeyA/S/D → slot 0/1/2)

**Fix.**

Pick one of these in station.ts key():
(a) Treat KeyW/KeyA/KeyS/KeyD and the arrow keys at the bench as 'stand up' (call game.leaveBench()), as E and Esc already do. Move the socket keys to Z/X/C or 7/8/9, and update SLOT_KEYS (station.ts:59) and hoverHint.
(b) Keep A/S/D, but have them only fit a held part, never remove one. Removal stays on click or Backspace: in act('slot'), return false when nothing is held and the call came from a key.
Also apply the same audit to the arcade bench, which also maps A/S/D.

**Verify.**

- New Playwright case in tests/station-garage.spec.ts: setUp, then pick diode, slot fly, then press KeyW, KeyA, KeyS, KeyD. Expect station.slots.fly to still be the diode (option b), or atBench false with the diode still fitted (option a). Retake garage-play-49.

**Rules:** DR-19, DR-22

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Reproduced. With the diode fitted across the motor, KeyW did nothing and KeyA emptied the socket: slots went from {fly:diode} to {}, and the prompt changed to 'P Pulse the motor' (verify log, shot verify-garage-play-06-after-W-A.jpg). In code, game.ts:164 sends every key to station.key() before walking sees it, station.ts:331 maps A/S/D to slot, and station.ts:206 removes a fitted part when nothing is held.

### R5-017

**R5-017 | P1 | lunch | playability | Supply cart A tips onto its side (≈56°) when Pip walks past it**

Found by: `lunch-models#3` (P1 playability). Batch: R-lunch (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

I walked Pip from near the rack (−14.2, 5) to (−12, 1.6), the natural path from the power room to the splitters. Cart A was shoved 1.8 m and left leaning on the storeroom wall at 55.9° tilt: pos (−13.16, 0.80, 1.17). It stayed tipped after 2 s (lunch-models-99b; j.mjs log: 'tilt after 2 55.6', 'settled 55.9'). The cart is one of the two power sources the whole job is built on. Tipped, its gauge face points at the wall and its outlets aim at the ceiling, and it reads as broken. The respawn rule (game.ts:342) only fires above y 2.1, so it never rights itself. It is a 40 kg box collider 1.7 × 1.3 × 1.1 with its centre of mass at mid-height. Pip's controller can lever it over against the wall lip.

**Evidence.**

- `src/props/prefabs.ts:23` (supply size [1.7,1.3,1.1], mass 40)
- `src/props/prefabs.ts:163-168` (model sits low on wheels, but the collider COM is at the box centre)
- `src/game.ts:342` (stuck/respawn only when y > 2.1)
- [lunch-models-99b-cartA-tipped-close.jpg](shots/lunch-models-99b-cartA-tipped-close.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/lunch-models/j.mjs`
- `mockups/review5/tools/lunch-models/c.mjs` (log: cartA after bump tilt 55.6)
- [verify-lunch-models-06-cartA-after-walk.jpg](shots/verify-lunch-models-06-cartA-after-walk.jpg)
- v2.mjs output: 'walk2 ... tilt 55.6', 'tilt settled 55.9'
- `src/game.ts:331` (heavy carry sets angvel 0 but never resets rotation)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The fix is correct (Rapier's RigidBody.setEnabledRotations(x,y,z,wakeUp) exists). It is simplest to apply it when the prop's body is built for kinds supply, capcart and dolly. Also reset the rotation upright in the heavy-carry branch at game.ts:331, so grabbing any heavy prop rights it.

Reviewer's fix: Lock pitch and roll on wheeled carts. Where props are created (game.ts prop body setup), for kinds supply, capcart and dolly set body.setEnabledRotations(false,true,false,true), so they can spin about Y but never tip. Also lower their centre of mass with setAdditionalMassProperties so the COM is about 0.3 m above the floor. As a fallback, extend the respawn check at game.ts:342: if an id'd prop's up-vector y < 0.6 for 3 s, set it upright at its current x/z with a dust puff (this also covers DR-15).

**Verify.**

- Re-run mockups/review5/tools/lunch-models/j.mjs: 'tilt settled' must be < 5°. Retake lunch-models-99b: cart upright, gauge readable. tests/lunch.spec.ts must still pass.

**Rules:** DR-15

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Reproduced it exactly. Walking from (−13.83,5) to (−12,1.6) leaves cart A at 55.6° tilt, which settles at 55.9° at (−13.16,0.79,1.16). Cart B stays at 0°. In verify-lunch-models-06 the cart leans on the storeroom wall with its wheels in the air. walkTo moves in a straight line through the cart's footprint, but a player taking the same line would hit it the same way. game.ts:342 respawns only when y>2.1.

### R5-018

**R5-018 | P1 | lunch | playability | Pip gets pinned between the wedged right door leaf and the doorstop; movement keys stop working and only a jump frees him**

Found by: `lunch-play#1` (P1 playability). Batch: R-lunch (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The wedge is dropped by the corridor (doorSide 1 at drop time), so it is fixed at (1.02, 0.2, -1.25) inside the kitchen. Coming back from the lift room along the natural path ((10,1) → (1,-0.5)), Pip stopped at (1.83,-0.60), squeezed between the open right leaf (a kinematic collider), the doorstop and the kitchen front wall.

Holding D, S, A, W, Shift+D or S+D for 1 s each did not move Pip by even 1 cm. Only Space plus S got him out. Other scripted walks to targets in every direction also stalled there for more than 60 s.

A new player has no reason to think of jumping, so in practice this is a broken control on the main route. The prompt there reads 'E Grab the doorstop', which tempts the player to un-wedge the door. That cuts every cable (see the separate finding). The camera at zoom 9 also hides Pip behind the half-wall (lunch-play-t02), so the player can't even see what is holding him.

(3) Add a generic de-penetration in the player step (src/game.ts movement block). If input is held for more than 0.4 s and Pip moves less than 2 cm, nudge him 0.15 m along the contact normal (Rapier character controller computedCollision), or briefly allow a 0.3 m step-up.

### R5-019

**R5-019 | P1 | lunch | playability | 'E Grab the doorstop' near the wedged door is a trap: one press un-wedges the door and cuts every cable through it**

Found by: `lunch-play#7` (P1 playability). Batch: R-lunch (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Once the door is wedged, Pip passes it on almost every later leg. nearest() favours any id'd item by 2 m (src/game.ts:192-194), so whenever Pip is within 1.65 m of the jammed doorstop the prompt reads 'E Grab the doorstop' (lunch-play-t02, t03; s13 log, repeatedly). E is the verb the player presses most, for bridges, the tray, the shelf and the cart.

Picking the doorstop up makes it dynamic again (src/game.ts:228). The door then auto-closes and kills every cable through it (src/lunch-runtime.ts:248): the thick kitchen feed, the fridge feed and the conveyor feed. Each costs 15 to repair, the oven stops, and the bake regresses. The prompt gives no hint of this, so the forgiving-interaction rule turns into an unfair, invisible fail.

**Evidence.**

- [lunch-play-t02-trapped-close.jpg](shots/lunch-play-t02-trapped-close.jpg)
- [lunch-play-t03-trapped-orbit.jpg](shots/lunch-play-t03-trapped-orbit.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s13-order.mjs` log: prompt 'E Grab the doorstop' at multiple steps
- `src/game.ts:192-194,228`
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:214,248`
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v4-interact.mjs` log: 'F7 near wedge … prompt E Grab the doorstop', 'F7 after E held wedge wedged false', 'thick:b,kitchen:DEAD oven off'
- [verify-lunch-play-10-near-wedge-prompt.jpg](shots/verify-lunch-play-10-near-wedge-prompt.jpg)
- [verify-lunch-play-11-door-shut-cut.jpg](shots/verify-lunch-play-11-door-shut-cut.jpg)

**Fix.**

(1) In Game.nearest(), skip the doorstop while lunch.doorWedged() is true and any cable crosses the door rectangle. Lunch can expose a doorBusy() helper that reuses the segmentHits test from :248. Lunch then shows no prompt there.
(2) If un-wedging must stay possible, require F-hold or a second press within 1 s, and show the prompt text 'Unwedge the door (it will shut on your cables)'.

**Verify.**

- Spec: after the clean route's kitchen feed, walk to (1.3,-0.9) and press E. Expect held !== 'wedge', doorWedged true, and thick not dead. Retake t03: the prompt must not offer the doorstop.

**Rules:** AGENTS 7, DR-02, DR-18, DR-19

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Reproduced. With the kitchen fed by the thick cable and the door wedged, the prompt near the door read 'E Grab the doorstop'. E picked it up (held wedge, doorWedged false). After walking to (-3,-4.5), the door shut and thick became 'b,kitchen:DEAD', the oven went off, and the card regressed to 'Keep the oven on until the tray is baked'.

### R5-021

**R5-021 | P1 | observatory | playability | Observatory: the dome shell and platform have no colliders — Pip walks inside the dome and vanishes; props sink into the platform**

Found by: `observatory-models#0` (P1 playability), `observatory-models#14` (P2 overlap). Batch: R-observatory (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*observatory-models* — **Dome shell has no collider and is not an occluder: Pip walks inside the dome and disappears completely behind it.** The dome is two half-hemisphere meshes (inner starfield BackSide R=2.55, outer cream shell R+.06) at (-6.1, .15, -5.3). The only collider is a 1.2×2×1.2 box around the telescope pier (room.ts:69). The shell, the 2.85 m platform ring and the navy disc have no colliders, so Pip can walk straight through the cream shell into the dome. I walked Pip to (-5.34,-6.74), behind the telescope and inside the shell. From the front orbit Pip stands inside the sky (shot 66). After a 180° orbit, the opaque cream shell hides 100% of Pip at the game camera (shot 72) and at zoom 9 (shot 66b). The shell is about 2.6 m tall and is not in the occluder set (only pillars fade, decor.ts:55), so it never fades. The same shell takes up the left 40% of the frame next to the rack in shot 33. This is the 'camera hides Pip' failure that AGENTS 8 and DR-12 forbid. Walking through a solid-looking cream wall also breaks the physical read of the room: the player can't tell the dome from a painted backdrop.

*observatory-models* — **Dome platform has no collider: pushed props and the astronomer sink into the 15 cm ring and disc.** The platform ring is cyl(R+.25,R+.3,.14) with its top at y .14, and the navy disc is at y .15 (room.ts:69). Neither has a collider. The clutter lane keeps clutter off at load, but anything Pip pushes onto the platform rests at floor level, 14–15 cm down into it. In shot 12-dome-o70, after Pip walks up, the yellow and purple beanbags sit sunk into the lavender ring and onto the disc. The astronomer coworker at (-4.4,-4.4) stands ≈1.9 m from the dome centre, on the disc, with its body origin at floor level, so its base is buried 15 cm (observatory.ts:16, shots 32/60). g.audit can't see any of this because the platform isn't a collider.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/observatory/room.ts:68-73`
- `src/stations/observatory/room.ts:69` (solid only 1.2×2×1.2 at the pier)
- [observatory-models-66-pip-inside-dome-shell.jpg](shots/observatory-models-66-pip-inside-dome-shell.jpg)
- [observatory-models-66b-pip-inside-dome-shell-o.jpg](shots/observatory-models-66b-pip-inside-dome-shell-o.jpg)

- [verify-observatory-models-03-inside-dome-orbit180.jpg](shots/verify-observatory-models-03-inside-dome-orbit180.jpg) (same Pip fully hidden by the shell)

- `src/game.ts:387-388` (single-ray occluder fade)

- [observatory-models-12-dome-o70.jpg](shots/observatory-models-12-dome-o70.jpg)

- `src/game.ts:83` (enableAutostep(.25,.2,true))

**Fix.**

*From observatory-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Collider: don't use 2.6 m-tall boxes at r 2.6. The shell is a hemisphere, so above ~0.5 m those boxes would sit outside the visible curve and thrown props would hit invisible walls. Use ~12 segments about 1.2 m tall (y 0–1.2) centred at r≈2.45, just inside the base of the shell, on the back half only (angles π..2π). Occlusion: decorRoot parts are batched, so the shell and the BackSide starfield dome need their own cloned transparent materials on game.root, pushed into game.occluders, as decor.ts:47-48 does for interior walls. The fade uses a single ray (game.ts:387), so a broad 5 m shell also needs a chest/head ray, or the DR-12 three-point check.

Reviewer's fix: In dressObservatory (room.ts:68-73), add a ring of thin solid() boxes along the back half-circle of the shell: 12 segments of 0.15×2.6×1.4 m at radius 2.6 around (dx,dz) for angles π..2π, each rotated tangentially. Add a low solid disc (cylinder collider r=2.85, h=.16) for the platform so props and Pip stand on it rather than in it. Register shellOut (and the starfield dome) as camera occluders using the same mechanism the pillars use (decor.ts:55 / game.ts occluder list), so they fade to ≤0.25 opacity when they sit between the camera and Pip. Use alpha-hash/dither, per DR-78, so the outline doesn't ghost. Alternatively, cut the shell to a quarter-sphere 'apse' that is lower at the room-facing sides.

*From observatory-models:* Add a fixed cylinder collider (r 2.85, half-height .075, centre y .075) at (dx,dz), using the solid() pattern with RAPIER ColliderDesc.cylinder, so the platform is a real step (Pip's controller climbs .15 m). Lift the astronomer by setting the NpcSpot y offset to .15 if NpcSpot supports y, or move it to (-3.6,-3.2), off the disc.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *observatory-models:* Re-run mockups/review5/tools/observatory-models/11-recheck.mjs. walk(-5.4,-7.0) must stop outside the shell (player.z > -2.5 or the path is blocked). From the 180° orbit (shot 72), Pip must be visible with at least 70% of its pixels, or the shell must be faded. Re-run g.audit(.02) to confirm zero new overlaps.
- *observatory-models:* Push a beanbag onto the platform (walk through it) and retake 12-dome-o70: the beanbag's bottom sits on the disc at y .15. Retake 60: the coworker's base is fully visible on the disc.

**Rules:** AGENTS 8, DR-12, DR-70, DR-71, DR-78

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced both halves. room.ts:69 has only a 1.2×2×1.2 pier collider, and the shell (room.ts:72) isn't in game.occluders (only pillars/interior walls, decor.ts:47-55, game.ts:387-388). Pip walked in through the open front to (-7.23,-6.23), then out through the cream shell sideways to (-3.29,-6.75), then back in through it to (-5.13,-6.97); every walk arrived. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-022

**R5-022 | P1 | observatory | playability | Knob drag is about 10 px per E6 step, far too twitchy (one flick jumps 100 nF → 68 µF)**

Found by: `observatory-play#9` (P1 playability). Batch: R-observatory (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Dragging a slotted can's knob is the main continuous control (R4A asked for one). The drag maps world-x on the board plane at 4 cm per step. From the bench camera, 4 cm is about 10 px at 1440×900. A natural 180 px mouse flick moved the shunt capacitor 17 steps, from 100 nF to the 68 µF end stop. That kills the tone and makes the next LOG a mistake. There is no detent feedback beyond a quiet tone, the knob tag text is unreadable (see the tag finding), and arrow keys are the only fine control. On a phone this is worse. Breaks DR-14/DR-18 in spirit (forgiving, non-finicky controls) and DR-22.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:290-292` (Math.round((x-t.x0)/.04))
- `tools/observatory-play/04-mouse.mjs` log 'after drag … shunt C 0.000068' after a 180 px drag
- [observatory-play-62-dragging-knob.jpg](shots/observatory-play-62-dragging-knob.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-play/03-knob-f0.mjs` output: 'drag 40 px -> 4.7e-7', 'drag 180 px -> 0.000068'

**Fix.**

Use screen-space pixels instead of board metres. Store clientX at mousedown (add it to Pointer in stations/types.ts) and step every 28 px (`Math.round((e.clientX-x0)/28)`). Alternatively, use 0.12 m per step in station.ts:292. Add a visible detent: scale-pulse the knob and flash the corner line on the scope each step. Clamp to ±1 step per 60 ms to stop flicks skipping the useful range.

**Verify.**

- Mouse test: a 180 px drag from 100 nF moves at most 6–7 steps (to about 1–1.5 µF). Re-run tools/observatory-play/04-mouse.mjs.

**Rules:** DR-14, DR-18, DR-22

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced it with real mouse drags on the shunt knob (found by hover at 748,529, from 100 nF each time). 10 px moved 1 step, 20 px 2, 28 px 3, 40 px 4, 90 px reached 3.3 µF, and 180 px reached the 68 µF end stop. That is about 10 px per E6 step, as claimed (station.ts:292 uses 0.04 m per step).

### R5-023

**R5-023 | P1 | qfn | playability | Moving a resistor or capacitor by its big coloured ends draws a track instead; the grab body is a 0.1 m sliver**

Found by: `qfn-play#8` (P1 playability). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The two-pin parts are drawn as two large coloured end caps, which are the pads (userData.pad, station.ts:173), with a 0.1 m body between them. Pressing a pad starts a stroke (station.ts:331-332). Only the body starts a move (bodyAt, :308-313). At the bench camera the body is about 30 px and the caps are the most visible, colourful thing on the part. In s4 a natural 'grab C1 by its end and drag it toward the chip' drew a 3-cell VDD track toward the chip (qfn-play-50, -51) and raised the toast 'No top-layer copper under the QFN body', which a new player won't connect to what they meant to do. Turning a part by clicking it again is also undiscoverable: the prompt says so only while hovering a selected body.

**Evidence.**

- [qfn-play-50-drag-pad-draws.jpg](shots/qfn-play-50-drag-pad-draws.jpg)
- [qfn-play-51-after-pad-drag.jpg](shots/qfn-play-51-after-pad-drag.jpg)
- [qfn-play-52-hover-body.jpg](shots/qfn-play-52-hover-body.jpg)
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:171-174`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:308-313`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:328-332`
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-qfn-play/v2-bench.mjs` log 'after pad drag C1': place unchanged, short toast
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:173`

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Don't use the 'press on an unrouted pad, drag away from the other pad = move' rule. Dragging outward from a pad is the normal way to start a track, so this would break routing. The proposed sizes also collide: a 0.13 m body reaches ±0.065 and would overlap caps 0.035 wide at ±0.072. Instead, make the caps low and flat so they read as copper pads (≤0.02 m tall). Make the body the tall grip (0.12 wide, caps moved to ±0.09). Add press-and-hold (≥0.3 s without moving) anywhere on a part to move it.

Reviewer's fix: Make the move handle clearly the biggest grip. Raise the body to 0.13×0.09×0.12 with an ink grip ridge, and shrink the caps to 0.035 wide. Add a rule in pointer(): a press on a pad of a part that has no copper attached yet, followed by a drag whose first step leaves the part's footprint in the direction away from its other pad, moves the part instead (scrambled parts are always unrouted at the start). Also show a small rotate-arrow decal on the selected part's body for 'click to turn'.

**Verify.**

- Repeat s4 step 1. Dragging C1 from (10,7) moves it, and design.traces stays empty. A spec asserts a drag that starts on an unrouted pad moves the part.

**Rules:** AGENTS 7, DR-18, DR-19

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Pressing a pad starts a stroke, not a move (station.ts:310, 331-332). My drag starting on C1's end pad began a stroke and raised the short toast, and C1 stayed at (10,7). The size claim is overstated. The body is 0.10 m wide and each cap 0.045 m (station.ts:173), so the body isn't a sliver. But the two colourful caps sit over the pad cells, and the caps plus the flat pads make up most of the part's clickable area.

### R5-024

**R5-024 | P1 | spectrum | playability | Clicking a mirror on the hall map turns the mirror instead of aiming the tower at it**

Found by: `spectrum-play#4` (P1 playability). Batch: R-spectrum (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

With Near IR selected and the mirror standing on mark A, the natural first move is to click on the mirror, meaning 'point the tower here'. But pointer() grabs whatever mirror is within 1.2 m of the cursor (handleNear), so a click on mark A rotates the mirror's board and leaves the tower untouched.
- **Observed:** in my run a click at A changed aim.mirrors.A from −1.05 to −0.42 while aim.tx stayed at the lab-pad heading 2.414. The map showed the tower beam still going straight into the shutter (shot 31).
- **What works:** aiming the tower needs a drag that starts away from every mirror and ends beyond it (shots 32–33).
- **Prompt:** the prompt says only 'Drag · Aim the beam'.
- **Size:** the mirror's 1.2 m grab zone is about 57 px on a 22 m map that is only about 360 px wide on screen. So on the small map, the area around the very target you want to aim at is mostly a 'turn the mirror' zone.

This is the one real puzzle in the room, and its first interaction does the opposite of what the player intends.

**Evidence.**

- [spectrum-play-31-bench-aimed-at-A-by-click.jpg](shots/spectrum-play-31-bench-aimed-at-A-by-click.jpg)
- [spectrum-play-33-bench-tower-on-mirror.jpg](shots/spectrum-play-33-bench-tower-on-mirror.jpg) (works only after a drag from near the tower to past A)
- `src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:212-215` (handleNear: any standing mirror within 1.2 m)
- `src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:357` (drag = handleNear(at) ?? 'tx')
- [verify-spectrum-play-13-bench-click-on-A.jpg](shots/verify-spectrum-play-13-bench-click-on-A.jpg)
- v1.mjs log: click near A {before tx 2.4135, A −1.047; after tx 2.4135, A 0.088; blocked 'metal'}

**Fix.**

In station.ts pointer(): if the press lands near a standing mirror that the tower's beam does **not** reach yet (`!this.reading().route.spots.includes(s)`), treat it as 'aim the tower at that mirror': `this.drag='tx'; this.aimTo('tx',SPOTS[s])` (it snaps to the board centre). Only when the beam already hits the mirror should a press near it start a mirror turn. Draw the turn handle as a knob on the ring rim (the 1.05 m circle at :302) rather than the whole disc, and change the cursor and prompt to 'Drag · Turn the mirror' only over that knob.

**Verify.**

- Add a spec: at the desk with band nir and the mirror on A, simulate a real mouse click at the map position of A (use a map→screen helper). Expect snap().station.reading.spots toEqual(['A']) and aim.mirrors.A unchanged. A second drag from A's rim toward the lab pad then turns the mirror.

**Rules:** AGENTS 7, DR-18, DR-19

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced this with a real mouse. At the desk with Near IR selected and the mirror on A, I hover-scanned the map for the 'grab' cursor and found it at px 760–792 × 500–532. A click near its centre changed aim.mirrors.A from −1.047 to 0.088, while aim.tx stayed at 2.4135 and the route stayed blocked by metal.

### R5-025

**R5-025 | P1 | global, lobby, meeting, playground, lunch, spectrum | playability | Survey (Tab) uses a fixed zoom 44: it crops big rooms on desktop and shows only the middle third (3 of 9 lobby doors) on a phone**

Found by: `camera-render#3` (P1 playability), `lobby-models#16` (P1 playability), `lobby-play#3` (P1 playability), `meeting-play#7` (P1 playability), `playground-play#11` (P1 playability), `lunch-play#10` (P1 clarity), `spectrum-play#15` (P2 playability). Batch: B3 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*camera-render* — **REGRESSION / still open (QA 7): survey uses a fixed zoom 44, which crops the big rooms, wastes 38% of the frame on small ones, and shows only a third of the room on a phone.** The survey distance is a constant 44 regardless of room size or aspect, and it is aimed at (.2,0,1) (src/game.ts:366-368).

At 1440×900, projecting the floor and wall-top corners (surveyfit.mjs) gives:
- Meeting and Lunch (33×20) span NDC x from -1.00 to 0.96. The front-left corner is on the screen edge and under the job card and gauges (camera-render-me-02-survey.jpg, camera-render-lu-02-survey.jpg).
- The 22×16 station rooms use only 62% of the width (camera-render-ga-02-survey.jpg).

At 390×844 portrait the room is 2.1–3.4× wider than the screen and all 6 test corners are off-screen. The meeting survey on a phone shows only the centre desks; the lunch survey shows only the kitchen door (camera-render-meeting-62-survey-phone.jpg, camera-render-lunch-62-survey-phone.jpg).

The survey's job (AGENTS 8, DR-21) is to show the whole room, every wall and the goal. QA 7 was claimed fixed but is still failing at 16:10 and broken on a phone.

*lobby-models* — **Phone survey (Tab) shows 3 of the 9 doors: the hub's whole purpose (choose a door) is cropped on portrait screens.** Survey zoom is a fixed 44 (src/game.ts:366). At 390×844, the lobby survey frames only Big Meeting, Lunch Rush and Overheating Arcade, plus reception (lobby-models-42). Cable Playground, Arcade Rush, Robot Garage and all three side doors are off-screen. The phone start shot shows two and a half doors (lobby-models-41).

At 1440×900 the survey does show all nine (lobby-models-02). This breaks DR-21 (the survey shows the whole room on a phone in portrait), and in the hub the survey is the door picker's overview.

*lobby-play* — **Phone survey (Tab) and phone start show 3 of 9 doors, and the current target is off-screen.** At 390×844 the start frame shows Big Meeting, Lunch Rush and part of Arcade (lobby-play-34). The survey that should show the whole room (DR-21) shows the same three doors and the reception (lobby-play-35). The target door 00, the three side doors and Robot Garage are all off-screen. The survey zoom is a fixed 44 (src/game.ts:366) and doesn't adapt to aspect, and in portrait the follow factor is forced to 1 (follow=cam.aspect<1?1:..., game.ts:366), so the survey keeps centring the room at the 16:10 yaw. A phone player can't find most of the jobs, or the one the card tells them to do, without walking around blind.

*meeting-play* — **Phone survey (Tab) at 390×844 shows only the middle third of the office: closet, boardroom, lounge and coffee corner are cut off.** The survey uses a fixed zoom of 44 with the room centre as its target. On the portrait phone viewport (390×844) the frame covers only the central desk pods (shot 47). The server closet (the reel), the boardroom and strip door (the goal), the coffee corner (the sneaky reel) and the lounge are all outside the frame. Survey is the only way to see the whole job on a phone, so a phone player can't see where the job starts or ends. At 1440×900 the same survey shows the whole room (shot 02), so this is an aspect problem. QA 7 (survey crops the vending side and lounge) was claimed fixed, but only for landscape. This breaks DR-21 (the survey shows the whole room, with every wall and the goal, at 16:10 and on a phone in portrait).

*playground-play* — **Phone 390×844: the survey crops off the lamp and the job card covers the cable strain meter.** At 390×844 the survey (Tab, fixed zoom 44, src/game.ts:366) shows only the left two-thirds of the room (shot 49). The lamp, socket and east wall (x>5) are off-screen, and the prompt pill sits over the front of the room. Survey exists to find the goal, so on a phone it fails (DR-21). While dragging (shot 50), the two-line objective card ('Drag the cable to the lamp's socket and plug it in') overlaps the top-right strain/reel meter: only the reel icon edge and the end of the bar peek out. That meter is the HUD read of cable state (DR-46), and the spool on the reel is off-frame mid-drag (shot 56). The thumbstick, plug and grab buttons also cover the bottom third, where the cable trails.

*lunch-play* — **On a phone the Lunch chain HUD covers the job card, and the survey shows only the kitchen middle.** At 390×844:
- The Lunch-only chain strip (oven → belt → lift + fridge bar) is drawn across the top of the job card, hiding its progress dots (lunch-play-06).
- The breaker-gauge panel sits on top of the prompt pill's row and next to the camera button.
- The survey (Tab, fixed zoom 44, src/game.ts:366) frames only the kitchen and the doorway (lunch-play-07). The power room with both carts, the storeroom, the lift room, the lunch crowd and Pip himself are all off screen.

The survey is a phone player's main tool for planning a seven-step route, and it fails here. DR-21 requires every wall and the goal visible in portrait. The desktop survey (lunch-play-02) is fine.

*spectrum-play* — **Phone start and survey: the station panel sits over the middle of the room, and the survey crops the quiet room and the left wall.** At 390×844 the 'DELIVERY 1/3 · TO THE STOREROOM / Through the brick wall' station panel sits in the middle of the screen (y≈430–500), just over the floor in front of Pip and the dock (shot 90). In the survey (fixed zoom 44) the room is cropped: the quiet room and the right wall run off the right edge, the left wall is cut, and the panel covers the desk area (shot 91). So 'Tab shows the whole room' fails on a phone.

**Fix.**

*From camera-render:* Replace `this.survey?44` with a fitted distance computed once per resize and per yaw change:

1. Target the room centre (0, 0, 0).
2. For the 8 corners of the room box (±W/2, 0 and 3, ±D/2), binary-search the distance (20 to 120) until every projected corner lies within |x|<0.88 and -0.62&lt;y<0.70. That leaves room for the top HUD card and the bottom key bar.
3. On portrait (aspect<1), also turn the survey yaw so the room's long axis runs vertically (yaw += π/2 when W>D), raise the pitch to about 1.0, and restore the old yaw on exit.

Cache the result per level so it doesn't run every frame.

*From lobby-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The formula has width and depth swapped. The room width must fit the horizontal FOV: dist = max((depth/2)/tan(vfov/2), (width/2)/(tan(vfov/2)*aspect)) * 1.1, then divide out lensScale(fov) (game.ts:376), since that scale is applied afterwards. For the 30 m lobby at aspect .46 this comes out at about 90, not 75-80, depending on fov. Clamp it to the camera far plane.

Reviewer's fix: In src/game.ts:366, make the survey distance fit the room: zoom = max(44, (max(level.width, level.depth/ cam.aspect)*0.5)/tan(fov/2)/cos(pitch)*1.1). For the 30 m lobby at aspect 0.46 that's roughly 75-80. Also set the survey pitch to about 1.0 in portrait, so the board reads top-down.

*From lobby-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep the fix, but drop the follow-factor rationale. The survey ignores `follow` (src/game.ts:368). In portrait, the fix should only change the survey and hub-start yaw/distance (and/or FOV).

Reviewer's fix: In src/game.ts updateCamera, when survey && cam.aspect<1: turn the survey yaw by π/2 so the room's 30 m axis runs up the screen. Compute the distance that fits the room's bounds, distance = max(level.width,level.depth)*0.5/tan(min(vfov,hfov)/2)*1.1, clamped to ≤ 80, or raise the survey FOV to 45° in portrait. Do the same for the hub start pose. Pair this with the edge arrow from the marker finding.

*From meeting-play:* In updateCamera, compute the survey distance from the room bounds and the camera aspect. From horizontal FOV hfov = 2*atan(tan(fov/2)*aspect), dist = max((level.width/2+1)/tan(hfov/2), (level.depth/2+1)/tan(fov/2)) / cos(pitch) * 1.05. In portrait (aspect<1), also rotate the survey yaw by π/2, so the 33 m long axis runs up the screen; that roughly halves the distance needed. Restore the yaw when leaving the survey.

*From playground-play:* (1) In updateCamera (src/game.ts:366), compute the survey distance from the room's bounding box and the aspect: distance = max(44, (max(width,depth)*0.6)/tan(fov/2)/min(1,aspect)), or pull back to about 60 when aspect<1, and centre on the room's middle. (2) In ui.css, under the portrait media query, move .strain below the card (top: card bottom + 8 px) or into the card's row, and cap the card to one line (ellipsis) when aspect<0.6. (3) Hide the prompt pill during survey.

*From lunch-play:* (1) CSS for body[data-touch] .lunch-chain (or @media (max-aspect-ratio:1/1)): place it under the card (top: card bottom + 8 px), or shrink it to a single row inside the timer pill.
(2) In updateCamera, pick the survey zoom by aspect: zoom = 44 * clamp((level.width/level.depth)/(cam.aspect*1.6), 1, 2.4). Or, for portrait, turn yaw 90° so the 33 m axis runs vertically.
(3) Move the phone breaker panel to the right edge above the action buttons.

*From spectrum-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The suggested survey formula is technically wrong. The horizontal FOV is 2·atan(tan(vfov/2)·aspect), not fov·aspect. A fit distance is d = (room half-width·1.1)/tan(hfov/2), with the camera pitch taken into account, then max(44, d).

Reviewer's fix: - On portrait, pin the station panel under the objective card at the top (as at the bench, ui.css:253), or collapse it to a one-line chip while walking.
- Make the survey zoom fit the room to the aspect: zoom = max(44, (level.width/2)/tan(fov·aspect/2)·1.1).

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *camera-render:* 1. Re-run surveyfit.mjs. Expect cornersOff 0 and widthFrac between 0.75 and 0.92 for every room at 1440×900 and 390×844. 2. Retake camera-render-meeting-62-survey-phone and camera-render-me-02-survey: all four walls and the boardroom door are visible.
- *lobby-models:* Rerun c.mjs's phone block and retake lobby-models-42. All 9 door frames are visible.
- *lobby-play:* Rerun mockups/review5/tools/lobby-play/e-phone.mjs. lobby-play-35 should show all four walls and all 9 doors, and lobby-play-34 should show the target door or an arrow to it.
- *meeting-play:* Rerun s4.mjs phone section. Shot 47 must show the closet reel, the boardroom door and the lounge, with all four room edges visible. Add a portrait check: project the four floor corners in survey mode and expect all inside NDC ±1.
- *playground-play:* Retake shots 49 and 50 at 390×844. All four walls and the lamp are inside the frame, and the strain bar is fully visible and not overlapped by the card.
- *lunch-play:* Retake lunch-play-06 and -07 at 390×844. The card dots must be visible. The survey must show cart A/B, the storeroom, the lift and Pip. Run this for every cable floor.
- *spectrum-play:* Take shots 90 and 91 again: the panel doesn't overlap the room's centre, and the survey shows all four walls and the quiet room.

**Rules:** AGENTS 8, DR-21, DR-41, DR-44, DR-46

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced the corner projection after settling the survey camera with 400 updateCamera calls. Meeting at 1440×900: NDC x runs from -1.00 to 0.96, so the front-left floor corner sits exactly on the screen edge (verify-camera-render-03-survey-meeting-1440.jpg). The whole room is still visible there, so the 16:10 case is a tight crop rather than a broken one. (7/7 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-026

**R5-026 | P1 | global, qfn, arcade, arcade-rush, garage, lobby, lunch, meeting, observatory, playground, spectrum | playability | Draw calls are 3–6× the ~250 budget in every room (663 in a 15-prop lobby, 1100–1500 in station rooms, up to 2344 at quality 2) — regression from R3B/LR15**

Found by: `camera-render#2` (P1 playability), `qfn-play#10` (P1 playability), `arcade-models#2` (P2 playability), `arcade-play#16` (P2 playability), `arcade-rush-play#19` (P2 playability), `garage-models#20` (P2 playability), `garage-play#19` (P2 playability), `lobby-models#17` (P2 playability), `lobby-play#19` (P2 playability), `lunch-models#7` (P2 playability), `meeting-play#19` (P2 playability), `observatory-models#19` (P2 playability), `observatory-play#18` (P2 playability), `playground-models#23` (P2 playability), `playground-play#19` (P2 playability), `playground-teach#14` (P2 playability), `progression#15` (P2 playability), `qfn-models#16` (P2 playability), `spectrum-models#16` (P2 playability), `spectrum-play#19` (P2 playability). Batch: B8 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*camera-render* — **REGRESSION (LR15): draw calls are 663–1422 per frame at quality 0 and 1203–2344 at quality 2, against the <500 target and the 176 that PROGRESS records.** Measured with renderer.info at the start camera (draws.mjs, fps.mjs).

At quality 0 (what every player gets today, see the quality finding), frame draw calls per room:

| Room | Frame draw calls |
|---|---|
| lobby | 658 |
| playground | 728 |
| meeting | 1156 |
| lunch | 1239 |
| arcade | 1416 |
| arcade-rush | 1410 |
| garage | 1156 |
| qfn | 1172 |
| observatory | 1078 |
| spectrum | 1078 |

At quality 2: playground 1203, meeting 1931, lunch 2055, arcade 2344, garage 1906, observatory 1805. The survey adds up to 265 more (meeting 1421).

PROGRESS.md:408-413 lists Big Meeting at 176 and Lunch at about 175. NEXT_STEPS §1 asks for under about 500; DR-24 asks for 250 or fewer.

Where the calls come from (drawsplit.mjs):
- The OutlineEffect pass re-draws every outlined mesh: a plain scene pass is 793 calls in the meeting, and outlines add +363.
- Shell-wall subtrees stay unmerged on root so they can scale: 161 visible meshes in the meeting, including windows, wall art and caps.
- Pip is 43 separate meshes.
- Station-room dressing sits on game.root rather than decorRoot: 339 meshes under root groups in the arcade.
- At quality 2, GTAO re-renders the scene for depth and normals: about +750.

On the host RX 9060 XT this still runs at 60 fps, but the render 'draw' phase costs 5–8.5 ms per frame at quality 2. On a mid laptop (4× CPU) that is about 30 ms, so adaptQuality will drop players to the flat look. That is AGENTS 3 (dense rooms) fighting AGENTS 9.

*qfn-play* — **About 1197 draw calls at the start camera (review 3 measured 850), far over the 250 budget.** snap().drawCalls = 1197 at the start shot and 1193 in the survey (s1 log). Review 3 (REVIEW_B perf table) recorded 850 for qfn, so the clutter pass (max:220, src/levels/qfn.ts:24) made it worse. The game reaches 60 fps on the host GPU in manual mode, but integrated and phone GPUs will drop frames, and src/game.ts adaptQuality will cut the effects the toon look depends on. Every clutter prop is its own set of toon and outline meshes. The board, pucks and labels add dozens more.

*arcade-models* — **REGRESSION: draw calls rose to ~1500 at the start view (A13 was 1181); station machinery and 12 cabinets are not merged.** `snap().drawCalls` is 1497 at the start view and 1488 in the survey (s1.mjs), and 1022 at a zoomed view (s9.mjs). DR-24 allows about 250, and review 3 B N9 / A13 recorded 1181, so this is a regression. A scene traverse (s8.mjs) shows where it comes from. The bench's `top` group holds 221 separate meshes: 16 bin blocks of 7 meshes each, plus bin walls, pads, links, LED, motor and meter. Each of the 12 cabinets has 12–24 meshes and is built straight into game.root (room.ts:83, 94, 95; station.ts:215), not into decorRoot, so freeze() (kit.ts:77) never merges them. The tray's riding blocks are another 48 meshes, and there are 144 loose single meshes. OutlineEffect draws every visible mesh twice. The host GPU holds 60 fps, but on integrated GPUs and phones (NEXT_STEPS asks for a phone bench check) this is the main frame cost. The prop clones are already instanced (125 InstancedMesh), so the cost is almost all station art.

*arcade-play* — **Draw calls 1422 at start and 1497 in survey (R3B measured 1181): a regression against the ≤ 250 budget.** Real-time run at 1440×900 on the host GPU (s11): 60 fps, but `drawCalls` 1422 at start and 1497 in survey. R3B N9 / A13 recorded 1181 and asked for a cut. Clutter (max 220) and 132 props have pushed it up about 20 %.

Lunch went from 1090 to about 175 after `batchProps`. The arcade's dynamic props, bench parts and cabinet sub-meshes aren't merged. On integrated GPUs and phones this will drop frames, which matters doubly since the phone bench already fails.

*arcade-rush-play* — **Draw calls are about 5.6× over budget in Arcade Rush.** `snap().drawCalls` is 1416 at the game camera on start, 1491 in the survey and 1178 at the bench view. The budget is about 250 (DR-24). This is A13 (1181 in R3B), still open and slightly worse. Rush is a speed mode played on the same dense arcade (132 props plus cabinets), so frame hitches during fast key input hurt directly. The fps reading in ?manual mode isn't reliable (31 at start, 60 in survey), so this needs a real-time check, but the draw-call count alone fails the rule.

*garage-models* — **Garage draw calls ~1156 at start and in survey (target ≤ ~250).** snap().drawCalls returned 1156 at the start view and 1156 in the survey, at 60 fps on the host GPU. The count includes every composer and outline pass. DR-24 sets ≤ about 250 at the game camera; Lunch was brought from 1090 to about 175 by merging. The garage dresses most fixtures as many small parts on decorRoot, but the station root (bench board, traces, sockets, labels: each sign() is its own MeshBasic material via cachedLabel) and the three robotMesh copies (about 40 meshes each, with per-call toon() materials) are not frozen. Performance holds on this GPU, but a weaker GPU or a laptop will not.

*garage-play* — **Draw calls 1156 at the game camera (and in survey).** snapshot() at the start reported drawCalls 1156 for 111 props (fps 60 on the host GPU). The DR-24 target is ≤ about 250. R3B measured 953, so dense clutter (max 220) has pushed it up. That's fine on this GPU, but a phone or iGPU will drop quality via adaptQuality. The bench labels (one canvas texture per sign), the pegboard tools, per-dash lane boxes (room.ts:70-71; about 30 separate meshes) and per-wheel parts on the decor robots are all separate meshes in decorRoot.

*lobby-models* — **About 590 draw calls for a 15-prop hub (693 in survey): doors, signs and portals are on game.root and never merged.** snap().drawCalls is 592 at the lobby start and 693 in the survey. The Playground has 109 props and 782 (all measured with fullfx at 1440×900).

The causes:
- Doors are built on the shell walls' upper groups (game.root), so freeze(decorRoot) (src/game.ts:105) never merges them.
- Each door has about 15 meshes, plus 3-5 signPlate meshes, each with its own MeshBasicMaterial (src/render/labels.ts:16).
- There are 9 board plates and 9 portal ShaderMaterials.
- Blade signs and lamps are also unmerged.

The fps is 60 on the host GPU, but DR-24 caps draw calls at about 250. A hub with this little in it should be the cheapest scene, and it leaves no headroom for the density fix above.

*lobby-play* — **Lobby draws 663 calls at start and 693 in survey for a 15-prop room.** snap().drawCalls is 663 at the start view and 693 in the survey (script a-views.mjs log), against DR-24's budget of about 250, in the emptiest room in the game. fps holds 60 on the host GPU, but this is the first room on every phone and the budget will be blown as soon as the empty-hall fix adds clutter. Likely sources: 9 doors each with a frame, header, leaf, panel, knob, portal shader plane, spill, threshold, lamp and cap, plus a unique CanvasTexture signPlate for every name, number, medal and board row (about 40 plates), each drawn twice through the outline pass.

*lunch-models* — **REGRESSION (LR15/DR-24): Lunch renders 1257 draw calls at start (1309 in lowfx), not the ~175 PROGRESS claims; 156 shell-wall meshes are never merged.** snapshot().drawCalls reads 1257 at start and 1303 in survey with fullfx, and 1309 with fullfx off. PROGRESS.md's performance table lists Lunch at '~175'. game.ts:450 now counts every pass of the frame (scene and outlines), so part of the jump is the counter. But a scene traverse still finds about 534 visible meshes per pass: 42 merged decor buckets, 123 instanced prop parts, 156 meshes under the shell walls, 207 other meshes (interior walls 35, port rings, plugs, pulses, puddles, bots, lamps, blobs, Pip) and 6 sprites. The shell walls (windows: sky, 5 frame bars, sill and 6 blinds × 10; posters; wallpaper) are built on game.root via shellWall(), so freeze(decorRoot) never merges them. Separately, the portable-lamp cord TubeGeometry is disposed and rebuilt every frame, because the condition distance(lamp,post) > .3 is always true. Host fps is still 60, but DR-24's ≤ about 250 budget is blown about 5×, and this room was the one perf was fixed for.

*meeting-play* — **Draw calls: 1237 at the start view and 1422 in the survey, five times the 250 budget.** snapshot().drawCalls measured 1237 at the start view and 1422 in the survey at 1440×900 with fullfx (s1 log). R3B measured 1064 for the meeting; it has grown since. Big Meeting is the densest cable floor (310 props, 24 coworkers, a live rope mesh, pulses and particles). At ~5× DR-24's ≤250 budget it is the most likely room to drop frames on a laptop iGPU. adaptQuality would then step bloom and AO down mid-run, changing the look during the drag. The host-GPU fps reads 60, but in ?manual mode fps isn't representative.

*observatory-models* — **Draw calls 1084 at the game camera (4× budget, up from 836 in R3B); 5 point lights (+1 on win).** snap() at start: drawCalls 1084, survey 1094, fps 60 on the host GPU. DR-24 sets about 250 at the game camera. Review 3 B measured 836 for this room, so this is a regression (dense clutter plus 319 non-instanced meshes, for example the per-LED spheres on game.root, the 7 rail cylinders, panel planes and bench parts, all drawn again by the outline pass). The scene traverse found 5 PointLights, at (-6.1,2.2,-4.7), (2.32,2.6,-6.2), (6.8,2.6,-6.2), (0,2.7,-1.6) and (-4,2.4,3), and lightUp adds a 6th. DR-66 allows 4. Materials are clean: only MeshToonMaterial (366) and MeshBasicMaterial (119), with no Standard or Phong.

*observatory-play* — **Draw calls about 1,100 at the game camera; survey drops to ~34 fps.** snapshot().drawCalls is 1,094 at start, 1,088 in the survey and 839–890 at the bench. That is 4× the DR-24 budget of ≤250, and worse than R3B's 836 for this room, a regression since clutter was added. fps holds at 60 at the game camera on the host GPU, but the Tab survey reported 34 fps. Weaker laptops and phones will stutter in exactly the view used to find the goal. Breaks DR-24.

*playground-models* — **778 draw calls at the start view and 782 in the survey, three times the 250 budget.** snapshot().drawCalls reports 778 at the default start camera and 782 in the survey (fps 60 on this host GPU). The scene has only 340 meshes (all MeshToon or MeshBasic), so the count is roughly tripled by the shadow pass plus the OutlineEffect re-render, and the 79 InstancedMesh batches are each drawn three times. DR-24 sets about 250 so dense rooms hold up on weaker GPUs. The playground is the lightest room and already exceeds it.

*playground-play* — **Draw calls of 700–970 at the game camera are 3–4× the 250 budget.** snapshot().drawCalls reads 695–886 during play and 970 on the win frame (b-clean, c-chaos logs) for a 109-prop room, against the DR-24 budget of about 250. FPS held at 60 on the host GPU, so this isn't blocking here. But the playground is the lightest room, and the count (which includes the composer and outline passes, game.ts:455) suggests per-part instancing by geometry+material produces many small batches.

*playground-teach* — **Draw calls are about 3× the DR-24 budget at the game camera (782 at start, 948 at win).** snapshot().drawCalls logged 782 at start, 758–800 during the drag, and 948 after the win (clean.mjs log). DR-24 asks for at most about 250 draw calls. It still runs at 60 fps on the host GPU, but a 20×20 m tutorial with at most 90 clutter props shouldn't need 3× the budget the Lunch merge reached (about 175). Low-end machines (the first-run audience of a tutorial) will drop frames during the drag, which is exactly where cable feel matters. Outside my dimension, but measured.

*progression* — **Draw calls in the hub and at the arcade bench are well over budget (663 in a 15-prop lobby, about 1200 at the arcade bench).** `snap().drawCalls` at the lobby start was 663 (lobby.mjs) for a room with 15 props, 9 doors and a board. Every door has a portal mesh, several signPlates, a leaf, a lamp and a glow, and the board has one signPlate per job (src/hub/lobby.ts:61-63, :77-98). At the arcade bench, snapshots during the run show 1160–1207 draw calls (arcade-full.mjs act-fail dumps), matching the open A13 item. FPS held at 60 on this host GPU, but the hub is the screen every session passes through, and weaker machines will feel it first.

*qfn-models* — **1201 draw calls at start (1193 in survey, 935 at the bench) against a budget of about 250: every model part is a separate mesh.** snap().drawCalls is 1201 at start, 1193 in the survey and 935 in the bench view, with 624 meshes (516 MeshToon, 108 MeshBasic) in the scene (s1.mjs, s4.mjs output; mockups/review5/tools/qfn-models/scene.json). FPS held 60 on the host GPU, but DR-24 sets about 250 draw calls at the game camera, and Lunch was cut from 1090 to about 175 by merging.

The cause is model construction:
- Every rbox and box in room.ts dressing is its own mesh: 12 crane bars, 7 + 4 reels of 4 meshes each, 4 oven windows, the shelf, the desks.
- Every miniBoard is 4 meshes, and there are about 15 of them.
- Each clutter prop is a template clone of 6–30 part meshes.
- The bench rebuilds per-board parts and per-segment copper and ratsnest dashes.

The outline pass doubles the cost. On weaker GPUs this will push the quality auto-drop (game.ts quality timer).

*spectrum-models* — **Draw calls 1133 at the start view (rule ≤ ~250) and 5 point lights (rule ≤ 4).** snap() at start reports drawCalls 1133 at 60 fps on the host GPU (s7-audit-norim.mjs log). That is about 4.5× the DR-24 budget, so lower-end GPUs and phones will drop frames. The room has 531 meshes in the scene dump. Most of the hand-built dressing (brick slabs, shelf boards, book rows, mesh posts every 1.6 m, rainbow stripes ×5, rail bands ×10, bench keys, ladder rungs) is separate meshes rather than merged or instanced. DR-66: the room adds 5 PointLights (room.ts:144-146) where the rule allows ≤ 4.

*spectrum-play* — **About 1125 draw calls at the start (1139 in the survey) for an 82-prop room.** snap() at the start reported drawCalls 1125 (survey 1139) with 82 props. That is 4–5× the ~250 budget; fps held 60 on the host GPU, but weaker machines will drop to the adaptive-quality path. The live canvas screens, per-label planes (every key plate, pad tag and mark is its own mesh) and per-segment beam meshes add up.

**Fix.**

*From camera-render:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep steps 1-3. For step 2, only static dressing may move into decorRoot: anything animated or toggled (the arcade cabinet screen and lamp, garage robot parts, station screens) must stay on root, because freeze() merges and removes source meshes (src/render/kit.ts:77-83). Measure the PROGRESS perf table again with the all-passes counter and state that method.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Merge each shell wall's static parts (wallpaper, cap, rail, window units, wall art) into one mesh per material per wall inside the `upper` and `inside` groups (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries). They scale as a group, so merging keeps the cutaway working. That saves about 140 meshes in the meeting.
2. Have station `dress()` build into game.decorRoot (src/levels/decor.ts:74 passes `back` and `side`; add a `root:game.decorRoot` and use it in src/stations/*/room.ts) so freeze() batches the counters, posters and racks.
3. Merge Pip's rigid sub-parts per bone (the 43 meshes down to about 10).
4. Mark big flat walls, floors and decals `outlineParameters.visible=false`; they already skip outline visually, but check they are skipped in the outline pass.
5. Re-measure, then update the PROGRESS perf table with the method: the frame total at quality 2, including outline and AO.

*From qfn-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Before instancing, check that the outline pass supports InstancedMesh. Otherwise instanced clutter loses its ink outlines, which are a hard toon rule. A quick first step is turning off outlines on tiny clutter (paper, mugs) and capping max at 150.

Reviewer's fix: Instance repeated clutter kinds (box, cabinet, chair, bin, cone) with InstancedMesh per kind and colour. Bodies stay in Rapier, and the instance matrices update only for awake bodies. Merge static decor per material in room.ts: shelf bins, the minis, the reel bank and posters are already in decorRoot and freeze() could merge them by material. Cap QFN clutter at max:150 until instancing lands.

*From arcade-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Steps (1) to (3) are sound. When cabinets move to decorRoot, keep the five broken cabinets' face and screen meshes outside the frozen group, because light(k) swaps their materials (room.ts:122-123). The six working cabinets can be frozen completely. Drop step (4): trayRide is already visible=false after delivery (station.ts:360), so it costs no draw calls.

Reviewer's fix: (1) In room.ts, build every cabinet into game.decorRoot, which is frozen and merged at game.ts:105. Keep only the marquee `face` and the `screen` as separate meshes, since light(k) swaps their material. Parent those two to game.root at the cabinet's world transform. (2) In station.ts buildBins(), merge each bin's 4 decorative blocks into one geometry per material: mergeGeometries over blockMesh children, keeping the labels as one merged plane per bin. They never change. (3) Build the bench's static parts (board base, supply posts, pads, rails, meter housing, power box base, sign-off base) into one group and call freeze() on it once after build(). Keep the live parts (LED dome, fuse disc, lever, lamps, posContent, acrossContent, heldMesh) separate. (4) Dispose trayRide after delivery instead of only hiding it. Target ≤300 draw calls at the game camera.

*From arcade-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Drop the Lunch comparison and the 'regression' framing. Report it as a DR-24 budget overrun measured as renderer.info.render.calls with fullfx (arcade 1497, lunch 1341). The suggested merges are fine. Note batchProps already exists (game.ts:139-149); check whether the arcade actually calls it before adding a new path.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Merge each static cabinet (room.ts `cabinet()`, called 11×) into one BufferGeometry per material with `mergeGeometries` after building.
2. Merge the bench shell and board static parts (station.ts:137-181) into the decor batch.
3. Instance the bin blocks (4 per bin × 4 bins → `InstancedMesh` per value).
4. Run clutter through the same `batchProps` path Lunch uses.

Target ≤ 300 calls.

*From arcade-rush-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Verify with THROTTLE=4 node tools/perf.mjs on a mid laptop, as NEXT_STEPS.md asks, in addition to the drawCalls check.

Reviewer's fix: Merge the static arcade decor the way Lunch was merged (from 1090 down to about 175): run the cabinets from `cabinet()`, the shelf, the counter, the bench body and the clutter through the static merge into `decorRoot`. Keep only clickables and animated parts (LED, fuse, lever, kid, coin) as separate meshes. Instance the clutter boxes, cones and beanbags by kind.

*From garage-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Treat this as cross-room. First establish what DR-24's 250 counts: this counter includes outline and shadow passes, so roughly 2–3× the scene meshes. Garage-only merging will not reach ≤300 on this counter. The proposed merges (bench statics, decor robots on decorRoot, shared label materials) are still valid savings.

Reviewer's fix: 1) Run kit freeze() on the static parts of the bench (desk, board base, traces, socket pads, label posts) by moving them under a static group. Keep clickables, the fuse, lamps, dots and the arc live.
2) Build the two decor robots into decorRoot so the level's freeze merges them, or instance them.
3) Share one MeshBasicMaterial per label texture across signs (the cached texture already exists; cache the material too).

*From garage-play:* - Merge static decorRoot meshes per material (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries) after dressGarage.
- Instance the lane dashes (one InstancedMesh).
- Atlas the bench sign labels into one texture.
- Merge decor robot copies.

*From lobby-models:* 1. In Lobby.door() (src/hub/lobby.ts:76-98), split the static parts from the moving ones. Static parts are the frame posts, lintel, threshold, title sign and medal; moving ones are the leaf, portal, spill and lamp. Merge the static parts per wall with mergeGeometries into one mesh per material, parented to the wall's upper group so they still fold.
2. Build the lintel sign textures into one canvas atlas per wall, so there's one MeshBasicMaterial per wall.
3. Draw the 9 board plates into a single canvas texture on one plane.

*From lobby-play:* Merge the static door parts per material per wall (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries after dress(); the leaf stays separate), put all sign text into one atlas CanvasTexture with UV offsets, instance the 9 lamps, cap sockets and knobs, and draw the board rows into one canvas. Target ≤ 250 at the start view.

*From lunch-models:* (1) In shellWall(), split each wall into a static part (lower wainscot, rail, base) parented to decorRoot, and the folding upper group. In the upper group, merge the window units, wallpaper, cap and wall art into one mesh per material after build. Call freeze(upper) right after decorate(), since the group only changes its transform.

### R5-027

**R5-027 | P1 | arcade, arcade-rush | teaching | Arcade: powering a cabinet on as found to look at it counts as a mistake and a fuse trip, and the prompt "P Power on" invites it**

Found by: `arcade-teach#0` (P1 teaching), `arcade-play#4` (P2 playability), `arcade-rush-play#3` (P1 clarity), `arcade-rush-teach#5` (P1 playability). Batch: R-arcade (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*arcade-teach* — **Looking at a broken cabinet counts as damage: powering each cabinet as found to diagnose it scores 6 mistakes (C) and loses the trip bonus.** All five cabinets start broken (logic.ts:62-83; the test 'every starting state is broken', logic.test.ts:204-206). The natural way to learn at a repair bench is to switch it on and see what is wrong. Every one of those looks is graded as a mistake. Pinball (across block) trips the fuse and counts a mistake plus a trip (station.ts:288 fault(true)). Rhythm (LED reversed) is dark, so after 0.6 s judge() gives tier 0 and fault(false) counts one (station.ts:390). Claw (220 Ω on 12 V) counts one for the LED over-rating, then another when the block pops (station.ts:300). Handheld (220 Ω on 9 V) counts one for 31.7 mA. Hopper (empty chain) trips again, which is the second trip and loses the 'Fuse tripped no more than once' bonus. My solve.mjs run, which powers every cabinet once as found and then fixes it cleanly, ended with mistakes 6, trips 2 and damage 6 against limits.damage 2 (station.ts:81). That is a C on damage, and the HUD in arcade-teach-22-result.jpg shows 6. The overall grade hides this only because time and cost are A, so the damage axis does not measure understanding. It punishes the observe-then-fix loop the room is built around. The same applies to experiments a learner should be encouraged to make, such as 'what does 100 Ω do?'. Juul's 'fair failure' and DR-02 both say only a mistake in the concept should cost anything, and seeing a fault that was already there is not a mistake. Review4 raised this as A7, and it is still open.

*arcade-play* — **The prompts invite mistakes: "P Power on" on cabinets that start broken, so looking first costs 3–5 mistakes against a 2-damage limit (A7 still open).** Every cabinet's start state is a fault:
- pinball: block across the LED → trip;
- rhythm: LED reversed → dark;
- claw: 220 Ω on 12 V → over-rating, then the block pops (+1 credit);
- handheld: 220 Ω on 9 V → 31 mA, over-rating;
- hopper: empty → trip.

Any failing live setup counts a mistake after 0.15 s (trip) or 0.6 s (station.ts:285, :376, :390).

After each sign-off the prompt actively suggests powering the broken start (station.ts:485): "P Power on" whenever the chain holds a block. Rhythm, claw and handheld all start with a block, so the prompt leads into 3 mistakes and one popped block.
- In s2, following the prompts, I reached `mistakes:4, trips:2` by the hopper. The bonus "Fuse tripped no more than once" was already lost, and damage was at 2× the limit of 2 (limits station.ts:81).
- tests/station-arcade.spec.ts:25-26 enshrines `mistakes:1` for pressing POWER just to look.

Juul and DR-02/DR-38 say failure should come from a decision, not from obeying the UI. The stories already describe each fault in words, so the test-to-see habit gets taught and then punished.

*arcade-rush-play* — **The prompt tells the player to do the graded mistake: 'P Power on' on a broken start costs a mistake and a trip.** Several rush faults start with blocks already in the chain: 'hot' (47 Ω), 'dim' (470×3), 'backwards', and 'across'. For these, `prompt()` returns {key:'P',text:'Power on'}, because any position holds a block. A new player does what the one-line prompt says. On the first cabinet (white LED on 9 V with 47 Ω), pressing P trips the fuse within 0.15 s and immediately counts mistakes 1 and trips 1. The "fuse tripped no more than once" bonus is half spent before the player has made a single decision. The 'dim' start (470×3) fails silently after 0.6 s and also counts a mistake.

Powering up to see what is wrong is the diagnostic step the cabinet story invites ("Too bright, and the block smells warm"), but it is graded as damage. This is A7 from R4, still open, and the prompt now actively steers players into it. It breaks DR-19 (a prompt must be a real, good action) and DR-02 (only a mistake in the taught concept may be penalised; looking isn't a mistake).

*arcade-rush-teach* — **Looking at a fault costs damage: powering on 'as found' counts a mistake and a fuse trip on half of all rush cabinets.** Over 2000 generated jobs, 50 % of starts trip the fuse on power-on (empty socket, across-block, 47 Ω on 9 or 12 V), and 3 % pop the LED. The natural diagnostic move, 'switch it on and see what's wrong', counts a mistake and a trip through `fault(true)`. The rush damage limit is 3, and the bonus 'Fuse tripped no more than once' is gone after the first look. In my run, the first press of POWER on cabinet 1 gave mistakes 1 and trips 1. This is review 4's A7 (experiments graded as damage) and it is worse in rush, because the generator makes tripping starts common. It punishes the inquiry the game should teach (observe the symptom, then reason), and it pushes players to never power on until they have guessed.

### R5-028

**R5-028 | P1 | arcade, arcade-rush | teaching | Arcade: trial and error is free and instant — the meter shows live current, swaps under 0.6 s are never counted, so ★ is found by sweeping blocks**

Found by: `arcade-play#5` (P1 teaching), `arcade-teach#1` (P1 teaching), `arcade-rush-teach#4` (P1 teaching). Batch: R-arcade (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*arcade-play* — **Brute force is free: the meter shows the live current at once, swaps under 0.6 s are never counted, and blocks are billed only at sign-off.** With power on I swapped 47 → 100 → 220 → 470 in position A, about 0.3 s each (s5).
- The meter and panel showed 62.5, 29.7, 13.6 and 6.4 mA, the first two over the LED's rating.
- `mistakes` stayed 1 and `trips` stayed 1. Only the parallel pair that tripped the fuse counted.

Why it's free:
- An over-rating or dim setup is only explained and counted after `runT>.6` (station.ts:390).
- Credits are billed from the final setup at sign-off (`served.push({cost:v.cost})`, station.ts:273), plus popped parts.
- So cycling the bins while watching the LIGHT bar, with its ★ zone painted on (drawMeter, station.ts:561), finds the elegant answer without the formula, at no cost in credits or grade.

R4B's "step until the bar turns green" is still the dominant strategy. DR-38 (tiers reward understanding; brute force costs credits) fails.

*arcade-teach* — **Trial and error is free and instant: swapping blocks while live never costs anything, so ★ can be found by sweeping.** The bench stays live while the player changes blocks (station.ts:6 'every change shows on the meter at once'). changed() resets runT, explained and faultCounted (station.ts:247), and a tier-0 setup only counts a mistake after it has run 0.6 s (station.ts:390). A pick or slot never adds to `spent`, which is charged only at sign-off (station.ts:273) or when something pops. In fail.mjs I powered 470 Ω, swapped to 100 Ω (29.7 mA, over the LED rating) for 0.3 s, then to 220 Ω. The mistake count did not change. The cheapest strategy is therefore the PhET-slider loop: try 470 (dim, the bar sits left of the band), try 100 (the bar passes the red line), try 220 (★). Nothing asks the player to use I = (V − Vf) ÷ R. The meter shows CHAIN Ω before power but not the voltage left across the chain, so the formula's key term V − Vf never appears as a live number. logic analysis (analyse.mjs) shows how forgiving the search space is. Pinball: the single 220 block is elegant (341 elegant chains of 3375). Claw: 117 elegant. Handheld: 66. Hopper: 186. Only the Rhythm pad (3 elegant, all 47‖47) needs real reasoning. DR-38 asks that brute-force cycling cost credits, and that the elegant tier needs the right margin rather than a lucky value.

*arcade-rush-teach* — **Trial and error is free and fast: the live meter plus free block swaps make guessing beat computing.** Rush should be where the player applies R = (V − Vf)/I under time pressure, but nothing rewards predicting. Swapping blocks while powered costs nothing: `spent` only adds the signed-off setup's blocks. The meter updates current at once. A tier-0 setup only counts as a mistake after running 0.6 s, so quick swaps are free. Over 300 rush jobs, a random one- or two-block chain is reliable 25 % of the time and elegant 11 %. Eleven chains cover every answer, and five of them (470, 470+470, 220, 220+470, 220‖470) cover 71 %. In my scripted brute-force run (job 9: 47, 100, 220, 470, 220+47, 100+100 with power on) six guesses cost one mistake, and the elegant 220 was found by sweeping. Red and green LEDs (Vf 2.0 and 2.1 V) give the same answer in 7 of 12 supply and band combinations. Supplies are always 3.3, 5, 9 or 12 V, so after a few minutes the player memorises '9 V → 470' instead of the relation.

Reviewer's fix: Pick one, in src/stations/arcade/station.ts:

(a) Predict-then-test:
- While powered, blocks can't be placed. `slot` with `this.powered` returns false, with the toast-free `hm` voice and the lever wobbling.

(b) Bill each block taken from a bin:

Note that the empty-chain trip already penalises the naive swap, so the spec should also cover the series-first swap (place in S, then remove A), which is currently free.

Reviewer's fix: Make prediction the mechanic and let sweeping cost something, without punishing a single experiment.
(1) In act('pick'), charge each block taken from a bin as `this.spent+=BLOCK_COST*.5`. Returning a block (the slot pop branch) refunds nothing, so the cost axis (limits.cost) reflects wasted parts. Recompute limits.cost so a clean run is still an A: sum of best() costs × 1.5.
(2) Add a bonus, 'Called it: three cabinets signed off on the first chain you powered', tracked by a `poweredArrangements` counter per job that increments in act('power') when powered goes true. Add it to the bonuses in station.ts:118-121.
(3) Add a fourth meter tile, 'ACROSS CHAIN  3.0 V' (r.vR when live; before power, show V − Vf in grey as a prediction). Replace or shrink HOTTEST BLOCK, since block heat already has its bar. Put it in drawMeter at station.ts:553-555.

*From arcade-rush-teach:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Drop (b), the hot-swap mistake. It punishes trying things and conflicts with the 'experiments are not damage' direction (review4 DESIGN_A.md:224/243 and finding 5). Keep (a), reward a first power-on in the band (a bonus plus a count on the card), and (c), widen supplies and bands so no single fix exceeds about 15%.

Reviewer's fix: Make prediction the scoring mechanic. (a) Track `powerOns` per cabinet and store `first:boolean` in `served` when the first power-on was already in the band. Add a rush bonus 'Five cabinets right on the first power-on' and count first-try cabinets on the result card. (b) In rush, treat changing a block while powered as a hot swap: a small spark and a mistake (real bench practice: power off before rework). Together with a PTC that latches until power-off (see the PTC finding) this is truthful. (c) Widen the inputs so memorising fails: supplies from [3.3, 3.7 (Li-ion), 5, 6, 9, 12, 24] and bands from 5–20 mA in 1 mA steps, keeping `best()` solvable. Raise the 'reliable' bar so it needs the margin, not luck.
