At zoom 9 the robot is out of frame for most of the 11 s route (garage-models-64-driving); only at the default zoom 26 is it visible (garage-models-76-drive-4s).

*garage-play* — **Win push-in frames the empty bench: the robot that just delivered is off-screen at the dock.** The payoff of the whole job is the robot driving its route and stopping at the delivery dock (−8.1, −5.6), where the dock lamp turns green (room.ts:111-113). But game.winFocus() returns `station.table + 0.5` for every station (src/game.ts:398), and the push-in uses distance 7 and pitch 0.5 (game.ts:373). The win shot is therefore Pip cheering in front of a bench with 'Press PULSE' on the scope (shots 30, 32, 33). The robot, the dock and the green lamp are about 9 m away and out of frame. The result card then covers the right half. The celebration doesn't show what the player achieved. This breaks DR-11 (the win push-in frames Pip together with the working machine) and repeats the QA 10 class of bug ('Pip missing / wrong subject') for the garage.

*garage-teach* — **The payoff drive doesn't show any lesson, and the win camera frames the bench, not the robot at the dock.** After job 3, the robot drives its route to the dock (station.ts:256-261, :357-364), the only toy in the room according to review 4. It drives non-stop and arrives.

The result shot (`garage-teach-29-win.jpg`, `-48-result-card.png`) frames Pip cheering at the empty bench while the robot and the green dock lamp are off-screen in the back-left. This breaks DR-11 (win frames Pip together with the working machine).

*gap4-juice-audio* — **Win confetti and the push-in centre on level.target, which in the Garage is the bench, not the delivered robot.** Game.win() bursts 90 confetti at `this.level.target` (src/game.ts:351). For station rooms the target is the bench, so in the Garage the win confetti erupts over the bench. The garage's own 20-confetti burst at the robot (garage/station.ts:364) fires 1.4 s earlier with only a single bell. The machine coming to life isn't where the celebration is.

*meeting-play* — **Win push-in frames the projector screen and boardroom coworkers, and Pip is not in the shot (QA 10 still open).** When the strip is reset and the projector comes on, the camera pushes in on winFocus (12.2, 1.7, -8.6), the projector screen on the back wall, from 8 m at pitch 0.32 with a 2.2 m right offset. Pip is standing at the boardroom door (about 12.4, -1.15), which is behind or below the camera. Pip never appears in the win frames. Meeting-play-26 (the moment the card slides in) shows the slide, two pendant lamps, confetti and three coworkers. Meeting-play-27/28 (the final result framing) show the screen, a pink and a blue coworker, and the result card over the right 40% of the frame. Pip is in neither. The payoff of the whole job (the hero plugging in, the room cheering at the hero) is lost. It reads as a cutscene about the coworkers rather than 'Good job, Pip'. The result card also covers the projector beam. This is the same defect QA 10 reported, and PROGRESS only claimed the push-in target fix (the pendant lamp), not Pip framing. It breaks DR-11: Pip and the working machine must both sit inside the centre 70% of the frame.

*lunch-play* — **The win push-in frames the underside of the lift car and leaves Pip out of the shot.** On delivery the camera pushes in on winFocus (12, 2.2, -7), offset 2.2 m right, at distance 9 and pitch 0.6 (src/game.ts:373-374, :398). By then the lift car has risen to y about 3.6. The frame (lunch-play-c20, c21) is filled by the grey underside of the car, a tiny tray, confetti and the capacitor cart at the bottom edge. Pip, who did the work and is standing at the winch at (11.8,-4.4), is not in frame at all.

The result tag then covers the right half. This is the payoff moment for the longest job in the game, and it reads as a camera glitch. QA 10 and R2 P0.1 asked for Pip in the win shot, and this still fails for Lunch.

*lunch-teach* — **The success moment never shows why it worked: no cap discharge in the win shot, Pip out of frame, no recap on the result card.** The win push-in frames the lift top and confetti (shot S-38). Pip and the cap cart are cut off at the bottom of the frame, and the cart is not doing anything visible anyway. The result card (shot S-39) shows time, damage, cost and three bonus lines, with nothing that closes the loop on the lesson, e.g. 'the lift wanted 9, cart A only ever saw 4.5'. The player's last memory is of confetti, not of the capacitor carrying the start. DR-28 and Juul's point is that understanding consolidates at the outcome; DR-11 also asks for Pip and the machine in frame.

*observatory-models* — **Win push-in leaves out the dome light-up payoff and crops Pip at the left edge.** When the last transmission is decoded, lightUp() brightens the dome. It adds a glow sprite and an 8-intensity point light at (dx,1.8,dz) = (-6.1,1.8,-5.3) (room.ts:108-110). The win camera instead pushes in on the bench and the gallery. In shots 50 (0.25 s) and 51 (1.5 s) the dome isn't in the frame at all, so the room's one celebratory change is never seen. Pip is cut by the left frame edge: only the helmet, one arm and the torso show, inside x 0–270 of 1440, outside the centre 70%. The result card then covers the right half of the frame.

*observatory-play* — **Win push-in cuts Pip at the frame edge and never shows the dome light-up payoff.** On the last LOG, the win camera pushes in on winFocus(), which is the bench table plus 0.5 m, then shifts 2.2 m to the right. Pip, standing at the bench, ends up half outside the left edge: only a hat, a mitt and an overalls strap show. The frame is filled with the bench back, a lamp, boxes and the spectrum wall, and the result card then covers the right half. The room's designed payoff, the dome's stars brightening (dressObservatory lightUp at dx=-6.1, dz=-5.3), is about 6 m to the left and completely off-screen. Large confetti pieces also fly over the scope, covering the 'STARS CLEAR' decode, the one in-game reward text. The ending feels flat, and the player never sees the observatory 'come alive'. Breaks DR-11 (Pip and the working machine in the centre 70%) and AGENTS 2 (show, don't tell).

*spectrum-play* — **The win push-in shows Pip at the desk with no beam, and the 'rainbow lights up' finale is out of frame.** At the win the camera pushes in on the desk (winFocus = table, game.ts:398). Pip is in frame, which is good, but the machine that 'came alive' (the tower's beam through the smoke and mesh into the quiet room) isn't drawn.
- **No beam:** station.update() sets beam.visible=!atBench (station.ts:374/390), and after win() the game stops stepping (game.ts:457 only steps while !won). The leaveBench() in win (game.ts:353) therefore never gets a station update, and the beam stays hidden. In shot 44 the turret points right and no thermal beam leaves it.
- **No finale:** lightUp() glows the floor rainbow stripes at z 6.2–6.9 (room.ts:148), which are below or behind the push-in camera and don't appear in shots 44 or 45.
- **No destination:** the quiet room, where the last message landed, is off-frame to the right.

The final beat is Pip waving at an unchanged desk.

*spectrum-teach* — **The win push-in frames the tower and desk, not the pod receiving the message through the cage.** On the last delivery the camera pushes in on the desk and the tower (shots 25 and 48). The pulse arrival and the star burst at the quiet-room pad (station.ts:235, :396) are off-frame. So is the pod's green lamp. Pip faces the camera with the transmitter behind. The payoff of the lesson, the thermal beam crossing smoke and mesh and landing, isn't shown. During deliveries at the desk, the hall beam and pulse are hidden (station.ts:374, :390, :397). The only success feedback is the map, the toast and confetti over the desk.

*spectrum-models* — **Win push-in crops Pip at the frame edge and the result card covers the tower.** The win camera (79–82) frames Pip cheering at the bottom-left. His feet are cut by the bottom edge and his left mitt reaches x ≈ 50 px (Pip spans about 11–33% of the width). The result card then covers the right 40% of the frame, including the tower, the machine that just delivered. DR-11 wants Pip and the working machine inside the centre 70%. The beam and pulse that made the moment aren't in the final frame.

*qfn-models* — **Win push-in crops Pip into the bottom-left corner behind the bench; the shot is half the side of Pip's head.** After the third board ships, the push-in frames the bench table + 0.5 m, shifted 2.2 m right for the result card. It uses distance 7 and pitch .5 and keeps the bench camera's yaw (π) (game.ts:373, winFocus game.ts:398). The camera therefore sits on the stand side behind Pip, and Pip lands at the near-left frame edge.

In qfn-models-50-win-0s, -51-win-push and -52-win-result, Pip is cut off at the left and bottom edges (roughly 30–40% outside the frame) and is mostly the back of a hat. The working 'machine' (the shipped boards stack and the board) is mid-frame.

DR-11 requires Pip and the machine inside the centre 70%, and QA 10 already complained that Pip was missing from the win shot. The cheering pose, the only character payoff of the job, is wasted.

*playground-play* — **Win push-in leaves Pip at the left edge, half outside the centre 70%, with the result card over the right 40%.** The playground push-in targets winFocus (the lamp at y 1.5) plus 2.2 m to the right (src/game.ts:372, :398), at distance 9 and pitch 0.6. Pip, standing by the switch, lands at x≈70–330 px of 1440 (shots 16, 17), partly outside the centre-70% band (216–1224 px) from DR-11. The result tag then covers x≈850–1310, so the celebrating Pip is squeezed against the left edge while the frame centre is the lamp pole.

*arcade-models* — **Win push-in frames the bench meter's black 'ALL FIXED' screen and Pip cut at the frame edge, not the five cabinets that came alive; big confetti squares cover the shot.** For stations, winFocus() (game.ts:398) is the bench table + 0.5 m, pushed in to 7 m at pitch .5 (game.ts:373). Shots -73/-74/-75 show the meter as a black panel with tiny 'ALL FIXED' text, Pip in the lower-left corner with feet cut off, and the result card over the right half. The payoff, five back-wall cabinets with lit marquees and screens, is off-frame (only the HANDHELD cabinet edge is visible at the right). At +0.15 s, cheer() confetti squares 60–100 px across fly through the camera and cover the meter and Pip (shot -73). DR-11 wants Pip and the working machine in the centre 70% of the frame. The A10 fix (no confetti through the bench camera) does not cover the win push-in.

**Fix.**

*From camera-render:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep per-station winFocus() and the 'frame Pip and the focus together' approach. Frame both into the left part of the screen that the result card leaves free: project and require x in [-0.85, 0.1] and y in [-0.6, 0.7] at 1440×900. Keep the existing rightward target shift, scaled to the separation. On portrait, check against the card's real rectangle.

Reviewer's fix: Add an optional `winFocus():T.Vector3` to each station:
- garage: the robot's dock position (-8, -6);
- arcade: the centroid of the back-wall cabinets;
- observatory: the receiver dish;
- spectrum: the storeroom pod;
- qfn: the finished board on the bench.

In updateCamera's pushing branch, frame Pip and the focus together. Set the target to their midpoint, and the distance to max(7, 1.25 × the separation / tan(fov/2)). Set the yaw so both sit on a line across the screen, and raise the target 0.6 m so Pip's boots land above 80% of the frame height.

*From garage-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep fix 1: an optional Station.winFocus(); GarageBench returns the midpoint of Pip and the robot once delivered, or the dock lamp plus a .4 lerp toward Pip, with distance raised to about 10 so both fit. Do not teleport Pip; snapping the player breaks the feel. A plain auto-walk is also unnecessary if the focus is the Pip–robot midpoint. For item 3, only bias the camera toward the robot while driving, and let any player orbit or zoom input override it so the camera stays player-controlled. Drop item 4, because the 1.4 s delay already exists. Instead, hold the card's panel (not only the grade) until about 1.2 s after delivered.

Reviewer's fix: 1) Add an optional `winFocus?():T.Vector3` to the Station interface (src/stations/types.ts). In game.ts:398 use `this.station?.winFocus?.() ?? station.table+.5`. In GarageBench return the robot's body translation once `this.delivered`, i.e. DOCK at (-8.1, 1.0, -5.6), aimed between the dock and Pip.
2) In startDrive() (station.ts ~258), after leaveBench(), auto-walk or teleport Pip to a 'watch spot' about (-5.8, -3.6) facing the dock, so the push-in (distance 7) frames Pip and the robot together inside the centre 70%.
3) While `driving`, have the camera follow the robot: set the focus to lerp(Pip, robot, .6) and clamp the zoom to at least 18 until delivered.
4) Delay the result card about 1.2 s after `delivered` so the green dock lamp and confetti read first.

*From garage-play:* Add an optional `winFocus?():T.Vector3` to the Station interface (src/stations/types.ts). Make game.winFocus() prefer it. GarageBench returns the robot's final position (−8.1, 0.6, −5.6).
To keep Pip in frame as well, pick one:
(a) Make the last step 'Meet the robot at the dock'. Replace 'Watch the robot drive' with a step done when Pip is within 2.5 m of DOCK after `delivered`, so Pip is there for the push-in. This also removes the passive wait (next finding).
(b) Target the midpoint of Pip and the robot, with distance clamped to 7 + 0.6 × separation.

*From garage-teach:* - **Make the route a recap:** add two painted stop lines on `ROUTE` (room.ts:19) where the robot brakes crisply to a halt, its eyes stay cyan ('no reset'), then pulls away with a load bump and no reboot. At each stop, a green ✓ pops over the head. The dock arrival stays the finale.
- **Station-specific win focus:** add `Station.winFocus?()`. The garage returns the robot's position or `DOCK` (`{x:-8.1,y:1,z:-6.05}`). Have `game.ts:398` prefer it, and move Pip next to the dock, or frame both from a high angle.
- **Suppress the prop prompt while driving:** have `prompt()` return `{key:'',text:'Watch the robot'}`, or have objectives skip the nearest-prop fallback while `driving`.

*From gap4-juice-audio:* Let a station provide `winSpot()` (for the garage, the robot's dock position). Use it in Game.win() for the confetti and for winFocus. Move the bell, confetti, a 'flash' and the jingle to the same frame, at the dock.

*From meeting-play:* In src/game.ts winFocus() for cable floors, return the midpoint between Pip and the machine instead of the machine alone: f = lerp(pip(x, 1.2, z), machine, 0.55). For the meeting, also choose the push-in yaw so the camera sits behind and to the left of Pip, looking past Pip at the screen: yaw = atan2(pip.x - 12.2, pip.z - (-9.8)) + 0.35. Use distance 9.5 and pitch 0.38, and keep the target offset to the LEFT (-1.8 * right) so the result card (right side) does not cover Pip or the screen. Turn Pip to face the screen during the push-in (animateRig already turns Pip toward yaw on win; have it face the machine instead). As a safety check, after computing the camera, project Pip's head and the screen centre to NDC; if either falls outside |x|<0.7, |y|<0.7, pull distance back by 1 m, up to 3 times.

*From lunch-play:* In winFocus(), for lunch return the midpoint of Pip's position and the lift car top: new T.Vector3((p.x+12)/2, 1.8, (p.z-7)/2). In the push-in for lunch use distance 11, pitch 0.42, and offset left by 1.5 m rather than right 2.2 m, so the tag on the right doesn't cover the subject. Optionally play a cheer pose on Pip, facing the lift.

*From lunch-teach:* Frame the win between the winch and the cap cart: winFocus for lunch at about (12,1.2,-5.5), backed off far enough to include Pip at the switch. On the result card for Lunch, add a pictogram strip with no sentence: the lift icon with a '9' spike, a blue cap icon taking the spike, and the cart A dial reading 4.5. Use the recorded peak and draw from the telltale fix.

*From observatory-models:* Either (a) aim the observatory's winFocus (game.ts:398 winFocus/station focus) between the bench and the dome, at about (-3.0,1.4,-3.4), with a 3/4 yaw from the front-left so the bench, the rack and the dome are in frame and Pip sits at 40–60% of the width; or (b) move the light-up so it shows in the bench framing: light the 7 gallery panels and lamps in sequence, and send a sprite 'beam' from the rack mast. Also nudge the camera 0.8 m to Pip's left so Pip isn't clipped. Keep the extra light within the DR-66 budget by reusing the existing dome pointLamp (raise its intensity) instead of adding a sixth.

*From observatory-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The confetti part of the fix does not work as written. cheer() ignores its `at` argument while game.atBench (shared.ts:12), and the final LOG happens at the bench. The confetti over the scope comes mostly from game.ts:350's win() bursts at level.target (the stand, y=2), not from cheer(). Move or lower those bursts in game.ts win() for stations, or change cheer() to honour `at`. The rest of the fix (a station winFocus override framing the stand and the dome) is fine.

Reviewer's fix: Let a station override the win focus. Add an optional `winFocus?:T.Vector3` (and `winSide?:number`) to the Station type. For the observatory, return the midpoint between the stand (0,-1.55) and the dome (-6.1,-5.3), about (-3,1.2,-3.4), with the right offset at 0 and a distance of 9, so Pip, the bench and the lit dome all fit inside the left 60% (the result card takes the right). Also open the dome shutter on win: rotate a shutter segment on shellOut and add a vertical light shaft through the slit. Spawn the win confetti above Pip (cheer(game,this,'#ffd66b',{x:stand.x,y:2.4,z:stand.z+1})) instead of over the table.

*From spectrum-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Fix 1 works as written: after the last send, current() is undefined, so reading() falls back to JOBS[last] and aim.tx isn't re-aimed, and update(0) redraws the last delivered route. Also set the beam's opacity to full in that call, because drawBeam caches on beamKey.

Reviewer's fix: 1. In game.win(), after leaveBench(), call this.station.update?.(0) once, or add a Station.onWin() that spectrum implements as `this.beam.visible=true; this.drawBeam(this.reading())` with the last delivered route kept, not the 'next job' route.
2. Give the station a `winFocus()` override. For spectrum, use the midpoint between TX and the last pad (about (3.9,1.5,3.5)) with distance about 10, so the tower, the beam, the smoke and the quiet room are all in frame.
3. Also light the three destination pad rings and the tower beacon in lightUp, rather than (or as well as) the floor stripes behind the camera.

*From spectrum-teach:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep any automatic fly-along short (≤ 1.5 s) and cancel it on any camera input, so it respects the player-controlled orbit camera rule. A simpler first step is to let the Station give its own winFocus: the midpoint of the last pad and the desk, with distance enough to frame both.

Reviewer's fix: On each successful SEND, leave the bench camera for about 1.5 s on a fly-along. Have the camera follow the pulse along drawnPath at about 9 m/s, show the stop or arrival burst at the pad with the pod lamp turning green and the recipient blob cheering, then return. For the final win, set the station's winFocus to the last pad plus Pip, or have the game's win focus use `PADS[lastJob.pad]`.

*From spectrum-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The station win pitch is .5 (game.ts:373: pitch = this.station ? .5 : …), not .32, which is Meeting's. 'Keep pitch 0.32' would actually change it. Keep .5, or tune it deliberately. The lateral shift is already 2.2 m to camera-right, so the fix should change both the focus point (the Pip–TX midpoint) and the sign and size of that shift.

Reviewer's fix: In src/game.ts winFocus for station levels, aim at the midpoint of Pip and TX (−0.4, 1.2, 2.3) with distance about 7 and a 0.6 m lateral shift to the left of screen, so the result card (right side) covers empty floor. For spectrum, pass the last delivery pad's position as the secondary focus so the delivered pod is in frame. Keep pitch at 0.32.

### R5-078

**R5-078 | P1 | global, arcade-rush, arcade, garage, lunch, meeting, playground, spectrum, observatory | fun | Grading has no teeth: default limits plus best-of-three make nearly every run an A (standing still in Rush earns A/A/A and a saved medal)**

Found by: `progression#2` (P1 fun), `arcade-rush-play#0` (P1 fun), `arcade-rush-teach#0` (P1 fun), `arcade-play#10` (P2 fun), `garage-play#8` (P1 fun), `lunch-play#13` (P2 fun), `meeting-play#5` (P1 fun), `playground-play#12` (P2 fun), `spectrum-play#9` (P1 fun), `observatory-teach#1` (P1 teaching). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*progression* — **Nearly every run grades A overall, so medals, the 'A on three jobs' bonus and replays mean little.** Every run I finished in this review graded **A** overall. Playground: 0:05, 0 damage, 0 cost, triple A (`progression-12`). Meeting: 0:21 with 2 breaks, triple A (`progression-36`). Arcade: 0:31 after throwing props, A/A/B, overall A (`progression-29`). Garage, after knocking a chair: A/A/D, overall A (`progression-38`). The causes: overall is the best of three (src/sim/grade.ts:5), cable floors use the 120 s / 10 / 300 default (src/sim/grade.ts:3), and station time limits are 360–720 s (arcade 480, src/stations/arcade/station.ts:81; garage 420, garage/station.ts:77; QFN 720, qfn/station.ts:51; observatory 360; spectrum 540). The time axis alone hands out an A almost every time, so the grade carries no information. The lobby bonus 'Earn an A on three jobs' (src/hub/lobby.ts:46) falls out of the first three jobs automatically. The door medal and the Jobs-board shelf will be a wall of identical gold A's. Good Job's loop is 'replay for a cleaner or faster run' (docs/GAME_DESIGN.md core loop), and that loop needs a grade that moves. Here a sloppy run and a perfect run get the same stamp. Best of three is a hard rule and isn't contested here; the problem is the tuning and what is shown.

*arcade-rush-play* — **Rush grade is free: standing still for 3 minutes earns A/A/A and is saved as the best medal.** Arcade Rush ends on the clock. `complete()` is `game.time>=RUSH_TIME` (180 s), whatever the player did, so `win()` always fires at 180 s. The grade then comes from the shared Good Job formula: time 180 is under `limits.time` (190), so the time axis is always A. The overall grade is the best of the three axes, so every Rush run grades A. I proved it with a run where Pip never moves: no tray, no bench, zero cabinets. The result card shows a big gold A with a green check, "Orders served: 0", time 3:00 A, damage 0 A and cost 0 A. localStorage records `arcade-rush: {grade:'A'}`, and that best result counts toward the lobby bonus "Earn an A on three jobs". A full expert run with 32 cabinets also grades A, so the grade can't tell 0 cabinets from 32. Rush is a score-attack mode, and its only real score (orders served) isn't graded at all. Players lose the reason to replay and improve, the lobby medal is meaningless, and DR-07 is broken outright ("standing still … can't earn A on all three"). DR-38 is broken too: understanding is not rewarded.

*arcade-rush-teach* — **Arcade Rush always grades A: zero cabinets earns a gold A and a bonus star.** In rush mode the time limit is 190 s (`limits.time=RUSH_TIME+10`) and the shift always ends at exactly 180 s. The time axis is therefore always A, and Good Job grading takes the overall grade as the best of the three axes. The result is an A however the shift went. I ran the shift twice. In the first run Pip never sat at the bench. The result card showed 'Orders served: 0', the rows 3:00 A / 0 A / 0 A, a big gold A with a star and a green check, confetti, and the bonus 'Fuse tripped no more than once' lit. In the second run nine cabinets were fixed elegantly, and the card was identical apart from the count. The number of cabinets served, which is the whole point of the mode, does not affect the grade. The cost axis works against success: `spent` grows with every signed-off block (limit 24), so a strong player who fixes 40 cabinets reaches cost 67 (grade D), and that axis is hidden behind the time A. The lobby records this A as the door medal, so the medal teaches the player that the mode doesn't matter. Nothing rewards applying I = (V−Vf)/R quickly and correctly, which kills the rush's reason to exist as practice.

*arcade-play* — **Grading is untuned: a 0:28 clean run against a 480 s limit, best-of-three makes any finish an A, and tossing a cone counts as damage.** Limits are `{time:480,damage:2,cost:⌈9×1.25⌉=12}` (station.ts:81, :107). The scripted clean solve finished in 0:28 with damage 0 and cost 9: A/A/A (shot 45). A careful human reading every toast finishes well inside 480 s.

Because the overall grade is the best of the three axes (src/sim/grade.ts:6), any finish with time ≤ 480 is an overall A, however many trips and pops there were. The time axis never discriminates.

The damage axis mixes bench mistakes with room props:
- the first thrown cone at t 2.6 already counted damage 1 (s6: "after 1");
- a thrown tray counted damage +1 and cost +10.

So playing with the room (the only chaos available) eats the same 2-point budget as electrical mistakes. Chaos is graded as a mistake, which goes against AGENTS 5 and DR-07.

*garage-play* — **Grades can't go below A: time limit 420 s is 10× the clean solve, and overall = best of three.** GarageBench.limits = {time:420, damage:1, cost:≈3.0} (station.ts:77), and grade() returns the best of the three axes (src/sim/grade.ts:6). The clean solve finishes at 46.5 s, about 39 s of play. My chaos run (one smashed crate, cost 8) and my error run (a short, a reversed capacitor and a failed TEST: mistakes 3) both stay far under 420 s, so both grade A overall, with damage and cost at C. A player who trips the fuse, vents the capacitor, fails tests and wrecks the room gets the same medal as one who reasons it out. The grade carries no signal, and the 'experiments cost damage' rule (a PULSE with a backwards diode counts a mistake) only lowers an axis nobody sees. This breaks DR-07 (each axis is tuned per room) and DR-38 (tiers and grades reward understanding).

*lunch-play* — **Lunch's grade can't fail: the default 120 s limit plus best-of-three means every run earns an A.** Lunch passes no limits, so grade() uses 120 s, 10 damage and 300 cost (src/game.ts:354, src/sim/grade.ts:3).

The scripted clean run took 91.8 s of simulated time (it sprints everywhere, never hesitates, and overlaps the bake) and graded A/A/A. A person will take several minutes, so the time axis will usually read B to D. Damage stays far under 10 for anyone not wrecking deliberately, and the overall grade is the best axis, so effectively every completed Lunch is an A. Meanwhile a player who wrecks a lot still gets an A on time if fast.

The result card also highlights the time row as the grade source (c21), even though all three axes are equal. The grade gives no signal about understanding (tripping breakers or scorching cables don't count as damage at all, only as lost bonus stars).

*meeting-play* — **Grading is always A: sprint chaos 0:29, clean coupler route 0:39, and a 14-break wreck run all grade A on the 120 s / 10 / 300 defaults.** Big Meeting calls grade() with no limits, so it gets the cable-floor default of 120 s / 10 damage / 300 cost, with the overall grade the best of three.
- The sprint-overstretch chaos run finished in 0:29 with 0 damage: A/A/A (shot 28).
- The clean coupler route finished in 0:39: A/A/A (shot 40).
- An aisle sprint at overstretch broke 14 things and cost 245 in 6 seconds (shot 68). That scores damage B but time A, so the overall is still A.
There is no grade reason ever to learn the coupler route, which is the 'clean solution' and the room's routing lesson. It is slower than chaos and never cheaper. Players will learn that the deadline (4:00) and the limits don't matter. This breaks DR-07 (each axis tuned per room; standing still or wrecking can't earn A on all three) and AGENTS 6. The result card also gives the A without showing which axis earned it.

*playground-play* — **Grading is untuned: default limits give AAA in 5 s and wrecking still earns an A.** The playground passes no limits, so grade() uses 120 s / 10 damage / 300 cost (src/sim/grade.ts:3). The clean run takes 4.98 s (b-clean), 24× under the time limit. 'Finish in under 45 seconds' (objectives.ts:28) is unmissable, and the result card shows A/A/A with the time row highlighted (shot 18). With overall = best of three, pure wrecking (more than 10 breaks) still gets A from time and cost, so the grade carries no information and gives no reason to replay (DR-07).

*spectrum-play* — **The grading has no teeth: the time limit is 540 s against a 46 s clean solve, and one thrown prop busts the cost axis.** **Time.** The station limits are {time:540, damage:1, cost:5} (station.ts:60, :82). My clean, bot-speed run finished in 0:46 with all three axes A (shot 45). A human who walks rather than sprints and pauses at the desk should still land well under 3 minutes, so the time axis is effectively always A: a player can dawdle for 9 minutes and still get A. With overall = best of three, every run ends A no matter how messy or slow.

**Cost.** The cost axis mixes the energy units of sends (1–4 each) with prefab breakage costs (coolbox 30, chair 25, crate 5). A single knocked crate already uses the whole 5-credit budget.

The result card shows three A's, so the grade can't tell a careful run from a sloppy one.

*observatory-teach* — **The grade can't tell understanding from luck: a tier-1, one-mistake run gets A on all three axes, and the cost axis rewards using fewer parts than the lesson needs.** The limits are time 360 s, damage 1, and cost = ceil(sum of cheapest reliable costs × 1.25) = ceil(9 × 1.25) = 12 (station.ts:63, :82). grade() takes the best of the three axes (src/sim/grade.ts:3-6).
(1) The shortcut run (no filter, one capacitor, a wrong whip logged once) spent 5–6 credits, under the 12 limit, so cost is A. It made 1 mistake (≤ 1), so damage is A. Time is A. Overall A (shot 18).
(2) The proper run (shunt C, then LC 10 mH + 1 µF, then right whip) spent 7–11 and got the same A/A/A (shot 37).
The cost axis is set from the cheapest *reliable* filter, so under-filtering always looks thrifty. It actively rewards not building the LC. Damage A tolerates one failed log, so the only thing that separates good play is three bonus stars drawn at about 9 px on the result card. This breaks DR-07 ('standing still or pure wrecking can't earn A on all three') and DR-38.

**Fix.**

*From progression:* (1) Give every level its own `limits` set from a measured par. Run 3–5 human clean runs and set time A at about 1.2× the median human time: for example Playground 40 s, Meeting 150 s, Lunch 300 s, and stations at about 1.3× their median human bench time, not 6–12 min. Pass them through `Level.limits` in src/levels/*.ts and use them at src/game.ts:354 for cable floors too. (2) Keep the overall grade as best of three, per AGENTS 6, but add a mastery mark that replays can chase: 'Crew Gold' = A on all three axes plus all 3 bonus stars, stored per job. Show it as a gold rim on the door medal (src/hub/lobby.ts:94) and on the Jobs-board shelf (src/ui/screens.ts:126). (3) Change the lobby bonus to 'Crew Gold on three jobs'.

*From arcade-rush-play:* Give rush levels their own grade. In `src/stations/types.ts`, add an optional `Station.grade?():{parts:Grade[];overall:Grade}`. In `src/game.ts:354`, use `this.station?.grade?.() ?? grade(...)`. In `ArcadeBench`, when `rush`:
- **Served axis** replaces time. Count only cabinets with tier ≥ 2: A ≥ 10, B ≥ 6, C ≥ 3, D below that.
- **Damage axis:** mistakes against 3.
- **Cost axis:** wasted credits only (see the cost finding).
- **Overall:** the served axis, capped one letter below by damage if damage > 2× the limit. Don't use best-of-three for rush.

If 0 cabinets were served, show a "Shift over: no orders served" fail card with the one-key retry (R), and don't call `record()`. In `src/ui/game-ui.ts:216-217`, replace the Time row with the Orders served row when `level.id.endsWith('-rush')`, as R3A N4 asked.

*From arcade-rush-teach:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The fix is sound. Correct the example: cost 67 against limit 24 is C (D needs >72). Keep the rush grade inside the Station.grade() hook and don't change grade.ts globally: the best-of-three rule is shared by every other level.

Reviewer's fix: Add an optional `grade?():{parts:Grade[];overall:Grade}` to the Station interface (src/stations/types.ts) and have game.ts:354 use it when present. For the arcade in rush mode, grade three rush axes: (1) cabinets fixed: A ≥ 8, B ≥ 5, C ≥ 3, otherwise D; (2) mistakes per cabinet: A ≤ 0.25, B ≤ 0.5, C ≤ 1; (3) elegant share: A ≥ 60 %, B ≥ 30 %. Take the overall grade from the cabinet count, capped one letter above the worst of the other two, so wrecking or idling can't earn an A. Show these rows on the result card instead of time/damage/cost when `rushStatus()` exists. Make every rush bonus need `served.length>0` (the 'Fuse tripped no more than once' ok() at station.ts:116 should be `this.served.length>0&&this.trips<=1`).

*From arcade-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Drop fix point 2. Room breakage must stay on the damage axis (AGENTS 5/6: destruction is graded, overall = best of three). Excluding it would break the hard rule. Keep point 1: set limits.time to about 150–200 s, after measuring a human solve; the scripted 28 s includes 15 s of soak. Keep point 3: label the axis that carried the grade, which DR-07 asks for. If bench mistakes and room breakage should read differently, show them as two sub-counts on the damage row, both counted.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Set the arcade `limits.time` to 150 s (about 2× a fluent human solve; measure with 3 play-testers).
2. In game.ts:353, for station rooms, grade damage on `station.score().mistakes` only. Report room breakage as a separate fun stat ("Arcade wrecked: 3 props") that never lowers the grade, or give it its own bonus.
3. Show which axis carried the overall on the result card. The time row is already highlighted; add the word 'best'.

*From garage-play:* Set limits.time to about 2.5× a thoughtful first solve, e.g. 150 s. Keep damage at 1–2.
Don't charge a PULSE short as a mistake. Count only failed TESTs, because PULSE is the free 'look' (station.ts:219-220). Shorts can still cost the 'no tripped fuse' bonus.
For the room as a whole, consider the product-owner-level question in DR-07 (best-of-three vs. median). At minimum, make the result card show which axis carried the grade.

*From lunch-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep best-of-three (AGENTS 6). Add Level.limits for lunch (e.g. time 300) so the time medal reflects the longer chain, and optionally count trips and scorches in cost. Do not frame it as making the overall grade fail.

Reviewer's fix: (1) Add optional limits to Level, and pass this.station?.limits ?? this.level.limits into grade(). For lunch use {time:300, damage:4, cost:60}.
(2) Count each breaker trip, short or scorch as +1 damage and +10 cost (the circuit event log already exists), so mistakes in the taught concept move a grade axis.
(3) On the result card, mark which axis gave the overall grade.

*From meeting-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Per-room limits are necessary but not enough. Change the overall from best-of-three to the median (or the mean rank), so a wreck that is A only on time cannot headline an A. Calibrate limits.time from walking-pace runs, not from drive.walkTo, which auto-sprints beyond 2.5 m (game.ts:473); a 60 s limit would grade honest first runs C. If the sprint overstretch is meant as the chaos shortcut, give it a cost: for example, pulling at strain > 1.0 for more than 0.5 s scuffs the cable sheath (+1 damage, +20 cost). Then it trades grade for speed instead of strictly dominating the coupler route.

Reviewer's fix: Add an optional limits field to Level (src/levels/types.ts) and pass level.limits in game.ts win(). For the meeting, time 60 s (the clean route at walking pace is about 45–55 s; the drive-script sprint route is 29–39 s), damage 3 and cost 80. Then a tidy coupler run gets A on damage and cost, a chaos sprint gets A on time but loses damage when it drags chairs, and a wreck gets an A only on time.
Consider grading on the median axis rather than the best, or show all three letters with the best highlighted and its axis named ('A: Speed').
On the result card, label which bar produced the headline grade.

*From playground-play:* Add level-level limits (types.ts Level.limits?) and pass them in Game.win (game.ts:354): playground {time:15, damage:3, cost:40}. Change the time bonus to 'Finish in under 12 seconds'. Consider letting the result card name the axis that earned the grade.

*From spectrum-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Also flag that the best-of-three overall in src/sim/grade.ts:5 is shared by every room. Changing it is a cross-room decision (for example, median or worst-of-three), not just a spectrum limit change. Measure the 180 s figure with a human run before committing to it.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Set limits.time to about 3× a human clean run. Measure one with a person; as a starting point use 180 s (bot 46 s × about 2 for walking without sprint × 1.8).
2. Split the cost axis: grade `energy spent` (send cost) against 5, and room breakage against a separate budget (for example 60). Or add breakage to damage only and leave cost as pure energy.
3. Consider not counting the first failed send as damage when the LINK meter was hidden (see the brute-force finding).

*From observatory-teach:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The cost or damage change is fine, but note that grade() returns the best axis. Per-axis letters will change, but any 'overall' readout stays A while time is A. Either add tier-weighted damage (count each tier-1 log as a mistake, limit 1 → B at 2), or have the room's result use the worst of the axes, or require bonus 1 for an A on the cost axis. The verify step should check per-axis letters, not overall.

Reviewer's fix: In ObservatoryBench.score(), return a cost that includes a margin penalty: add (2 − tier) × 3 credits per job logged below tier 2 ('the decode will need a re-send'). Equivalently, set limits.cost from the cheapest reliable cost (9, no ×1.25 slack) and charge tier-1 logs. Alternatively, count each tier-1 log as half a mistake in `damage`. Keep damage at 1 but do not count logs made while S/N ≥ decodeSnr (those are near-misses, not damage). On the result card (src/ui/game-ui.ts:217), show which axis earned the grade, per DR-07.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *progression:* A unit test in src/sim/grade.test.ts per level: the scripted clean-route time from tests/*.spec.ts grades A on time, and 3× that time grades C. Rerun progression-38: the garage card still says A overall but shows no Crew Gold rim. Take a lobby shot with mixed results and check the medals differ.
- *arcade-rush-play:* Add a test in tests/station-arcade-rush.spec.ts: open arcade-rush, `wait` 181 s with no input. Expect `won` (or the fail card) with an overall grade other than 'A', and localStorage to have no arcade-rush A. Re-run the clean spec (2 cabinets) and expect a grade of C or lower. Re-run the s2-clean.mjs expert run (32 cabinets) and expect A. Retake arcade-rush-play-40 and arcade-rush-play-26.
- *arcade-rush-teach:* Re-run mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-teach/result.mjs idle: the card shows D and no lit bonus. Re-run `result.mjs good` (9 cabinets): the card shows A. Add a unit test that a rush station with served=[] grades D.
- *arcade-play:* Rerun s3-win.mjs: a 0:28 run is A on time. A scripted run at 200 s is B on time. A run that throws 5 props and solves cleanly still has damage 0 on the card.
- *garage-play:* Unit test: grade(43, 3, 8, garage.limits) is not A on every axis. Clean spec: still all A with time ≤ 150 s.
- *lunch-play:* Unit test grade() with the lunch limits: a 92 s / 0 / 15 run gives A, and a 400 s / 6 / 90 run gives B or lower overall. Rerun s2-clean.mjs: the result shows A.
- *meeting-play:* Rerun s2.mjs, s3.mjs and the s7 aisle-sprint run: the result cards must differ (the wreck run's headline must be named as coming from time only, and its damage bar must show C or D). Extend tests/routes.spec.ts so each meeting route asserts the grade parts it is expected to earn.
- *playground-play:* Unit test in grade.test.ts for the playground limits. b-clean finishes as A (about 5–8 s), and a run with 12 breaks shows damage C.
- *spectrum-play:* A clean spec run grades A on time under 180 s and B at 200 s. A run with one broken crate keeps cost A. tests/station-spectrum.spec.ts gains assertions on grade parts.
- *observatory-teach:* Re-run b.mjs (shortcut) and c.mjs (tier 3). The shortcut's result card must not be A/A/A; the tier-3 run stays A on all three. Add a unit or spec assertion on snapshot().station after the shortcut sequence: score().cost > limits.cost.

**Rules:** AGENTS 5, AGENTS 6, DR-07, DR-38

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — src/sim/grade.ts:3-6: overall = best of the three parts, with a default of 120 s / 10 / 300. The station limits are arcade 480 s (:81), garage 420 s (:77), observatory 360 s (:63), qfn 720 s (:51) and spectrum 540 s (:60). Damage is also an easy A: a floor allows 10 breaks, so any run with 10 or fewer breaks grades A overall no matter its time or cost, and in stations the time axis alone gives an A. (10/10 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-079

**R5-079 | P1 | global, arcade, arcade-rush, garage, observatory, qfn, spectrum | fun | Station rooms have no cable, no chaos route and no physical bonus: the cable, the game's star, disappears after job 02 and every station follows one carry-then-menu template**

Found by: `progression#4` (P1 fun), `progression#5` (P1 fun), `arcade-play#6` (P1 fun), `arcade-rush-play#9` (P1 fun), `garage-play#9` (P1 fun), `observatory-play#2` (P1 fun), `qfn-play#2` (P1 fun), `spectrum-play#7` (P1 fun), `spectrum-play#8` (P1 fun). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*progression* — **The cable, the game's star, disappears after job 02: 5 of 8 jobs (6 of 9 doors) have no cable act, and their room step is a 2–6 s fetch.** Taken across the whole campaign, the game changes genre halfway. The first three doors are Good Job floors: a springy cable, strain, slingshot, and 24 coworkers reacting (`progression-34` Meeting mid-drag). From door 03 on, the rope is hidden and not simulated: `if(this.station||this.hub)…visible=false` (src/game.ts:92), with no simulateCable/drawCable for stations (src/game.ts:104, :348). Every station level has `obstacles:[]` (src/levels/arcade.ts:26, garage.ts:28, qfn.ts:22, observatory.ts:22, spectrum.ts:32). The room part of each station is one carry: Pip had the arcade tray and was seated at the bench by 5.7 s (arcade-flow.mjs: `held blocks t 2.2`, `atBench true t 5.7`). The rest is a tabletop of 9–13 hotkeys and a side panel (`progression-24`; `garage-play-13-bench-view`; `observatory-play-11-bench-view`). The station jobs are good puzzles, but they read as a second game bolted on. The verbs taught in 00–02 (drag, wrap, plug, slingshot) are never used again, the strain meter never appears again, and the slingshot reward the Playground trains (the pins) has no follow-up. The research doc and R4A already flagged that the cable is missing in stations. Seen as one progression, it is the main reason the campaign stops feeling like Circuit Crew after about 3 jobs.

*progression* — **Station jobs share one template (carry, 'Sit at the bench (E)' step, button sub-jobs), and none has a chaos route or chaos bonus.** All five station jobs follow the same script:
1. Carry one thing (tray, robot, parts crate, motor cart, pod).
2. Complete a separate objective step whose only content is pressing E: 'Step up to the service bench (E)' (src/stations/arcade/station.ts:110), 'Sit at the garage bench (E)' (garage/station.ts:98), 'Sit at the layout bench (E)' (qfn/station.ts:72), 'Sit at the signal bench (E)' (observatory/station.ts:86), 'Sit at the dispatch desk (E)' (spectrum/station.ts:87).
3. Solve 3–5 sub-jobs by picking parts with number keys and slotting them with letter keys.
4. Get the result card.

Only the spectrum job sends Pip back into the room between sub-jobs (pod and mirrors, spectrum/station.ts:89-92), and only the garage has a payoff in the room afterwards (the robot drives its route). Every station bonus list is bench precision only: 'reliable', 'elegant', 'no failed test/fuse' (arcade :119-121, garage :103-104, qfn :75-77, observatory :89-91, spectrum :95-97). None is physical or chaos, unlike the Playground pins (src/ui/objectives.ts:28). So for a chaos player, 5 of the 8 jobs offer nothing to chase in the room, and the dense clutter is scenery that costs points (see the grading finding). Played in order, 03→07 feel like the same room five times with a different panel.

*arcade-play* — **No cable, no chaos route, no physical bonus: the 22×16 m hall is a corridor to a menu, and throwing the tray at the bench doesn't count.** Everything the job needs happens on the bench keypad. The room contributes one carry of about 18 m (spawn → storeroom → bench, about 8 s at sprint in s1).

No cable:
- `rope.maxLength` is 10 but the cable is neither simulated nor drawn in station rooms (game.ts:104, :92). DR-05 fails.
- The action bar still shows the F plug button and the Q slingshot button (shots 01, 10). F only shrugs. These are false affordances.

No chaos route:
- The level has `obstacles:[]` and no designed shortcut (src/levels/arcade.ts:26). DR-01 fails.
- Throwing the tray (Q) at the bench from 1.9 m didn't deliver it. It flew over the bench to z −5.1/−6.1, and I had to walk round the right end to fetch it (s4, s10).
- `dropped()` is only called from the E drop path (game.ts:210); a throw never calls it.

No physical bonus:
- All three bonuses are bench metrics (station.ts:118-121). DR-10 fails.

The 132 props are scenery to push through on the way. Compared with the Playground pins or the Meeting glass, this room has no moment a player would want to show a friend.

*arcade-rush-play* — **No cable anywhere in Rush, and the action bar still offers a plug (F) and a slingshot (Q) that do nothing.** AGENTS 4 says the cable is the star in every playable room. In arcade-rush the rope isn't simulated or drawn (rope maxLength 10 exists, but `game.ts:104` skips it for stations). The room's only physical act is a 6-second tray carry, and everything after that happens in a menu-like bench view. Meanwhile the walking HUD action bar shows the F 'plug' button and the Q 'slingshot' button (greyed) on every walking frame. They are false affordances: F does nothing (`cableReady=false` for stations) and there is nothing to slingshot. A new player who presses F gets a shrug puff. DR-05 already knows the station rooms have no cable; Rush makes it worse, because the shift is pure bench time.

*garage-play* — **No chaos route, no chaos bonus, and no cable: throwing the robot onto the stand doesn't count, and all three bonuses are bench metrics.** The robot only counts as 'on the stand' through station.dropped(), which game.ts calls only on a deliberate E release (src/game.ts:210). Throwing it with Q never triggers the check. I threw the robot from 3 m (02-wrong.mjs): it flew over the bench and landed upside-down by the tool chest, nothing happened and it had to be fetched again (shots 43, 44). The level has obstacles:[] (src/levels/garage.ts:28), and the bonuses are 'every fix reliable', 'elegant' and 'no failed test / no fuse' (station.ts:101-104), all bench numbers. Nothing in the 220-prop room is worth knocking over, and no physical bonus can be found in the world. The room also has no cable at all: rope.maxLength 10 with length 0, and the cable is hidden for stations (game.ts:92/104). The bench harness is a static TubeGeometry (room.ts:81-82). So the star mechanic of the game is absent from a room about wiring. This breaks DR-01 (a chaos route that finishes the job), DR-10 (a findable chaos bonus) and DR-05 (each job involves a physical cable act), and AGENTS 4 and 5.

*observatory-play* — **The room part is a 4-second errand: no cable, no chaos route, no physical bonus (the cable is not the star).** The room has 142 props, three astronomers, a dome, a telescope and a spectrum gallery. The only room verb is one carry: grab the motor cart and drop it at least 4 m from the receiver, about 2–4 s of play. Everything else (three transmissions) happens in a menu-like bench view. There is no draggable cable: game.ts hides and doesn't simulate the rope in station rooms. The receiver cable 'route' is a two-state lever on the bench. There is no room obstacle (`obstacles:[]`), no designed chaos shortcut beyond throwing the cart, and all three bonuses are bench metrics (reliable, elegant, no failed log). Nothing in the room is worth chasing. The noise source for jobs 2 and 3 (the 'dome motor whine') has no physical presence at all. The dome, telescope and gallery are scenery the player never uses. Against AGENTS 4 and 5 this is the biggest fun gap in the room. R4A proposed the 'Noisy Neighbours' redesign (the real cable is the receiver line, plus clip-on cans and whips carried up the mast), and none of it is built. Breaks DR-01, DR-05, DR-10 and DR-26.

*qfn-play* — **After the first ~5 s the 120-prop room is only a backdrop: no cable, no chaos route, no physical bonus.** The whole room phase is spawn → crate (2.3 m, about 1 s) → bench (about 10 m, about 2 s). s2 timing: crate grabbed at t=1.0, crate on the bench at t=3.2, seated at t=5.3. After that the whole job (three boards, about 40 inputs) happens at the bench camera. There's no cable in the room: it's hidden and not simulated in station rooms (src/game.ts:92, :104), even though the level declares anchor (-10,6) and length 10 (src/levels/qfn.ts:22). All three bonuses are bench metrics (station.ts:74-77). obstacles is []. The pick-and-place, reflow oven and AOI along the back wall (room.ts:347-366) are scenery the job never touches. Shipped boards appear as flat slabs on the side table (station.ts:296-297) that nobody carries anywhere. Review 4 (DESIGN_A §2) said 'after the crate the room contributes nothing', and it is still true. It fails the cable-is-the-star rule, the chaos-route rule and the bonus-in-world rule.

*spectrum-play* — **No cable anywhere in the room, and the slingshot doesn't exist here.** AGENTS 4 makes the cable the star of every room. Spectrum has a level `anchor` and `length:10` (levels/spectrum.ts:32), but station rooms neither simulate nor draw the cable (game.ts:104 and :348 skip simulateCable when a station exists). No cable is visible in any of my shots, and snap().rope stays {length:0, maxLength:10}. There is no drag, route, wrap, plug or slingshot act; the closest stand-in is the drawn beam, which can't be grabbed.

*spectrum-play* — **No chaos route and no chaos bonus; the only physical horseplay (throwing the pod) is punished.** **No chaos goals.** All three bonuses are tidy ones: 'Every delivery reliable', 'Elegant: least power, fewest mirrors', 'No failed send' (station.ts:94-97). Nothing in the room rewards slapstick, and there is no absurd shortcut.

**Thrown pod is ignored.** A pod thrown over the brick wall or onto a pad isn't accepted, because station.dropped() only runs on an E-drop (game.ts interact).

**Chaos is costly.** Throwing the pod once on the open floor marked it damaged: snap went from damage 0, cost 0 to damage 1, cost 30 (shot 51 HUD). The station's own limits are damage 1 and cost ceil(4×1.25)=5 (station.ts:60, :82), so one playful throw blows the cost axis by 6×. Only 'best of three' plus a 540 s time limit hides it.

**What works.** Coworkers do react: a thrown plant next to the tea coworker raised alarmed=2 within 0.2 s (shot 65), and that is good. But nothing invites the player to cause it.

**Fix.**

*From progression:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The proposed gate `this.station&&!this.level.length` does not work: every station level already sets `length:10` (arcade.ts:26, garage.ts:28, qfn.ts:22, observatory.ts:22, spectrum.ts:32), so that check would turn the rope on in all stations at once with a meaningless anchor at (-10,6). Add an explicit Level flag (for example `cable:true`, or a `stationCable:{anchor,length,target}` block) and gate src/game.ts:92/:104/:348 on it. Set real anchors, lengths and obstacles per room as each cable act is built.

Reviewer's fix: Give every station one real room cable act that feeds the bench, using the existing rope sim. Allow `station` levels to set `length>0` and keep the cable when they do (src/game.ts:92/104/348 checks become `this.station&&!this.level.length`). Per room, with a reel anchor and obstacles in src/levels/&lt;id>.ts:
- Arcade: the bench is dead until Pip drags the bench's mains lead (14 m) from the wall socket across the busy hall. After each fix, the cabinet's own plug must be plugged back in, so fling-able beanbags and cones are on the route.
- Garage: route the robot's charge lead from the pad to the test stand around the lifts.
- Observatory: the noisy motor cable is the cable the player reroutes. The bench already has 'ROUTE: PAST MOTOR', so make it a physical drag.
- QFN: carry the finished board on a reel cart to the reflow oven.
- Spectrum: the pod's feed cable limits how far the pod can go.
Add one chaos shortcut per room: an overstretched slingshot that knocks the storeroom shelf down and spills the tray onto the bench.

*From progression:* (1) Delete the 'Sit at the bench (E)' step from all five stations; the marker and the 'E Work at the bench' prompt already cover it. (2) Give each station one physical or chaos bonus with a target that is visible in the survey:
- Arcade: 'Knock the prize pyramid over with a thrown beanbag'.
- Garage: 'Ride the robot's route without touching it'.
- QFN: 'Stack the scrap boards'.
- Observatory: 'Roll the motor cart into the far wall'.
- Spectrum: 'Bounce the beam off three mirrors'.

Put these in each station's `bonuses` array. (3) Vary the room beat between sub-jobs, as spectrum does. For example, the arcade kid carries the fixed cabinet's plug away and Pip must re-seat it, and the garage robot needs a push back onto the stand after each test.

*From arcade-play:* 1. Chaos delivery: call `this.station?.dropped?.(p)` for a thrown prop when it comes to rest. In `Game.step`, track the thrown prop, and once its speed is under 0.3 m/s call `station.dropped`. Widen the arcade test to accept a tray resting on or within 1.2 m of the bench top (`q.y>.9 && |q.x−t.x|<2.3 && |q.z−t.z|<.9`). Add a 'basket!' cheer and a bonus: "Deliver the tray by throwing it".
2. Give the room one physical cable act. Each signed-off cabinet must be re-plugged with a short room cable from a floor strip at the back wall (the existing reel prop at (−7.6,6.2) becomes the job reel), or drag the serviced cabinet's lead to its back-wall spot. Either way the strain colours and slingshot reach the room. Alternatively hide F and Q on the action bar in station rooms (src/ui) so there is no false affordance.
3. Add one chaos bonus target: knock the prize-shelf balls (room.ts:105) off with a thrown block, or bowl the cones (`cones` recipe) like the Playground pins.

*From arcade-rush-play:* Short term: in `src/ui/game-ui.ts` `updateActions()`, hide the F and Q action buttons (`el.hidden=true`) when `g.station||g.hub` has no cable. Design fix: give the bench a short power lead (for example 6 m) that Pip must plug into a wall socket at shift start. Reuse the playground rope with `level.length`, an anchor at the bench and a target socket on the back wall at (−3,−7.6). Strain colours show if Pip wanders, and a yank (slingshot) unplugs the bench as harmless chaos: the power drops and the kids groan, with no mistake counted.

*From garage-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** For the chaos shortcut, catch the robot in flight: in GarageBench.update(), if the un-held dynamic robot's horizontal distance to STAND is < 1.2 m while y < 1.6 (or on contact with the stand's collider), snap it with placeOnStand. Alternatively, scale the throw impulse down for items heavier than about 5 kg so a 3 m lob lands near the stand. A rest-distance check alone won't trigger.

Reviewer's fix: (1) Chaos shortcut: in GarageBench.update(), if the robot body is dynamic, not held, at rest (linvel < 0.3) and within 1.6 m of STAND, call the same placeOnStand path with a 'thunk' and dust burst, so a lob onto the rolling road works. Add a bonus: 'Land the robot on the stand from 3 m away'.
(2) Cable act: replace the static harness with a short real lead (Rope, about 4 m) that Pip drags from the stand's socket to the bench's harness port with F. It is finite and shows strain, and the robot isn't 'wired' until it's plugged in. For job 3, the star ground could be Pip dragging the controller's ground lead to the battery post (R4B redesign).
(3) Delivery bonus: 'The robot delivers without bumping a parcel', or the reverse, 'bowl over the parcel stack at (−10, −3.2) on its route'. Place the parcels on the lane on purpose.

*From observatory-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Same direction, with correct anchors: rack RX at room.ts:16/:80, dome pier solid at room.ts:68. Whether the global rope is re-enabled for one station is an architecture choice, because every station hides it (game.ts:92). Gate it behind a per-level flag as proposed, so other stations are unaffected.

Reviewer's fix: Minimum viable version:
(1) Turn on the real rope in this room. In game.ts:92/104, let a level opt in (`level.cable:true`) and anchor it at the receiver rack (room.ts RX, -3.25,-2.45), with its plug at the bench's RECEIVER jack (0-0.88,1.1,-2.15). Replace the route lever with the rope's actual path: compute `rerouted` from the minimum `segmentDistance` between rope points and the cart and the dome motor (sim/cable.ts), so dragging the cable around the dome pier (solid at room.ts:453) lowers the noise live.
(2) Give the dome motor a body: a red drum on the dome rim at (dx+2.2,1.2,dz) with a spinning fan and sparks while jobs 2 and 3 run (reuse buildMotor()).
(3) Add one chaos bonus to station.ts:88-91, e.g. 'Fling the motor cart into the far corner (≥ 9 m)' or 'Knock the gust-flattened whip upright by throwing something at the mast', and mark its target in the survey.
(4) Add a room spec in tests/station-observatory.spec.ts that solves job 1 by dragging the rope clear (no lever).

*From qfn-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The oven-leg idea alone doesn't meet DR-05, because DR-05 needs a cable act. The test-lead variant (finite lead with strain and slingshot from a wall socket to J1 for a power-on test) should be the required part, not optional. The oven leg covers DR-01 and DR-10.

Reviewer's fix: Give each shipped board one physical leg in the room, using what is already modelled. On SHIP, the board pops out of the jig as a carryable id'd prop ('board1'…'board3', small MASK-green slab). Pip carries it to the reflow oven's in-conveyor (1.8-2.55, z -6.9) or throws it on (that's the chaos shortcut, and it always succeeds if it lands on the conveyor). The oven's windows pulse, and the board comes out by the AOI, whose screen shows a green tick. Make 'Ship' a goal: the step text becomes 'Board 2 baked'. Add a bonus 'Toss a board straight onto the oven belt'. Optional cable beat: the bench's test lead (finite 6 m) has to be dragged from a wall socket to the board's J1 for the power-on test, which gives the room a short cable with strain and slingshot.

*From spectrum-play:* Give the room one physical lead that matters, without changing the teaching:
- **Option A:** the transmitter tower's power or coax lead is a real reel (anchor at the storeroom side wall, about 10 m). Pip drags it from a floor box to the tower base at the start (step 0 'Power up the tower'). Its strain colours and wrap round the desk are visible, and an overstretch plus Q slingshot can fling the cones and crates by the tea corner.
- **Option B:** the pod is tethered to a long data lead, so carrying it to the quiet room means routing a finite cable round the desk and tower.

Either way, enable the rope in game.ts for this station (a `station.cable?:true` flag) and draw it with the existing rope renderer.

*From spectrum-play:* Add one truthful chaos shortcut and a matching bonus:
- **Smoke shortcut:** knock the smoking toaster off the tea counter (throw a prop at it, or shove the counter). The smoke stops, so SMOKE loss becomes 0 for the rest of the run, and visible or near-IR then work for Delivery 3.
- **Pod lob:** accept a pod that comes to rest within 0.9 m of the current pad after a throw. Hook a check in station.update() for `pod.lastSpeed<.2 && dist(pod,pad)<.9 && !held`, then park it. Bonus: 'Lob the pod onto a pad'.
- **Pod damage:** exempt the pod and mirrors (id'd job items) from prefab damage cost, or cap their cost at 2.
- **Cost axis:** separate breakage from send energy so the 5-credit energy axis isn't dominated by room breakage. For example, limits.cost = energy budget + 60 breakage, or grade energy separately.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *progression:* `snap().rope.maxLength>0` and the cable is visible in the start shot of every station level (DR-05 check). Add one spec per station that reaches `won` using a cable act, plus a slingshot spec that moves a prop more than 1 m.
- *progression:* Each station's `job.bonuses` contains at least one bonus whose `ok()` reads room physics (prop positions or velocities). A scripted chaos spec earns it. The survey shot shows its target.
- *arcade-play:* New spec 'arcade: throwing the tray onto the bench delivers it' (walk to (0.4,0.3), Q, advance 2 → `trayReady` true). A survey shot shows the chaos target. `snapshot().rope.maxLength>0` and the cable is visible, or the action bar hides F/Q at `level.station`.
- *arcade-rush-play:* Start shot: no F or Q button in a station room (or a visible bench lead). If the lead is built, `snap().rope.maxLength>0` and the cable is drawn at the game camera.
- *garage-play:* New spec 'robot garage: throw the robot onto the stand': hold robot, face the stand at 2.5 m, press KeyQ, advance(2), expect station.onStand true. Check snapshot().rope.maxLength > 0 and that a cable is visible at the game camera.
- *observatory-play:* snapshot().rope.maxLength > 0 in observatory. A new spec reaches won with the cable dragged around the dome and no `route` act. Survey shot (observatory-play-02) shows the cable from rack to bench.
- *qfn-play:* Spec: after ship(), a 'board1' item exists; throw it at (1.8,-6.3) and expect the step to complete. Survey shot shows the board on the conveyor. snap().rope.maxLength>0 with a visible cable if the test-lead variant is chosen.
- *spectrum-play:* snap().rope.maxLength > 0, and a cable is visible at the game camera in the start shot. A scripted overstretch plus Q moves at least one prop more than 1 m (DR-06).
- *spectrum-play:* New spec 'spectrum chaos': knock the toaster down, then deliver job 3 on visible light to reach won===true. A pod lobbed onto the storeroom pad parks it (podPad==='store'). The bonus list shows a chaos bonus. A run with one thrown pod still grades A on cost.

**Rules:** AGENTS 3, AGENTS 4, AGENTS 5, AGENTS 6, DR-01, DR-02, DR-03, DR-05, DR-06, DR-10, DR-19, DR-26

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — src/game.ts:92 hides the plug, target, socket and anchor when station||hub. :104 runs simulateCable and drawCable only for non-station levels, and :348 skips the cable sim for stations. Every station level has obstacles:[] (arcade.ts:26, garage.ts:28, qfn.ts:22, observatory.ts:22, spectrum.ts:32). My runs reached the bench at 6.6 s in the garage and 6.7 s in the arcade, so the room part is a few seconds of carrying. (9/9 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-080

**R5-080 | P1 | arcade, arcade-rush, global | fun | Arcade: the play-test kid, the TILT marquee, the lit cabinet and the confetti — the success moment — are all outside the bench camera**

Found by: `arcade-play#3` (P1 fun), `arcade-rush-play#6` (P1 fun), `arcade-rush-teach#10` (P1 teaching), `arcade-teach#10` (P1 fun), `camera-render#8` (P2 clarity). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*arcade-play* — **The payoff is off-camera: the play-test kid, the cabinet's TILT marquee and lamp, and the back-wall cabinets lighting up are never in the bench view, and the bench camera can't be orbited.** The design's feedback loop is:
- "a kid plays each cabinet for 3 s" and hops, cheers or slumps;
- the serviced cabinet's marquee flashes TILT! on a trip;
- its lamp glows in the LED colour;
- the five broken cabinets on the back wall light up as each one is signed off.

None of this is in the bench frame:
- The serviced cabinet and kid stand at `t.x+OX-2.75`, about x −2.95 (station.ts:215). The bench camera (distance 5.9, pitch 0.98, FOV 30) frames about x −2.7…2.3. Only a sliver of the kid's hair and one arm shows at the left edge (crop of shot 22).
- `room.light()` fires on the back wall, behind and above the monitor, also out of frame.
- The bench camera ignores right-drag: yaw snaps back to `want` every frame (game.ts:372), and wheel zoom is disabled at the bench (game.ts:175). Shot 92, after orbit(−400): identical framing.

So during the 3 s play test the player stares at a purple progress bar. On sign-off they get a toast and a bell. The only laugh R4B found (TILT) is now invisible.

From the room camera (standing up mid-test, shots 40/41) the kid is a tiny shape hidden behind the bench head and marker. It is still a realistic human child (orange shirt, skin-tone sphere head, brown hair: station.ts:225-231), which breaks DR-60's blob-only cast.

For a Good Job-style game the success beat is the reward. Here it happens off-screen five times.

*arcade-rush-play* — **The success moment is invisible from the bench: confetti, the lit cabinet and the cheering kid are all outside the bench camera.** Signing off a cabinet is the payoff of every 5-second rush loop, and from the bench view nothing physical happens.
- `cheer()` spawns the confetti 1.8 m behind the table, at about y 2.4, which is above and behind the meter and out of frame.
- `room.light()` relights a cabinet on the back wall, out of frame.
- The serviced cabinet and the play-test kid stand at x ≈ −2.95, off the left edge of the bench camera. Only a dark pink sliver shows.

So the kid's hop during the play test and the cheer when it passes, which were built as the station's main reaction, are never seen while working. At +0.1 s and +0.5 s after sign-off the frame shows only a toast ('Dance: Elegant ★') and a reset board. Rush repeats this 10–30 times, and each completion lands as a text pill. This breaks DR-11 (juicy success with flash, sound and hitstop, the machine in frame) and DR-47 (the device shows its state on itself).

*arcade-rush-teach* — **The success consequence is off-screen: the play-test kid and the cabinet lamp sit outside the bench camera.** The design says a kid plays each cabinet while it runs in spec, hopping, cheering or slumping, and the cabinet's lamp, screen and 'TILT!' marquee react. All of these live on the serviced cabinet at the bench's left end (x = table − 2.95). The bench camera (distance 5.9, pitch 0.98) frames only the bins, board, meter and lever. In every bench screenshot only a sliver of pink cabinet shows at the far left edge. The kid and the TILT marquee are never seen. In rush the player spends nearly the whole shift at the bench, so success and failure appear only as a meter bar and a toast. The 'show it in the world' half of the lesson is missing.

*arcade-teach* — **The play-test kid, the room's only 'it works' character beat, is off-screen in the bench view.** The success loop is 'a kid plays the cabinet while it runs in spec' (station.ts:7, :225-232, :427-431). The kid hops, mashes buttons and cheers with arms up when the test passes, and slumps at a dark screen. The serviced cabinet and the kid stand at the bench's left end, t.x+OX−2.75 (station.ts:215). The bench camera (view distance 5.9, pitch 0.98, station.ts:80) frames only the bench. In arcade-teach-06/-07 (play test running and passed) only a sliver of the pink cabinet shows at the left edge, and no kid. They appear only after standing up with Esc (arcade-teach-32, -33). So the reward reaches the player as a purple progress bar and the text 'PLAY TEST PASSED ✓'. The cabinet's marquee lamp and screen, which react to the LED (station.ts:409, :426), are out of frame too, and so is the slump on failure. This loses the in-world consequence DR-28 and DR-47 call for, and the fun beat DR-11 asks for.

*camera-render* — **The bench camera frames the tabletop only, so the Arcade play-test happens off-screen (cabinet and kid cut at the left edge).** The arcade bench view (distance 5.9, pitch 0.98, lookY 0.3; src/stations/arcade/station.ts:80) centres the chain board. The cabinet being fixed sits at the bench's left end and shows only as a pink sliver at x 0–50 px (camera-render-ar-30-bench.jpg).

During the 3 s 'PLAY TEST 1.1/3 s' the kid plays that cabinet, and its light-up is the in-world proof the fix worked. The player sees neither (arcade-models-38-bench-running.jpg); only the monitor bar moves. Orbit and wheel are locked at the bench (bench.mjs shows the camera unchanged after a 300 px drag and an 800 wheel), so the player can't look either.

In the garage, the test stand where the robot sits during PULSE is half under the right job card (camera-render-ga-30-bench.jpg). This undercuts DR-28 and DR-47 (show the effect in the world, on the device) and AGENTS 2 (play by doing, not reading).

**Fix.**

*From arcade-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The fix is sound. One check: if the serviced cabinet moves to about (t.x+OX−1.55, t.z−1.25), its fixed collider at station.ts:224 and the kid's at :232 must move with it, and it must not overlap the back-row bins (world x≈−1.7, z≈−2.5) in the bench frame. Verify by retaking the bench shot.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Bring the play test into frame:
   - Move the serviced cabinet to the bench's back-left corner, facing the camera: `group(root,t.x+OX-1.55,0,t.z-1.25,0)`, 0.8× scale. Its screen and marquee then sit above the bins, in frame.
   - Or add a picture-in-picture: render a 320×200 inset from a second camera aimed at the kid while `soak>0`.
   - Stand the kid (as a small blob with a cap, `blob()` from render/actors, not a human) on a step between the cabinet and the bench, at about x −1.9.
2. While soaking, have the cabinet screen animate (scrolling `hot()` colours) and play chiptune blips.
3. On sign-off, do a 1.2 s camera beat:
   - lerp `view.lookX` toward the back-wall cabinet that just lit (room.ts:122) with a 0.15 s hitstop, then return;
   - or set `this.game.focus` to `m.at` for 1 s.
4. Allow ±0.6 rad of bench yaw from right-drag (keep `want` as the rest yaw, spring back after release) so players can look left.

*From arcade-rush-play:* Bring the cabinet into the bench shot. Either move the serviced cabinet and the kid to stand behind the meter at the back-left of the bench (x ≈ −1.6, z ≈ −3.4), or set `view.lookX=-.55` and `distance 6.4` so the cabinet's screen and the kid show at the left of the frame. On sign-off:
- burst confetti from the cabinet marquee (inside the frame);
- flash the marquee white for 80 ms and add a 0.06 s hitstop (`game.timeScale`);
- pop the kid up with arms raised and a ★ bubble;
- fly a ticket sprite into a 'FIXED n' counter on the marquee.

Keep the toast as secondary feedback.

*From arcade-rush-teach:* Bring the cabinet into frame. Either move it to sit behind the bins at about (t.x+OX−1.9, t.z−.9) facing the camera, with the kid on its front side, or widen the bench view (`view={distance:6.8,pitch:.9,lookY:.35}`) and shift the bench contents right (OX=.15). The marquee, cabinet lamp and kid should all be inside the frame at 1440×900. Keep the toast area clear of them.

*From arcade-teach:* Move the serviced cabinet into the bench frame. Either place it behind the bins at the bench's back-left, at about group(game.root, t.x+OX−1.6, 0, t.z−1.25, .25) with the kid facing it at +z, so the marquee, screen and kid sit above the bins in the station view. Or widen the view (distance 6.6, lookY .45, a little left) so the existing cabinet fits.

Move its solid() colliders to match, and check the cabinet doesn't hide the meter.

Keep the purple soak bar, but make the kid's cheer the main signal, with a speech bubble 'Again!' at soakDone.

*From camera-render:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep the arcade soak camera ease (lookX about -1.8, distance about 7.2, pitch about 0.85, only while the soak runs). Drop the garage lookX/card change: the stand is not covered.

Reviewer's fix: Add `view.soak?:{lookX:number;distance:number;pitch:number}` to stations. While the arcade soak runs (`HOUSE.soak`), ease the bench camera to lookX -1.8, distance 7.2, pitch 0.85, so the cabinet's screen and the kid sit in the left third with the board still visible. Ease back afterwards.

### R5-081

**R5-081 | P1 | global, playground, meeting | fun | "Q Let go to slingshot" shows at strain 0.97 when the cable has no energy (nothing slingshots below ~1.007), so Q does nothing and the sprint chaos route is undiscoverable**

Found by: `cable#0` (P1 fun), `playground-play#13` (P2 playability), `meeting-play#10` (P1 fun). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*cable* — **The 'Q Let go to slingshot' prompt shows when the cable has no energy, so pressing Q does nothing.** The prompt 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable' and the lit Q action button appear whenever rope.strain > 0.97 (src/ui/objectives.ts:79, src/ui/game-ui.ts:200). The slingshot's energy is a different number: energy = max(0, length − maxLength)² × 60 (src/sim/cable.ts:71). releasePlug only flings when energy > 1 (src/game.ts:259-261), which needs more than 0.13 m of overstretch (strain > 1.007 on the 19 m reel). The reel's spring force (cable.ts:78) then pulls Pip back to exactly maxLength within about 0.5 s of stopping, so the energy goes to 0 while the prompt stays on.

Measured:
- pg3 'idle': strain 1.045 after a sprint, then 0.7 s standing gives strain 1.0001. The prompt still says slingshot. Q gives fastestProp 0.02 and no pins move.
- pg2: the same thing after a 1.6 s camera zoom. Cable-24 shows nothing happened.
- Meeting mt4: the walk limit gives strain 1.022, then 1 s standing gives 1.000, Pip pulled 0.5 m back. The prompt reads 'Let go to slingshot the cable' (cable-113). Q or F only drops the plug.

The slingshot only works if the player presses Q while still holding sprint into the cable ('held' run: fastestProp 53.8). Nothing teaches that. A player who reads the prompt, stops and presses Q gets a thud. This is the game's signature cable moment (AGENTS 4), and the only text hint for it is wrong. It is a false prompt (DR-19) and makes the slingshot effectively undiscoverable (DR-06, R4B M9 still open).

*playground-play* — **'Q Let go to slingshot' shows at strain 0.97, but nothing slingshots below about 1.007.** The prompt and the Q button's 'ready' glow turn on at strain >0.97 (src/ui/objectives.ts:79, src/ui/game-ui.ts throw.ready). Rope energy is (length−max)²×60 (src/sim/cable.ts:70), and releasePlug only slingshots when energy>1 (src/game.ts:261), which needs about 0.13 m of overstretch: strain ≈1.007 on the 19 m reel. Between 0.97 and 1.007 (e.g. the 'aim-around' run reached 0.998 and showed the prompt), Q just drops the plug with a thud. The prompt promises an action the key does not perform (DR-19).

*meeting-play* — **The sprint-overstretch chaos route is undiscoverable: at the walking stall the prompt says 'Q Let go to slingshot', which throws the plug away, instead of hinting that sprinting stretches further.** Walking with the single 23.2 m reel, Pip stalls at x≈10.0, z -1.6 with strain 1.02. That is 1.73 m from the snap zone, which needs <1.6 (shots 15, 16), so the target ring is right there. The only prompt is 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable'. Doing that (or pressing F, which also calls releasePlug) flings the plug back toward the last bend, wasting the walk.
Nothing in the world or HUD suggests holding Shift. Sprinting is the secret that gets the extra 0.4 m and makes the 'Plug in' prompt appear (shot 17, strain 1.04). This is the room's best chaos beat: the cable goes red, coworkers duck with '!' bubbles, chairs drag (shots 17, 68). Most players will never find it, or will find it only by accident. R4B M9 is still PARTIAL.
This breaks DR-37 (range tricks such as sprinting to overstretch get a visible hint) and DR-06 (the slingshot is discoverable, with a reward in reach). It also undermines DR-01, which needs the chaos route to be playable, not just scripted.

**Evidence.**

- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:200`
