**Fix.**

*From cable:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The charge idea is workable, but its arithmetic doesn't match its claim. With charge += dt*40*(strain-0.9), standing at strain 1.0 adds 4 per second, so the threshold of 8 is reached after about 2 s, not about 1 s. It also invents energy that the rope model says isn't there: at rest the spring force is 0. A simpler fix that is truthful at this level: (1) Show the Q prompt and light the Q button only when rope.energy > 1, i.e. while Pip is actually pulling past the length (over > 0.13 m). Otherwise keep 'F Drop the plug', or better, show no text and let Pip lean and dig in. (2) Keep a short grace window in Rope: peak = max(peak*exp(-dt/0.35), energy), and have release() return peak. Then letting go of W and pressing Q within about 0.3 s still flings. (3) Optional: while strain > .97 and energy < 1, pulse the reel icon to say 'pull harder' with no words. Verify: v1.mjs 'stand0.3' shows no slingshot prompt, and 'walkW' plus Q still gives fastestProp > 2.

Reviewer's fix: Make the stored charge, not the instantaneous stretch, drive both the prompt and the fling.

1. In `Rope` (src/sim/cable.ts), add a `charge` field. Each update while strain > 0.97: `charge = min(60, charge + dt*40*(strain-0.9))`. Otherwise: `charge *= exp(-dt/1.2)`.
2. Make `release()` return `max(energy, charge)` and reset both.
3. Show the Q prompt and light the Q button only when `charge > 8` (expose `rope.charge` in the snapshot).
4. Add a visible wind-up: the strain-HUD reel icon pulses, and the twang arcs (game.ts:299) grow with charge.

Result: standing at the limit 'loads' the cable within about 1 s, and Q always delivers once the prompt shows.

*From playground-play:* Gate the prompt and button on g.rope.energy>1 (or strain>1+0.13/maxLength) instead of strain>.97. Keep the red colour and jitter at 0.97 as a warning.

*From meeting-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Lead with world cues, not text. At a walking stall within 4 m of the target, Pip leans into the pull with skidding boots and dust, the plug end strains toward the ring, and the ring pulses. Pressing F there gives a 'so close' wobble (with the snap distance widened to about 1.8 m for the feedback check) instead of releasing the plug. Show a Shift key glyph on the sprint slot of the action bar only after a failed F at the stall, rather than as a sentence in the prompt pill.

Reviewer's fix: In promptFor, when holdingPlug && strain>0.97 && !g.extension && dist(plug, target) < 4, return {key:'Shift', text:'Sprint to stretch it'} (the action bar already has the slot style for keys). Otherwise keep the slingshot prompt. In drawCable, add a visual: when stalled at a strain of 0.97–1.05 and not sprinting, pulse the hose's last metre and puff dust at Pip's feet as the boots skid (Pip leaning forward in the rig). Optionally widen the forgiving snap for the overstretched cable to 1.8 m, so a walking player who presses F gets a 'so close' wobble rather than a slingshot.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *cable:* Add a routes.spec test, 'standing at the limit then Q still slingshots': pick up the plug, walk(9,3.7), advance(2.5, [KeyW, ShiftLeft]), then advance(1) with no keys, press Q, advance(0.05). Expect fastestProp > 2. A second assert: when the prompt text contains 'slingshot', Q always yields fastestProp > 2. Retake cable-22/23/24.
- *playground-play:* At strain 0.98 the prompt reads 'F Drop the plug'; at 1.02 it reads the slingshot line, and Q moves a prop (fastestProp>2).
- *meeting-play:* Rerun s2.mjs. At 'walk D strain 1.02' the prompt must name Shift/sprint (shot 15). Add a test to tests/objectives.spec.ts: at the stall, expect .prompt-pill to contain 'Sprint'.

**Rules:** AGENTS 4, DR-01, DR-06, DR-19, DR-37

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced it in mockups/review5/tools/verify-cable/v1.mjs (Playground). I picked up the plug, walked to (9,3.7) and sprinted for 2.5 s, which gave strain 1.0446 and energy 43.1. After standing still for 0.6 s, strain was 1.0006 and energy 0.01, but the pill still read 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable' and the Q button was lit (verify-cable-01-stand-limit-prompt.jpg). (3/3 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-082

**R5-082 | P1 | garage | fun | Garage: the robot's reboot (red eyes, dizzy wobble) faces away from the bench camera, edge-on exactly when it matters**

Found by: `garage-play#7` (P1 fun), `garage-models#4` (P2 clarity), `garage-teach#9` (P2 clarity). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*garage-play* — **The robot's reboot (red eyes, dizzy wobble) faces away from the bench camera, and failure and pass moments are barely visible.** The failure gag is the robot's controller rebooting: red eyes, a dizzy wobble and stars (station.ts:384, 376). The face and eyes are on the head's +x side (room.ts:57-58), and placeOnStand sets an identity rotation (station.ts:340). From the bench camera, which looks down −z, you see the robot's flank. The eyes are not visible; only the small antenna lamp turns orange-red, and the wobble is a few pixels (crops 79, 80). The star burst is 6 'star' particles at the robot's top. In the room view after standing up, the event is a tiny glow (shot 82). The nearest coworker is 5.3 m from the bench, so game.alarm({table},3) on a fuse trip (station.ts:238) reaches no one: the bang has no audience. Passing a TEST gives a small 'Elegant' toast (shot 21), and cheer() bursts 12 confetti 1.8 m behind the table, out of frame. The most entertaining beats in the room are mostly lost. This breaks DR-47 (the device shows its state readably), DR-28 (failure shows its cause in the world first) and DR-11/DR-04 (juicy moments, the world reacts).

*garage-models* — **Robot faces away from the bench camera: the reboot cue (red eyes) is edge-on exactly when it matters.** placeOnStand() sets the robot's rotation to identity (station.ts:340). robotMesh's face (screen and eyes) is at local +x (room.ts:57-58), so on the stand the face points +x, to the right. The bench camera looks along -z from the +z side, so the player sees the robot's left flank: cargo bin, head side and two wheels (garage-models-54-bench-view, -56-bench-arc, -57).

When the controller reboots, the eyes turn red and the robot wobbles (station.ts reboot() and the eye-material swap in update). That is the in-world failure cue at the faulty part (DR-28, DR-47), and from the bench only a 5 px antenna bead shows it (red dot at about (895,170) in -57). The face's 'personality' is also never seen at the bench.

Parked on the pads, all robots have rotation π/2 (garage.ts:8, room.ts:87), so their faces point at the back wall. At the default game camera the player only ever sees the robots' backsides (garage-models-01-start, -10). The face reads only when orbiting 180° (-11, -23) or while driving (-76).

*garage-teach* — **The reboot consequence happens off-face: the robot's eyes face sideways and the reboot stars sit behind the TEST STAND sign.** Both reset faults (stop spike and start sag) are meant to *show* the controller rebooting: red eyes, a dizzy wobble and stars over the robot (station.ts:384, :376).

- The robot sits on the stand with identity rotation and front = +x (room.ts:44, `placeOnStand` station.ts:340), so from the bench camera its face screen and eyes are edge-on and out of view.
- The stars burst at y+0.9 over the head, but the TEST STAND plaque (room.ts:78, y 0.9) sits right there from the bench angle.

In `garage-teach-44-crop-robot-reboot.jpg` and `garage-teach-07`, the only visible cue is a tiny red antenna bead and the controller's 35 mm lamp turning orange; the stars are clipped behind the sign. The wobble is subtle at 6.8 m. The player must read the scope ('RESET at shutdown!') or the toast to learn what happened, which breaks DR-28 (the world first) and DR-47 (state on the device).

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *garage-models:* Retake garage-models-56/57 (PULSE with nothing fitted). Both red eyes must be visible and ≥8 px each in the bench view. Retake garage-models-01-start: the robot faces (eyes) are visible from the default yaw.
- *garage-teach:* Retake the reboot frames (`garage-teach-07` and `-22`) from the bench camera with the HUD hidden via `g.page` CSS. A first-time viewer can tell the robot rebooted without the scope or toast.

The nearest NPC (−3.6, −6.3) is 5.27 m from the table, and game.alarm radius is 3 (station.ts:225, 238), so nobody reacts. (3/3 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-083

**R5-083 | P1 | playground | fun | Playground bowling "pins" are white traffic cones that fall when Pip walks into them, so the slingshot strike bonus comes free**

Found by: `playground-models#6` (P1 fun), `playground-play#7` (P1 fun), `props-gallery#13` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*playground-models* — **The bowling pins fall when Pip just walks into them, so the slingshot bonus comes free; they also read as white cones.** The pins exist to give the slingshot a reward (R4B, P4). But they are ordinary 'cone' props (mass 1, a 0.5×0.62×0.5 box collider), and Pip's character controller pushes dynamic bodies (setApplyImpulsesToDynamicBodies). Walking to (3.6,4.6) bowled all six. The confetti burst fired and the 'Knock down all six pins' star lit at 0:19 without the cable ever being touched (shot -33: three stars, confetti, pins scattered). The signature chaos toy is short-circuited by walking.
Visually, each pin is a traffic cone with a square base plate, recoloured #fffaf0. Its stripe band (#fff6e6) disappears on white, so the six read as white cones, meringues or soft-serve swirls (shot -30), not bowling pins. They also sit only about 20 luma above the 205-luma floor (pins 225), against the ≥25 target. With their square bases the six pins tile into a grid.

*playground-play* — **The pins are hard to slingshot on purpose but trivial to walk through, so the strike rewards walking, not the cable.** The pins (src/levels/playground.ts:18) sit in a cleared lane at x 4.4–5.5, z 4.7–5.9. slingshot() (src/game.ts:255-258) only flings props within 1.1 m of the rope polyline, and pushes them radially away from the reel. In testing: the spec slingshot flung the crate row but knocked down 0 pins (c-chaos 1). Overstretching south from (9,3.7), and south-east from (8.6,6.6), also knocked down 0 pins (d-wrong pins S/SD). A deliberate loop south of the pins and back up the east side, then a sprint and Q, knocked all 6 (f-aim 'behind'), but nothing in the scene suggests that loop. Meanwhile, walking or dragging the cable along the lane to (9,5.2) knocked all 6 on the way (d-wrong 'frontlane', pins 6 on arrival), and walking through the triangle knocked 3 (shot 28). pinsDown also counts a pin that only slid 0.5 m (game.ts:252-253). The bonus meant to showcase the slingshot (PROGRESS 'pins to fling at') is earned by bumping into it.

*props-gallery* — **Playground bowling "pins" are white traffic cones on square plates: low contrast on the pale floor, with a stepped collar.** The six Playground pins are `cone` props recoloured `#fffaf0` (playground.ts:18). Pins are the room's designed chaos bonus ("knock down all six pins") and the slingshot's reward target (DR-06, DR-10), but the model reads as white traffic cones: a square 0.5 m base plate plus a cone. The cone's reflective band is a separate `cyl(.12,.15,.1)` that is wider than the cone at that height, so it shows as a stepped collar (prefabs.ts:139, `props-gallery-10-sheet12-cone-strip.jpg`). On white the band vanishes. White on the about-200-luma Playground floor gives very little contrast at the game camera (`props-gallery-61-playground-pins-close.jpg`, `-41-playground-survey.png`). The square box collider also means a pin must tip a full 45° about a plate edge to count as down, unlike a real round-based pin.

### R5-084

**R5-084 | P1 | global, observatory, qfn | fun | In station rooms, room chaos is graded on the bench's tiny mistake and parts-credit scales (one knocked chair = Cost D; prop dollars mixed with parts credits)**

Found by: `progression#3` (P2 fun), `observatory-play#7` (P1 fun), `qfn-play#3` (P2 fun). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*progression* — **In station rooms, room chaos is graded on the bench's tiny mistake and parts-credit scales: one knocked chair gives Cost D.** A knocked prop adds `damage++` and its prefab cost (src/game.ts:335), at room scale: chair 25, plant 15, monitor 130 (src/props/prefabs.ts:10-26). In station rooms, win() then adds the bench mistakes and parts credits to the same tallies (src/game.ts:353) and grades them all against the station's limits. Those limits are damage 1–2 mistakes and a cost equal to the parts budget × 1.25, a few credits: garage `cost:…*1.25*10/10` (src/stations/garage/station.ts:77), arcade `limits.cost=ceil(parts*1.25)` (arcade/station.ts:107). Measured: in the garage I knocked one chair before working the bench (0 bench mistakes, elegant parts on all three jobs), and the card shows **28 / D** for cost (`progression-38`, garage-chaos.mjs: `dmg 1 cost 27.8`). In the arcade one broken mug moved cost to B (15 vs a limit of about 13, `progression-29`). Room damage and failed bench tests also share the damage axis with a limit of 1–2, so two knocked mugs score the same as two blown fuses. The station rooms were filled with 80–150 clutter props to make them feel like Good Job floors, yet touching them is punished far harder than on the cable floors (limit 10/300). The message to the player is 'don't play with the room', the opposite of AGENTS 5. The card also mixes units: '28' coins is a chair's repair price added to 2.8 credits of diodes.

*observatory-play* — **Chaos with job items wrecks the damage and cost axes (prop dollars mixed with parts credits).** Station limits are {time:360, damage:1, cost:ceil(cheapest×1.25)=12}. The cost axis adds `game.cost`, the prop-damage cost from prefabs: cart 50, chair 25, monitor 130, desk 80. That sits on a scale 20–100× larger than the 1–3 credit filter parts the bench shows as 'Parts cost'. In my chaos run, throwing the motor cart (the room's only fun move, and a valid way to finish step 1), plus one knocked prop, put damage at 2 and cost at 53. That is a D on cost and B on damage. A single chair knocked over gives cost 25+9 = 34, which is C. The overall grade survives only because 'best of three' leans on the generous 360 s time limit. The result card still shows the player red-flagged axes for exactly the slapstick AGENTS 5 says must never be a fail. Failed LOG presses also count as damage (limit 1), so two experiments cost the damage A. Breaks DR-07 (each axis tuned per room), DR-02 (chaos never a failure) and DR-38 (experiments are learning, not damage).

*qfn-play* — **Room chaos and bench mistakes share a damage limit of 1 and a cost limit only 25% over track par, so one throw costs a grade.** QfnBench.limits = {time:720, damage:1, cost:ceil(Σpar×1.25)=124} (station.ts:51, :68). At the result, game.ts:353 adds the station score (board send-backs and track cost) to the room's game.damage and game.cost. Room damage comes from any prop that hits at more than 5.5 m/s (game.ts:335), and the crate itself counts. In s8 a single crate throw at a coworker showed damage 1 and cost 5 on the HUD, then damage 2 and cost 10 on the pause screen (qfn-play-90, -91). That already exceeds limits.damage=1, so the damage axis drops to B before the player has even sat down. A clean bench run costs 99 of the 124 cost budget, so knocking over one cart (cost 50) drops the cost axis to B. 'Damage' therefore means two different things (a broken mug and a board sent back from test) on one axis tuned for the bench alone. Pure wrecking is no worse than one layout mistake. The best-of-three overall hides it, but the per-axis medals on the result card read as a telling-off for chaos.

**Fix.**

*From progression:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Prefer the reviewer's 'cleaner option': grade the three Good Job axes at room scale (room time, breaks and repair coins, with a per-room `limits`), and express bench quality only through the existing tier and mistake bonus stars. The first option (damage limit = limits.damage+10) would make blown fuses almost free on the damage axis. If it is used, keep bench mistakes as a separate star rather than diluting them.

Reviewer's fix: Keep room chaos and bench quality on separate scales. In src/game.ts:353-354, grade stations as: damage = room breaks + bench mistakes, against `limits.damage + 10` (a room allowance as on the floors); cost = room cost + bench credits × 10 (show bench credits as coins), against `limits.cost*10 + 300`. A cleaner option: show the bench quality only through the tier stars (the bonuses already cover mistakes and elegance), and let the three Good Job axes stay room-level, with time, breaks and repair cost tuned like the floors. Either way, document the units in src/stations/types.ts.

*From observatory-play:* Separate the units in game.ts:353. For station rooms, grade cost on the station's parts credits only (`this.cost = s.cost` and keep prop damage on the damage axis), or scale prop cost into credits (`prefabs.cost/25`). Raise the station damage limit to ~5 so knocking a few props stays A. Count failed LOGs as a separate 'retries' stat shown on the result card, not damage (station.ts:195 `this.mistakes++` feeds damage via score()). Keep the 'No failed decode logged' star as the precision reward.

*From qfn-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Don't raise damage to 1+6. That would let 7 send-backs earn A and mix the two meanings again. Instead rank the damage axis as the worse of two separate ranks: room breakage against the cable-floor default (10) and bench send-backs against 1. Alternatively show them as two rows. Excluding prop.spec.id==='parts' from game.ts:335 is fine.

Reviewer's fix: Either keep the axes separate (grade room breakage with the floor's own rule and send-backs as 'mistakes'), or tune the limits for both: limits={time:720, damage:1+6, cost:ceil(par×1.25)+60}. Exclude the job item: in game.ts:335, skip the damage counter when prop.spec.id==='parts' (the crate is meant to be thrown). Show on the result card which axis earned the overall grade.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *observatory-play:* Re-run 08-chaos-grade2.mjs and read the result card. Cost row ≤ 12 (A) and damage A after one cart throw. Add a grade unit test for the station path.
- *qfn-play:* Rerun s8-alarm.mjs, then the clean solve. The result shows damage A after one crate throw plus a clean bench. A spec that wrecks 5 props and then solves cleanly still gets three A medals except damage B or better.

### R5-085

**R5-085 | P1 | arcade-rush, qfn | fun | The chaos shortcut is punished: a job item thrown onto the bench lands there but never counts as delivered (Arcade tray, QFN crate)**

Found by: `arcade-rush-play#8` (P1 fun), `qfn-play#1` (P1 fun). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*arcade-rush-play* — **The chaos shortcut is punished: a tray thrown onto the bench lands there but doesn't count, and it's graded as damage.** The only physical job act in Rush is carrying the resistor tray to the bench. The obvious Good Job shortcut is to throw it. I threw the tray (Q) from about 3 m away. It landed on the bench top at (−1.74, 1.07, −1.85), inside the 2.6 m acceptance radius of the table, but `trayReady` stayed false. `station.dropped()` is only called from the E-drop path in `interact()`, never on landing.

The throw also counted as damage: the HUD went to damage 1 and cost 10, because the job item hit the bench at more than 5.5 m/s. After the throw the card still says 'Carry the tray…' while the tray visibly sits on the bench. The prompt points at a nearby prop ('E Grab the paper'), not the tray, so a new player thinks the game is broken. Clean first and chaos second means the chaos route has to work too (DR-01), and chaos mustn't fail or cost the player (DR-02).

*qfn-play* — **Throwing the parts crate at the bench never delivers it, so the one chaos act in the room is ignored.** The only physical job in the Fabrication Bay is carrying the crate. The obvious Good Job move is to throw it (Q) at the bench. The throw path (src/game.ts:183) applies an impulse and never calls station.dropped(). Only the E put-down path calls it (src/game.ts:210 → station.ts:378-383). In s3 the crate landed at (1.84, 0.62), 2.15 m from the stand, which is inside the 2.2 m accept radius, but partsReady stayed false. The prompt then switched to 'E Grab the bin' because the crate was out of reach. A thrown crate that sails over the bench (s7 'bench-top' case) lands behind it next to the yellow cart, where the straight walk back fails. So the chaos shortcut is silently refused, and the player has to walk over, pick it up and put it down properly, which is the 'tidy' route. AGENTS 5 asks for chaos shortcuts second, never punished. Here chaos is ignored and costs time, and the throw also adds damage (see the grading finding).

Do not exempt all job items from impact damage in game.ts:335: that removes chaos cost across every room and works against DR-07. Reviewer's fix: In `ArcadeBench.update()`, while `!trayReady`, check every frame whether the tray body is within 2.6 m of `table`, its speed is under 0.6 m/s and it isn't held. If so, run the same acceptance as `dropped()`, plus a 'Nice throw!' confetti burst and the jingle. In `src/game.ts:335`, skip impact damage for props with `spec.id` (job items), or at least for 'blocks' landing on the bench. Also widen the side-table catch: make the side table's top a sensor that accepts the crate on contact, so a crate that lands on the bench top or side table counts.

### R5-086

**R5-086 | P1 | lunch | fun | Lunch: the cables are too long for length, strain or the slingshot to matter, so the crowd can never be hit**

Found by: `cable#6` (P1 fun), `gap6-world-reacts#3` (P2 fun). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*cable* — **In Lunch the cable's length almost never matters, and the slingshot and strain beats are unreachable.** Lunch's loose leads are 32, 30 and 32 m (thin) and 30 m (thick) (src/lunch-runtime.ts:61), in a room about 32 m wide.

- Sprinting thin-2 from Supply A along the corridor into the far north-east corner peaked at strain 0.963 (ln2 log; cable-131).
- Sprinting thin-1 east along the corridor reached 0.927 (ln1).
- Q then threw nothing (fastestProp 1.9, then 0).
- The thick cable slows Pip to 0.65× (game.ts:318), so it can't be sprint-overstretched either.

The Lunch-specific cable code also has none of the main cable's feel: no twang arcs, jitter or corner sparks (only Game.drawCable has them, game.ts:296-300), no hitstop, and no auto-whip off corners (game.ts:286).

So the third cable floor, the longest job, drops the 'finite length, strain, slingshot' pillar (AGENTS 4; DR-05, DR-06). Strain colours never appear in a normal solve, and the cables behave like free extension leads.

*gap6-world-reacts* — **Lunch's cables are too long to slingshot anywhere near the crowd, so the room's coworkers can never be hit by cable chaos.** The thin leads are 32/30/32 m and the thick lead 30 m (src/lunch-runtime.ts:61), in a 32 × 20 m floor. I picked up thin-1 at Supply A (−10.8,2), walked past the corridor crowd at (−3.8,9) and (−2.4,8.9), then sprinted east for 2 s. Strain only reached 0.77, with Pip at (10.8,5.9), the far side of the room (world-reacts-14). Q then just drops the end: release() only slingshots at energy>1 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:199-201), so alarmed stays 0, fastestProp is 0 and nothing flies (world-reacts-15). Sprinting with a live cable right past three seated coworkers drew no reaction either, because the taut-cable proximity alarm (src/game.ts:301) needs strain >0.9 and only runs for the main rope, not Lunch's cables. Lunch is the room with the biggest audience (9 blobs, a corridor queue), yet the signature act (AGENTS 4, DR-06) can't reach them, and the only reactions come from bot snags and breaker trips.

**Fix.**

*From cable:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The proposed lengths would break the intended solution. Thin-2 (A to conveyor through the door, about 21 m) at about 24 m is fine, and so is thick (about 17.6 m to the kitchen post) at about 20-22 m. Keep thin-1 at about 32 m, or reroute the lift feed in the spec.

Port the strain proximity alarm to Lunch: in lunch-runtime render, for each held cable with strain >0.85, alarm along its points at radius 2.2 every 0.7 s, as src/game.ts:301 does. Add a Lunch bonus such as 'Fling the lunch queue's trays' to give the slingshot a target (DR-10).

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

- *gap6-world-reacts:* Rerun mockups/review5/tools/world-reacts/chaos.mjs lunch. With the shortened lead, strain must exceed 1.02 in the corridor, Q must give fastestProp >2 and alarmed ≥2, and world-reacts-15 must show bubbles on the bench blobs.

**Rules:** AGENTS 4, DR-05, DR-06, DR-10

### R5-087

**R5-087 | P1 | global, garage | fun | Sign-off swaps in the next cabinet/board in the same frame, and the Garage logs a pass before the TEST cycles finish: no visual beat at the bench**

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#11` (P2 fun), `garage-teach#10` (P1 fun). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*gap4-juice-audio* — **Sign-off swaps in the next cabinet or board in the same frame, so there's no visual beat at the bench.** At sign-off (arcade/station.ts:271-278), the station records the verdict, fires cheer(), then on the same call:
- `index++`, powerOff();
- loads the next job's start setup;
- runs showJob().

juice-audio-15 was taken immediately after the arcade sign-off. The bench already shows cabinet 2 (RHYTHM, 3.3 V, 47 Ω), and the only trace of success is a small toast, 'Pinball bumper: Elegant ★'. The confetti goes off behind the table, out of the bench camera (shared.ts:11-15, which correctly fixes A10). The repaired cabinet lights up (`room.light`) off-screen.

The reward for each solved puzzle is invisible at the camera the player is using. The same immediate swap happens in the garage (station.ts:229), QFN (qfn:287) and observatory/spectrum (jobIndex++).

*garage-teach* — **A passing TEST is logged before the test plays: the board jumps to the next job while the five cycles are still running.** In the TEST branch (station.ts:223-231), a passing verdict is pushed to `logged`, `jobIndex++` runs and `capture=undefined` is set in the same frame the cycles start (`cycleT=0`).

In `garage-teach-15-j1-test-pass.jpg`, taken 1.5 s into the test:
- the scope already says 'Press PULSE';
- the panel already shows 'Job 2/3 · Stop at the line';
- the beads of the job 1 cycles are still running;
- the only reward is a small 'Elegant' toast.

The player never sees five clean stops on the scope or the robot passing its test. The certificate arrives before the evidence, which deflates the success moment (DR-11) and teaches 'TEST is a submit button'.

The cycle lamps exist (station.ts:179) but turn green only after the job has already moved on. The `cheer()` confetti is barely visible from the bench (none in the shot).

**Evidence.**

*From gap4-juice-audio:* Add a 1.0–1.2 s 'served' beat before loading the next job:
- keep the solved board lit, with the LED or load glowing and a green 'PASS ★' stamp on the monitor;
- bounce the tier medal in the station panel;
- add a .05 s hitstop;
- then slide the next board in.

In the arcade, briefly cut or pan to the cabinet lighting up (`room.light`), or show a picture-in-picture of it on the bench monitor.

*From garage-teach:* - **Defer the bookkeeping:** keep `logged.push` (for scoring) but delay `jobIndex++`, `capture=undefined` and the panel switch until the cycle animation finishes (`cycleT ≥ SPEC.cycles·0.6+0.4`). Do it in `update()` behind a `pendingAdvance` flag.
- **Show the passes while they run:**
  - the scope stacks the five stop traces overlaid, each in green with a ✓;
  - each cycle lamp pops green with a rising tone, one per cycle;
  - on the fifth, a stamp 'PASSED · RELIABLE / ELEGANT' slams onto the scope with a 60 ms hitstop;
  - the robot does a happy wheel-spin on the rollers.
- Only then switch to the next job's ask.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Rules:** DR-11, DR-28, DR-31

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — station.ts:226-230 pushes `logged`, increments jobIndex and clears `capture` in the same call that starts the cycle animation (cycleT=0 at :223). I reproduced it: in verify-garage-teach-07, 0.3 s after Enter on a passing job 1, the panel already reads 'JOB 2/3 · Stop at the line', the scope says 'Press PULSE' and the prompt says 'P Pulse the motor', while the job-1 cycles are still running. ### R5-088

**R5-088 | P1 | lunch | fun | Lunch failure is the quietest cue in the game: no audible fridge warning in 120 s, the burn warning is a slightly redder oven window**

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#6` (P1 fun), `lunch-play#17` (P2 clarity). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*gap4-juice-audio* — **Lunch's job-ending failure is the quietest cue in the game, the fridge never warns audibly across 120 s, and spoil and burn sound alike.** The fail sting at src/lunch-runtime.ts:285 is `tone(120,.7,.05,'triangle')`: peak gain .05 on a 120 Hz triangle, falling to 60 Hz. That is about the level of grabbing a mug (`pop()`: sine 320 at .05 plus triangle 520 at .03), quieter than a footstep-adjacent thud, and far below the slingshot (.12) or a breaker trip (.1). At low frequency on laptop speakers it is nearly inaudible. Three bandpassed groans at .06 follow.

During the 120 s spoil wait the logs show no fridge warning sound at all. Only one alarm voice is heard just before the fail ([wait 120s] contains only coworker syllables and the final t120). The oven has a beep warning from 60 s (lunch-runtime.ts:282); the fridge has nothing.

Spoil and burn use the identical sting. The fail card (`failed()`, src/ui/game-ui.ts:224-227) lands with no sound, while the win card gets a thud and a bell (game-ui.ts:219-220).

The only way to lose a job ends on a murmur. A player looking elsewhere (the fridge is often off-screen, juice-audio-12) misses the cause entirely (DR-11, DR-28).

*lunch-play* — **The burn warning is nearly invisible: only a slightly redder oven window and a beep.** After baking, the tray waits on the oven door. From 60 s (BURN_WARNING) the oven window swaps to HOT_WINDOW and a beep sounds every 2 s (src/lunch-runtime.ts:280-282, :294). At the game camera (lunch-play-b02, 1:43, ovenWait 64 s), the oven looks almost the same as during a normal bake: no smoke visible, no badge, and the tray is a tiny item that is hard to see (b01).

The burn then ends the job with a card (b04). The fridge gets a sad-food badge before it spoils, but the burn has no matching cue. DR-47 says device state should show on the device.

   - spoil: add a fridge door clunk (lowpass noise 250 at .1);
   - burn: add a sizzle (highpass noise 3000, .8 s, at .06).

### R5-090

**R5-090 | P1 | meeting | fun | Meeting: the glass wall cannot be smashed; a sprint shove slides a pane into the room, lifted and unbroken**

Found by: `gap6-world-reacts#2` (P1 fun), `meeting-play#20` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*gap6-world-reacts* — **Meeting's glass wall can't be smashed: thrown props, sprinting and even throwing the pane leave it intact, and a sprint silently slides it open.** The documented Meeting chaos route is 'smash the glass wall (big cost) to shorten the route' (docs/LEVEL_01_BIG_MEETING.md:21). I tried three ways. (1) A bin thrown at the pane at (9.3,−6.1): the bin counts as broken (damage 1) and two boardroom blobs startle, but all three panes stay `enabled` and undamaged (world-reacts-17). (2) A 1.2 s sprint into the pane: no smash, damage 0, alarmed 0. Instead the 2.6 m pane slides 1.1 m into the boardroom (glass-0 x 9.3→10.39, glass-1 →10.5) and Pip walks in through the gap (world-reacts-18). The shortcut opens for free and without a sound. (3) Grabbing the pane (prompt 'E Grab the thing') and throwing it with Q: it topples onto Pip intact, damage 0 (world-reacts-22, -23). Glass only breaks when the pane's own lastSpeed exceeds 5.5 and it then decelerates (src/game.ts:335), which a 7 kg pane (src/props/prefabs.ts:17) never reaches from these actions. The most Good Job–like gag in the room (the research doc cites reviewers 'giggling … launching workers through glass windows', docs/RESEARCH_good_job_nintendo.md:42) never fires. The free slide also hands the chaos player the shortcut at no cost, which skips the risk/reward the doc intends.

*meeting-play* — **Shoving a boardroom glass pane at a sprint slides it into the room, lifted and unbroken, instead of shattering.** LEVEL_01's chaos route says 'smash the glass wall (big cost) to shorten the route'. In s7, sprinting Pip into the west glass pane glass-2 at (9.3, -3.6) for 1.2 s pushed the pane 2.6 m east into the boardroom (x 11.9) and raised it to y 1.7 (resting tilted on chairs or the table). It didn't break (damage 0, cost 0), and Pip entered the boardroom through the gap (shot 73). Damage only counts on a 5.5 m/s impact followed by a sudden stop, which a shove never produces. So the intended 'smash' reads as a ghost pane sliding about with Pip seen through it. The direct anchor→door line crosses this pane at z≈-2.95, so it matters for the chaos route.

*From gap6-world-reacts:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Make the panes Fixed, as the finding says. Note the pace check is computed at src/game.ts:319. Keep the cost at 250 as the doc's 'big cost'.

Reviewer's fix: Make glass panes Fixed bodies (not dynamic or grabbable) until they break. Turn on Rapier contact-force events on the glass colliders (`ActiveEvents.CONTACT_FORCE_EVENTS`, with a threshold of about 40 N). Break the pane when any dynamic prop hits it above 3 m/s relative speed, when Pip touches it at sprint pace (>5.5), or when a slingshot impulse passes within 1.1 m. On break, call `consume`, emit the existing 14-shard burst and `audio.glass()`, call `alarm(pos,5)`, and add the 250 cost. Leave a shard decal on the floor. Exclude 'glass' from nearest() so the 'Grab the thing' prompt disappears.

*From meeting-play:* Make glass panes fixed until hit: create them as Fixed bodies. On contact with Pip at sprint speed (>5 m/s), any prop faster than 4 m/s, or the taut cable at strain>1, switch the pane to 'shatter': consume it, spawn a glass burst plus shard debris, count damage and cost 250, and alarm the boardroom. A walking push should only rattle the pane (a small wobble tween).

### R5-091

**R5-091 | P1 | lunch | fun | Lunch: the fridge spoil timer runs from second 0 with no card step, so exploring or causing chaos ends the job at 2:00**

Found by: `lunch-play#2` (P1 fun), `lunch-teach#7` (P1 teaching). Batch: R-lunch (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*lunch-play* — **The fridge spoil timer runs from second 0 with no card step, so exploring or causing chaos ends the job at 2:00.** LunchJob starts at temperature 0.28 and rises 0.006 per second (src/sim/lunch.ts:8). The job fails at exactly t = 120 s unless the fridge is fed or the cooler box (locked in the dark storeroom) is used. Idling, I saw:
- the HUD bar turn warm at about 45 s;
- the sad-food icon over the fridge at about 87 s (lunch-play-f01 at 0.79, f02 at 1:57);
- the job end with the spoil card at 2:00 (f04).

The job card's 7 steps never mention the fridge (src/ui/objectives.ts:40-50). It only appears as the third bonus, whose wording is on the pause and result screens. For the whole first two minutes the card says 'Wedge…', 'Mop…', 'Power the feed post…'.

The scripted bot only survives because the spec plugs the fridge at 31 s, as step 3 of its own plan. A new player who walks the card's steps in order, plays with the bots, throws things at the crowd or simply reads the room will spoil the lunch long before reaching the capacitor puzzle. The penalty is the harshest in the game: a full restart of a 7-step chain.

This is a timer fail, not a mistake in the taught concept made by the player's own decision. It punishes the Good Job-style messing about that AGENTS 5 protects, and the hidden fridge requirement is a hidden rule (DR-37).

*lunch-teach* — **The fridge spoils the whole job at 120 s, yet the fridge is never a step on the card, and the intended solution never needs its 'time battery' idea.** The fridge warms at 0.006/s from 0.28 and fails the job at 1.0 (src/sim/lunch.ts:8-9), which is exactly t=120 s if it is not powered (s6 run: failed at 120.0). The 7 card steps (src/ui/objectives.ts:42-50) never mention it. It appears only as the third bonus star, whose text is hidden during play, and as the HUD thermometer. A first-time player who follows the card (wedge, mop, find out which cable feeds the post, possibly through a scorch, a short or a door cut) can easily pass 120 s and lose the job to an idea they were never introduced to. That is a fail state outside the taught concept's on-ramp (DR-02 'only a mistake in the taught concept', DR-37 'hidden rules shown before you can fail them').
Meanwhile the doc's fridge insight, 'the fridge is a time battery: unplug it while the oven bakes' (docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:25,36), is never required. The scripted solution keeps the fridge on cart A for the whole bake (tests/lunch.spec.ts:19-20), and by the time the fridge is unplugged for the lift it is at 0.03 and irrelevant. So the room fails players for the fridge without ever teaching the fridge. On the positive side, the in-world cues before the spoil (sad icon, red thermometer, puff and groan, shot 42) are good, and the fail card is clear (shot 43).

**Fix.**

*From lunch-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Option (b), making spoiling not end the job, contradicts the product doc (LEVEL_02:14), so it needs owner sign-off. Prefer (a), a fridge card step or a marker pulse from t=0, together with (c), a slower rate or a warming hold until the kitchen door first opens.

Reviewer's fix: Pick one, ideally (a) together with (b).
(a) Add a first card step 'Keep the lunch in the fridge cold' (done when the fridge has been powered for 2 s, or when cooled), with the marker on the fridge socket (-4,-1.8). Turn on the fridge socket ring pulse from the start.
(b) Soften the fail. Spoiling no longer ends the job: the fridge groans, the sad icon stays, cost +60, and the third bonus is lost. The tray can still be delivered, so the only job-ending fail is the burned tray, which comes from a sequencing decision.
(c) If the hard fail stays: start at 0.0 and use a rate of 0.0035 (about 285 s). Also hold the warming until Pip first opens the kitchen door, so exploration time isn't counted.

*From lunch-teach:* (1) Add a card step, or make the fridge a parallel 'keep alive' goal shown next to the chain, e.g. 'Keep the fridge cold' with the marker on the fridge whenever temperature > 0.55.
(2) Slow the first warm-up: start the temperature at 0.15, or warm at 0.004/s so the first spoil is at about 210 s, and keep 0.006/s once it has been powered once.
(3) Make the time-battery insight load-bearing. Put the conveyor's or lift's socket on the same cart as the fridge with a single outlet (cart capacity 1 at lunch-runtime.ts:50), so the fridge must come off for 20–30 s while it visibly warms but stays under 80%. Or retune so that kitchen (4) + fridge (2) is the only way to bake, forcing a mid-bake swap.
(4) Update LEVEL_02 to match whichever is chosen.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *lunch-play:* Spec: open the level, advance(150) without touching anything. Expect job.failed false (option b or c), or expect the card's current step to name the fridge at t = 0 (option a). Retake lunch-play-f02 and check that the card text and the marker point at the fridge.
- *lunch-teach:* Blind playtest: five first-time players, count spoils before the first bake (target ≤1). Spec: tests/lunch.spec.ts intended solution includes one fridge unplug that raises temperature by ≥0.2 and still wins.

**Rules:** AGENTS 5, AGENTS 6, DR-02, DR-27, DR-37, DR-39, DR-42

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The arithmetic holds: 0.28 + 0.006/s reaches 1.0 at 120 s (src/sim/lunch.ts:5,8). Idling reproduced it: at t 119.9 the temperature was 0.999 and failed was false, and at t 120.0 failed was true and the spoil card dropped. None of the card's steps mention the fridge (src/ui/objectives.ts:40-50), and in the reviewer's f02 the card still says 'Wedge…' at 1:57 while the bar is red. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-092

**R5-092 | P1 | global | fun | The slingshot has no recoil: the plug and cable never snap back, props just get an invisible kick**

Found by: `cable#1` (P1 fun). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

When the slingshot fires:
- The plug only moves 15% of the way toward the last bend (lerp 0.15, src/game.ts:262). The cable is redrawn in the same place.
- Props within 1.1 m of the cable get an impulse directed away from the anchor (game.ts:257), with a screen shake of at most 0.5.
- There is no hitstop: plugFlash has 0.09 s (game.ts:249), the slingshot has none. There is no whip sound shaped to the motion, and no cable movement.

In cable-26/27/28, the 'slingshot' reads as the cable going white and a chair and cone sliding a little. The cable itself, the star, does nothing. In cable-32/33 (pins), most of the strike came from dragging the pins during the sprint (pinsDown 2 before Q), not from the release.

In Good Job!, the satisfaction comes from watching the stretched cord whip back through the room. Here the cause (a stretched cable) and the effect (things fly) aren't connected on screen, so it doesn't read as a slingshot and isn't rewarding (DR-06, DR-11).

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:255-257`
- `src/game.ts:258-264`
- `src/game.ts:249`
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:198-203`
- [cable-26-pg-sling-held-0s.jpg](shots/cable-26-pg-sling-held-0s.jpg)
- [cable-27-pg-sling-held-0.2s.jpg](shots/cable-27-pg-sling-held-0.2s.jpg)
- [cable-28-pg-sling-held-after.jpg](shots/cable-28-pg-sling-held-after.jpg)
- [cable-31-pg-pins-taut.jpg](shots/cable-31-pg-pins-taut.jpg)
- [cable-33-pg-pins-after.jpg](shots/cable-33-pg-pins-after.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/cable/log-pg.txt` (pg4: pinsDown 2 before Q)
- [verify-cable-03-sling-0s.jpg](shots/verify-cable-03-sling-0s.jpg)
- [verify-cable-04-sling-0.15s.jpg](shots/verify-cable-04-sling-0.15s.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-cable/v1.mjs` (sprintNow: len 19.85 -> 19.39 -> 19.71 after Q)

**Fix.**

Animate the recoil and hit props from the moving plug.

1. On release with energy > 1, start a 0.35 s recoil: tween `plugPosition` back along the current route (ropePoints, from the end toward the last bend and then the anchor) by `min(3, over*4 + 1.5)` m, with an ease-out curve.
2. Each recoil frame, sweep a 0.6 m-radius capsule from the plug's previous position to its new one. Give any prop it touches `impulse = clamp(energy*.22, 4, 30)`. Direct it along the recoil direction (toward the anchor) plus 0.5 up.
3. Add `hitstop = .06` at the start, and a whip sound (rising noise sweep 400→2500 Hz over 0.15 s).
4. Spawn 6 dust puffs along the cable as it slackens.
5. Keep the 1.1 m 'whip' kick for props lying on the cable, but use the same direction.

Put this in one shared helper used by both Game.releasePlug and LunchRuntime.release.

**Verify.**

- Take a frame sequence at +0, +0.1, +0.2 and +0.35 s after Q in the pg3 'held' setup. The plug should visibly travel at least 2 m toward the reel. Spec: after Q, snapshot plug or rope length drops by at least 1.5 m within 0.4 s, and fastestProp > 2.

**Rules:** DR-06, DR-11

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — In code, releasePlug only lerps the plug 15% toward the last bend (game.ts:262), slingshot() applies one static impulse to props within 1.1 m of the frozen route (game.ts:255-257), and there is no hitstop (plugFlash sets one, game.ts:249; slingshot does not). I reproduced the sprint-then-Q sequence (verify-cable-03-sling-0s.jpg, verify-cable-04-sling-0.15s.jpg).

### R5-093

**R5-093 | P1 | global | fun | Win, every bench sign-off, the Meeting extension and the pin strike all play the same cheer/jingle, and two jingles overlap at the last station step**

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#0` (P1 fun). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

There is one celebration cue in the game. `Sound.cheer()` (src/render/audio.ts:73) is `jingle()` (audio.ts:75) followed by four coworker 'cheer' voices. Game.win() fires it (src/game.ts:350). The same cue also fires for every bench sign-off: arcade sign-off src/stations/arcade/station.ts:275, garage TEST pass garage/station.ts:228, observatory log observatory/station.ts:198, spectrum send spectrum/station.ts:235 and QFN ship qfn/station.ts:285. Mid-job milestones use the bare jingle too: the Meeting extension reel (game.ts:236) and the Playground pin strike (game.ts:347). The hooked audio logs agree. Each of the five arcade cabinets logged the identical 21-oscillator jingle (523/659/784/1047 arpeggio, then a held 523/659/784 chord), a 1319 bell and about 12 cheer syllables. For the 5th cabinet, 'cab5 signoff' carried one jingle and the 'win step' a frame later carried a second full jingle plus a second crowd. QFN showed the same pattern: three identical ship jingles, then the win jingle. Garage: three TEST-pass jingles, then the win jingle. The Meeting coupler-extension attach mid-route logged the exact win jingle. So the player hears the 'job won' sound 4–6 times per station room. The real finish is indistinguishable from a sub-step, and at the final step it is just a louder, muddier double. DR-11 asks that the success moment be the juicy peak. Here it is the 6th repeat of a sound that has stopped meaning anything.

### R5-094

**R5-094 | P1 | global | fun | Hitstop exists only for the Playground/Meeting cable plug-in; win, failures, trips, pops and Lunch plug-ins never freeze**

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#1` (P1 fun). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Hitstop is set in exactly one place: `plugFlash()` sets `this.hitstop=.09` (src/game.ts:249). Its only caller is the cable seating in Game.action('cable') (game.ts:205). frame() honours it (game.ts:456). A grep for hitstop, timeScale and slow finds nothing else: no time.scale and no slow-mo anywhere.

These moments get no hitstop:
- the job win, Game.win() (game.ts:350);

- the garage dead-short fuse (garage/station.ts:237);
- every bench sign-off;
- the slingshot release (game.ts:256);
- Lunch plug-ins: lunch-runtime.ts:156 calls `g.audio.plug()` without `plugFlash()`, so Lunch's 9 cable connections get neither the freeze nor the flash/ring/star burst that Playground and Meeting get.

DR-11 requires 'a short hitstop' at success and failure moments. Today the freeze lands on the least important beat (a plug that will be followed by a switch press) and never on the beats that matter. ?manual skips the frame loop entirely (game.ts:457), so no spec can even observe hitstop.

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep drive.advance() free of hitstop, or make it opt-in. Otherwise every ?manual spec that advances right after a trip or win would silently lose sim time. Expose a counter instead, e.g. snapshot().hitstops++, so tests can assert that a hitstop fired.

Reviewer's fix: Add a `Game.freeze(s:number)` helper (`this.hitstop=Math.max(this.hitstop,s)`) and call it with these values:
- win(): .12
- Lunch fail (lunch-runtime.ts:285): .15
- breaker trip and short (meeting-strip.ts:82, lunch-runtime.ts:264): .08
- scorch: .06
- arcade trip(), popBlock() and popLed(), garage tripFuse(): .07
- station sign-off, ship, log and send success: .05
- slingshot release (game.ts:256): .06

In lunch-runtime.ts:156 replace `g.audio.plug();g.burst(...)` with `g.audio.plug();g.plugFlash(target.pos)` so Lunch connections match the other cable floors.

Expose `hitstop` in snapshot(). Make drive.advance() honour it, for example by consuming the hitstop before stepping, so a spec can assert `snap().hitstopFired`.

**Verify.**

- New unit/spec: after the arcade 'power' that trips (tests/station-arcade.spec.ts first cabinet), snapshot reports a hitstop > 0 or a counter incremented. Manual non-?manual play: the frame visibly holds on the TRIP marquee. Lunch plug-in shows the cyan ring and star burst (retake juice-audio-10).

**Rules:** DR-11

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — A grep for hitstop/timeScale over src/ finds only game.ts:48, :249 (plugFlash) and :456. lunch-runtime.ts:156 calls g.audio.plug() plus a 12-spark burst with no plugFlash. win(), trips, shorts, the Lunch fail, the arcade and garage fuses and the slingshot (game.ts:256) never set hitstop. DR-11 (mockups/review5/RULES.md:99) asks for hitstop on success and failure moments.

**What is wrong.**

The 'flash' particle type (src/render/particles.ts:30, life .18 s) is used only by plugFlash (game.ts:249) and the arcade LED pop (arcade/station.ts:311). Failures have no flash either.
- Lunch spoil (lunch-runtime.ts:285) is six grey puffs at the fridge.
- The Meeting and Lunch trips are 14–18 small sparks at the strip.
- The QFN send-back shows only the problem rings.

In the immediate-frame captures (taken without the 900 ms settle):
- juice-audio-02 (Playground win, +0.15 s): confetti, no burst at the lamp.
- juice-audio-06 (Meeting trip): only a few specks at the strip; the projector and the coworkers show nothing.
- juice-audio-12 (Lunch spoil): the cause is a small sad-face badge at the top of the frame.
- juice-audio-26 (QFN send-back): only pink rings.

DR-11 asks for flash, sound and hitstop together. Without a flash, the failure cause also isn't 'shown in the world first' at a readable size (DR-28).

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:350-351`
- `src/render/particles.ts:30`
- `src/game.ts:438` (fx.update in render: real-time)
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:285`
- `src/meeting-strip.ts:82`
- [juice-audio-02-playground-win-0.15s.jpg](shots/juice-audio-02-playground-win-0.15s.jpg)

**Fix.**

1. In Game.win() add `this.burst({x:target.x,y:1.6,z:target.z},'#fff3c8',1,'flash');this.burst({x:target.x,y:.05,z:target.z},'#ffe36e',1,'ring');this.burst(target,'#ffe36e',8,'star')`.
2. Add a CSS full-screen flash: a `.hud-flash` div with opacity 0→.35→0 over 120 ms, white for success and #ff7a6b for failure. Trigger it from Game.win(), lunch-runtime.ts:285, meeting-strip.ts:82, the arcade trip and popBlock, garage tripFuse, and the QFN/observatory/spectrum tier-0 branches. Keep it ≤120 ms near a taught part (DR-79).
3. For the Lunch fail, also add a 'flash' plus an 8-particle dust ring at the fridge or oven position.

**Verify.**

**Rules:** DR-11, DR-28, DR-79

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — game.ts:350-351 win() spawns only confetti (90 + 40). 'flash' is used only at game.ts:249 and arcade/station.ts:311. The Lunch fail (lunch-runtime.ts:285) is smoke puffs only. My immediate Meeting trip shot shows only a few sparks and dust at the strip. Nothing lights up at the projector or the coworkers.

### R5-096

**R5-096 | P1 | garage | fun | Garage delivery payoff plays a ~22-per-second machine-gun beep: the test-cycle animation keeps running under the drive**

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#7` (P1 fun). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

On the third TEST pass, startDrive() is called (src/stations/garage/station.ts:230 → :256) while the 5-cycle test animation is still running (`cycleT>=0`, started by `kick(v,s,true)` a moment earlier).

Each frame:
1. The drive sets `this.motorOn=d&lt;ROUTE_LEN?1:0` (station.ts:364), i.e. 1.
2. The cycle branch (station.ts:367-369) stores `before=this.motorOn` (1), then sets motorOn from the cycle phase.
3. In every 'off' sub-phase, and after the last cycle until c ≥ cycles+2, `!this.motorOn&&before` is true, so `land(true)` fires every frame.
4. land() ends in `this.game.audio.tone(320,.25,.03,'sine')` (station.ts:397) and resets the current-pulse flow.

The hooked log [driving] holds 135 copies of s320@0.030 in about 6 s of sim, plus more in [job2 pass] and [job3 pass -> drive]. The robot's victory drive, the room's payoff, is accompanied by a buzzing stutter. The pulses on the board also restart every frame. The delivery itself has only a single 1568 bell (station.ts:364) before the win jingle.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:230`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:256`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:364`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:367-369`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:397`
- juice-audio/garage.mjs log [driving] (135 cues of s320@0.030)
- [juice-audio-24-garage-delivered-win.jpg](shots/juice-audio-24-garage-delivered-win.jpg)
- node mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap4-juice-audio/garage.mjs [driving] (135 cues)
- The [pulse ok] and [job2 pass] drains also contain long s320 runs, so land() repeats outside the drive too (likely the same before/after pattern while kickT runs). Check animateKick/kick paths as well

**Fix.**

1. In startDrive() set `this.cycleT=-1;this.kickT=-1;` before driving starts. Alternatively, guard the cycle branch with `if(this.cycleT>=0&&!this.driving)`.
2. In land(), early-return when `this.driving`.
3. Give the drive its own cue: a soft motor whirr (sawtooth 90 Hz through lowpass 500 at .02, gain following motorOn) and a 'docked' clunk plus chime at DRIVE_TIME.

**Verify.**

- Re-run juice-audio/garage.mjs. The [driving] drain contains no repeated s320 cues (at most 1). tests/station-garage.spec.ts still passes with delivered=true.

**Rules:** —

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The code path holds. Drive sets motorOn=1 each frame (garage/station.ts:364) before the cycle branch (:367), and the cycle started at TEST (:223) is still running. So in every off sub-phase, and for 1.2 s after the last cycle, `!motorOn&&before` calls land() each frame, and land() plays tone(320,.25,.03) at :397.

### R5-097

**R5-097 | P1 | global | fun | Coworkers only react when something is counted as 'broken', so every reaction costs damage, money and the 'Break nothing' bonus**

Found by: `gap6-world-reacts#0` (P1 fun). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The world reacts to Pip's chaos in exactly one place. `alarm()` is called from the prop-impact branch in src/game.ts:335, and that branch also sets `prop.damaged=true`, `damage++` and `cost+=prefab.cost`. Startling a coworker and breaking a prop are the same event: you can't get the '!' bubble without a damage point and a cost. A thrown bin that lands upright next to the trainee (world-reacts-01) shows no crack, dent or spilt contents, yet the HUD jumps to damage 1 / cost 8, and the Playground's 'Break nothing' star (src/ui/objectives.ts:30) goes dark in the same frame. The same happens with the Lobby chair (damage 1, cost 25, world-reacts-02), the Meeting plant (damage 1, cost 15, world-reacts-03), the Lunch mop (damage 1, cost 5, world-reacts-05), the QFN cart (damage 1, cost 50) and the Arcade mug (damage 1, cost 5). For the player, the slapstick that should be free play (DR-03/DR-04) is silently charged as wrecking. There is no visual sign of what was 'broken', so the grade feels arbitrary. Every throw at a desk also takes a step toward losing 'Break fewer than 5 things' (objectives.ts:38). This conflates DR-04 (the world reacts) with DR-07 (the damage axis), and it works against AGENTS 5 (chaos second, never punished as a fail) in spirit.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:335`
- `src/game.ts:137`
- `src/ui/objectives.ts:30`
- `src/ui/objectives.ts:38`
- [world-reacts-01-playground-throw-aim.jpg](shots/world-reacts-01-playground-throw-aim.jpg)
- [world-reacts-01-playground-throw-react.jpg](shots/world-reacts-01-playground-throw-react.jpg)
- [world-reacts-02-lobby-throw-react.jpg](shots/world-reacts-02-lobby-throw-react.jpg)
- [world-reacts-03-meeting-throw-react.jpg](shots/world-reacts-03-meeting-throw-react.jpg)
- [world-reacts-05-lunch-crowd-react.jpg](shots/world-reacts-05-lunch-crowd-react.jpg)
- [verify-gap6-world-reacts-02-pg-bin-react.jpg](shots/verify-gap6-world-reacts-02-pg-bin-react.jpg) (HUD 1 / 8, bin upright, bubble on trainee)
- [verify-gap6-world-reacts-05-meet-glass-sprint.jpg](shots/verify-gap6-world-reacts-05-meet-glass-sprint.jpg) (sprint only: damage 1, cost 25)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap6-world-reacts/v.mjs` pg timeline: [0.7,1,1,8] [t,alarmed,dmg,cost]

**Fix.**

Split the impact branch at src/game.ts:335 into two tiers. (1) Impact: lastSpeed>4 and a deceleration >3. Call `this.alarm(pos,3.5)`, play the thud or clatter and the dust, and do not touch damage or cost. Allow it again after a 1 s per-prop cooldown, rather than once per prop forever. (2) Break: only for fragile kinds (add `fragile:true` to glass, monitor, mug, plant, printer and coffee in src/props/prefabs.ts), or any kind at lastSpeed>9. This tier sets `damaged`, counts damage and cost, and shows a visible state: swap in a cracked or tilted variant mesh, or a lid-off/soil-spill decal, so the player can see what they paid for.

**Verify.**

- Rerun mockups/review5/tools/world-reacts/throw.mjs playground 6 throw 01. Expect alarmed ≥1 at +0.5 s with damage 0 and cost 0 for the bin, and the 'Break nothing' star still lit in world-reacts-01-…-react.png. Throwing a mug at a wall still counts 1 damage and shows a broken-mug mesh.

**Rules:** AGENTS 5, DR-03, DR-04, DR-07

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The only alarm() call on an impact is inside the damage branch at src/game.ts:335 (prop.damaged=true; damage++; cost+=). I reproduced it: I threw a bin at the playground trainee, and at +0.7 s alarmed went to 1 in the same tick that damage went 0→1 and cost 0→8. The HUD shows 1 / 8 and the bin sits upright and undamaged beside the trainee.

### R5-098

**R5-098 | P1 | meeting | fun | Letting go has no payoff in Meeting, and none of the three bonuses rewards chaos**

Found by: `meeting-play#11` (P1 fun). Batch: R-meeting (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

### R5-099

**R5-099 | P1 | global | fun | Bonus stars aren't saved and the result card never shows the previous best, so there is no hook to replay**

Found by: `progression#8` (P1 fun). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Each job has three bonus goals, shown as three stars on the job card and as a ★ list on the result card (src/ui/game-ui.ts:216-217). The save record only keeps `{grade,time,damage,cost}` (src/ui/store.ts:4, :13). Stars earned are thrown away when the card closes, so the lobby door, the door medal and the Jobs-board tag can't show how many stars a job has. After finishing Playground and returning, the door looks the same as one finished with zero stars (`progression-14`, `progression-20`). The result card shows this run's numbers only, with no previous best and no delta. The 'new best' star appears only when the overall grade improves (`improved:!old||run.grade&lt;old.grade`, store.ts:15), and since almost every run is A (see the grading finding), it shows on the first clear and never again, even when a replay cuts time from 0:21 to 0:12. `record` also takes the best of each stat separately (store.ts:13), so the Jobs-board 'best' row can combine a time from one run with damage from another, a run that never happened. Taken together, a finished job offers no visible reason to go back in.

**Evidence.**

- `src/ui/store.ts:4`
- `src/ui/store.ts:13-15`
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:208-220`
- `src/ui/screens.ts:107-118`

- `src/ui/store.ts:3` (comment: per-stat best is intentional)

**Fix.**

(1) Extend `Best` with `stars:number` (a bitmask of the three bonuses, OR-merged across runs), and pass `this.objectives.results()` into record() at src/ui/game-ui.ts:208. (2) Show stars on the door plate under the medal (src/hub/lobby.ts:94: three small star plates), on the job tag (src/ui/screens.ts:115) and in the lobby (a hub bonus 'Collect 15 stars'). (3) On the result card, under each row, print the previous best and a green or red delta ('best 0:21 · −0:09'). Fire the newbest star and bell when any stat or star improves, not only the grade.

**Verify.**

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — src/ui/store.ts:4 Best holds only {grade,time,damage,cost}. src/ui/game-ui.ts:208 passes no bonus results to record(), and the stars are only rendered at :216-217. improved = grade-only (store.ts:15). After the Playground clear, localStorage held only {grade,time,damage,cost} (r-keys.mjs output: '{"playground":{"grade":"A","time":5.08,"damage":0,"cost":0}}'), even though the card showed 2 of 3 stars.

### R5-101

**R5-101 | P1 | global, garage, lunch, meeting, observatory, qfn, arcade, lobby, playground, spectrum | clarity | Job yellow (#ffc94d) is the default colour of decor in every room (32 Meeting mugs, crates, cabinets, carts, chairs, books, a trainee, a beanbag), while several job items are not yellow**

Found by: `props-gallery#1` (P1 clarity), `garage-models#1` (P1 clarity), `lunch-models#4` (P1 clarity), `meeting-models#6` (P1 art-style), `observatory-models#3` (P1 clarity), `qfn-models#3` (P1 clarity), `arcade-models#4` (P2 clarity), `garage-play#14` (P2 clarity), `lunch-play#12` (P2 clarity), `meeting-play#21` (P2 clarity), `gap3-recheck-list#6` (P2 art-style), `lobby-models#20` (P2 art-style), `playground-models#10` (P2 clarity), `playground-play#20` (P2 art-style), `qfn-play#13` (P2 clarity), `spectrum-models#1` (P2 clarity). Batch: B9 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*props-gallery* — **Job yellow is the default colour of decorative props: yellow mugs on all 32 Meeting desks, yellow beanbags, yellow desk lamps, and yellow clutter beside the Lunch wedge.** DR-45 reserves job yellow (`#ffc94d`/`#ffc629`) for job items. Several decorative prefabs default to it anyway:
- **Mug:** defaults to `#ffc94d` (prefabs.ts:12). The Meeting desk loop spawns mugs with no colour (meeting.ts:16), so every one of the 32 desks carries a job-yellow mug, visible in `props-gallery-20b-crop-meeting-yellow-mugs.jpg`.
- **Beanbag:** defaults to `#ffc94d` (prefabs.ts:26). The Meeting lounge places a yellow one at (10,4.6) right next to Pip's spawn path; it is the same yellow as Pip's hat and the job reel (`props-gallery-29-meeting-lounge-close.jpg`).
- **Desk lamp:** the `deskClutter` lamp picks from `['#e5484d','#3f7fd6','#ffc94d','#6cc58a']` (prefabs.ts:47), so a quarter of the desk lamps are job yellow.
- **Clutter palettes:** these feed every recipe, including boxes, carts, chairs, reels and cabinets:
  - garage `#ffc629`: yellow carts, chairs, boxes and a yellow cabinet stack (`props-gallery-51c-garage-close-o300.jpg`, `-51b`);
  - lunch `#ffc94d`: yellow boxes on the cart next to the yellow doorstop wedge (`props-gallery-52c-lunch-close-o300.jpg`) and in the corridor beside the yellow cable bridges (`-52b`);
  - arcade `#ffd84d` and observatory/spectrum `#ffd66b`, both within about 10 ΔE.

The player learns that yellow means a job part (reel, strip, wedge, splitter, bridge, plug). Dozens of yellow decoys dilute that cue and send the grab prompt to junk (DR-17, DR-43). This is related to the known RESEARCH_ART F4, but the default prefab colours (mug and beanbag) and the Meeting hand placements are separate root causes that F4's per-kind palette fix alone does not touch.

*garage-models* — **Job-yellow everywhere: yellow crates, 2.2 m yellow cabinet columns, yellow carts, a yellow chair and a yellow reel compete with the job items.** The garage clutter palette passes the job yellow '#ffc629' as one of its five colours (garage.ts:31 `colors:['#c98f5a','#d7a56d','#2fb3a6','#ffc629','#9fb8c8']`). Every crates, cart and cabinets recipe can draw it. On top of that, the level props add a yellow chair at (-2.6, 5.2) (garage.ts:16), a yellow mail cart at (-1, 6.6) (garage.ts:19), a yellow reel at (-4.4, 6.8) (garage.ts:12), and the dolly's yellow-flanged reel at (9.3, 4.1).

In the start shot about 2.8% of the play-area pixels are job yellow (r>220, 170&lt;g<215, b<90). These include:
- a yellow-drawered cabinet column directly behind the bench scope at (-1.6, -4.91), which fills the top-left of the bench view;
- a second yellow column at (-8.21, 3.21);
- yellow crate pairs at the right wall;
- two yellow mail carts next to spawn.

The actual job items (the PULSE button, the part tray and the robot's lid) use the same yellow, and so does the objective marker cone. A first-time viewer of the start shot cannot pick out the 'job thing' by colour. The grab prompt also offers yellow junk ('Grab the crate', 'Grab the splitter'). RESEARCH_ART F7 already noted that yellow job highlights lose contrast in the garage. This makes it worse.

*lunch-models* — **Job-item yellow (#ffc94d) is used by decorative clutter: 9 crates, 12 mugs and a crate right beside the bridges; teal and white crates too.** Lunch's job items are all #ffc94d: the wedge, bridges, splitters, thick cable, kitchen post and mop wringer. But the clutter palette in lunch.ts:18 includes '#ffc94d', and the mug prefab defaults to '#ffc94d' (prefabs.ts:12). From the live prop dump, 9 crates and 4 clutter mugs are job yellow. Examples: a box at (0.32, 8.25) beside the wedge and mop route, a box at (14.88, 6.97) next to the bridges, and boxes at (−13, −8.39) and (−15.35, −7.52) in the storeroom right where the player hunts for the capacitor cart. The 8 kitchen mugs placed by lunch.ts:14 are also job yellow, in a perfect row across the two counters. In lunch-models-76 a yellow crate sits a metre from the yellow bridge ramps, and in -37 and -38 the eight yellow mugs are the most saturated shapes in the kitchen. A first-time player can't tell yellow-means-use-me apart from noise. That breaks DR-45 and the grab-prompt flow: the prompt says 'Grab the mug' at the post (lunch-models-34). The same palette adds 6 teal '#5f8fa8' crates and 7 white '#e9f0f2' crates. Cardboard should stay kraft (DR-51, 'no teal boxes').

*meeting-models* — **Job-yellow is used by 32 desk mugs, a beanbag, desk lamps and the lounge pendant, while the job items themselves are orange (strip) and teal (coupler).** DR-45 says job items share one visual language: yellow #ffc94d/#ffc629 with ink stripes, and no decorative clutter uses it. In the meeting this is reversed. The mug prefab default colour is #ffc94d (prefabs.ts:12), and meeting.ts:16 places one mug per desk without a colour: 32 job-yellow cylinders across the office (meeting-models-16, -18, -33, -47). The lounge beanbag is explicitly #ffc94d (meeting.ts:29), the lounge pendant shade is #ffc94d (decor.ts:163), and desk-lamp variant 4 picks yellow (prefabs.ts:47). Meanwhile the job items are the orange #ff8a3d strip (prefabs.ts:26), the teal coupler (prefabs.ts:15), and the yellow reels and cable. In mid-drag shots (-33) the yellow cable runs past five yellow mugs, a yellow coworker and a yellow reel, so it isn't the most saturated thing near Pip (DR-53). On a first look a player can't tell "things for the job" from mugs. It also dilutes the yellow grab cue (#ffd84a) and the pip ring (#ffc629).

*observatory-models* — **Job items don't use the job-yellow language, while yellow crates, beanbags and chairs do.** The first job item, the motor cart, is teal '#5f8fa8' with a red drum (observatory.ts:7). Meanwhile decorative clutter uses the job yellow. The placed beanbag at (-6.8,3.2) has no colour, so it takes the prefab default '#ffc94d' (prefabs.ts:26). The chair at (1.6,1.6) is '#ffc94d' (observatory.ts:10). The clutter palette includes '#ffd66b' (observatory.ts:21), which produces about a dozen yellow star-chart crates and yellow beanbags. In the survey and start shots the brightest, most saturated yellow shapes are the crate stack behind the bench, the yellow beanbag on the spawn rug and the yellow chair. None of them is part of the job, and the cart blends in with the teal coworker and teal crates. This breaks DR-45 (job items share one visual language, and no decorative clutter uses it) and DR-43 (the goal should be among the top-contrast shapes).

*qfn-models* — **Job-item yellow and yellow+ink-stripe language is spent on decor: a yellow cart beside the bench, a yellow chair, the striped crane, yellow stock bins and reels behind the crate.** DR-45: job items use #ffc94d/#ffc629 with ink stripes, and no decorative clutter may. In this room the only job item is the parts crate (qfn.ts:6, #ffc629), yet at least eight decorative things share its colour, and the most prominent one also has the ink stripes:

1. **Overhead crane:** two yellow legs and a 6.3 m yellow beam with 12 black ink bars (room.ts:35-39). This is the exact job-item 'yellow with ink stripes' language, it is the largest yellow shape in the frame, and it sits in the machine bay.
2. **Cart #ffc629 at (4.6, −3.6)** (qfn.ts:9). It is 2.3 m from the side table where the crate must go, so at the bench (qfn-models-15, -50, -85) the yellow tray competes with the crate.
3. **Chair #ffc94d at (8.4, 4.9)** (qfn.ts:10) (qfn-models-60).
4. **Stock bin #ffc629 on the stock shelf** (room.ts:51), 1 m behind the crate's taped spot (qfn-models-20, -74).
5. **Yellow flanges on 2 of the 4 stock-shelf reels** (room.ts:52) and on 3 PnP feeder reels (room.ts:32).
6. **PnP side posts and Y-beam** in YEL (room.ts:31).
7. **Yellow pendant shades** over the PnP and AOI (room.ts:70).
8. **Defaults:** the mug default colour is #ffc94d (prefabs.ts:12), and the mug at (−2.8, 3) has no colour. The clutter splitter also defaults to #ffc94d (prefabs.ts:24).

For a first-time player told to 'Bring the parts crate', the yellow tray cart next to the bench and the yellow bins on the stock shelf are plausible wrong answers. The striped crane trains the eye to read stripes as scenery, which undoes the language the other rooms teach.

*arcade-models* — **The job item is not in the job colour language: the tray is clutter pink (#ff7eb6, the exact first clutter colour) while yellow #ffd84d is spread over clutter boxes, beanbags and chairs.** DR-45 says job items share one visual language (yellow #ffc94d/#ffc629 with ink stripes, plus the #ffd84d grab cue) and no decorative clutter uses it. In the arcade, the resistor tray is `color:'#ff7eb6'` (src/levels/arcade.ts:133). That is the same hex as the first entry of the arcade clutter palette (arcade.ts:155 colors), the pink beanbags, the pink chairs (arcade.ts:138) and the pink storeroom boxes (#ffa6c9, arcade.ts:135). Meanwhile LEMON #ffd84d, the grab-cue colour, appears on clutter boxes, beanbags and chairs all over the floor (shots -01, -21, -55, -57). In the start shot the tray is a small pink rectangle on a dark counter, surrounded by pink boxes, a pink storeroom box at the door and pink beanbags. It is not one of the three highest-contrast shapes (DR-43), so the player relies on the marker to find it. The resistor-stock bricks on the storeroom shelf (room.ts:112) are also pink, mint and lilac blocks, the same candy look as the tray's blocks, so a player may try to grab them.

*garage-play* — **Job yellow and cable-job props in a cable-free room: yellow crates, a yellow reel, extra reels from the 'parts' recipe.** The garage clutter palette includes '#ffc629' (job yellow, garage.ts:31), and the recipes list 'parts' twice. Each 'parts' cluster adds a reel and a splitter (src/levels/clutter.ts:45). A hand-placed yellow reel stands at (−4.4, 6.8) (garage.ts:12), and the dolly carries another. The start and survey shots show tall yellow crate stacks (left wall), yellow boxes on carts, a yellow cart near spawn, and two or three cable reels (white by the rug, yellow front-left, a yellow reel on the dolly at right; shots 01, 02). This room has no cable job. Reels and splitters are the most recognisable job items from the cable floors, so they are pure false affordances here, and the job-yellow clutter competes with the robot's yellow lid and the pale marker. This breaks DR-17 (no false affordances) and DR-45 (no decorative clutter in job yellow).

*lunch-play* — **Clutter crates in job yellow sit next to the yellow doorstop and read as job items.** The Lunch clutter palette includes '#ffc94d' (src/levels/lunch.ts:19), the exact yellow used for job items: the doorstop, the feed post, cart A, the bridges and the thick cable. The start and survey shots show at least 6 bright yellow crates around the corridor, the lift room and the vending area (lunch-play-01 at about (960,590), lunch-play-02, c01, c02, x01).

The first task is 'find the doorstop', a small ridged yellow wedge on the floor, so the yellow crates are direct false affordances. In c01 the yellow crate beside the mop looks just as much like 'the thing to grab' as the doorstop did. The job-yellow language (ART R1.2) only works if nothing decorative uses it.

*meeting-play* — **Lounge beanbag uses the exact job-item yellow (#ffc94d).** The lounge beanbag at (10, 4.6) is coloured '#ffc94d'. That is the job-item yellow shared by the reels, the plug, the target marker family and the reel flanges. In the survey and lounge shots (02, 76) the yellow blob near the boardroom is the brightest job-coloured shape on that side of the room, near the goal, competing with the strip and the marker. Its rounded shape also reads more like a yellow coworker or a bun than a seat. This breaks DR-45 (no decorative clutter uses the job-item yellow).

*gap3-recheck-list* — **Books use job yellow #ffc94d, so every bookshelf carries job-coloured blocks.** This turned up while re-checking the bookshelf colour wrap (which passes: every row is filled in both rooms). The book palette at src/props/prefabs.ts:52 includes '#ffc94d', the exact job-item yellow from DR-45. Every shelf in the Meeting lounge and around the Playground lamp shows 5–6 job-yellow blocks at chest height, next to the job's own yellow plug and reel. The earlier report only called the books 'saturated candy bars'; the job-yellow collision is what breaks DR-45.

*lobby-models* — **The lobby's floor mug and the door knobs and padlock use job yellow (#ffc94d/#ffc629) on non-job decor, and the mug is lone litter that hijacks the reception prompt.** DR-45 reserves job yellow for job items. In the hub it appears on decor:
- The lone mug at (0.9, 1.3) on the rug uses the prefab default '#ffc94d' (src/levels/lobby.ts:8, src/props/prefabs.ts:28).
- Door knobs are sphere(.05) in '#ffc629' (lobby.ts:90).
- The padlock block is '#ffc629' (lobby.ts:93).
- The pendant shades are '#ffc94d' (lobby.ts:61).
- The reception and Workshop signs use a '#ffc629' background.

The mug is a single yellow speck on the floor in the middle of the rug, and it's the nearest prop at reception. The only prompt the player gets there is 'Grab the mug' (lobby-models-09, -12): a fallback prompt pointing at litter, the pattern L2 complained about.

*playground-models* — **One trainee is painted job yellow (#ffc94d), the same hue as the plug and reel.** The third trainee at (9,1.6) has color '#ffc94d', identical to the reel flanges, the plug coupler (#ffcc52) and the BLOBC 'yellow'. In the survey and the overstretch shot it reads as a yellow job object: a dropped reel or a lamp. That puts a blob-shaped coworker in the job-item colour, which breaks both DR-45 (no non-job thing in job yellow) and DR-52 (blob hues only on coworkers, and job yellow is reserved). The kit's BLOBC list itself contains #ffc94d, so any level can repeat this.

*playground-play* — **The trainer blob uses the exact job yellow #ffc94d.** The headphone trainer at (9,1.6) is coloured '#ffc94d' (src/levels/playground.ts:20), the job-item yellow of the reel and splitter (prefabs.ts:15, :24). It is a large saturated yellow shape near the pins and the slingshot lane (shots 20, 22, 30, 54), competing with the job language (DR-45) and with Pip's yellow hat as the brightest yellow near Pip.

*qfn-play* — **Job yellow is spent on decor and on 'locked' parts, and the crate is just a yellow box.** The only room job item is the parts crate, a stock 'box' prop tinted #ffc629 (src/levels/qfn.ts:7) with no stripe or icon. The same job yellow appears on a decorative cart at (4.6,-3.6) (qfn.ts:9) and a chair at (8.4,4.9) (qfn.ts:10). The 'parts' clutter recipe (qfn.ts:25, clutter.ts:45) adds splitters whose prefab colour is #ffc94d, plus the pick-and-place crane and the shelf bins. When the crate was thrown over the bench it came to rest beside the yellow cart, and the two read as a pair (qfn-play-84). On the bench, locked connectors (board 3 J1 and J2) get a #ffc629 end cap meaning 'fixed by the enclosure' (station.ts:166), which is the opposite of what yellow means everywhere else ('grab me'). A new player tries to drag the yellow caps first.

*spectrum-models* — **Job items don't carry the job-yellow language, while yellow clutter crowds the pod.** DR-45 says job items share one yellow language (#ffc94d/#ffc629 with ink stripes) and no decorative clutter uses it. Spectrum inverts this. The two carry-and-place job items, the RX pod (coolbox #fbf3e2 with a teal lid) and the mirror boards (#dfe8f0 with a lilac rail), contain no job yellow. Meanwhile three non-job props use it: a #ffc94d office chair beside the desk (src/levels/spectrum.ts:18, x −4.4 z 4.6), a #ffc94d box by the entrance (:20, x −8.7 z 7.1), and #ffd66b crates from the clutter palette (:34 colors[1]). Two yellow crates sit right against the pod dock in the start and dock shots (01, 13, 52). The storeroom door knob and the tea mug are also #ffc94d. A first-time player scanning for 'the yellow thing' finds a chair and boxes. The pod is cream on a cream floor (norim luma 178 vs floor 207), so it relies only on its teal lid to stand out.
