### R5-113

**R5-113 | P1 | global | clarity | Gamepad: camera reset labelled RS but bound to Select/View, LS toggles survey unlabelled**

Found by: `hud-ui#5` (P1 clarity), `gap8-meta-settings-errors#1` (P1 playability). Batch: B2 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*hud-ui* — **Gamepad mapping disagrees with its labels: 'RS' is shown for camera reset, but RS-click does nothing and Back resets; L3 survey is never shown.** The action bar's camera button and the pause controls map both pair the reset-camera icon with an 'RS' pill (src/ui/screens.ts:55, :169). In code, reset is button 8 (Back/View) and survey is button 10 (L3) (src/game.ts:190). Button 11 (RS click) is unmapped. With an emulated pad, pressing RS after an orbit changed nothing (mean pixel diff 2.4, which is noise), while Back snapped the camera home (diff 76). Survey on L3 appears nowhere on the title, the pause map or the HUD. Sprint isn't listed for the pad either. Also, with a pad connected, the prompt pill still prints keyboard keys ('F Pick up the plug') while the action bar shows B (hud-ui-60d).

*gap8-meta-settings-errors* — **Gamepad camera reset is labelled RS, but RS does nothing; it is Select/View, and LS toggles the survey with no label.** The action bar's camera button shows a 'RS' pill (src/ui/screens.ts:55), and so does the pause-menu controls map (src/ui/screens.ts:169). Game.pollPad maps pad buttons as {8:'camera',10:'survey'} (src/game.ts:190). In the standard Gamepad mapping, 8 is Back/Select/View, 10 is the left-stick click and 11 (RS) is the right-stick click. RS is unbound. I tested with a fake standard-mapping pad injected through navigator.getGamepads. Pressing button 11 left the orbited, zoomed-in view unchanged (shot 71). Button 10 threw the camera into the survey (shot 72). Button 8 reset to the home view (shot 73). So a pad player who follows the HUD gets nothing, and a player who clicks the left stick by accident (common while sprinting) is thrown into the survey without knowing why. The survey has no pad label anywhere on the HUD or in the pause map.

**Evidence.**

### R5-114

**R5-114 | P1 | lunch | clarity | Lunch: the water short plays the success chime and ticks "Mop up the leak" / "Power the feed post" when a failing cable is merely plugged in**

Found by: `lunch-teach#5` (P1 clarity), `gap4-juice-audio#4` (P1 teaching). Batch: R-lunch (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*lunch-teach* — **The job card ticks off 'Power the feed post' and 'Mop up the leak' when a failing cable is merely plugged in, then tells the player to 'keep the oven on' while it is dead.** kitchenFed() (src/ui/objectives.ts:19) is true when any cable has 'kitchen' in its ports, is closed and is not dead. It does not check that the post has power. Step 2 ('Mop up the leak (or bridge it)', :43) and step 3 ('Power the kitchen's feed post', :44) are both done when kitchenFed is true, and steps latch forever (:100-103).
Two reproduced cases:
(1) A thin cable into the post. Step 3 ticks and the card moves to 'Keep the oven on until the tray is baked'. Six seconds later the cable scorches, the oven goes off, and the card still says 'Keep the oven on…' (shot 13; log 'thin+6.3' shows oven:off).
(2) The thick cable through the un-mopped leak. Cart B shorts at the moment of plugging, yet steps 2 and 3 both tick (the leak step is skipped while the leak is the very cause). The card reads 'Keep the oven on until the tray is baked' with water still at 1.0 (shots 16 and 17).
In the two most instructive failures of the room, the only text the player gets (AGENTS 2 allows just the card and prompt) congratulates them on the step that failed and points them past the cause. That directly undermines DR-28 (show the cause) and DR-42 (the card agrees with the world).

*gap4-juice-audio* — **Lunch water short plays the success plug chime and ticks 'Mop up the leak' and 'Power the feed post' as done, while Supply B is tripped and the puddle is still there.** I plugged the thick cable into the kitchen feed post through the unmopped leak, the documented short case. The audio log shows the full `plug()` success chime (two highpass clicks plus the rising 880/1109/1319 bells) and, in the same frame, the trip/short sound (75 Hz square plus lowpass noise). Two objective step-done bells (1175) follow.

The card in juice-audio-11 has moved to step 4, 'Keep the oven on until the tray is baked', with three dots green. The puddle is still on the floor, a red lightning-bolt scar sits at the leak, and Supply B is tripped (`tripped:true`, event `short`).

The cause is `kitchenFed` (src/ui/objectives.ts:19). It only checks that some cable has the 'kitchen' port, `lead.closed` and not `dead`. It doesn't check that the source is live or that the oven is on. Steps 2 and 3 (objectives.ts:43-44) both accept kitchenFed, and steps latch forever (objectives.ts:101-103). So a short teaches 'that worked', with two success chimes and a skipped step. The leak step will never come back even after the player resets the breaker into the same puddle.

This breaks DR-28 (the failure cause shown first) and DR-47 (state shown truthfully). The success and failure sounds collide on one event.

**Evidence.**

- `src/ui/objectives.ts:42-44`
- `src/ui/objectives.ts:100-103`

**Fix.**

*From lunch-teach:* Make kitchenFed mean 'powered': `g.lunch?.powered('oven')||g.lunch?.powered('kitchen-lamp')`, or route.source not tripped and lead not dead. Make step 2 done only on `water<.1 || (dry route: the feeding cable's lead.wet===false && powered)`.
Let the lunch steps un-latch while their condition is false and the next step's done() is false. Add an `unlatch?:boolean` field to Step and set it for steps 2 and 3, so that a scorch or short moves the dots back and the card shows the real current step again.

*From gap4-juice-audio:* 1. Change kitchenFed to require a live feed: `c.ports.includes('kitchen')&&c.lead.closed&&!c.lead.dead&&g.lunch.circuit.loads.find(l=>l.id==='oven')?.state==='on'`. Alternatively check that the cable's source port isn't tripped.
2. Make step 2 ('Mop up the leak') depend only on water<.1 or a bridge being present over the leak, not on kitchenFed.
3. In lunch-runtime.ts:156, play only the mechanical click at connect (`noise` ×2, no bells). Play the bell part one circuit step later, and only if no trip or short event fired for that source. Otherwise let the trip sound stand alone.

### R5-115

**R5-115 | P1 | observatory | clarity | Observatory: the scope shows a green S/N and "Decodes" while 40–50% of characters are junk and the log is going to fail**

Found by: `observatory-play#0` (P1 clarity), `observatory-teach#6` (P1 clarity). Batch: R-observatory (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*observatory-play* — **Scope shows a green S/N and a perfect decode while the log is going to fail (tone level is ignored on screen).** The scope's decode line is the feedback the player trusts most. Its colour and the decoded text are driven by S/N only. The judge also requires the tone level to be at least 50% (SPEC.minLevel). If the player turns a shunt capacitor too far (easy with the drag knob, see the knob finding), the noise and the message both collapse. S/N then rises (34 dB in my run), the S/N reads GREEN, the decoder prints a perfect 'CQ CQ DE PIP', and the panel's 'Signal/noise' row is green. Only one small grey row, 'Tone level 7%', is red. The player presses LOG, which counts a mistake (damage, and the 'No failed decode' star is lost), and gets 'The tone itself is down to 7%…'. This contradicts the screen they just read. It teaches the wrong lesson, that the screen lies, and it punishes trusting the main visual. It breaks DR-31 (displayed values must match the judged state), DR-47 (device state on the device) and DR-42 (the prompt shows '← → Turn the knob', not why).

*observatory-teach* — **The decoder readout and the verdict disagree: 'Decodes' is shown while 40–50 % of the characters are junk, and the win screen ends on a garbled message.** decoded() garbles each character with probability (12 − S/N)/12 (logic.ts:247-248). judge() says 'Decodes' from 6 dB (logic.ts:172-176). So at 7.1 dB the toast says '“DOME OPEN” · Decodes', while the scope's decode line shows about 41 % junk. At 6 dB, half the characters are junk.
In the shortcut run, the final win frame shows the scope reading '%TAR% ?LE?R' with the confetti (shot 17). The payoff message is unreadable at the moment of victory, contradicting the 'Decodes' verdict and the success sound.
The player can't tell which to believe, the readout or the toast. That muddies the threshold idea (S/N decides whether a message gets through), which is the core concept of the room.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:269-271` (decode colour and text use r.snr only)
- `src/stations/observatory/logic.ts:247-252` (decoded() depends only on snr)
- `src/stations/observatory/logic.ts:171` (judge fails on level < SPEC.minLevel)
- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:359` (panel S/N row ok-colour ignores level)
- [observatory-play-63-tab-at-bench.jpg](shots/observatory-play-63-tab-at-bench.jpg) (S/N 34.2 dB green, 'CQ CQ DE PIP' clean, Tone level 7%)
- [observatory-play-62-dragging-knob.jpg](shots/observatory-play-62-dragging-knob.jpg)
- `tools/observatory-play/04-mouse.mjs` log: 'The decode fails: The tone itself is down to 7%'
- [verify-observatory-play-02-shunt68u-rerouted.jpg](shots/verify-observatory-play-02-shunt68u-rerouted.jpg)
- [verify-observatory-play-03-shunt68u-scope-crop.jpg](shots/verify-observatory-play-03-shunt68u-scope-crop.jpg) (S/N 34.2 dB green, clean CQ CQ DE PIP)
- [verify-observatory-play-04-shunt68u-log-fail.jpg](shots/verify-observatory-play-04-shunt68u-log-fail.jpg) (fail toast while the scope still reads clean)
- `src/ui/ui.css:225` (.no is grey ink-2; .bad is red #c0392b)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-play/01-logic.mjs` output: read(68µF) snr 34.2, level 0.072, decoded 'CQ CQ DE PIP', judge tier 0
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-play/03-knob-f0.mjs` output: panel row classes ok:Signal/noise, no:Tone level (grey)
- `src/stations/observatory/logic.ts:247-252`
- `src/stations/observatory/logic.ts:172-176`
- [observatory-teach-17-win-push.jpg](shots/observatory-teach-17-win-push.jpg)
- [observatory-teach-12-job2-single-cap-3u3.jpg](shots/observatory-teach-12-job2-single-cap-3u3.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-teach/num.mjs:` snr 7.1 junk frac 0.41
- [verify-observatory-teach-05-win-push.jpg](shots/verify-observatory-teach-05-win-push.jpg)

**Fix.**

*From observatory-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep the proposed fix, and also emit the 'bad' class (red) rather than 'no' (grey) for failing rows in updatePanel (station.ts:353-360), or restyle .station-panel .build li.no in ui.css:225 to red. Apply the level-based garble only when r.level < SPEC.minLevel. Otherwise a level just above 0.5 would print a garbled decode while LOG rates Reliable.

Reviewer's fix: In station.ts drawScope(), compute `ok = r.snr>=SPEC.reliableSnr && r.level>=SPEC.minLevel && (!j.latch||r.latchOk) && (!j.beacon||r.antenna>=.3)` and colour the decode line from that. When r.level < SPEC.minLevel, print the decode faded with dropped letters, e.g. pass `snr=min(r.snr, dB(r.level/SPEC.minLevel)+SPEC.decodeSnr)` into decoded(), so a weak tone garbles visibly, and draw the TONE bar at the left in red with a 'too quiet' icon. In updatePanel(), mark the Signal/noise row ok only when the level also passes. Apply the same rule in logic.ts decoded(): add a `level` argument and garble when level < SPEC.minLevel.

*From observatory-teach:* Make the readout follow the same thresholds. In logic.ts decoded(): bad = snr ≥ reliableSnr ? 0 : snr ≥ decodeSnr ? 0.12*(reliableSnr−snr)/(reliableSnr−decodeSnr) : 0.5 + 0.5*min(1,(decodeSnr−snr)/12). That gives a clean message above 12 dB, an occasional single flicker between 6 and 12 dB, and mostly junk below 6 dB.
After a successful LOG, freeze the decode line on the logged message for that job: store `this.logged[i].message` and draw it in green on the scope until the next job's first change.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *observatory-play:* Add a test to tests/station-observatory.spec.ts: shunt C at 68 µF, rerouted. Expect the scope decode not to equal the message (expose `decodedText` in snapshot()) and the S/N row class to be 'no'. Retake observatory-play-63 (a 68 µF shunt): the decode line must be red or garbled.
- *observatory-teach:* Unit tests: decoded('STARS CLEAR',7,e) has ≤ 2 junk characters over 20 epochs, and decoded(…,3,e) has ≥ 5. Re-run b.mjs: the win shot shows 'STARS CLEAR'.

**Rules:** DR-11, DR-28, DR-31, DR-42, DR-47

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced it. With a 68 µF shunt C, the cable rerouted and the cart 7.97 m away, the scope reads 'S/N 34.2 dB' in green and decodes a clean 'CQ CQ DE PIP'. The panel's Signal/noise row has class 'ok' (green). LOG then fails with 'The tone itself is down to 7%…' and mistakes goes to 1. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-116

**R5-116 | P1 | spectrum | clarity | Spectrum: the LINK monitor says "TOO WEAK" when the beam simply misses the pod, pointing the player at power instead of aim**

Found by: `spectrum-play#11` (P1 clarity), `spectrum-teach#7` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-spectrum (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*spectrum-play* — **The LINK monitor says 'TOO WEAK' when the beam simply misses the pod, which invites the player to turn the power up.** When the aimed beam misses the pod (here the tower is aimed at the mirror, which still faces the tower), read() sets margin −Infinity. The LINK screen's status ladder has no 'missed' case: !podOk, then !detectorOk, then blocked, then m&lt;works gives 'TOO WEAK'. So it prints 'no signal' plus 'TOO WEAK' (shot 33; crop 99), while the right panel correctly says 'Path: misses the pod'. 'Too weak' points a new player at the POWER keys, the wrong fix, and the two readouts contradict each other.

*spectrum-teach* — **A beam that misses the pod shows 'TOO WEAK' on the link screen, which points the player to power when the real problem is aim.** When the aimed beam misses (route.missed), read() sets the margin to −Infinity (logic.ts:244). drawLink's status chain has no missed case, so it falls through to `m&lt;SPEC.works` and prints 'TOO WEAK' in red (station.ts:338). Shot 13 shows the conflict: the panel says 'Path: misses the pod', the prompt says 'Aim, or another band', and the big link screen says TOO WEAK. The cause of a miss is geometry (angle in = angle out), but the biggest readout calls it a strength problem. The 1/10/100 mW keys sit right beside it, inviting a wrong fix that can never work.

### R5-117

**R5-117 | P1 | arcade-rush | clarity | Bench mistakes are invisible until the result card: the HUD damage tally reads 0 while mistakes climb to 7**

Found by: `arcade-rush-play#10` (P1 clarity). Batch: R-arcade (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Station mistakes (fuse trips, tier-0 runs, pops) are added to `game.damage` only inside `win()`. During the whole shift the HUD damage tally reads '0' and stays hidden, even when `station.mistakes` is 7 and `trips` is 5. The player gets no running signal that their experiments are graded, until the result card at the end. That breaks the Good Job loop of seeing the bill tick up. It also hides the cause of the lost 'Fuse tripped no more than once' bonus, except through a tiny star colour on the job card.

**Evidence.**

- `mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s3-wrong.mjs` log: tally '2:38 / 0 / 0' while mis 7 trips 5
- [arcade-rush-play-33-100-live.jpg](shots/arcade-rush-play-33-100-live.jpg) (HUD shows only the clock)
- `src/game.ts:353` (mistakes added to damage only at win)
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:165` (tally uses g.damage)
- [verify-arcade-rush-play-03-hud-after-trip.jpg](shots/verify-arcade-rush-play-03-hud-after-trip.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v1-bench.mjs` log: 'hud tallies tally:false:2:53 || tally:true:0 || tally:true:0' with mis 1, and tally '2:32 / 0 / 0' at mis 3

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** When showing g.damage+station.mistakes live, stop adding once g.won is true. win() already folds the mistakes into g.damage (game.ts:353), so a naive sum would show double on the result frame. Alternatively, have win() stop adding them and always show the sum.

Reviewer's fix: In `src/ui/game-ui.ts:165`, display `g.damage+(g.station?.score().mistakes??0)` and `g.cost+(g.station?.score().cost??0)`, so the tallies pop as they rise. Also give the bench fuse a visible tally: a small row of 3 pips on the fuse plate that turn red per trip, matching the bonus.

**Verify.**

- At the bench, trip the fuse once. The HUD damage tally appears with '1' and animates. Screenshot crop of the HUD.

**Rules:** AGENTS 6, DR-41, DR-47

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced it. After the prompted P trip (mistakes 1, trips 1), the HUD tallies were 'tally:true:0 || tally:true:0', meaning the damage and cost boxes stayed hidden at 0. They stayed that way through mistakes 3. g.damage only gets station mistakes inside win() (game.ts:353), and the tallies read g.damage and g.cost (game-ui.ts:165).

### R5-118

**R5-118 | P1 | meeting | clarity | Joining the coupler and second reel makes no visible change to the cable**

Found by: `cable#5` (P1 clarity). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The clean Meeting route is the only place the game teaches 'join two leads to get more length'. When the coupler and then the extension reel are attached (attachNear, src/game.ts:233-236; or E with a held part, :207), both props are consumed (`consume(p)` hides them). rope.maxLength jumps from 23.2 to 37.2 m, and the only feedback is a confetti burst and the HUD bar dropping from about 60% to about 35%.

The cable stays one seamless hose from the server-closet reel (cable-71 → cable-72 → cable-73). There's no second reel, no joint, and no new section. After the join, the server reel's spool reads against 37.2 m of capacity it doesn't hold (cable-74).

The player can't see why the cable now reaches, or that it is two cables. That works against AGENTS 4 (finite length readable) and DR-26 (concept taught by a visible physical act), and against DR-46 (cable state readable without text).

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:207`
- `src/game.ts:233-236`
- `src/game.ts:292`
- [cable-71-mt-mailcart-close-before.jpg](shots/cable-71-mt-mailcart-close-before.jpg)
- [cable-73-mt-extension-attached.jpg](shots/cable-73-mt-extension-attached.jpg)
- [cable-74-mt-reel-spool-after-ext.jpg](shots/cable-74-mt-reel-spool-after-ext.jpg)

**Fix.**

Make the join physical and visible.

1. Don't hide the extension reel. On attach, snap it to the plug's current point and record `joinAt = rope.length` (the arc length where the leads meet).
2. In drawCable, draw a coupler mesh (the coupler prop's model, oriented by the curve tangent) at `curve.getPointAt(min(1, joinAt/len))`.
3. Tint the section past the joint differently: a second jacket colour, or the thick cable's ink bands at a narrower spacing (hoseGeometry's `bands`).
4. Drive two spools:
   - The server reel shows `left = 1 − min(len, 23.2)/23.2`.
   - The extension reel, either carried along at the joint or left on the mail cart with a lead, shows its own 14 m.

**Verify.**

- Rerun mockups/review5/tools/cable/mt2.mjs. In cable-73, a coupler joint and a differently striped section must be visible at Pip's position. Then walk 10 m on: the joint stays at the attach spot and only the extension's spool shrinks. Update the spec 'holding the plug, F at the mail cart…' to assert that a joint position is in the snapshot.

**Rules:** AGENTS 4, DR-26, DR-46

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — attachNear (game.ts:233-236) and the held-part path (game.ts:207) call consume(), which hides the prop and disables its body, then set rope.maxLength=level.length+14. In cable-71 the yellow extension reel is in Pip's hand. In cable-73 it is gone and the hose is one seamless white cable, with only the HUD bar dropping.

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#3` (P1 clarity). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The Lunch fail path reuses `g.won=true` to stop play (src/lunch-runtime.ts:285). PipRig keys its celebration pose off `won`:
- the bounce at src/render/pipRig.ts:57;
- both arms thrown overhead and waving at :77;
- the head tilted up at :88;
- Game turns Pip to face the camera at src/game.ts:407.

So at the moment lunch spoils, Pip cheers with arms up in the power room. Screenshot juice-audio-12 shows it: arms raised and bouncing, the failed fridge a small icon far up-frame. The groans say failure; Pip's body says success.

winAt is set only in win() (game.ts:350), so the push-in camera (game.ts:369) doesn't run for a fail. The cause (the fridge at (−5.3,−2.1), or the oven) stays wherever it happened to be, often off-screen. The DR-11 framing rule (keep Pip in frame with the machine) is broken in the fail case. DR-28 (the cause shown in the world first) is weakened.

**Evidence.**

- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:285`
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:57`
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:77`
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:88`
- `src/game.ts:369`
- `src/game.ts:407`
- [juice-audio-12-lunch-spoil-instant.jpg](shots/juice-audio-12-lunch-spoil-instant.jpg)
- [juice-audio-13-lunch-spoil-card.jpg](shots/juice-audio-13-lunch-spoil-card.jpg)
- [verify-gap4-juice-audio-12-lunch-spoil-instant.jpg](shots/verify-gap4-juice-audio-12-lunch-spoil-instant.jpg)
- `src/game.ts:411` (won:this.won fed to rig)

**Fix.**

1. Add `failed=false` to Game. In lunch-runtime.ts:285 set `g.failed=true` alongside won, and set `g.winAt=performance.now()` with `g.winFocus` pointing at the fail spot `at`.
2. In PipRig.update take a `failed` flag. Use a slump pose: arms down and slightly forward (lx=rx≈-.3), head pitch +.35 (looking down), no bounce, and one squash of .3. Optionally play a head-shake (yaw sin(t*10)*.25 for 0.6 s).
3. Stop the face-camera turn at game.ts:407 when failed, or turn Pip toward the fail spot instead.

**Verify.**

- Re-run mockups/review5/tools/juice-audio/lunch.mjs part C. In juice-audio-12, Pip is slumped (arms below shoulders), and the fridge sits inside the centre 70% of the frame together with Pip before the card drops.

**Rules:** DR-11, DR-28

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — lunch-runtime.ts:285 sets g.won=true on failure. game.ts:411 passes won:this.won to the rig, and pipRig.ts:57/77/88 apply the bounce, arms overhead and head-up pose. winAt stays 0, so there's no push-in (game.ts:369), and game.ts:407 turns Pip to the camera. My reproduction (verify-12) shows Pip in the power room with both arms raised. The fridge is a tiny sad-face badge at the top edge.

### R5-120

**R5-120 | P1 | global | clarity | The same sound is used for different faults: overload trip = water short, arcade PTC trip = garage dead short, and every bench 'doesn't work' is one 160 Hz buzz**

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#5` (P1 clarity). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The audio palette doesn't separate fault types, so sound can't teach what went wrong (DR-28, DR-47).
- The Meeting overload trip (src/meeting-strip.ts:82) is byte-identical to the Lunch overload trip and the Lunch water short. lunch-runtime.ts:264 handles both `trip` and `short` in one branch: `tone(75,.25,.1,'square')` plus `noise(.25,.1,300)`. Logs: Meeting [projector E -> TRIP] gives s75@.1 and Nlowpass300@.1. Lunch [SHORT] gives the same pair. An overloaded breaker and a short through water are opposite lessons (too many loads vs. a low-resistance path), yet they sound the same.
- The arcade PTC trip (arcade/station.ts:290: noise bandpass 1800 plus 120 Hz square .35 s plus groan) is the same as the garage dead-short fuse (garage/station.ts:238: noise bandpass 1800 plus 120 Hz square .3 s plus groan). Logs: arcade [FUSE TRIP] and garage [FUSE SHORT] match.
- Every tier-0 verdict uses `tone(160,.25,.06,'square')` plus `voice('groan',1)`: garage TEST fail (garage/station.ts:225), observatory log (observatory/station.ts:195), spectrum send (spectrum/station.ts:231) and QFN CHECK (qfn/station.ts:281). This covers a spike reset, a weak signal, a missed pad and a bad layout alike.
- Beyond the trip itself there is no 'machine powering down' sound. The projector, kettle and heater in Meeting, and the oven and lamps in Lunch, go dark silently.

**Evidence.**

- `src/meeting-strip.ts:82`
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:264`
- `src/stations/arcade/station.ts:290`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:238`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:225`
- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:195`
- `src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:231`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:281`
- juice-audio meeting.mjs, lunch.mjs, arcade.mjs, garage.mjs logs
- verify-gap4-juice-audio meeting.mjs [projector E -> TRIP] and lunch.mjs [SHORT] logs
- spectrum fail is at station.ts:232 (not 231)

**Fix.**

Add named fault cues in src/render/audio.ts and use them at the call sites:
- `breakerTrip()`: a heavy clack (lowpass noise 300 at .1), then a descending 'power-down' whirr (sawtooth 220→55 over .6 s, lowpass 800, vol .05) for each load that drops.
- `short()`: a sharp zap/crackle (highpass noise 4000 .08 s at .14, plus 3 random 2–3 kHz square blips over 0.15 s), and with water a hiss (highpass 6000 noise .5 s at .04).
- `ptcTrip()`: a tick plus a rising thermal hum, distinct from the garage `fuseBang()`.
- `verdictFail(kind)`: pitch or timbre per kind (reset = robot 'bonk' sweep, weak = falling sine, layout = double buzz).

In lunch-runtime.ts:264 branch on event.kind ('short' → short(), 'trip' → breakerTrip()). Use breakerTrip() in meeting-strip.ts:82.

**Verify.**

- Re-run the juice-audio scripts. Meeting trip, Lunch short and Lunch overload (thin cable to oven plus fridge) produce three different signatures, and arcade and garage fuse logs differ. A blind listen test: name the fault from the sound alone.

**Rules:** DR-28, DR-47

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — meeting-strip.ts:82 and lunch-runtime.ts:264 both play tone(75,.25,.1,'square') + noise(.25,.1,300). Lunch uses one branch for 'trip' and 'short'. Arcade trip at :290 (bandpass1800 + 120 Hz square .35) and garage tripFuse at :238 (bandpass1800 + 120 Hz square .3) are near-identical. Tier-0 verdicts at garage:225, observatory:195, spectrum:232 and qfn:281 all use tone(160,.25,.06,'square').

### R5-122

**R5-122 | P1 | meeting | clarity | The grab cue is built flat and then rotated upright, so the 'floor brackets' stand vertically as floating yellow L shapes with half of them buried in the floor**

Found by: `meeting-models#4` (P1 clarity). Batch: R-meeting (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The grab cue is meant to be "four floor-level corner brackets around whatever E would take" (game.ts:96 comment). Each bracket is built as a horizontal slab, `BoxGeometry(w,.03,d)` placed at (x,0,z) in an x-z ring (game.ts:97). Then game.ts:99 also sets `this.reticle.rotation.x=-Math.PI/2`. R_x(-90°) maps (x,0,z) to (x,z,0), so the whole cue stands up as a vertical picture frame through the target at y .03 (game.ts:436). The two lower brackets go to y≈-.5 under the floor, and the two upper ones stand about 0.5 m up in mid-air, facing one world axis regardless of the camera. In the shots they show as stray yellow L sticks next to beanbags, plants and desks (meeting-models-23, -25, -47, -48, -21, and crops -62, -65). From most yaws they are edge-on and invisible. The cue is one of the few allowed world-UI elements (AGENTS 2), and the only way to tell which of 300 props E will take (DR-18), so it has to read. As built, it reads as a modelling glitch, or as part of the prop.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:96-97`
- `src/game.ts:99`
- `src/game.ts:436`
- [meeting-models-23-lounge.jpg](shots/meeting-models-23-lounge.jpg)
- [meeting-models-25-lounge-back.jpg](shots/meeting-models-25-lounge-back.jpg)
- [meeting-models-47-clock-close.jpg](shots/meeting-models-47-clock-close.jpg)
- [meeting-models-62-crop-plant-in-boxstack.jpg](shots/meeting-models-62-crop-plant-in-boxstack.jpg)
- [meeting-models-65-crop-reticle-vertical.jpg](shots/meeting-models-65-crop-reticle-vertical.jpg)
- [verify-meeting-models-06-beanbag-reticle.jpg](shots/verify-meeting-models-06-beanbag-reticle.jpg)
- [verify-meeting-models-03-pod-close-orbit.jpg](shots/verify-meeting-models-03-pod-close-orbit.jpg)
- [verify-meeting-models-07-beanbag-reticle-orbit.jpg](shots/verify-meeting-models-07-beanbag-reticle-orbit.jpg)
- [meeting-models-25-lounge-back.jpg](shots/meeting-models-25-lounge-back.jpg) (upright L by the desk leg)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Deleting the rotation line is the correct core fix. For the footprint scaling: game.ts:436 already calls reticle.scale.setScalar(1+sin(...)*.1) every frame, so a static per-axis scale would be overwritten. Compute `const k=1+Math.sin(this.last*.008)*.1; reticle.scale.set(fx*k,1,fz*k)`, with fx and fz taken from the marked prop's prefab size.

Reviewer's fix: Delete `this.reticle.rotation.x=-Math.PI/2;` from game.ts:99 (the brackets are already horizontal). Keep `reticle.position.set(mark.x,.03,mark.z)`. Scale the bracket ring to the prop footprint: `reticle.scale.set(max(.6,size[0]+.2)/1.06, 1, max(.6,size[2]+.2)/1.06)` from prefabs[kind].size, so the corners hug the base of big props like the desk and sofa instead of hiding under them. Optionally give the brackets a thin INK under-stroke (a slightly larger black copy at y .02) so they read on the pale floors.

**Verify.**

- Retake meeting-models-23 and -47 with c.mjs and f.mjs. Four yellow L corners should lie flat on the floor around the beanbag or bin, with nothing standing vertically. Orbit 8 yaws (g.orbit ±175): the corners stay visible on the floor from every yaw.

**Rules:** AGENTS 2, DR-18

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The brackets are built flat as BoxGeometry(w,.03,d) at (x,0,z) (game.ts:97). game.ts:99 then sets reticle.rotation.x=-PI/2, which maps (x,0,z) to (x,z,0), so the frame stands vertically through the target at y .03. The lower corners end up under the floor and the upper ones about 0.5 m up. I reproduced this: in verify-06 there are two upright yellow L's above the beanbag, and in verify-03 an upright L beside a bin.

### R5-124

**R5-124 | P1 | observatory | clarity | Key prompt points at the wrong thing in jobs 2 and 3 and after the cart is set down**

Found by: `observatory-play#5` (P1 clarity). Batch: R-observatory (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The one-line prompt is the only how-to text the rules allow, and here it often names the wrong action.
(1) At the start of job 2 it says '← → Turn the knob' for the shunt capacitor left over from job 1. My sweep shows no shunt-C value can pass job 2: S/N peaks at 12.3 dB at 10 µF, but the tone drops to 44%, below the 50% minimum. The prompt steers the player into a dead end.
(2) At the start of job 3 (the antenna job) the prompt is still '← → Turn the knob'. It stays that way after fitting the 75 cm whip, until the whip is stood up, and never points at the rack or the whip, which are the job's subject.
(3) The scope also stays in SWITCH-ON mode from job 2 into job 3, so the signal spectrum the antenna job needs isn't shown.
(4) In the room, after the cart is set down, the card says 'Sit at the signal bench (E)' while the prompt says 'E Grab the cart', then 'E Grab the chair' (nearest-prop fallback).
In every case the prompt contradicts the card. Breaks DR-42 and DR-19.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:376-378` (fallback: knobSlot ? 'Turn the knob' : 'Take a can')
- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:199` (log advances job but keeps scopeMode)
- `src/ui/objectives.ts:70,82-83` (station.prompt returns null off-bench → nearest prop)
- `tools/observatory-play/02-wrong.mjs` log 'job2 shunt-C only sweep … [1e-5,12.3,0.44]'
- [observatory-play-16-log1.jpg](shots/observatory-play-16-log1.jpg) (job 2 starts: 'Turn the knob')
- [observatory-play-21-log2-gust.jpg](shots/observatory-play-21-log2-gust.jpg) (job 3 starts in SWITCH-ON view, prompt 'Turn the knob')
- [observatory-play-23-r75-flat.jpg](shots/observatory-play-23-r75-flat.jpg)
- [observatory-play-09-cart-set-down.jpg](shots/observatory-play-09-cart-set-down.jpg) (card: Sit at bench; prompt: Grab the cart)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-play/01-logic.mjs` output f5: [3.3e-6,7.1,0.83,tier1] … [1e-5,11,0.44,tier0]
- [observatory-play-103-cart-dropped-zoom9.jpg](shots/observatory-play-103-cart-dropped-zoom9.jpg) (card 'Sit at the signal bench (E)', prompt 'Grab the bean bag')
- [observatory-play-21-log2-gust.jpg](shots/observatory-play-21-log2-gust.jpg)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Reword subclaim 1: 'no shunt-C value reaches Reliable in job 2'. The 'can this knob reach tier ≥2?' check stays valid; use solutions(job,{cartDistance}) filtered on the other slot.

Reviewer's fix: In station.ts prompt():
- For a beacon job with r.antenna<.3, return {key:'Click',text:'Fit a whip'} until a rod other than the start rod is fitted, then {key:'O',text:'Stand the whip up'} when !vertical.
- For a latch job when the series slot is empty, return {key:'1–3',text:'Take a can'} rather than the knob.
- Only offer 'Turn the knob' when turning that knob can change the verdict. Cheap test: does any value of that slot's kind, with the other slot fixed, reach the reliable tier? Use logic.solutions() filtered by slot.
- In act('log') success, reset `this.scopeMode='signal'` and `this.knobSlot=undefined` when the job index advances.
- Off-bench, return {key:'E',text:'Work at the bench'} only near it. Otherwise return null once cartMoved, and make objectives.ts skip the nearest-prop fallback in station rooms when the current step's `at()` is the bench (show nothing; the marker leads).

**Verify.**

- Extend tests/station-observatory.spec.ts. After log 1, expect `.prompt-pill` not to contain 'Turn the knob'. After log 2, expect snapshot().station.scope==='signal' and the prompt to contain 'whip'. Retake observatory-play-09/16/21.

**Rules:** DR-19, DR-42

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Subclaims 2, 3 and 4 are confirmed. Shot 21 shows job 3 starting in SWITCH-ON with '← → Turn the knob': the scopeMode is kept (station.ts:199) and the fallback is station.ts:378. Shots 09 and 103 show 'Grab the cart' and 'Grab the bean bag' while the card says 'Sit at the signal bench'. Subclaim 1 is partly wrong.

Found by: `progression#7` (P1 clarity). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

`requires` is only checked by the lobby door (src/hub/lobby.ts:73, :121, :132). On a fresh profile, the title's Jobs board lists 03R Arcade Rush as playable, and Play launches it (`progression-17`: the Play button aria-label is 'Play 03R Arcade Rush' with no progress at all). playSelected/the data-job click (src/ui/game-ui.ts:77, :99) never check it, and `?level=arcade-rush` also loads straight in. Where the lock does apply, it opens on any result: with Arcade seeded at grade C, the Rush door opened and the lobby's job card and bouncing marker named '03R · Arcade Rush' as the next job, ahead of 04 Garage (`progression-19`, `progression-21`). The cause is that `nextUnfinished` and the lobby steps walk `levels` in order, and Rush is a required step there (src/hub/lobby.ts:41-43). The intent is 'unlocked once the station is understood' (docs/EXPANSION_PLAN.md audit table). In practice a player who scraped a C is pushed into a timed version of the job they just struggled with, before the next new job. 'Finish every job' (src/hub/lobby.ts:45) also requires Rush, so the optional mode is mandatory for the hub's bonus.

**Evidence.**

- `src/hub/lobby.ts:73`
- `src/hub/lobby.ts:132`
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:77`

- `src/levels/arcade.ts:31`

- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-progression/rush-lock.mjs` ('go label Play 03R Arcade Rush'; 'url ...?level=arcade-rush screen play'; 'rush? true'; doors arcade-rush [false,false]; 'lobby card 03R · Arcade Rush')
- [verify-progression-05-jobs-rush-selected-fresh.jpg](shots/verify-progression-05-jobs-rush-selected-fresh.jpg)

**Fix.**

(1) Add `export const isLocked=(l:Level)=>!!l.requires&&!(bestFor(l.requires)&&bestFor(l.requires)!.grade<='B')` to src/ui/store.ts, which unlocks at B or better. Use it in lobby.ts:73, in jobTag (src/ui/screens.ts:109, with a padlock overlay and a disabled Play), in GameUI.playSelected, and in main.ts boot, which redirects a locked `?level=` to the lobby. (2) Leave Rush out of the hub's required steps and out of 'Finish every job'. Add `optional:true` to Level, filter it in src/hub/lobby.ts:41 and :45, and in `nextUnfinished` (store.ts:19). Offer Rush as a bonus instead: 'Beat a Rush shift with 8 cabinets'.

**Verify.**

- Rerun mockups/review5/tools/progression/lobby-progress.mjs. On a fresh profile the Jobs board shows Rush with a padlock and Play does nothing. With Arcade at C, the Rush door stays locked and the marker points at 04 Garage. Add a case to tests/lobby.spec.ts: `page.goto('/?level=arcade-rush')` on a fresh profile lands in the lobby.

**Rules:** AGENTS 2, DR-42, DR-50

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced all three leaks. (a) On a fresh profile (localStorage cleared), the Jobs board selects 03R and Go's aria-label reads 'Play 03R Arcade Rush'. Clicking it navigated to ?level=arcade-rush, which loaded and ran with the Rush timer at 2:56 (verify-progression-06). (b) A direct URL loads, since `requires` is only read at src/hub/lobby.ts:73 and :132; there is no check in game-ui.ts:77/:99 or in boot.

### R5-127

**R5-127 | P1 | qfn | clarity | Bench prompt says 'Drag · Draw from a pad' while the board's first task is placement, and keeps saying it mid-drag**

Found by: `qfn-play#7` (P1 clarity). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

prompt() returns {Drag, 'Draw from a pad'} whenever any net is unjoined (station.ts:432). Each board starts with scrambled parts and a connector facing the wrong way: board 1's J1 at (10,1) rot 1 fails 'mouth out', and the ask says 'Place J1, R1 and C1'. Yet the only instruction line tells the player to draw first. Drawing first leads into dead ends on a one-layer board, because 'placement comes before routing' is the very lesson (logic.ts:80). While a part is being dragged by its body the prompt still reads 'Draw from a pad' (qfn-play-53). On board 3 the prompt never mentions vias or the thermal pad, even though the chip shows 135 °C.

**Evidence.**

- [qfn-play-14-bench-board1.jpg](shots/qfn-play-14-bench-board1.jpg)
- [qfn-play-53-drag-body.jpg](shots/qfn-play-53-drag-body.jpg)
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:428-434`
- `src/stations/qfn/logic.ts:80`
- [verify-qfn-play-11-mid-drag.jpg](shots/verify-qfn-play-11-mid-drag.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-qfn-play/v2-bench.mjs` log 'start prompt' and 'mid-drag'

**Fix.**

Order prompt() as follows. drag → {Drag,'Drop it on the board'}. Placement problems in the live report (mouth or off-board) → {Drag,'Move J1 to an edge, mouth out'}. Any part never moved yet on a fresh board → {Drag,'Slide the parts into place'}. Then the net, check, thermal ({V,'Cool the chip'} when thermal.temp>limit and the nets are done) and ship cases.

**Verify.**

- Start-of-board bench shot shows the placement prompt. A mid-drag screenshot shows 'Drop it on the board'.

**Rules:** DR-19, DR-42

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Reproduced. At board start the live problems list opens with 'J1 must sit on a board edge with its mouth facing out', yet the prompt reads 'Drag · Draw from a pad'. In the middle of a body drag of C1 (drag={id:C1}) the prompt still reads 'Draw from a pad' (verify-qfn-play-11). prompt() has no drag or placement branch (station.ts:428-434).

### R5-128

**R5-128 | P1 | qfn | clarity | 'Too long' (orange) and 'short enough' (green) decoupling loops look the same on the copper, and the failing panel row isn't red**

Found by: `qfn-teach#6` (P1 clarity). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

drawLoops (station.ts:223) draws each loop with an *additive* glow, '#7dffb0' (ok) or '#ffa040' (too long), at ×1.4, opacity .55, over copper that is already saturated red (VDD/VIN) and blue (GND). Additive colour on red or blue washes to pale cream, peach or lavender either way. In the crops, the 10-cell too-long loop (qfn-teach-05-loopcrop) is a peach stripe on red and lilac on blue; the 4-cell good loop (qfn-teach-30-loopcrop) is a cream stripe on red and pale cyan on blue. Without reading the panel, a first-time player can't tell which loop is bad. The beads are near-white in both states too (hot('#c8ffe0'|'#ffd0a0',2), station.ts:230). The panel doesn't help: a failing loop row uses class 'no', which styles the value in neutral ink-2 (src/ui/ui.css:225), so '10 cells · ≤ 4' looks like a normal stat (qfn-teach-07-b1-farcap-panel). Meanwhile 'Track + vias 22 · par 22' is also neutral, because the row is keyed on tier===3 (station.ts:418), not on cost ≤ par. On that board the cost *was* at par, so a met target looks unmet. The device-shows-its-state rule (DR-47) fails for the station's key visual.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:223`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:230`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:414`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:418`
- `src/ui/ui.css:225`
- [qfn-teach-05-loopcrop.jpg](shots/qfn-teach-05-loopcrop.jpg)
- [qfn-teach-30-loopcrop.jpg](shots/qfn-teach-30-loopcrop.jpg)
- [qfn-teach-07-b1-farcap-panel.jpg](shots/qfn-teach-07-b1-farcap-panel.jpg)
- `src/ui/ui.css:225` (li.bad already exists, red #c0392b)
- [qfn-teach-05-b1-farcap-check-beads.jpg](shots/qfn-teach-05-b1-farcap-check-beads.jpg) (panel: '10 cells · ≤ 4' neutral, '22 · par 22' neutral)

**Fix.**

Draw the loop as a normal-blended (not additive) outline *beside* the copper. Use two thin parallel strips offset ±0.045 from the track centreline, with an ink edge (outline on). Solid green #2fbf71 when ok; when too long, orange #ff7a1a with a slow 2 Hz pulse and a dashed pattern. Draw a small sad or happy face icon at the cap. Panel: give failing reliability rows class 'bad' (red, ui.css:225 already defines li.bad) instead of 'no'. Compute the par row's ok as `r.cost<=r.par`, independent of tier.

**Verify.**

- Retake qfn-teach-05 and qfn-teach-30 crops. In greyscale and in colour, the too-long loop reads orange or dashed and the good loop green or solid. Measure ΔE between the two loop strips: > 40. Panel crop: '10 cells · ≤ 4' renders red, '22 · par 22' green.

**Rules:** DR-43, DR-46, DR-47

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Confirmed. station.ts:223 uses additive blending (#7dffb0 vs #ffa040 ×1.4, opacity .55). In the crops, the 10-cell bad loop reads peach/lavender and the 4-cell good loop cream/pale cyan, which are hard to tell apart (qfn-teach-05-loopcrop vs qfn-teach-30-loopcrop). The beads are near-white in both states (station.ts:230).

### R5-129

**R5-129 | P1 | spectrum | clarity | After setting the pod or a mirror down, the prompt offers 'E · Pick up the pod/mirror' while the card says to go to the desk**

Found by: `spectrum-play#5` (P1 clarity). Batch: R-spectrum (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The moment the pod lands on the storeroom pad, the card moves to 'Sit at the dispatch desk (E)'. But Pip is still next to the pod, so the pill says 'E · Pick up the pod' (shot 10). The same happens after standing a mirror on mark A: the card says 'Delivery 2: Into the shuttered lab' while the pill says 'E · Pick up the mirror' (shot 28).

Both tell the player to press E. Pressing the key the pill shows undoes the step just completed: update() unparks the pod and clears podPad (station.ts:378-379). That is the 'prompt points at the nearest prop, not the current step' failure. It is especially confusing because the card's own instruction also ends in '(E)'.

**Evidence.**

- [spectrum-play-10-pod-on-store-pad.jpg](shots/spectrum-play-10-pod-on-store-pad.jpg)
- [spectrum-play-28-mirror-stood-A.jpg](shots/spectrum-play-28-mirror-stood-A.jpg)
- `src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:435` (pick-up prompt for any nearest pod or mirror)
- `src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:378-379` (picking it up unparks it)
- [verify-spectrum-play-04-pod-on-store-pad.jpg](shots/verify-spectrum-play-04-pod-on-store-pad.jpg)
- [verify-spectrum-play-11-mirror-stood-A.jpg](shots/verify-spectrum-play-11-mirror-stood-A.jpg)
- v1.mjs log 'mirror stood ui': pill 'E Pick up the mirror'

**Fix.**

In station.ts prompt(false):
- If the nearest grab is the pod and `this.podPad===this.current()?.pad`, return null, or `{key:'E',text:'Work at the desk'}` when near the desk.
- Likewise, if the nearest is a mirror parked on a mark in the current beam route, return null.
- Keep the pick-up prompt only when the pod sits on a wrong pad or loose.

Optionally also show a small parked tick over the pad for 1 s.

**Verify.**

- Retake shots 10 and 28. The prompt pill is empty, or points to the desk, and never offers to pick the just-placed item up again. Add a spec expecting the `.prompt-pill` text to not contain 'Pick up' right after podPad==='store'.

**Rules:** DR-19, DR-42

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced both cases. After setting the pod on the storeroom pad, the card reads 'Sit at the dispatch desk (E)' while the pill reads 'E Pick up the pod' (shot 04). After standing the mirror on A, the pill reads 'E Pick up the mirror' (v1 log). nearest() (game.ts:192) doesn't exclude parked fixed bodies, and prompt() returns a pick-up prompt for the nearest pod or mirror (station.ts:435).

### R5-130

**R5-130 | P1 | global, playground | overlap | The cable passes through light props (crates, plants, cones, bins), props past the 20-obstacle cap, and coworkers, so routing is not taught**

Found by: `cable#9` (P1 overlap), `playground-play#9` (P1 fun), `playground-models#24` (P2 visual-bug), `gap6-world-reacts#4` (P2 fun). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*cable* — **The cable lies through light props (plants, cones, bins) and through props past the 20-obstacle cap.** Only props with mass ≥ 3 that sit within 1.2 m of the current route, capped at the nearest 20, become cable obstacles (src/game.ts:273-274).

- Plants (mass 2), cones (1), bins (0.5), reels (2), mops, wedges and lamps under 3 are ignored outright.
- Light props are only shoved when strain > 0.88 (game.ts:333).

At normal strain the hose passes straight through plant pots and cones. In the dense Meeting and Playground, the 20-prop cap can also drop heavier props along a long route. playground-play-61 shows the taut cable passing through a beanbag (mass 4). The meeting boardroom glass front (decor.ts:144-145) is `solid` for Pip but isn't a cable obstacle, so the gold cable cuts through its corner rail (cable-67, cable-68).

*playground-play* — **Crates and other light props don't wrap the cable, so it clips through the 'obstacle course' and routing comes down to one pillar.** simulateCable only counts props with mass ≥3 as rope corners (src/game.ts:273). Crates (box mass 2), cones (1), bins (0.5) and plants (2) (src/props/prefabs.ts:10-14) never wrap. The playground's 'obstacle course' is mostly crates (src/levels/playground.ts:9-12, comment 'crate stacks … to drag the cable through'). In play, the taut cable passes straight through the crate stack at (8.2–8.9, 8.2–8.4) (shots 30, 51, 61) and through crates near Pip. The clean route has exactly one bend (pillar-a) (b-clean log bends:1). Because the rope is a taut visibility string, Pip's walked path doesn't matter unless it goes round a heavy prop, so 'route and wrap' (AGENTS 4, the cable is the star) is a single decision. The visual clipping also breaks DR-73.

*playground-models* — **The cable passes through dynamic props instead of draping over them.** The rope only wraps level.obstacles (the two pillars). Boxes, bookshelves and chairs are ignored by the rope path, so a dragged cable runs straight through a cardboard box (shot -61) and through tipped shelves. Combined with the hose's 20 cm thickness, this is very visible at the close camera, and it undercuts 'the cable is physical'.

*gap6-world-reacts* — **The cable passes straight through coworkers, and they don't notice.** Coworkers are not rope obstacles. The rope wraps only around `this.obstacles` plus furniture (src/game.ts:280), and npcs are never added. Dragging the Playground plug from spawn to (−6.3,−5.6) runs the cable straight through the teal trainee at (−6.6,−3.4): 0 bends, strain 0.53, alarmed 0 (world-reacts-24). The hose enters the blob's base and comes out behind it. Pip's own lack of collision with blobs is already reported. This is the cable side of the same problem, and it is a missed gag: in a Good Job–style game, the star object snagging a coworker's legs is the obvious joke, and the clean player would trigger it for free on the way to the socket. A blob can also never 'block the job' or 'help' it, since nothing ties the two systems together.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:333`
- `src/levels/decor.ts:144-145`
- `src/levels/meeting.ts:34-35`

**Fix.**

*From cable:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Besides nudging light props, let floor-standing boxes count as wrap obstacles: lower the filter to mass>=2 for kind 'box', or add a per-prefab `wrap:true` flag, and keep the y<1.8 test so stacked tops don't double count. Also include the height axis in the AABB (|e4|*h/2, |e6|*h/2) so tipped props keep their footprint. After adding the glass-front obstacles, rerun tests/routes.spec.ts. The Meeting single-reel and coupler routes have very thin length margins (see finding 10), and a corner wrap at x=11 adds length.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Light props: at any strain, apply a small lateral impulse (about 0.4 × dt × mass) pushing them perpendicular out of the hose when their centre is within 0.25 m plus half their size of a cable segment. The cable then nudges pots and cones aside.
2. Raise the furniture cap from 20 to 32, but only count props within 3 m of Pip or of an existing bend.
3. Add the two boardroom glass-front spans to `meeting.obstacles`, or let `solid()` take a `cable:true` flag that registers an Obstacle:
   - `{id:'glass-front-w', minX:9.3, maxX:11, minZ:-2.07, maxZ:-1.93}`
   - `{id:'glass-front-e', minX:13.8, maxX:16.5, minZ:-2.07, maxZ:-1.93}`

*From playground-play:* Lower the wrap threshold to mass ≥1.5 for props resting on the floor (y<0.8) in src/game.ts:273, so crates, plants and stacked boxes wrap. A crate can still be dragged by the strain impulse at game.ts:334, which gives the comedy of a cable hauling a crate round. Keep the 20-nearest cap for performance. Then rebuild the crate row and crate pile in playground.ts:11-12 as two deliberate 'chicanes' the clean route must go around, so the player makes two or three wrap decisions.

*From playground-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Scope the fix to light props (mass < 3), since heavier furniture is already wrapped. Either include boxes as wrap obstacles: lower the threshold to mass ≥2, or include them when they are not being dragged. Or keep the vertical drape lift for props below 3 kg only. The strain>.88 drag at game.ts:333 already pulls props of mass ≤15 along the rope, so a drape must not fight that.

Reviewer's fix: In drawCable(), after cablePath, lift hose points that fall inside a prop's AABB to that prop's top + hose radius + .02 (a drape). Take the AABB from prop.body.translation() and the prefab size; the cost is about 110 props × about 40 points per frame, which is cheap. Optionally, push light props (mass < 3) sideways when the taut cable sweeps through them, which also feeds the slingshot.

*From gap6-world-reacts:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Rope obstacles are AABBs (minX/maxX/minZ/maxZ) with corner wrapping, not circles, so add each standing npc as a 0.9×0.9 m box. Skip seated npcs, or the Meeting pods become cable mazes. Do not alarm on every contact at strain>0.3 every frame: throttle it to once per 0.7 s, as drawCable does.

Reviewer's fix: Add each npc as a round rope obstacle (radius 0.45 at the blob centre) in the obstacle list built at src/game.ts:280, so the cable wraps around blobs. When a rope segment is within 0.5 m of a blob and strain >0.3, set npc.alarm=1 and play a 'hop' (body.position.y += .25 for 0.2 s). At strain >0.95, tip the blob 20° in the direction of the pull. Seated blobs only wobble.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *cable:* Retake cable-67/68 (the meeting plug-in): the cable must enter through the doorway (x 11–13.8). Playground: drag the cable through the plant cluster by the north wall at strain 0.5. In a zoom-9 screenshot, no hose passes through a pot, and the pots have moved.
- *playground-play:* Close shot at the (8.2,8.3) stack while overstretched: the cable bends round the crate edge with no interpenetration. The b-clean log shows bends ≥2 on the clean route, and routes.spec playground still passes.
- *playground-models:* Drag the plug past the crate row at z 4.6 (routes.spec slingshot path) and take a zoom-9 shot. The cable rides over the boxes, and no hose section is hidden inside a box.
- *gap6-world-reacts:* Rerun blobcable.mjs. Expect snap().rope.bends ≥1 around the trainee, alarmed ≥1 within 0.5 s of contact, and world-reacts-24 to show the cable bending around the blob with the '!' bubble.

**Rules:** AGENTS 4, DR-73

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — In code, only props with mass>=3 enter the obstacle list (game.ts:273), and boxes are mass 2 (prefabs.ts:10). Light props are shoved only at strain>.88 (game.ts:333). The Meeting glass front is a physics collider only (decor.ts:144-145; solid() at decor.ts:21-24 creates no Obstacle), and meeting.obstacles (meeting.ts:34-35) lacks it. (4/4 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-131

**R5-131 | P1 | meeting, playground, arcade | overlap | Coworkers have no colliders: Pip walks straight through blobs and thrown props pass through them**

Found by: `meeting-play#8` (P1 overlap), `playground-models#4` (P1 overlap), `arcade-play#18` (P2 overlap). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*meeting-play* — **Coworkers have no colliders: Pip walks straight through blobs and thrown props pass through them.** addNpc builds coworkers as plain THREE groups with no Rapier body. Pip can stand inside a standing coworker: shot 85 shows the green coffee-corner blob's body wrapped around Pip's legs. Thrown props and slingshotted chairs fly through coworkers instead of bonking them.
In a physics-comedy office with 24 coworkers this throws away the cheapest slapstick there is (bumping a coworker, knocking a mug off a blob's head). It also looks broken: an interpenetration the player causes all the time on the dense desk aisles. The audit (game.ts audit) treats coworkers as 0.36 m balls for start overlap only, so the design already assumes they are solid.
This breaks DR-70 (nothing interpenetrates) and DR-04 (the world reacts to chaos). It also undercuts DR-03 (something funny happens in the first 30 s without looking for it).

*playground-models* — **Coworkers have no colliders: Pip walks into the trainees and their bodies clip through Pip.** addNpc() builds only a visual group. No Rapier body or collider is created, so Pip's character controller, thrown props and the cable all pass through the three trainees. Walking to the supply cage put Pip's centre 0.41 m from the teal trainee at (-6.6,-3.4). The blob's body visibly intersects Pip's arm and legs (shots -13 and -14), and the mug-holding arm sticks through Pip's torso. Thrown boxes fly through blobs instead of bonking them. That costs the 'world reacts to chaos' comedy and looks like a clipping bug in the first room a player sees. g.audit() cannot catch it because it only tests coworkers against fixed colliders and props at load.

*arcade-play* — **Pip walks into coworker blobs: NPCs have no colliders.** `addNpc` builds meshes only, with no Rapier body (game.ts:127-134). Walking to (−6.5,−5.8) put Pip inside the sleepy technician blob at (−6.5,−5.2). The blob and Pip's torso interpenetrate (shot 74). Thrown props also pass through coworkers instead of bonking them, which removes a natural slapstick beat and the world reaction (DR-04).

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:488-489` (audit uses Ball(.36) for coworkers)

**Fix.**

*From meeting-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Give the 2 standing coworkers a kinematic capsule (radius .34, half-height .3, centre y .65). For seated coworkers, do not add a separate body at the chair position. Either attach the blob's collider to the chair's own rigid body (as an extra collider), or use a sensor that only triggers the bonk and wobble and the alarm, so the chairs are not ejected. Rerun g.audit(0.02) and expect no new overlaps.

Reviewer's fix: In addNpc, create a fixed (or kinematicPositionBased) Rapier body with a capsule collider: half-height 0.3, radius 0.34, centred at y 0.65 (seated: y 1.0, radius 0.3). Register the collider handle on the Npc. In step(), use world contact events, or a cheap per-frame check of dynamic props within 0.6 m of each npc whose speed is above 2.5 m/s, to call this.alarm(npc.position, 1.2) and give the npc a 0.25 s squash-wobble. Pip bumping a blob at a sprint triggers the same. Coworkers should not count as damage.

*From playground-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The fix needs one more change. audit() (game.ts:497-498) tests each standing coworker's Ball(.36) against every fixed collider. Once NPCs get fixed colliders, each coworker will report an overlap with its own collider. Store the collider handle on the Npc and skip it in the audit, or tag NPC colliders and exclude them from the fixed list. A fixed body is fine, because NPCs never translate.

Reviewer's fix: In addNpc(), for standing NPCs, create a fixed rigid body at (p.x,.55,p.z) with ColliderDesc.capsule(.22,.33) (matching the blob capsule .33 radius and .35 length) and friction .5. For seated ones use a ball(.33) at the seat height. Store the collider on the Npc so the alarm() logic can also fire when a prop contacts it (a bonk reaction). The audit at game.ts:498 keeps working, since it then sees them as fixed colliders.

*From arcade-play:* In game.ts addNpc, create a fixed (or kinematic) capsule collider (radius 0.42, half-height 0.3, at y 0.6) per NPC. On contact with a prop moving faster than 3 m/s, call `this.alarm(npc.position,1.5)` and add a wobble.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

- *arcade-play:* Walk Pip into each arcade NPC: Pip stops at a centre distance ≥ 0.74 m. Throw a crate at a blob: `alarmed ≥ 1` within 0.5 s.

### R5-132

**R5-132 | P1 | lobby | overlap | Lobby: side-wall blade signs cut through the door title signs and lintels (L1 regression)**

Found by: `lobby-models#0` (P1 overlap), `lobby-play#7` (P2 overlap). Batch: R-lobby (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*lobby-models* — **REGRESSION (L1): side-wall blade signs cut through the door title signs and lintels, the bracket never reaches the wall, and every side door now carries its name twice.** The L1 fix (19deb71) added a blade sign over each of the three left-wall doors (05 Fabrication Bay, 06 Signal Observatory, 07 Spectrum Delivery). The blade group sits on game.root at world x = s.x+0.95 = -14.05, z = door z (src/hub/lobby.ts:82). Its parts collide with the door's own title plate:
- The grey post box(.06,.5,.06) sits at local x -0.62, which is world x -14.67, y 2.70-3.20.
- The lintel title plate (lobby.ts:92) is at side-wall-local z .30, which is world x about -14.70, y 2.25-2.86.
- So the post runs down through the middle of the title sign. The blade plate (1.7 m wide, 0.48 m tall, y 2.62-3.10, world x -14.90 to -13.20) also crosses the lintel rbox (world x -15.0 to -14.72, y 2.42-2.68) and the title plate.

On screen the post spears 'Signal Observatory' (lobby-models-18), the blade plate covers half of 'Fabrication Bay' (lobby-models-16, -44, -46), and from inside the room the post crosses the '05' digits (lobby-models-47).

The bracket also doesn't touch the wall. The wall face is at world x -14.875, the arm box(1.3,…) ends at local -0.65 (world -14.70) and the post is at -14.67, so the whole sign hangs about 17 cm off the wall (DR-72).

The plate is a single-sided MeshBasicMaterial facing world +z, so from the -z side it disappears and leaves a bare grey L-bracket. Each side door now shows its name twice ('05 · Fabrication Bay' on the blade, 'Fabrication Bay' on the lintel), which goes against DR-41's one-value-once rule.

This is the first thing a player sees on the left wall, and it reads as broken signage. It's a regression of the L1 fix listed in the re-check list.

*lobby-play* — **Side-door blade signs cut through the edge-on wall plate, so each side door has two signs, one unreadable.** Side doors still get the frame title plate on the wall (lobby.ts:92), which reads edge-on from the atrium, plus the newer blade sign (lobby.ts:82, group at s.x+.95, plate 1.7 m wide at y 2.86). The blade plate spans world x -14.9…-13.2 and passes through the wall plate at x about -14.7. The blade's first characters are hidden inside the edge-on plate ('6 · Signal Observatory' in lobby-play-40, and '07 · Spectrum Delivery' clipped by the 'Spectrum Deliv…' plate in lobby-play-16). Each side door shows a readable sign crossed with an unreadable one (lobby-play-10, -14). The bracket arm ends at x -14.7, short of the wall face, and reads as hanging in the air next to the lamp.

### R5-133

**R5-133 | P1 | lobby | overlap | Lobby: door leaves swing out through Pip (no collider, 1.66 m arc) and hide him at every side-wall door**

Found by: `lobby-models#2` (P1 overlap), `lobby-play#0` (P1 playability). Batch: R-lobby (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*lobby-models* — **Door leaves swing out into the lobby through Pip (no collider, outward arc 1.66 m, the approach point inside the arc).** Every job door opens on a spring when Pip comes within 2.6 m: d.leaf.rotation.y = -d.open*1.25 (src/hub/lobby.ts:130). The leaf (rbox 1.66×2.26, lobby.ts:90) is hinged at frame-local x -0.84, and the negative rotation swings it out into the lobby (+z).

The door's interaction point is at = door + 1.1 m (lobby.ts:77-78). It sits 0.84 m across and about 0.96 m out from the hinge, about 1.28 m away, which is inside the leaf's 1.66 m sweep. At intermediate angles near 0.9 rad the leaf passes straight through Pip's centre. At full open (1.25 rad) its line is still only 0.43 m from his centre.

The leaf has no collider, so in every 'Enter' shot it cuts through Pip's arm, back or hat:
- lobby-models-13: the leaf is at Pip's left arm.
- lobby-models-14: the leaf is behind and through Pip.
- lobby-models-18: the leaf passes through the hat.
- lobby-models-22: the leaf cuts Pip's right side.

This is the moment the hub is about, walking up to a door, and Pip clips through the leaf every time. It breaks DR-70 (nothing interpenetrates) and the spirit of DR-73 (nothing passes through Pip). The leaf's back face is also a blank white slab: no colour panel, number or knob (lobby-models-14, DR-63).

*lobby-play* — **Opening door leaves hide Pip at every side-wall door and half-hide Pip at back-wall doors.** When Pip walks up to a door, its leaf springs open (src/hub/lobby.ts:128-130, rotation.y = -open*1.25 about a hinge at local x -0.84, line 90). The leaf swings out into the lobby, toward the camera. On the three left-wall doors (Fabrication Bay, Signal Observatory, Spectrum Delivery) the hinge is on the camera side, so the open leaf sits between the camera and the spot where Pip has to stand (door.at = x+1.1). At the default camera only Pip's yellow ring shows: lobby-play-14 at QFN, lobby-play-15 at Spectrum, lobby-play-16 at zoom 9 (Pip is gone completely), and lobby-play-36 on a phone (a sliver of blue). On back-wall doors the leaf covers Pip's left half at the default yaw (lobby-play-31, Arcade Rush) and all of Pip after a small orbit (lobby-play-12, Playground door: only the leaf and the marker tip show). Leaves are not in game.occluders (src/game.ts:387-388 fades occluders only; lobby.ts never registers any), so nothing fades. This happens at the hub's one core moment, choosing a door: the player loses their avatar right when the prompt appears and can't see the portal glimpse that is meant to sell the destination. It breaks AGENTS 8 and DR-12. It also wastes the portal effect (DR-13: the target, the doorway, is hidden by its own door).

**Fix.**

*From lobby-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Option (a), swinging inward, isn't clean. A 1.66 m leaf turned +1.25 rad ends about 1.2 m behind the wall's back face, in the void outside the room. With the camera pitched up (pitch clamps to 1.25 rad) the leaf tops show above and behind the 3 m wall cap. Either clamp the inward swing to about 0.35 rad (the opaque portal already reads as 'open'), or hide the leaf when open > .3. Option (b), the barn door, also needs adjusting. A leaf at frame-local z .15-.23 collides with the medal at z .18 (x .91-1.25), so move the medal (finding 7). The rail at y 2.33-2.39, z .2 would cross the lower 6-12 cm of the lintel title plate, which hangs down to y 2.255 at z .16. Shrink or raise the title plate so its bottom is above 2.40 (for example h 64, centred at 2.66), or hang the rail behind the plate. Keep the spec idea: leaf world bounding box vs a 0.36 m sphere at Pip, approached from both sides.

Reviewer's fix: Pick one of these in src/hub/lobby.ts:
- **(a) Swing inward:** change :130 to d.leaf.rotation.y=+d.open*1.25. The leaf turns behind the opaque portal plane (z .05) and into the wall box, so it simply disappears into the corridor. That's the reading you want, and nothing sweeps the lobby. Optionally draw a leaf silhouette on the corridor's hinge-side wall in portal.ts's side-wall branch: darken where h.z > -1.66 and the hinge side matches.
- **(b) Barn door:** keep rotation 0. Slide d.leaf.position.x = -.84 + d.open*1.75. Move the leaf to z .19 so it clears the post fronts at z .13, and add a rail box(3.8,.06,.06) at (0.9, 2.36, .2).

With either option, also mirror the colour panel, the number plate and a second knob onto the leaf's -z face (DR-63). For example, part(leaf, box(1.3,.9,.02), toon(color), .83, 1.55, -.03) plus a signPlate rotated π.

*From lobby-play:* In src/hub/lobby.ts door() (line 90), stop the leaf from swinging into the camera's view. (a) Preferred: open every door inward, into the corridor. Use leaf.rotation.y=+open*1.25 in update() (line 130) and set leaf material depthTest so the wall hides it. The portal plane at z .05 already shows the corridor, so the leaf can simply hide once open>0.5 (leaf.visible=open<0.5) after a quick inward swing. (b) If the outward swing stays, mirror the hinge on side doors: leaf group at lx +0.84, leaf geometry offset -0.83, and rotation.y=+open*1.25, so the leaf opens toward world -z, behind Pip from a +z camera. Also push the leaf's meshes into game.occluders with a transparent clone of the glossyToon material, so the existing fade catches them. Also change the occlusion ray to sample feet, chest and head (DR-12), not only p.y+.4.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *lobby-play:* Rerun mockups/review5/tools/lobby-play/b-doors.mjs and retake lobby-play-14/15/16 and the phone shot 36. At least 70% of Pip's pixels should be visible at every door, and the portal's destination glimpse should be visible past Pip. Add a check to tests/lobby.spec.ts: at each door.at, raycast from the camera to Pip's head, chest and feet, with no unfaded hit.

**Rules:** AGENTS 8, DR-12, DR-13, DR-63, DR-70, DR-73

For Lunch the hinge is at world (-3.16, -9.76) and door.at is (-2.32, -8.9), 1.20 m from the hinge and inside the 1.66 m sweep. At full open the leaf line is about 0.53 m from Pip's centre (the finding says 0.43), close to his arm. I reproduced a clean interpenetration. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-134

**R5-134 | P1 | meeting | overlap | Office chairs at every Meeting desk pod face away from their desks; seated blobs push through backrests and sink 17 cm**

Found by: `meeting-models#0` (P1 overlap), `characters#8` (P2 overlap). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*meeting-models* — **Office chairs at every desk pod face away from their desks, so seated coworkers sit facing into the backrest; 2 boardroom coworkers also sit backwards.** Every pod chair is spawned rotated 180° wrong. The chair model's backrest is at local -z (`prefabs.ts:71`, back at z -.26, reclined with rotation.x -.12), so it faces +z. `meeting.ts:15` gives the chair `rotation: dz<0?Math.PI:0`. For the -z desk (dz=-.48) the chair sits at z-1 and is turned PI, so its backrest points +z, toward the desk. The same happens for the +z desk. The result is that all 32 empty chairs face away from their monitors (crop meeting-models-69: the seat faces the camera and the backrest touches the desk edge). Seated coworkers are oriented by `game.ts:133` (restYaw = atan2 toward the nearest desk), so they face the desk while the chair faces away. That pushes each blob's belly and arm stubs through the backrest. You can see it at the default game camera, not just close up: in meeting-models-01-start the purple and blue blobs at the bottom have orange or blue panels painted across their bellies, and meeting-models-68 is a zoom crop of a green blob with a blue backrest through its torso and an arm poking out of it. The boardroom has the opposite bug. Its chairs are rotated correctly (meeting.ts:30), but restYaw points every boardroom blob at the nearest pod desk (x≈4.85, to the west). The two blobs at x 10.8, (10.8,-7.9) and (10.8,-6.85), therefore face away from the table and into their chair backs (meeting-models-60, -55). There are about 22 coworkers in this room, and they are its main life and comedy. A whole office sitting backwards inside its furniture is the most visible modelling error in the level. It also breaks DR-70 (nothing interpenetrates at rest), which the audit can't catch because NPCs are not props.

*characters* — **Seated blobs push through their chair backrests and sink 17 cm into the seat.** The seated blob is placed at the chair's centre. Its capsule (r 0.33, centre y 0.9 with the 0.35 lift) reaches 0.33 m back, but the backrest's front face is only 0.215 m behind the seat centre, so about 11 cm of body passes through the back pad. From behind, an orange or purple 'tooth' of the blob shows through the backrest (characters-41c, -43b). The capsule bottom is at 0.395 m while the seat pad top is at about 0.565 m, so the body also sinks about 0.17 m into the cushion. The blobs also yaw their whole body to watch Pip while the chair stays fixed (game.ts:424-428), so the clipping sweeps through the armrests as they turn. The player orbits (AGENTS 8) and passes behind these desks on the clean route to the boardroom.

- Count: 26 NPCs (2 standing, 20 seated at pods, 4 in the boardroom), not ~22

- `src/props/prefabs.ts:70-71`

**Fix.**

*From meeting-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Steps 1 and 2 are right: `rotation:dz<0?0:Math.PI`, and boardroom `yaw:i%2?-Math.PI/2:Math.PI/2`. Step 3 is wrong as written. The chair's forward (its seat-facing direction) is local +z, and a blob's yaw also maps +z to its facing direction, so a seated blob's yaw should EQUAL the chair's rotation.y, not rotation + PI. With the chairs fixed, adding PI would turn every blob backwards again. Use `restYaw = nearestChair.spec.rotation ?? 0`.

Reviewer's fix: 1) In src/levels/meeting.ts:15, change the chair rotation to `rotation:dz<0?0:Math.PI`, so the backrest is on the far side from the desk. 2) In src/levels/meeting.ts:30, push the boardroom NPC spots with an explicit yaw toward the table: `npcs.push({x,z,yaw:i%2?-Math.PI/2:Math.PI/2})`. NpcSpot already has `yaw?` (src/levels/types.ts:7). 3) Make restYaw robust: in game.ts:133, when seated, take the yaw from the chair prop under the NPC (nearest `chair` prop's rotation + PI) instead of the nearest desk, so blob and chair always agree. 4) Optional: shrink the seated blob or lift it, since its capsule bottom (y≈.395) is about 12 cm below the seat top (≈.52) and its .33 radius passes through the armrests at x ±.27 (prefabs.ts:73). Raise body.position.y for seated blobs from .35 to .45, or narrow the armrests to ±.31.

*From characters:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The capsule geometry is at src/render/actors.ts:32. With the seat top at about .59, the body y that puts the capsule bottom about 4 cm into the cushion is about .50 (.55-.045), close to the .52 proposed. Fine as given.

Reviewer's fix: In addNpc (src/game.ts:128), for seated blobs set `body.position.y=.52` (the seat top minus a 4 cm cushion sink) and offset the body 0.13 m forward along the chair's facing: `body.position.z=.13` in group space, with the group yaw set to the chair's rotation. Scale the seated body z to .9. In render(), turn the seated blob's watch by rotating `npc.body` (yaw clamped to ±0.6 rad) instead of the group, so the blob looks round within the chair rather than spinning through it.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *meeting-models:* Retake meeting-models-01-start, -47 and -55/-60 with mockups/review5/tools/meeting-models/a.mjs, f.mjs and g.mjs. No chair backrest should be visible across any coworker's front, and the boardroom blobs at x 10.8 should face the table. Add a unit check: for every seated NpcSpot, the nearest chair's forward vector (rotation→+z) points within 30° of the blob's restYaw.
- *characters:* Retake characters-41c/43b/44b (s5.mjs). No blob colour may show through the backrest from behind or from the side. Optionally, check `audit()` with seated blobs included.

**Rules:** AGENTS 8, DR-70

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Checked in code. The chair backrest is at local -z (prefabs.ts:71), so the seat faces +z. meeting.ts:15 gives `dz<0?Math.PI:0`, which points every backrest toward its desk. For dz=+.48 the chair is at z+1 with rotation 0, so its back faces the desk at -z. The dz<0 case mirrors this. Seated blobs face the nearest desk (game.ts:133), so all 20 seated pod blobs sit with a backrest across their front. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)
