### R5-137

**R5-137 | P1 | spectrum | overlap | The NIR beam passes visibly through a solid bookshelf inside the glass lab (clutter sits in the beam corridor)**

Found by: `spectrum-models#0` (P1 overlap). Batch: R-spectrum (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The clutter `shelf` recipe puts a full bookshelf just inside the lab, right on the line from the hatch to the lab pad. The scene dump gives its posts at x 4.31/6.23 and z −4.33/−4.70, so it is centred at about (5.27, −4.51), 2.0 × 0.45 m, with 6×3 coloured book blocks. Delivery 2 traces the beam from the hatch midpoint (5.4, −3.2) to the lab pad (7, −6). At z = −4.5 that line is at x ≈ 6.14, inside the shelf's x span of 4.27–6.27. The beam is a pure plan-ray against `walls()` (src/stations/spectrum/logic.ts:110-127) and ignores props, so the pink beam is drawn straight through the books (shots 70, 71, 72). This is the one room whose lesson is "what an obstacle does depends on the band", and a solid wooden bookshelf letting near-IR straight through contradicts the shutter and brick next to it. It also reads as an obvious render bug: a glowing line through solid geometry. The level's clutter lanes (src/levels/spectrum.ts:34-37) protect walking routes, but not the beam corridors from the hatch to the pad, from mirror A to the hatch, or through smoke to the quiet room.

**Evidence.**

- [spectrum-models-70-lab-beam-through-bookshelf.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-70-lab-beam-through-bookshelf.jpg)
- [spectrum-models-71-lab-beam-through-bookshelf-high.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-71-lab-beam-through-bookshelf-high.jpg)
- [spectrum-models-72-lab-beam-gamecam.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-72-lab-beam-gamecam.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/spectrum-models/scene.json` (bookshelf posts 4.31..6.23, -4.33..-4.70)
- `src/levels/spectrum.ts:34-37`
- `src/stations/spectrum/logic.ts:85-92`
- [verify-spectrum-models-06-lab-beam-vs-shelf-z9.jpg](shots/verify-spectrum-models-06-lab-beam-vs-shelf-z9.jpg) (reproduced, beam through shelf books)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-spectrum-models/v1.mjs`
- `mockups/review5/tools/spectrum-models/scene.json:` bookshelf boards 2×0.06×0.45 at (5.27,{.27,.87,1.47},-4.51); some of the books are #ffc94d
- `src/levels/clutter.ts:42` (shelf recipe = bookshelf + box + bin), :80 (lane test)
- `src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:22` BEAM_Y=1.25

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The lane part is right: clutter.ts:80 rejects any item within lane r + rad*.7, so beam-corridor lanes will keep clutter off the beams. Drop the optional 'legHits treats props with mass ≥ 9 as wood' idea. logic.ts is pure, unit-tested plan geometry. Making links depend on loose props would let a knocked-over prop break the clean solution, which goes against 'never fail for chaos'. If anything, keep it to visuals: tint the beam where it passes a prop, or keep heavy clutter out of the lab corridor entirely.

Reviewer's fix: In src/levels/spectrum.ts `clutter.lanes`, add beam-corridor lanes so clutter is never seeded on a taught beam path: {points:[[5.4,-3.3],[7,-6]],r:.9} (hatch to lab pad), {points:[[-.4,2.3],[3.56,0.01],[5.4,-3.2]],r:.7} (tower to mirror A to hatch), {points:[[-.4,2.3],[1,5.8],[8.2,4.8]],r:.7} (C-mirror and quiet room legs), and {points:[[-.4,2.3],[-8.2,-5.8]],r:.6} (storeroom radio leg, for clarity). Better still, derive the lanes from logic.ts (TX, SPOTS, PADS, HATCH) so they can't drift. Optionally make legHits() in logic.ts treat any prop with mass ≥ 9 standing in the leg as a 'wood' hit, so a knocked-over shelf is a real obstacle.

**Verify.**

- Rerun mockups/review5/tools/spectrum-models/s6-solve2.mjs. Shots 70/71 must show the pink beam reaching the lab pad without crossing any prop. Add a unit check in src/stations/spectrum/logic.test.ts (or a clutter test) that no clutter PropSpec footprint intersects the segments hatchMid→PADS.lab and TX→SPOTS.A for seed 7.

**Rules:** AGENTS 10, DR-16, DR-69, DR-70

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced this myself. I placed a mirror on mark A, set NIR, aimed tx→A and A→lab, and opened the hatch. The pink beam runs straight through the clutter bookshelf inside the lab (verify-spectrum-models-06-lab-beam-vs-shelf-z9.jpg); shots 70, 71 and 72 show the same. The scene dump puts the shelf at (5.27,-4.51), 2.0×0.45 m, boards at y .27/.87/1.47, under 1.8 m tall.

### R5-138

**R5-138 | P1 | garage, observatory, arcade, global, spectrum | visual-bug | Carried items tilt on edge at head height beside Pip (tray ~70°, robot on its side, roll cart across the face, pod mast over the hat); the marker cone pierces them**

Found by: `garage-play#1` (P1 visual-bug), `observatory-models#6` (P1 visual-bug), `arcade-models#3` (P2 visual-bug), `arcade-play#22` (P2 art-style), `characters#4` (P2 visual-bug), `garage-models#18` (P2 art-style), `spectrum-models#5` (P2 visual-bug), `observatory-play#17` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*garage-play* — **Carried robot tips onto its side, floats beside Pip's head, and the marker cone pierces it.** The delivery robot is a 'cart' prop with mass 8 (src/props/prefabs.ts:16), so it uses the 'light' carry. The body is driven to 1.05 m ahead at y = Pip+0.55 with angvel zeroed, but its rotation is never corrected (src/game.ts:330-331). While Pip lifts and turns, contacts tip the 1.2 × 0.65 × 0.75 box. In the zoom-9 orbit shots the teal robot hangs at about 70° with its wheels and underside toward the camera, beside and above Pip's head, held by one outstretched mitt (shots 74 and 08). In the game-camera shots 09 and 10 it reads as a tilted yellow block at head height. The objective marker is pinned to the robot's own translation (station.ts:97) and sits 2.1 m up, so the yellow cone pokes through the carried robot (shots 08, 73, 74). The robot is the hero of the room, the only thing Pip carries, and the thing that drives off at the end, so this is the most-seen model moment in the job. It breaks DR-65 (carried items sit level in front of the chest in both mitts, never beside or intersecting the head) and DR-44 (the marker sits above clutter, not inside the held item).

*observatory-models* — **Carrying the 'roll' cart lifts it to head height and tilts it across Pip's face; the motor drum detaches on a tilt.** Step 1 says 'Roll the noisy motor cart away', and the prompt while holding says 'Keep rolling it away'. In fact E lifts the 1.2 m mail cart: snap() gives the cart centre at y 1.30 while Pip's origin is at y 0.77, so the tray spans about 0.98–1.62 m and the motor rides on top to about 2.0 m (11-recheck.mjs output). At zoom 9 the cart swings to a 35–45° tilt in front of Pip and covers Pip's face and helmet (shot 41). At the default camera it hides the motor (shot 70). After set-down it lands tilted on a chair, and the drum and fan blades stick into Pip's arm (shot 42). The motor group copies the cart's quaternion, but its offset is world-up (`motor.position.set(p.x,p.y+.33,p.z)`, station.ts:313), so whenever the cart tilts the drum drifts off the tray, out of the cart's local frame. This breaks DR-65 (carried items level in front of the chest, never over the head) and contradicts the verb on the card.

*arcade-models* — **The carried resistor tray (and any carried prop) keeps a random tilt: the tray is carried ~70° on edge beside Pip's head.** The carry code (src/game.ts:331) drives only the held body's linear velocity toward a point 1.05 m ahead at p.y+0.55 (≈1.32 m) and zeroes the angular velocity each frame. It never restores orientation, so any tilt picked up from a collision while walking stays. On the spec's route from the storeroom to the bench, the tray arrives standing almost on edge at Pip's right shoulder, with its 6 riding resistor blocks still glued to its tilted face (station.ts:369 copies the tray quaternion to trayRide). Shot -32 and crop -32b show this. A carried cone (shots -71, -72) sits tip-first at Pip's face, tilted about 60°. This is the job's one carry beat, and a tray of loose parts carried vertically reads as a physics glitch: the blocks would spill. ART F16 reported this (research-art-46) and it is still open. At pickup (shot -30) the tray also sits beside the head, held by one raised mitt, rather than level at chest height in front of both mitts.

*arcade-play* — **The tray is carried tilted beside Pip, not level in front of the chest.** In the game-camera carry shot (shot 10) the pink tray hangs diagonally off Pip's right side, with the blocks tilted. At zoom 9 (shot 09) it floats beside Pip's head, offset to the left.

The carry target puts the prop 1.05 m ahead at chest height but zeroes only angular velocity (game.ts:331). The tray keeps whatever tilt it had at pickup, and the blocks riding on it copy that rotation (station.ts:369). This breaks DR-65.

*characters* — **REGRESSION-check DR-65 still open: carried crate floats ahead of the mitts at head height and tilted; the arcade tray stands vertical beside the helmet.** Light props are driven toward a point 1.05 m ahead of Pip at p.y+0.55, which is about 1.33 m above the feet: head height, not chest. Only linear velocity and angular velocity are set; there is no orientation target, so the prop keeps whatever tilt it had when grabbed. Meanwhile the arms reach forward to about 0.5 m at shoulder height. Result:
- The crate hangs about 0.3 m beyond the mitts, tilted about 25°, at face height. From the default rear camera it covers Pip's head (characters-21, -21b, -27).
- The arcade resistor tray is carried rolled about 30° off the right mitt and, from behind, reads as a vertical slab beside the helmet (characters-81, -82). That is ART F16 / research-art-46, not fixed.

The carry is the second most common pose in the game. It looks like telekinesis and hides the hero.

*garage-models* — **Robot is carried at head height with one mitt, its long axis pointing away from Pip.** The robot is a 'cart' prop (mass 8 < 15), so game.ts:331 carries it as a light item:
- target 1.05 m ahead at p.y+.55, so its centre is at about 1.46 m;
- the body spans y 1.13–1.79 and the antenna reaches 2.0 m;
- its spec rotation π/2 is kept, so its 1.2 m length points straight away from Pip.

In garage-models-50/51 Pip holds a 1.2 m robot above shoulder height with one raised mitt near his face. It reads as a weightless box balanced in front of the head, not a heavy robot hugged at the chest. DR-65 asks for level, in front of the chest, held by both mitts.

*spectrum-models* — **The pod is carried at head height beside Pip's face, its detector mast towers over the hat, and the mirrors are carried upright beside the head.** The carry target for light props is y = p.y + .55, 1.05 m ahead (src/game.ts:331), independent of prop height. The pod (coolbox, 1.0×0.6×0.65, mass 6) therefore rides with its lid at Pip's head height, offset to his side in most views, held up by one mitt. Its podTop mast and green detector head rise about 0.5 m above the hard hat (51b, 52, 53b). From the default camera the pod covers Pip's face and right arm (50). The whiteboard-based mirror (1.7 m tall) is carried vertically beside his head, with the rail edge-on past his ear and shoulder (61). DR-65 asks for level carries in front of the chest, held by both mitts, never vertical beside the head. In this room Pip carries the pod for most of the job (three deliveries).

*observatory-play* — **'Roll the cart' is actually a lift: tilted carry clips clutter, and the cart is set down on its end.** The step and prompts say 'Roll the noisy motor cart away' and 'Keep rolling it away'. But the cart (mass 8) is picked up like a box and carried at a ~40° tilt in front of Pip. It sweeps through chairs and clutter, and the motor drum and fan sit at Pip's face height. On E it is dropped with its carried orientation, so in two of two runs it landed standing on its end or on its side on a chair. The motor cart also reads small at the game camera: the 'MOTOR' tag isn't readable and the noise sparks are 3 tiny particles every 0.5–1.1 s. A second, decorative violet cart (6.8,4.4) with the same silhouette also prompts 'Grab the cart'. Breaks DR-65 (carried items level in front of the chest), DR-47 (a noisy device should look noisy) and DR-17 (no look-alike false affordance).

**Fix.**

*From garage-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** For option (1), add a dedicated 'robot' PropKind in src/props/prefabs.ts (size about [1.2,.65,.75], mass ≥ 15) and use it in src/levels/garage.ts:8. Alternatively, have game.ts:331 also treat spec.id==='robot' as heavy. Note that heavy also blocks jumping (game.ts:180), which is fine for this item. Option (2) (slerp to an upright yaw-only quaternion, lower and closer target) is fine as written.

Reviewer's fix: Pick one:
(1) Make the robot a push-along item. Add `heavy:true` to its PropSpec, or give the 'robot' id mass ≥ 15 in level props, so it takes the existing 'heavy furniture is pushed along the floor so it stays upright' branch (game.ts:331): wheels on the floor, Pip pushing a rolling robot. That fits the fiction and the wheel spin can animate while it moves.
(2) Keep lifting, but in the carry branch slerp the body rotation each step to an upright quaternion around Pip's heading (b.setRotation(slerp(current, yawOnly(heading)), true)), lower the target to Pip.y+0.25, and reduce `ahead` to 0.75.
Either way, the marker must not sit on the held item (see the marker finding).

*From observatory-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The heavy path triggers at mass ≥ 15 (game.ts:331), not ≥ 30. Don't change the 'cart' prefab mass globally: carts are used in garage (id 'robot'), meeting ('mail-cart' job item), qfn, spectrum and arcade. Add a per-spec override instead (e.g. PropSpec mass or push:true for id 'motor') read in game.ts:331. The quaternion-applied offset in fix part (1) is correct.

Reviewer's fix: (1) station.ts:313: apply the offset in the cart's frame: `const off=new T.Vector3(0,.33,0).applyQuaternion(qv); motor.position.set(p.x+off.x,p.y+off.y,p.z+off.z)`. (2) Make the cart a push prop, not a lift, the same way the heavy bookshelf already prompts 'heavy: push it'. Either flag spec.id==='motor' as push-only in game.ts's grab/carry code, so the body stays on its wheels at y .33 and is dragged at the handle (handle at -w/2 in prefabs.ts:115), or give the cart mass ≥30 so it uses the push path. Keep the carry target level (rotation locked to yaw) if it must stay a lift.

*From arcade-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Locking rotations while held (b.lockRotations(true,true), and setRotation to a yaw-only heading on pickup) is the simplest robust fix; the slerp is not needed. Restore with lockRotations(false) on drop or throw. Lowering to p.y+.35 is fine.

Reviewer's fix: In src/game.ts:331, after setting linvel: build a target quaternion of yaw-only `heading` (setFromAxisAngle(Y, heading)). Slerp the body's rotation toward it, e.g. b.setRotation(q.slerp(target, min(1, dt*12))), or set an angvel proportional to the axis-angle error (×10). Lower the carry height to p.y+0.35 (≈1.12 m, chest) and the distance for light props to 0.6 + size[2]/2, so the item sits between the mitts. For trays, also lock the rotation fully (b.lockRotations(true) while held, restore on drop). Point the arm IK at the item's side edges (two mitts) instead of one raised mitt.

*From arcade-play:* In game.ts:331, for light held props, also slerp the body rotation toward yaw=heading with pitch/roll 0 (`b.setRotation(q.slerp(target,.3))`). Reduce `ahead` to 0.7 for the tray, so it sits between the mitts.

*From characters:* In src/game.ts:331, for non-heavy props compute `ahead=.32+kind.size[2]/2` (front of chest plus half depth) and `y=p.y-.78+1.0+kind.size[1]*.3`, so the item centre sits at about 1.0–1.1 m, chest height. Drive orientation each step: `const want=new T.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new T.Euler(0,this.heading,0)); b.setRotation(slerp(current,want,.25))` (or set angvel from the quaternion error). For flat kinds (size[1] < .2: tray, strip, splitter, paper, bridge), use the same level target. In pipRig.ts:74, use reach -1.25 for light items and fold the elbows to -.45 so the mitts meet the item's sides (lz/rz from the item's half width, passed in as `carryWidth` on PipState).

*From garage-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Base the target y on the real numbers: p.y+.15 puts the centre at about .92, so the body spans about .6–1.25 and the head top is about 1.5. Check this against Pip's head height in the rig before choosing. Use setRotation only for wide items (size[0] > 1), so small items keep their current behaviour.

Reviewer's fix: In game.ts:331, when held.spec.id==='robot' (or prefab size[0] > 1):
- target y = p.y+.15 (≈1.06, chest);
- ahead = .45 + size[2]/2;
- set the rotation so the long axis is perpendicular to the heading (setRotation from Euler(0, heading+π/2, 0)).
In the PipRig, pass `carrying:'wide'` so both arms reach to ±.35. Add a 0.8× walk speed while carrying for weight.

*From spectrum-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The mirror part of the fix is wrong. A 1.7 m board carried perpendicular to the heading with its bottom at .25 m reaches 1.95 m, above Pip's head (about 1.4–1.6). It would hide his whole body from the default camera behind him, so his head would not 'stay visible over it'. Instead, carry tall flat boards edge-on (board plane parallel to the heading), low in front of the chest with the bottom near .3 m. Or tilt them to lie flat like a tray at waist height. For the pod, target.y = p.y - .1 + size[1]/2 is reasonable (p.y ≈ .77 is the capsule centre).

Reviewer's fix: In game.ts:331, compute the light-carry height from the prop's size so its bottom sits at the waist: target.y = p.y - .1 + kind.size[1]/2 (Pip's body centre ≈ .9 gives a bottom at about .8 m). Set ahead = .45 + kind.size[2]/2 and lerp heading-aligned yaw onto the body (setRotation from this.heading) so the box faces forward between both mitts. For tall flat props (whiteboard/mirror, size[1] > 1.2) carry them low and in front, bottom at .25 m, rotated so the board is perpendicular to the heading. Pip then 'pushes' the board like a sign, and his head stays visible over it. Update pipRig carry arm pose (rig.update carrying) to reach to the new height.

*From observatory-play:* - Give the motor cart a push mode: while held, keep it on its wheels (lock rotation to yaw, y at the rest height) and place it 0.9 m ahead of Pip with the push-bar pose, like the Lunch dolly. On drop, reset the rotation to upright yaw (station.dropped hook → setRotation(yaw only)).
- Raise the motor's readability: an animated buzz (scale jitter 2%), 6–8 bright sparks per second while job 1 runs, and a pulsing ring decal on the floor whose radius equals CART_SAFE (4 m) around the receiver, so 'far enough' is visible.
- Recolour or reshape the decorative cart (a book trolley with books), or remove it.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

### R5-139

**R5-139 | P1 | global, playground | visual-bug | The cable runs through Pip's legs, body and head to reach the glove (P3 / DR-73 still open)**

Found by: `cable#3` (P1 visual-bug), `characters#1` (P2 visual-bug), `playground-models#3` (P1 visual-bug), `playground-play#16` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*cable* — **REGRESSION / still open (P3): the cable runs through Pip's legs and body to reach the glove.** For routing, the plug is simulated 0.65 m ahead of Pip (game.ts:267). The drawn end is Pip's right glove (handPosition, game.ts:289-293). cablePath only lifts the last 1.8 m off the floor (game.ts:10-20). The cable trails behind Pip because he is walking away from the reel, so its last segment passes through his boots, shins and belly to reach the hand in front.

Seen in:
- the Playground win push-in (cable-18: the gold cable goes between the boots into the socket; R2 bug 3 / P3, never fixed);
- the pillar wrap (cable-41);
- the crate drag (cable-51);
- Lunch thick and thin drags (cable-84, cable-130).

It's on screen in nearly every drag frame and in the reward shot, so it cheapens the 'hero cable' (DR-73, ART R15.3).

*characters* — **REGRESSION-check DR-73 still open: the cable runs through Pip's legs and body when holding the plug, at the win push-in, and on the Lunch thick cable.** The cable's last point is Pip's glove (handPosition → rig.hand under the right elbow). The rope solver never treats Pip's body as an obstacle, so whenever the reel is behind or beside Pip, the hose runs straight from the glove down through his leg or hip to the floor:
- Playground idle hold, back view: the hose crosses the right leg (characters-19, third panel).
- Lunch: the striped thick cable falls from the glove through both thighs (characters-77).
- Playground win push-in, the hero shot: the gold connected lead and plug lie under and through Pip's right boot (characters-64b).

R2 bug 3 (P3 in the earlier checklist) is not fixed. The cable is the star (AGENTS 4), and in the moment it is most on show it clips through the hero. Related: on the first F at the Lunch dolly, the right mitt pushes into the reel drum (characters-75), and the dolly then parks against Pip's hip (characters-76; DR-74's 1.3 m follow distance).

*playground-models* — **The cable runs through Pip's body, head and feet (P3 still open).** The cable's last segment goes from the rope's end (Pip's centre) straight to the right glove, so it nearly always passes through Pip:
- Idle carry (shot -41): the hose comes from the reel, enters Pip's lower back and the plug pops out of the glove on the other side.
- Near the strain limit (shot -44, crop -60): the pull pose raises the hand beside the hard hat, so the 20 cm-thick orange cable climbs through the shoulder and the hat brim, and the plug is hidden behind the head.
- Plugged in and at the win push-in (shots -45, -46, -47): the gold cable lies straight through Pip's boots.
This is the R2 'cable through the legs' bug and is still unfixed. The cable is the star of the game and Pip is the hero, so the two most-watched objects visibly clip in the tutorial's hero shots.

*playground-play* — **REGRESSION CHECK P3 (still open): the cable runs up through Pip's legs and under the boots in the win shot.** cablePath draws from the floor straight to the glove (src/game.ts:283-285, handPosition at :280). From behind (shot 59) the white cable enters Pip at the left boot and runs inside the leg to the hand. In the win push-in (shots 17, 18) the gold cable passes under Pip's boots into the socket. R2 bug 3 and research-art-18 raised this, and it is unchanged (DR-73, ART R15.3).

**Fix.**

*From cable:* Route the last metre around Pip's body.

1. In drawCable (and in the Lunch render loop at lunch-runtime.ts:315), when holding, take the incoming route direction `d` (last bend → Pip). Insert a waypoint at Pip's hip on the side the cable arrives from: `pip + perp(d)*0.35 − d*0.25`, at y 0.5. Then rise from there to the glove.
2. Alternatively, switch to a drag pose: hold the plug in the trailing hand at the hip, behind Pip (plugPosition = pip − forward*0.45 for routing). Grab-drag reads better and matches Good Job's cable carry.
3. After plugging in, make the socket side end at the socket face. Keep Pip's win-pose spot 0.6 m to the side of the cable line (winFocus, game.ts:398).

*From characters:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Do part 1 (push hose samples out of a capsule of r≈0.38 around Pip, y 0–1.4, before hoseGeometry) in src/game.ts drawCable and the Lunch cable draw. Skip part 3 (moving Pip 0.5 m back from the socket at the win): it changes plug-in reach and the tested coordinates for a cosmetic gain. Setting the dolly follow distance to 2 m or more (src/lunch-runtime.ts, the `d>1.3` check in the thick-cable follow) is DR-74's fix, which is separate and fine.

Reviewer's fix: 1) In drawCable (src/game.ts:290-305) and the Lunch cable draw, add a short Pip-clearance leg before the hand: insert a point 0.45 m behind Pip at hip height (p.y-.2, offset by -heading), and when the previous rope point is in front of Pip, insert one at the side of the hand instead. Simplest version: treat Pip as a vertical capsule (r .38, y 0..1.4) and push any interpolated hose sample that falls inside it out radially before building hoseGeometry. 2) In pipRig.ts:75, when holdingPlug, turn the right forearm so the lead leaves the glove backwards (elbow x +.3), so the tube naturally trails behind the hip. 3) At plug-in (the win), set the plug's end segment to come off the socket away from Pip, and move Pip 0.5 m back from the socket before the push-in. For the Lunch dolly, use a follow distance of at least 2 m (src/lunch-runtime.ts:237), as DR-74 asks.

*From playground-models:* In game.ts drawCable(), after cablePath, re-route the tail around Pip's capsule. Find the last path point within 0.5 m of Pip's axis. Replace the inside points with a waypoint at Pip pos + (heading-right × 0.42) at y 0.55 (a 'belt loop' on the hand side), then go to the hand. While connected and Pip stands within 0.6 m of the cable, push the rope's floor points out of the 0.36 m capsule radius before building the hose. Cap the pull-pose hand height (pipRig) at y 1.2 so the plug never rises past the chest, which also satisfies DR-65.

*From playground-play:* In drawCable, insert a control point 0.35 m in front of Pip at y 0.5 (along the heading), before the hand point, so the lead rises in front of the body. After plugging in, drop the last segment so it lies on the floor from the socket outward, away from Pip's feet (offset the end point by −heading×0.4).

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *cable:* Retake cable-18 (the win), cable-41 and cable-84 at zoom 9 from the front and from the back (orbit ±700). No hose pixels should overlap Pip's legs or torso. A check in pg1: the distance from each cablePath sample to Pip's capsule axis must be > 0.3 m, except for the final 0.4 m into the glove.
- *characters:* Retake characters-19 (s2.mjs), characters-64b (s8.mjs) and characters-77 (s9.mjs). No hose pixels may overlap Pip's legs or boots. Optionally, check in the specs that every rope point stays more than 0.35 m horizontally from the player except the final hand point.
- *playground-models:* Add a check script that, for every frame of d.mjs, measures the minimum distance from the hose's centre-line points to Pip's capsule segment (radius 0.32). Expect ≥ 0.32 + hose radius except within 0.15 m of the glove. Retake -41, -44, -45 and -47.

**Rules:** AGENTS 4, DR-65, DR-73, DR-74

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Visible in cable-19b-crop-win-legs.jpg: the gold cable runs between Pip's boots into the socket. In cable-41-pg-wrap-pillar-close.jpg, the hose rises through Pip's legs and hip to the glove in front. ### R5-140

**R5-140 | P1 | global, playground | visual-bug | A faded pillar leaves its opaque cap, plinth, rail and switch plaque floating in mid-air**

Found by: `camera-render#5` (P1 visual-bug), `playground-models#0` (P1 visual-bug), `playground-play#14` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B3 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*camera-render* — **A faded pillar leaves its opaque base, rail and cap behind, which read as glass-case shelves that slice through Pip at 1.06 m.** pillar() puts only the 3 m body on game.root as an occluder. The base (0.16 m), the rail band at 1.06 m, the cap at 3.02 m, the sticker, and the poster or extinguisher go to game.decorRoot and get merged by freeze() (src/levels/decor.ts:53-58).

When the body fades to 0.15, those parts stay opaque, footprint-sized slabs. The rail's top face draws as a solid striped shelf at waist height, with the transparent hazard stripes drawn over it. Pip's legs below 1.06 m and his boots disappear behind the 'shelf' and the base (camera-render-pg-43b-crop-pillar-faded.jpg). Mid-fade it looks like a display cabinet with Pip trapped inside (camera-render-pg-41b-crop-pillar-midfade.jpg).

The faded body also keeps a faint outline hull (OutlineEffect alpha follows opacity), a mild outline ghost. This breaks DR-12 (Pip still hidden) and DR-78 (faded occluders keep clean sorting and outlines).

*playground-models* — **Faded pillars leave their cap, plinth, rail and switch plaque floating in mid-air.** When a hazard pillar comes between the camera and Pip, only the 1.4×3×1.4 m body fades. The body is on game.root and registered in game.occluders. The orange cap slab (y 3.02), the BASE plinth (y 0.08), the rail band (y 1.06) and the small cream plaque (y 0.35) are on decorRoot, which freeze() merges into opaque meshes, so they never fade. At the close camera (zoom 9) the player sees an opaque orange tabletop floating in the air above Pip, a brown tray on the floor and a cream square hovering at knee height, with a ghostly hazard texture in between. This happens whenever Pip passes behind pillar-a (-1.3,-1.3) or pillar-b (3.2,2.7), and both sit on the clean route and the slingshot run. It reads as broken geometry exactly when the camera is meant to be helping. It also breaks the occlusion rule: the cap still hides part of the view, and a stray outline ghost shows around the faded body.

*playground-play* — **A faded pillar leaves its cap, base and rail opaque, floating like a tabletop.** pillar() fades only the 3 m body mesh on game.root (src/levels/decor.ts:55). The base trim, the 0.12 m cap at y 3.02 and the rail at 1.06 go on decorRoot (decor.ts:56) and stay fully opaque. When Pip walks behind pillar-b, the striped body goes ghostly while an orange slab hangs in mid-air over Pip and a brown base slab sits on the floor (shots 40, 41). It reads as a floating table, and the ghost stripes still cover Pip at opacity 0.15 (DR-78).

**Evidence.**

**Fix.**

*From camera-render:* In pillar(), build every part (body, base, rail, cap, sticker, poster, extinguisher) under one `group(game.root,…)` with cloned, transparent materials, and push all of them to game.occluders, as interiorWall() already does (decor.ts:48). When the ray hits any part, fade the whole group: keep a Map&lt;mesh,group> so all siblings share the target opacity.

Alternatively, while the body opacity is below 0.6, set `visible=false` on the rail, cap and poster so no opaque slab remains. Also set `outlineParameters.visible=false` on faded materials once opacity < 0.5 to kill the hull ghost.

*From playground-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The fix is right, with one caution. toon() returns shared cached materials (toon(BASE), toon(CAP), toon(RAIL) are reused by the shell walls and interior walls), so each pillar part must get its own material.clone() before transparent=true. Otherwise every wall rail and cap in the room fades together.

Reviewer's fix: In decor.ts pillar(): build the plinth, cap, rail and plaque as children of one group on game.root, each with a cloned transparent material (material.clone(); transparent=true), and push each mesh into game.occluders. Simpler alternative: parent them under the faded body mesh `m` and in game.ts:388 traverse occluder children so the whole assembly shares one opacity. Fade the plaque too, or drop it. Use the same fade target (≤0.25) and keep depthWrite on so sorting stays stable (DR-78). Better still, switch occluder fades to alpha-hash/dither (material.alphaHash=true) so outlines do not ghost.

*From playground-play:* In pillar() put the cap, base and rail on game.root with cloned transparent materials, push them to game.occluders, and fade them together. Or parent them to the faded body so the existing fade loop (game.ts:388) drives the whole group. Consider fading to 0.1 with alphaHash to avoid sorting ghosts.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *camera-render:* Retake camera-render-pg-43 (Pip at (-1.3,-3.1) behind the pillar at (-1.3,-1.3), default zoom). Pip's boots, belt and hat must all be visible, with no opaque horizontal slab crossing him. Repeat at zoom 9 (camera-render-pg-44-pillar-faded-z9).
- *playground-models:* Re-run mockups/review5/tools/playground-models/b.mjs (visit pillar-a at zoom 9) and retake playground-models-18 and -20. No orange slab should hover above Pip, and the base and cap should fade together with the body.
- *playground-play:* Retake shot 41 (zoom 9 behind pillar-b): no opaque slab floats above Pip.

**Rules:** DR-12, DR-72, DR-78

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — In code, src/levels/decor.ts:55-56 puts only the 3 m body on root as a transparent occluder. The base, the cap at 3.02 m and the rail at 1.06 m (pillar footprint plus 0.03 m) go to decorRoot, where freeze() merges them as opaque geometry. I looked at camera-render-pg-41b-crop-pillar-midfade.jpg and pg-43-pillar-faded.png. (3/3 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-141

**R5-141 | P1 | lunch | visual-bug | Lunch storeroom darkness is still a flat lid plane at 1.5 m that the lamp and stacked boxes poke through**

Found by: `lunch-models#6` (P1 visual-bug), `camera-render#12` (P2 visual-bug), `lunch-play#20` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B8 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*lunch-models* — **Storeroom darkness is still a flat lid at y 1.5: the lamp shade at 2.2 m shines bright above it and the plane edge reads as a tinted sheet (LR1 still open).** The unlit storeroom is shown by an 8.9 × 10 m unlit plane at y 1.5 with opacity 0.8, a cut-out radial hole and depthWrite false. Everything taller than 1.5 m pokes through it fully lit. The floor lamp's shade (y 1.78–2.22) shows cream and bright while everything under the lid is violet (lunch-models-70 'lid on' vs -71 'lid off'; also the start shot -01 and survey -02). At zoom 9 inside the room, the lid only tints. Crates, the floor and Pip are clearly readable, so 'dark room, can't find things' isn't sold either. The rule that nothing in the dark storeroom can be grabbed (canGrab) then feels arbitrary, because the player can plainly see the boxes. The capacitor cart and coolbox are hidden by mesh.visible=false (lunch-runtime.ts:293) rather than by darkness, so they pop in when the room lights.

*camera-render* — **Lunch storeroom darkness is still a flat 'lid' plane at 1.5 m that the lamp and stacked boxes poke through (LR1 still open).** The storeroom is darkened by a translucent plane at y 1.5 with opacity 0.8 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:64-66). From the kitchen side and in a low orbit it reads as a dark sheet of glass over the room. The floor lamp's pole and 2.2 m shade stick up through it, and box tops above 1.5 m show lit above the sheet (camera-render-lu-55-storeroom-lid-back.jpg, camera-render-lu-05-orbit-low.jpg). In the start view the lamp shade glows above the 'dark' room (camera-render-lu-01-start.jpg).

Raised in R1, R2 P1.9 and QA 12; never fixed. This breaks DR-76.

*lunch-play* — **The dark storeroom is still a tinted lid plane; boxes and the lamp show through it while only the cart is hidden.** The storeroom darkness is still an unlit plane at y 1.5 with opacity 0.8 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:64-66). From the game camera the room's crates, bins and floor lamp are all clearly visible, just purple-tinted, and the lamp shade at 2.2 m is drawn untinted above the lid (lunch-play-v01, 01-start, 03).

Meanwhile the capacitor cart and cooler box are made invisible, and props inside can't be grabbed (:143-145, :293). So the room doesn't read as 'pitch dark, find a light'. It reads as 'a purple room with some boxes and nothing useful'. The player gets no cue that something important is hidden there. LR1, raised in R1, R2 and QA 12, is still open.

**Fix.**

A raised lid also shows parallax at the high game camera: it spills a dark strip onto the power-room floor beyond the store-front wall (z 0…0.3), so the per-material storeDark uniform is the right fix. If the lid is raised anyway, shrink it toward −z by about 0.5 m to compensate.

Reviewer's fix: Replace the lid with per-material darkening.
(1) Add a 'storeDark' uniform to toon's onBeforeCompile (src/render/toon.ts rimShader). Multiply outgoingLight by mix(1., .28, storeDark × inBox(vWorldPosition, minX −16.5, maxX −7.75, minZ −10, maxZ 0)), with a 0.4 m smoothstep at the doorway.
(2) Tween storeDark from 1 to 0 over 0.5 s when lit() turns true.
(3) Keep the capacitor cart and coolbox visible, but darkened (they then fade in with the light instead of popping).
(4) If that is too costly, at least lower the lid to y 2.4 above everything in the room, and give the lamp shade its own dark material while the room is unlit.

*From camera-render:* Replace the lid with a darkness factor applied in the shader. Add a uniform box (min/max xz of the storeroom) to the toon rim onBeforeCompile (src/render/toon.ts:23) that multiplies outgoingLight by a `uDark` value (0.25 when unlit, 1 when lit) for fragments whose world position lies inside the box. That needs a vWorldPosition varying. Fade uDark to 1 when the portable lamp enters.

Alternatively, keep a plane but put it at y 2.95 (wall-cap height), and lower the lamp and boxes below it.

*From lunch-play:* Replace the lid with darkened materials. While !lit(), multiply the storeroom decor and clutter material colours by 0.22 (or swap them to a shared dark toon variant). Keep the cart and cooler as near-black silhouettes with a faint rim, rather than invisible, so the room reads as dark but holding something. Hide the lamp's shade highlight until lit.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

- *lunch-play:* Retake v01 and c07. Before lighting, the storeroom is dark, with silhouettes and no plane edge or lamp poking through. After lighting it is the same as now.

**Rules:** DR-37, DR-47, DR-76

In verify-lunch-models-10 (game camera inside the storeroom), the floor-lamp shade draws bright cream above the violet lid, while the crate grid and Pip under the lid stay fully readable, just tinted. ### R5-142

**R5-142 | P1 | meeting | visual-bug | Meeting: the strip's load gauge (the room's only electricity readout) floats in mid-air in the boardroom doorway with a bare back**

Found by: `meeting-models#2` (P1 visual-bug), `meeting-play#2` (P1 visual-bug), `meeting-teach#9` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: R-meeting (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*meeting-models* — **The strip's load gauge (the room's only electricity readout) floats in mid-air in the boardroom doorway, and its show/hide logic is dead after decor freezing.** `meeting-strip.ts:52` mounts the load gauge at (t.x+.95, 1.55, t.z+.06) = (13.25, 1.55, -2.19), and the comment there says it is "on the wall above the strip". The boardroom front at z -2 is glass only from x 9.3–11 and 13.8–16.5, with door posts at x 11 and 13.8 (decor.ts:144-146). x 13.25 is therefore in the open doorway. The gauge is a bare ink board with a decal (kit.ts:108) hanging 1.55 m up in empty air, and at the game camera it lines up with a boardroom chair, so it reads as a TV on a chair back (meeting-models-28, -30, -37, crop -63). It is the teaching instrument for the room's only electricity beat (the load budget, DR-47), so it must read as a device mounted on the strip or the wall. A second problem: `render()` toggles `this.gaugeMount.visible=g.stripPlaced()` (meeting-strip.ts:85). The mount is a child of `game.decorRoot`, and `freeze(this.decorRoot)` runs right after the MeetingStrip is built (game.ts:103 then :105). freeze merges its meshes into per-material buckets and removes the emptied group (kit.ts:77-85). The visibility toggle now acts on a detached group, so the gauge shows from frame 1, before the strip is placed (meeting-models-28 was taken before step 1 was done). This breaks DR-72 (nothing floats; signs are mounted) and DR-63 (gauges have housings, not bare boards).

*meeting-play* — **Strip load gauge floats in mid-air in the boardroom doorway, is unreadable at the game camera, and its 'only when placed' visibility is defeated by freeze().** The load gauge is mounted at (t.x+0.95, 1.55, t.z+0.06) = (13.25, 1.55, -2.19). That point is inside the open door gap of the boardroom glass front, which spans x 11–13.8 at z -2, so nothing is behind or under the gauge. Orbited side and back shots show a thin black slab hovering at head height in the doorway with no wall, post or stand (shots 75, 76, 77). From the front it hangs over the boardroom carpet between chairs (23).
At the default game camera the dial is about 45×30 px, and its needle and zones cannot be read (shots 20, 22, 78). Yet the code comment says 'A gauge on the wall above the strip shows its load the whole time', so it is meant to be the main cue for the load lesson.
The gauge group is added to game.decorRoot, which freeze() merges and strips of empty groups after construction. The per-frame `gaugeMount.visible=g.stripPlaced()` therefore does nothing, and the gauge is visible from frame 1, before the strip exists (shots 02, 07).
This breaks DR-72 (nothing floats; signs mounted 0.5–1 cm off a surface), DR-63 (gauges have housings and finished backs; the back is a bare black box), DR-47 (device state readable at the game camera) and DR-48 (readable size).

*meeting-teach* — **The load gauge floats in the open boardroom doorway, with a bare black slab back.** The gauge is mounted at (t.x+0.95, 1.55, t.z+0.06), which is (13.25, 1.55, -2.19) (meeting-strip.ts:52).

- That is inside the door gap, which runs x 11 to 13.8 (decor.ts:144-145; LEVEL_01 says the same). There is no wall or post behind it, so it hangs in mid-air.
- From inside the boardroom it reads as a black rectangle floating in the doorway (shots 05, 09).
- Seen from the open plan, it hovers among the chairs behind the glass line (shots 03, 13).
- It is the room's only teaching instrument, and it looks like a stray decal rather than part of the strip.

**Evidence.**

**Fix.**

*From meeting-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Mounting on 'the door post at x 13.8' won't work as specified. The post is box(.1,2.6,.1), and a 0.56 m gauge would hang 23 cm off each side of it, so it still reads as floating. Mount it instead on the glass partition's frame face east of the post (x≈14.3, z -1.94, facing +z) with a backing plate the same size as the gauge, or on a short pedestal/stalk standing next to the strip. ### R5-143

**R5-143 | P1 | global | visual-bug | First-time players always get render quality 0 (Number(null) → 0), and a saved value overrides ?lowfx**

Found by: `camera-render#1` (P1 visual-bug), `gap2-quality2-retake#0` (P1 art-style). Batch: B8 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*camera-render* — **First-time players always get the lowest render quality: Number(localStorage.getItem()) turns null into 0, so AO, bloom and DPR above 1 never run (also silently downgrades every review-5 'fullfx' screenshot).** src/game.ts:70 reads the saved quality with `const saved=Number(localStorage.getItem('circuit-crew-quality'));if(saved===0||saved===1)this.view.setQuality(saved);`. With nothing stored, getItem returns null and Number(null)===0, so every fresh profile calls setQuality(0). That turns off GTAO and UnrealBloom and caps the pixel ratio at 1 (src/render/toon.ts:100). Nothing ever writes '2', because adaptQuality only steps down (src/game.ts:393-395), so the full look is never seen.

Verified on a bare URL (?level=garage, no manual flag, fresh context): `{stored:null, quality:0, dpr:1}` (quality.mjs).

The hard rule's 'restrained glow' (AGENTS 9, DR-66) is therefore absent: lamps, neon and screens get no bloom halo, props lose their contact AO, and HiDPI screens render blurry.

It also means every review-5 screenshot taken through cap.mjs with fullfx:true is at quality 0. Reviewers judging AO and bloom were looking at the low path. Compare camera-render-arcade-20-quality0.jpg with -21-quality2.png: AO grounds the cabinets and beanbags at quality 2 only.

*gap2-quality2-retake* — **Confirmed: real players always get render quality 0 (null → 0), a saved value overrides ?lowfx, and the step-down only ratchets one way.** src/game.ts:70 runs `Number(localStorage.getItem('circuit-crew-quality'))`. With no key stored that is Number(null) === 0, which passes the `saved===0||saved===1` test, so setQuality(0) runs on every fresh profile. That turns off GTAO and bloom and caps DPR at 1 (src/render/toon.ts:99-101). I measured it with tools/quality2-retake/00-fresh.mjs. Garage on a fresh profile reads quality 0, DPR 1, `_GTAOPass:false,_UnrealBloomPass:false` in three cases: the review's ?manual&fullfx URL, plain ?manual, and the real player URL /?level=garage with no manual flag. Stored '1' gives 1 and stored '2' gives 2 (2 only works because the line ignores it and the renderer default stays at 2). Three side effects make it worse. (a) A stored value overrides the renderer's own low setting. With '1' stored, ?manual and ?manual&lowfx both come up at quality 1 with bloom on (06-lowfx.mjs), so ?lowfx is not honoured. (b) adaptQuality (src/game.ts:392-395) only steps down, saves each step, and returns early at q===0. Nothing in src/ can raise quality again; grep finds no settings control. A player who hits one slow 3 s spell keeps lower quality for good. (c) The step-down isn't needed on this host GPU. 05-fps.mjs ran every room in real time (no ?manual) at quality 2, at DPR 1 and DPR 1.5, for 10 s each: 58–60 fps, draw pass 3–10 ms, and quality never stepped down. So nobody since ac29daf (2026-09-29) has seen the bloom or AO tuning, and every review-5 'fullfx' screenshot except camera-render-*-21-quality2 and the quality2-retake set was taken at quality 0. Several art findings were measured on a render players were never meant to get; see the per-claim findings below.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:70`
- `src/game.ts:393-395`
- `src/render/toon.ts:100`
- `src/render/toon.ts:104`
- `mockups/review5/tools/camera-render/quality.mjs`
- [camera-render-arcade-20-quality0.jpg](shots/camera-render-arcade-20-quality0.jpg)
- [camera-render-arcade-21-quality2.jpg](shots/camera-render-arcade-21-quality2.jpg)
- [camera-render-garage-20-quality0.jpg](shots/camera-render-garage-20-quality0.jpg)
- [camera-render-garage-21-quality2.jpg](shots/camera-render-garage-21-quality2.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-camera-render/v1.mjs` output: FRESH { stored: null, q: 0, dpr: 1, dev: 2 }; CAPQ 0
- `src/render/toon.ts:98-100` (default quality=2; setQuality(0) caps DPR at 1)
- `src/game.ts:394` (returns early when q===0)
- `src/game.ts:392-395`
- `src/render/toon.ts:99-104`
- `mockups/review5/tools/quality2-retake/00-fresh.mjs` (output: 'player-url fresh {stored:null,quality:0,dpr:1,...GTAO false, Bloom false}')
- `mockups/review5/tools/quality2-retake/06-lowfx.mjs` (stored 1 + ?lowfx -> quality 1)
- `mockups/review5/tools/quality2-retake/05-fps.mjs` (q2 holds 58-60 fps in all 9 rooms at DPR 1 and 1.5)
- [quality2-retake-19-garage-start.jpg](shots/quality2-retake-19-garage-start.jpg) vs quality2-retake-19-garage-start-q0.jpg
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap2-quality2-retake/v0.mjs` output: '?level=garage stored= undefined {q:0,dpr:1,...GTAOPass:false,UnrealBloomPass:false}'; '?level=garage&manual&lowfx stored= 1 {q:1,...UnrealBloomPass:true}'
- `src/render/toon.ts:70` (low = lowfx || manual&&!fullfx) and :104 (if(low)setQuality(0)), which game.ts:70 then overrides
- `mockups/review5/tools/cap.mjs:18-23` (no localStorage write, so fullfx captures ran at q0)

**Fix.**

*From camera-render:* In src/game.ts:70, use `const raw=localStorage.getItem('circuit-crew-quality'); if(raw==='0'||raw==='1')this.view.setQuality(Number(raw) as 0|1);`.

Also give adaptQuality a way back up. For example, after 20 s of slowAvg < 1/58, step the quality up one level and save it. Otherwise one slow start (shader compile) pins a player to low quality forever.

In mockups/review5/tools/cap.mjs (later reviews), add `localStorage.setItem('circuit-crew-quality','2')` through addInitScript when fullfx is set.

*From gap2-quality2-retake:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Same intent, cleaner form. Have createRenderer return `low` (or a defaultQuality). In game.ts:70: `const raw=localStorage.getItem(key); if(raw!==null&&!this.view.low){const s=Number(raw); if(s===0||s===1||s===2)this.view.setQuality(s);}`. Add a step-up path to adaptQuality. Ship the bloom fixes from findings 1–4 before or alongside making q2 the real default.

Reviewer's fix: In src/game.ts:70, treat a missing key as 'use the default' and accept 2, but never override the low setting from ?lowfx or plain ?manual. For example: `const raw=localStorage.getItem('circuit-crew-quality');const low=params.has('lowfx')||(this.manual&&!params.has('fullfx'));if(raw!==null&&!low){const saved=Number(raw);if(saved===0||saved===1||saved===2)this.view.setQuality(saved);}`. Better still, let createRenderer decide the low case and expose it. In adaptQuality (src/game.ts:392-395), add a recovery path: after 20 s at ≥58 fps, step up one level and save it. Also clear the stored value when the build version changes, so a past downgrade doesn't stick. Optionally add a Quality row (Low / Medium / High) to the pause menu.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *camera-render:* 1. Fresh browser context on ?level=garage (no manual flag): `__game.view.getQuality()===2` and `renderer.getPixelRatio()===min(devicePixelRatio,1.5)`. 2. Add a smoke-spec assertion that a fresh load is not quality 0. 3. Retake camera-render-arcade-21 without forcing the quality.
- *gap2-quality2-retake:* Add a Playwright test: open /?level=garage in a fresh context, read window.__game.view.getQuality() (or expose it through snapshot()). Expect 2, and expect 0 with ?lowfx even when '1' or '2' is stored. Rerun mockups/review5/tools/quality2-retake/00-fresh.mjs: 'player-url fresh' should print quality 2.

**Rules:** AGENTS 9, DR-24, DR-55, DR-66

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Checked in code and at runtime. src/game.ts:70 runs Number(localStorage.getItem(...)); getItem returns null on a fresh profile, Number(null) is 0, and that passes the `saved===0` check. I opened a fresh Playwright context on ?level=garage with no manual flag and deviceScaleFactor 2. The result was {stored:null, q:0, dpr:1, devicePixelRatio:2}: AO and bloom were off, and the pixel ratio was 1 on a 2x screen. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-144

**R5-144 | P1 | meeting | visual-bug | Meeting win payoff is unreadable: window frames, sill and blinds draw on top of the projector slide, and at quality 2 the light-up blooms the slide and graph white**

Found by: `meeting-models#1` (P1 visual-bug), `gap2-quality2-retake#2` (P1 art-style). Batch: R-meeting (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*meeting-models* — **Win payoff is broken: window frames, sill and blinds draw on top of the projector slide, and the boardroom chart poster is mounted on a window pane.** Back-wall windows are placed every 3.2 m by `windowXs` (decor.ts:70): x = …8.1, 11.3, 14.5. The only skip is x < -11.5 (decor.ts:124), so two windows sit right where the boardroom's projector screen goes. The screen's ink backing is a 4.4 × 2.5 box at (12.2, 1.9, z -9.82±.04) and the screen plane is at z -9.77 (decor.ts:151, 155). The window units are in the wall's upper group at local z .16–.26 (dressing.ts:27-31): the sky plane is at world z -9.84, the frame bars are .08 deep reaching z -9.76, the blinds are at -9.81 and the sill is box(w+.4,.06,.22) centred at -9.74. The window at 11.3 (frame x 10.0–12.6) therefore lies completely inside the screen, and the one at 14.5 (13.3–15.7) overlaps it by 1.1 m. Frame bars, mullion, sill and blind slats stick 1–3 cm in front of the screen plane. When the projector lights up, the player's reward image (the bar-chart slide) is crossed by white mullions, a horizontal sill, the blind slats and a second window's frame (meeting-models-39-win, -40-win-later, crop -61). The 'graph' poster `wallArt(back,'graph',15.2,1.9,.18,0,.9)` (decor.ts:129) is centred on the 14.5 window's glass: a poster hung on a window (meeting-models-30, -28, -40). The deadline clock at x -3.1, radius .34 (decor.ts:126), also overlaps the right frame of the -1.5 window by about 2 cm (frame half-width 1.28 → -2.78 vs clock edge -2.76; meeting-models-47). These are the hero shot and the end-of-level camera, so the defect is in every screenshot a player takes of the win. It breaks DR-72 (signage mounted on a wall face), DR-77 (overlapping coplanar faces) and DR-11 (a juicy, clean win frame).

*gap2-quality2-retake* — **At quality 2 the Meeting win's projector 'light-up' blooms the screen white: the slide and graph that are the payoff disappear.** Meeting's lightUp sets the projector screen to a MeshBasicMaterial at colour ×1.25. It also puts a 4 m additive glow sprite at 0.35 opacity in front of the screen, a 7-intensity point lamp, and a 5.1 m beam cone that becomes visible on win. At quality 0 the slide's bars and red trend line read clearly. At quality 2 (same push-in frame) the beam and sprite bloom over the screen's whole left half: the bars and trend line are washed out, the lamp shade at left melts into the glare, and the coworker's head blends into it. Measured on the screen region (x 60–840, y 180–480): pixels above 245 luma are 23.6% at q2 and 9.6% at q0, and contrast std falls from 44.9 to 35.2. Whole-frame blown pixels are 3.94% at q2 and 0.81% at q0. This is not the known 'Pip missing from the win shot' issue (QA 10, meeting-play). Even the machine half of the payoff is unreadable, because the projected slide is the only thing that says 'the meeting can start'. It is a new finding that appears only at quality 2.

**Fix.**

The clock alternative 'x 0.1, radius .3 fits' is wrong as reasoned. The gap between the 1.7 and -1.5 frames (-0.22…0.42) is the same 0.64 m as the clock's current gap, so moving it changes nothing. Keep x -3.1 and shrink the face to radius ≤ .30 (ring cyl .30, face .27, ticks at .2) instead. Drop the blinds from the verify criteria.

Reviewer's fix: In decor.ts meeting(): skip windows that intersect the boardroom back wall. Change line 124 to `backWindows(game,back,x=>x< -11.5||(x>9.3&&x<16.5),.2)`, which leaves the boardroom with a windowless back wall behind the screen. If you want a window there, keep the one at 14.5 but move the screen to x 11.3 and shrink it to 3.4 m wide, `box(3.4,2.1,.08)` / `PlaneGeometry(3.2,1.9)`. Move the 'graph' poster to a clear wall face, for example x 15.9 (only if the 14.5 window is skipped), or onto the boardroom glass frame post at x 13.8. Pull the screen plane forward to z -9.70 and the backing to -9.74, so no window part can ever sit in front of it. Move the clock to x -3.1 with s=.85, radius .29, or to x 0.1, which sits exactly between the -1.5 and 1.7 frames: gap from -0.22 to 0.42, radius .3 fits.

*From gap2-quality2-retake:* In src/levels/decor.ts:169, set the slide colour to setScalar(1.0), so it stays below the 1.3 threshold. Drop the 4 m glow sprite, or shrink it to glow(…,1.2,.25) and place it at the projector lens (12.2, 1.9, −9.8) rather than over the screen. Lower the beam opacity from .14 to .07 and flag it userData.noBloom, or move it to a non-bloom layer. As the general fix, add a selective-bloom layer: render bloom only for meshes tagged as hot emissives (bulbs, arcs, LEDs) and never for screens that carry information.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

### R5-145

**R5-145 | P1 | lunch | visual-bug | Lunch cables never wrap furniture: they pass straight through tables, chairs, coworkers, bots and the dolly**

Found by: `cable#4` (P1 visual-bug). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

LunchRuntime routes every cable with `cable.rope.update(end, g.level.obstacles)` (src/lunch-runtime.ts:243), which means walls only. The furniture-corner logic that Playground and Meeting use (game.ts:273-282) isn't applied.

- cable-131: a taut thin lead (strain 0.96) runs diagonally across the lounge, through the round table, a blue chair, a pink coworker and the bot lane.
- cable-89: the thin lead passes through a cleaner bot.
- cable-84: the thick cable runs under and through its own dolly.

Lunch is the room with the most cables (4 plus splitters). The cable rule (AGENTS 4: 'wraps') and the routing lesson (keep leads out of the bots' path and the door) depend on cables lying around objects. Here routing is only about walls, and props can't be used to snag or wrap a lead.

**Evidence.**

- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:243`
- `src/game.ts:273-282`
- [cable-131-ln-thin-taut.jpg](shots/cable-131-ln-thin-taut.jpg)
- [cable-89-ln-thin-overstretch.jpg](shots/cable-89-ln-thin-overstretch.jpg)
- [cable-84-ln-thick-drag-close-orbit.jpg](shots/cable-84-ln-thick-drag-close-orbit.jpg)
- `src/game.ts:348` (Lunch runs lunch.step instead of simulateCable)
- `src/props/prefabs.ts:20` (bridge mass 3)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** When reusing the furniture builder in Lunch, exclude more than the dolly, tray and bots. Leave out cable bridges (kind 'bridge', mass 3, which would pass the mass>=3 filter): cables are meant to lie ON them (bridgeNear, lunch-runtime.ts:206-208). Wrapping a bridge would break the wet-cable/bridge lesson. Also leave out splitters, the supply carts and the capacitor cart (they carry ports, so a cable end sits inside their boxes), the mop and the door leaves. Use an allowlist of solid furniture kinds (table, chair, sofa, shelf, cabinet, desk, cooler, vending).

Reviewer's fix: Share the furniture-corner logic.

1. Factor the furniture-obstacle builder in Game.simulateCable (game.ts:270-282) into `furnitureNear(route, exclude)`, returning `Obstacle[]` plus the wrapped set.
2. Call it per cable in LunchRuntime.step: `cable.rope.update(end, [...g.level.obstacles, ...furnitureNear(cable.points)])`. Exclude the dolly, tray and bots, which are dynamic and would fight.
3. For NPCs and bots, push them gently aside instead, or let the cable lie under them visually by raising the hose 0.12 m over their footprint in cablePath.

**Verify.**

- Rerun mockups/review5/tools/cable/ln2.mjs and retake cable-131. The thin lead should bend around the lounge table and chairs. Spec in lunch-rules.spec.ts: drag thin-2 past the lounge table, then check that snapshot.lunch.cablePoints['thin-2'] has at least one bend near the table's corners.

**Rules:** AGENTS 4

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — lunch-runtime.ts:243 calls rope.update(end, g.level.obstacles), which means walls only. simulateCable (with the furniture logic) never runs on Lunch (game.ts:348). cable-131 shows the orange taut thin lead crossing the round lounge table, a blue chair and the pink coworker. cable-84 shows the thick hose passing under and through the dolly's deck.

### R5-146

**R5-146 | P1 | lunch | visual-bug | The thick-cable dolly isn't the cable's source; it rides 1.3 m beside Pip and the cable passes through it (DR-74 still open)**

Found by: `cable#7` (P1 visual-bug). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

While the thick cable is held, the dolly with the big yellow drum is driven toward Pip whenever it is more than 1.3 m away (src/lunch-runtime.ts:237). The hose itself is drawn from Supply B straight to Pip's glove and ignores the drum.

- cable-83: the dolly sits between the camera and Pip's legs.
- cable-84: the striped cable runs under the dolly's deck and wheels, not off the drum.
- cable-136: the dolly is left behind in the corridor while the cable lies elsewhere.

The prop that looks like 'the reel of thick cable' has nothing to do with the cable's length or path. It parks next to Pip and blocks him. This is known as DR-74 (rule says P1), and is still open at HEAD.

- mockups/review5/RULES.md:459

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Account for the plug offset. The held end is 0.6 m ahead of Pip (lunch-runtime.ts:241), so sampling at len-2.2 leaves the dolly only about 1.6 m behind Pip. Sample at arc length max(0, len-2.8) to meet DR-74's 2 m.

Reviewer's fix: Put the dolly on the cable path.

1. Sample the held thick cable's route at arc length `max(0, len − 2.2)` and drive the dolly toward that point, so it trails 2.2 m behind along the cable. That keeps it out of the camera line by construction.
2. Split the drawn hose: supply → dolly drum (slack) and drum → glove (taut, showing strain).
3. Spin the drum with paid-out length, and scale a wound-cable cylinder on the drum the way the reel spool works (game.ts:292), so the drum shows the length left.

**Verify.**

- Retake research-art-38/39 and cable-83/84 at the default camera and orbited 180°. The dolly must be at least 2 m behind Pip along the cable, and the cable must visibly leave the drum. Check in ln2.mjs: the distance from the dolly to Pip is at least 1.9 m throughout the thick drag.

**Rules:** DR-74

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — lunch-runtime.ts:237 drives the dolly toward Pip whenever it is more than 1.3 m away. The hose is routed from Supply B to the glove and never touches the drum (lunch-runtime.ts:239-243, 312-315). In cable-84 the dolly sits right beside Pip and the striped hose runs under its deck. In cable-136 the dolly is left behind. This matches the open DR-74 (mockups/review5/RULES.md:459, which cites this exact line).

### R5-147

**R5-147 | P1 | meeting | visual-bug | Seated coworkers hover in mid-air when their chair is taken or knocked away**

Found by: `characters#0` (P1 visual-bug). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Big Meeting seats 22 of its 24 coworkers on task chairs. The chairs are ordinary dynamic props, and the prompt next to every desk is "Grab the chair". A seated blob is not attached to its chair. It is a static group at the chair's spawn spot with its body lifted 0.35 m (`seated?.35:0`). When Pip grabs the chair, or a throw or cable drag knocks it away, the blob stays at 0.35 m and floats over bare floor: its capsule bottom sits about 0.40 m up, with nothing under it (characters-51, -52, -52b). Grabbing or wrecking chairs is one of the first things a Good Job-style player does in an office. The result reads as a broken model, not a joke, and it happens at every one of the 22 desks. A coworker falling on their bum, or popping up to stand with the alarm pose, would be a free laugh (DR-03, DR-04).

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:128` (seated=level.id==='meeting'&&!p.standing; body.position.y=seated?.35:0)
- `src/game.ts:134` (baseY fixed at spawn; no link to the chair prop)
- `src/game.ts:429` (body.position.y=npc.baseY+cheer*.35+typing every frame)
- `src/levels/meeting.ts:15-18` (chair prop and npc pushed at the same x,z; chair is a normal grabbable prop)
- [characters-50-meeting-before-chair-grab.jpg](shots/characters-50-meeting-before-chair-grab.jpg)
- [characters-51-meeting-blob-floating-no-chair.jpg](shots/characters-51-meeting-blob-floating-no-chair.jpg)
- [characters-52-meeting-blob-floating-no-chair-side.jpg](shots/characters-52-meeting-blob-floating-no-chair-side.jpg)
- [characters-52b-crop-floating-blob.jpg](shots/characters-52b-crop-floating-blob.jpg)
- [verify-characters-05-meeting-after-chair-grab-o5.jpg](shots/verify-characters-05-meeting-after-chair-grab-o5.jpg)
- [verify-characters-05b-crop-floating-blob.jpg](shots/verify-characters-05b-crop-floating-blob.jpg)
- [verify-characters-03-meeting-after-chair-grab-o3.jpg](shots/verify-characters-03-meeting-after-chair-grab-o3.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-characters/v1.mjs`
- `src/levels/meeting.ts:19` (npcs pushed only while length<22, so 20 desk NPCs) and :26 (4 boardroom NPCs on dynamic chairs)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The main fix (find the chair at build time, and in render() drop or pop the blob up when the chair moves more than 0.35 m, tilts, or is held) is right. Don't take the 'cheaper alternative' of fixed or kinematic chairs left out of nearest(). It removes grabbable clutter from a dense physics room, which goes against the Good Job chaos rule. snapshot() (src/game.ts:504) also has no npc field yet, so the proposed spec needs `npcs:this.npcs.map(n=>({seated:n.seated,y:+n.body.position.y.toFixed(2)}))` added there.

Reviewer's fix: In src/game.ts, give each seated Npc a `chair?:Prop` reference when it is built in addNpc. Pick the nearest `kind==='chair'` prop within 0.3 m of the NpcSpot, the same way `desk` is found on line 133. In render(), each frame, compare the chair's body translation with npc.group.position. If the chair is more than 0.35 m away horizontally, or tilted more than 25° (from its quaternion), or is `this.held`, set `npc.seated=false`, ease `npc.baseY` to 0 over about 0.25 s with a squash on landing (reuse the `duck` scale), call `this.alarm(npc.group.position,1.5)`, and play the 'alarm' voice. That gives the "fell off the chair" gag. Optionally, when the chair comes back within 0.4 m, sit again (baseY back to 0.35, snapping to the chair's x,z). A cheaper alternative: make occupied chairs fixed or kinematic and leave them out of nearest().

**Verify.**

- Retake characters-50/51/52 with mockups/review5/tools/characters/s7.mjs (grab the chair at (-6.85,-7.05), walk away). The blob must land on the floor or stand, and none may hover. Add a spec to tests/routes.spec.ts: grab that chair, advance(1), then assert that no npc group has body y > 0.05 without a chair under it. That needs a snapshot field such as `npcs:[{seated,y}]`.

**Rules:** DR-03, DR-04

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Reproduced it myself. In meeting I grabbed the chair beside (-6.85,-7.05) with E, carried it away, dropped it and orbited at zoom 9. The blue glasses-and-tie blob hangs in the air with no chair under it, and its shadow lies well clear of its base (verify-characters-05, -05b).

### R5-148

**R5-148 | P1 | lunch | visual-bug | The baked tray glides through mid-air for 3 m between the end of the conveyor and the lift car**

Found by: `lunch-models#1` (P1 visual-bug). Batch: R-lunch (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The conveyor group is centred at x 3.5 with an 8.5 m belt, so it ends at x 7.75. The lift car's near edge is at x 10.7. The runtime moves the tray linearly with x = −0.5 + along×12.5 up to x 12, at a fixed y 1.18. So for the last quarter of transport the tray slides through empty air: through the wall gap, over the lift-room floor, about 1.1 m up, with nothing under it (lunch-models-94, -95). This is the payoff beat of the clean run ('send the tray up'), and it reads as a bug. It also hides the idea that the conveyor delivers onto the lift.

**Evidence.**

- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:92` (conveyor at x 3.5, rbox 8.5 long → x −0.75…7.75)
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:278` (tray x = −.5 + along*12.5 → up to 12)
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:96` (strip-curtain flaps at x 8.15)
- [lunch-models-94-tray-over-gap.jpg](shots/lunch-models-94-tray-over-gap.jpg)
- [lunch-models-95-tray-over-gap-side.jpg](shots/lunch-models-95-tray-over-gap-side.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/lunch-models/g.mjs`
- [verify-lunch-models-05-tray-over-gap.jpg](shots/verify-lunch-models-05-tray-over-gap.jpg)
- v1.mjs output: tray {x:9.25,y:1.18,z:-7}
- `src/levels/lunch.ts:26` (clutter lane [[-.6,-7],[7.6,-7]] r .75 stops at 7.6)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** If you extend the belt, also extend the clutter lane at lunch.ts:26 from [7.6,−7] to [10.6,−7], so clutter can't spawn on the new section. The belt has to pass through the lift-divider doorway (lunch.ts:37-38 leaves z −7.85…−6.15 open); a 0.9 m belt at z −7 fits.

Reviewer's fix: Extend the belt into the lift room. In buildKitchen(), add a second conveyor section in the lift room: rbox(2.4,.25,.9,.1) at (9.5,.95,−7) with a matching belt plane box(2.4,.03,.75) sharing this.belt's texture (offset x so it scrolls in sync), plus two leg pairs at x 8.6 and 10.4. Add solid(g,2.4,.3,.9,9.5,.95,−7). Alternatively, clamp the tray path: x = min(7.6, −.5 + along×8.1) while along < 1, then hand the tray to the lift car with a short 0.4 s hop tween (x 7.6 → 12, y arcs to 1.4) once the car is down. Either way the tray must never be over bare floor.

**Verify.**

- Re-run lunch-models/g.mjs (tray at transport .78) and retake lunch-models-94/95: there should be belt under the tray at every transport value from 0 to 1. Also replay tests/lunch.spec.ts 'intended Lunch Rush solution' and confirm it still delivers.

**Rules:** —

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Reproduced it. With job.tray='conveyor' and transport .78, the tray sits at (9.25, 1.18, −7) (v1 output). That is past the belt end at x 7.75 (lunch-runtime.ts:92: group at x 3.5, 8.5 m rbox) and past the lift-divider gap. In verify-lunch-models-05 it hangs over bare lift-room floor with nothing under it. Line 278 sets x = −.5 + along×12.5, which runs up to 12.

The seat dimple and seam are not visible at the game camera. ART F5 reported this and it is still open (P5 'bread loaves').

*lobby-models* — **The lobby beanbag still reads as a lilac macaron or a lying coworker: two stacked even lobes in BLOBC purple, the same hue as the receptionist.** The beanbag at (8.6, 5.8) is coloured '#b392f0' (src/levels/lobby.ts:7), which is exactly BLOBC[0] (src/render/kit.ts:9) and the receptionist blob's purple. The model (src/props/prefabs.ts:130-136) is a squashed sphere of radius .45 (scale y .48) with a second sphere of radius .34 (scale 1.12, .72, .78) behind it. That's two even stacked lobes, the shape ART R7 forbids. The seat dent (sphere .2, scale y .18, darker) is invisible from the default camera, and the torus seam is hidden under the bulge.

At the default camera it's a lilac double-blob next to the Workshop (lobby-models-01, -26). Close up it's a purple macaron or cushion (lobby-models-36, -37). research-art-20 flagged the same thing ('looks like a coworker lying down'), and it isn't fixed.

This breaks DR-52 (no prop in a blob hue reads as a coworker, macaron or bread) and the beanbag row of DR-61.

*meeting-models* — **Beanbags still read as squashed blobs or buns, and they use coworker and job hues (DR-52 known F5, confirmed in the meeting lounge).** The beanbag is two stacked, flattened spheres (sphere .45 scaled y .48 plus sphere .34 scaled 1.12/.72/.78), a torus seam and a flat dark disc (prefabs.ts:130-137). At the game camera and in survey the meeting's two lounge beanbags read as a yellow bun or macaron and a blue blob lying on the floor (meeting-models-02, -20, -21, -59). At zoom 9 from the side (-26) the higher back lobe reads as a head with a bump, much like a sitting yellow coworker. Their colours make it worse: #ffc94d (meeting.ts:29) is both a BLOBC coworker hue (kit.ts:10) and job yellow, and #5b9cf0 is a BLOBC hue. ART R7 asks for a pear or teardrop sack with a seat dent, a pinched top or seam and a lean, never two stacked even lobes. The lounge is the room's chaos-comedy corner, so props there need to be named correctly at a glance (DR-61).

*observatory-models* — **Beanbags are round lumps in coworker hues: 13 of them read as lying blobs or dumplings.** The room has 13 beanbags: 2 placed plus 11 from the 'lounge' and 'reading' recipes (scene count, 08-count.mjs). Their colours come from the clutter palette, and include '#8fd3c8' (an exact BLOBC coworker hue, kit.ts:10), '#9b7bf0' (near BLOBC '#b392f0') and the default '#ffc94d' (also in BLOBC). The model is a squashed sphere plus a back lobe sphere, a thin torus seam and a small dark dimple (prefabs.ts:130-136). At the game camera and top-down (shots 06, 70) they read as round pastel lumps the same size and colour as the blob astronomers standing next to them. At zoom 9 (shots 10-o90, 12-dome) the seam and dimple are lost under the toon ramp, so they look like dumplings or lying blobs, not pear-shaped sacks. The teal one by the dome in shot 12 sits beside the teal-scarfed coworker, and the two shapes are nearly the same. This is the known P5 'bread loaf' issue, repeated 13 times in this room.

*playground-models* — **Beanbags still read as bread loaves or burger buns, in cardboard brown.** There are six beanbags, from three 'lounge' clusters: (-9.09,-1.67), (-7.99,-1.52), (-1.33,1.73), (-0.23,1.88), (1.02,6.67), (0.87,7.77). Each is a flattened sphere plus a second squashed sphere with a thin torus seam. The lounge recipe picks their colour from the default FLOOR kraft palette (#c98f5a/#d7a56d/#e0b47a), so they are the same brown as the cardboard boxes. At the game camera they read as bread rolls, brioche or potatoes (start, survey). At zoom 9 the two even lobes read as a burger bun or a cinnamon bun (shots -14, -15, -19). There is no seat dent you can read, no pinched top and no fabric colour. They also share the box colour family, which breaks DR-51 (fabric is saturated, cardboard is kraft). ### R5-150

**R5-150 | P1 | lobby | model-detail | Lobby progress reward (wing lamp) sits off the top of the frame and medals are ~10 px; done doors barely celebrate**

Found by: `lobby-models#6` (P1 model-detail), `lobby-play#17` (P2 fun), `progression#9` (P2 clarity). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*lobby-models* — **The 'wing lights up' reward lamp is a grey ball on top of the wall cap, nearly off the top of the frame at the default camera, with its fixture upside down.** A finished job should light its wing. That's the only physical sign of progress in the hub, and it backs the bonus 'Light every wing'. The lamp, however:
- is a sphere(.13) at frame-local y 3.35, z .12, with a DMETAL cylinder above it at y 3.5 (src/hub/lobby.ts:96);
- sits on top of the 3.0 m wall, whose cap runs from 3.07 to 3.18, so it perches like a pearl on the cap with its 'fitting' on top (an upside-down sconce);
- unlit, reads as a random grey knob (lobby-models-13, -15, -21, -32);
- lit, uses a 1.4 m glow sprite at 0.35 opacity, more than 5× the bulb's size (DR-66 says at most 1.5×).

At the default camera (zoom 23) the lamps land at y ≈ 5-25 px. The lit glows are cut by the top edge of the frame (lobby-models-19, -43). So the reward the hub promises in its own comment ('a wing lights up when repaired', lobby.ts:2) is practically invisible.

This breaks:
- DR-47: state on the device, readable at the game camera.
- DR-72: mounted, not perched.
- DR-66: glow size.

*lobby-play* — **The wing lamps, the hub's progress reward, sit above the frame where the default camera crops them, and done doors look like undone ones.** Finished doors light a lamp at y 3.35 above the frame header (src/hub/lobby.ts:96-97). At the default camera that is the very top edge of the screen. In lobby-play-29 (4 jobs done) the lit lamps are small glows at y about 5–15 px, half cut off. Side-door lamps sit behind the blade-sign bracket. Apart from that, a done door looks the same as an undone one: the same frame, the same closed leaf, and a 0.34 m medal letter that's hard to read. 'Light every wing' should make the room visibly change as the player progresses (the GAME_VISION quote in the file header), but at a glance the lobby with 4 jobs done looks like the lobby with none.

*progression* — **The lobby barely celebrates or signposts progress: the wing lamp sits at the frame edge, medals are about 10 px, Pip returns to the centre.** After finishing Playground and choosing Jobs, Pip reloads into the lobby at the fixed spawn (0, 5.5) (src/game.ts:81 uses `level.spawn`), not at the door he came out of. Nothing happens: no wing light-up, no cheer from the 3 coworkers, no camera beat. The reward is a lamp at y 3.35 above the door (src/hub/lobby.ts:96). At the lobby game camera it lands on the very top edge of the frame as a faint glow dot (`progression-14`; `progression-30`, the arcade door at the top border). The medal is a 0.34 m plate (src/hub/lobby.ts:94), about 10 px at the default camera, and only readable at zoom 9 (`progression-20`). The 'next job' marker is a small cone over the door at the back wall (`progression-02`, at about (340, 60) px) and is easy to miss. Doors show only a number and name; nothing tells a new player what kind of job is behind 05 versus 06. The portal thumbnail only shows once the door opens. The lobby is the only place that communicates the campaign, and today it reads like a corridor of identical doors.
