### R5-222

**R5-222 | P2 | arcade-rush | fun | The cost axis punishes success: every elegant sign-off adds credits, so 32 cabinets grade C on cost**

Found by: `arcade-rush-play#1` (P2 fun). Batch: R-arcade (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Every sign-off adds that cabinet's parts to `spent` (`this.spent+=v.cost`). Rush caps cost at 24 credits. A cabinet's elegant fix uses 1–2 blocks, so a skilled player passes the cost limit at about 14 cabinets. My clean expert run served 32 elegant cabinets with zero mistakes and ended with cost 52, which grades C. Doing more, better work lowers a grade axis: the opposite of the bonus "Eight cabinets or more". In the story Arcade the parts cost is a fixed budget for five jobs. In Rush the job count is open, so a fixed cost cap is a penalty on throughput. A player who reads the result card learns "fixing more cabinets is bad". That teaches the wrong lesson and kills the score-attack loop.

**Evidence.**

- [arcade-rush-play-26-result.jpg](shots/arcade-rush-play-26-result.jpg) (52 credits → C)
- `src/stations/arcade/station.ts:107` (limits.cost = 24 in rush)
- `src/stations/arcade/station.ts:273` (spent += v.cost on every sign-off)
- `mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s2-clean.mjs` log: cab31 … spent 52, mist 0, result cost C
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v1-bench.mjs` log: 'soak … spent 1' then 'after signoff … spent 2' (one 470 block charged at sign-off)
- [arcade-rush-play-26-result.jpg](shots/arcade-rush-play-26-result.jpg) (cost 52 → C while the overall is still A)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The waste-only charge works, but clamp it per cabinet against the cheapest tier≥2 chain, not only best(j). A player who signs off a different chain that is also minimal must not be charged. Keep the pop charges at station.ts:300 and :308. The cost axis only matters once finding 0 replaces best-of-three for rush. Without that change this fix has no effect on the medal.

Reviewer's fix: In rush, charge only waste. At sign-off: `const waste=Math.max(0,v.cost-partsCost({chain:best(j)??[],reversed:false}));this.spent+=this.rush?waste:v.cost;`. Keep the pop charges at `station.ts:300` and `:308`, since those are real waste. Alternatively, scale the limit with the work done: `limits.cost = 3 + served*0.5`, computed at win. With the served-axis grade from the previous finding, cost becomes a secondary axis that rewards using the fewest blocks.

**Verify.**

- Run mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s2-clean.mjs again. Expect cost to be 0 (the fixes are minimal) and the cost grade to be A after 32 cabinets. Add a unit test in src/stations/arcade/logic.test.ts or a station test: signing off best(j) adds 0 waste.

**Rules:** AGENTS 6, DR-07, DR-38

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The code confirms it. Every sign-off does spent+=v.cost (station.ts:273), and the rush cost limit is 24 (station.ts:107). In my v1 run, spent rose from 1 to 2 when I signed off a single 470 block. Shot 26 shows 52 credits graded C. The priority is too high, though. Because the overall grade is the best of three (grade.ts:6), the C on cost never lowers the overall grade or the saved medal.

### R5-223

**R5-223 | P2 | arcade-rush | fun | The clock gives no grace: an order mid play-test at 0:00 is simply lost**

Found by: `arcade-rush-play#11` (P2 fun). Batch: R-arcade (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

When `game.time` reaches 180, `current()` returns undefined, `complete()` is true and `win()` fires on the same frame. In my expert run, the 33rd cabinet was at 'PLAY TEST 1.8 / 2 s' when the clock hit zero. The win push-in shows that unfinished play test frozen on the monitor, and the cabinet is not counted. Losing an almost-finished order to a hard cutoff reads as unfair. Overcooked-style rush modes let the last order land, or at least show a 'last order' warning. There is also no countdown juice: no red clock, no ticking and no 'LAST 10 SECONDS' marquee.

**Evidence.**

- [arcade-rush-play-25-win-pushin.jpg](shots/arcade-rush-play-25-win-pushin.jpg) (monitor frozen at PLAY TEST 1.8/2 s)
- [arcade-rush-play-80-hud-clock-at-170s.jpg](shots/arcade-rush-play-80-hud-clock-at-170s.jpg) (0:09 left, no urgency styling)
- `src/stations/arcade/station.ts:127` (current() undefined at RUSH_TIME)
- `src/stations/arcade/station.ts:487`
- [arcade-rush-play-25-win-pushin.jpg](shots/arcade-rush-play-25-win-pushin.jpg)
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:167`

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Changing complete() alone is not enough. current() returns undefined once time ≥ RUSH_TIME, so update() skips the soak, act('signoff') returns false and the panel hides. current() must keep returning the job in progress during the overtime window, e.g. `if(this.game.time>=RUSH_TIME&&!(this.soak>0&&this.game.time&lt;RUSH_TIME+RUSH_SOAK))return undefined;`. Then auto-sign it.

Reviewer's fix: In rush, if `powered && soak>0 && !soakDone` when the time reaches RUSH_TIME, allow up to `RUSH_SOAK` seconds of overtime. `complete()` returns `time>=RUSH_TIME && !(this.soak>0&&!this.soakDone&&time&lt;RUSH_TIME+RUSH_SOAK)`. If the soak passes, auto-sign it with the 'LAST ORDER!' marquee. Under 30 s, turn the HUD clock red with a scale pulse and add a soft tick every second under 10 s (R3A N4 asked for red under 30 s).

**Verify.**

- Script: start a correct cabinet at t = 179.0 and advance 3 s. Expect served to include it and `won` true at about 181 s. HUD crop at 25 s left shows the red clock.

**Rules:** DR-02, DR-11

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The code and the screenshot confirm it. current() returns undefined at game.time>=RUSH_TIME (station.ts:127), and complete() fires on the same frame (station.ts:487). Shot 25 shows the monitor frozen at 'PLAY TEST 1.8 / 2 s' at the win push-in. The HUD only toggles .late when time > level.deadline (game-ui.ts:167, default 240), so the rush clock never gets any urgency styling.

### R5-224

**R5-224 | P2 | global | fun | The slingshot direction is opposite between floors, and light litter is launched at more than 50 m/s**

Found by: `cable#11` (P2 fun). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Direction: Game.slingshot pushes props away from the anchor, `v = pos − anchor` (src/game.ts:257). LunchRuntime.release pushes them toward the anchor, `v = anchor − p`, as its comment says ('back toward its anchor', lunch-runtime.ts:198-202). The same key and the same prompt fling things in opposite directions on different floors. Physically, a released stretched cable recoils toward the reel.

Speed: the impulse is `min(energy*.22, 45) * min(1, mass/4 + .25)`, so a 0.05 kg paper or 0.15 kg mug gets roughly a quarter of the full impulse. The pg3 'held' release measured fastestProp 53.8 m/s. Props at that speed can tunnel through the 0.35 m walls and read as noise, not as comedy.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:257`
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:198-202`
- `mockups/review5/tools/cable/log-pg.txt` (pg3 held: fastest right after 53.77)
- `src/game.ts:123` (setCcdEnabled(p.mass<4))
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-cable/v1.mjs` (sprintNow Q fastest 53.77)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Drop step 3 (enable CCD for 1 s): CCD is already on for every prop under 4 kg (game.ts:123). Keep the shared whip helper, the toward-anchor direction and the speed clamp (impulse<=mass*14).

Reviewer's fix: Use one shared `whip(points, anchor, energy)` helper for both floors.

1. Direction: toward the anchor along the nearest segment's tangent, plus 0.5 up.
2. Speed: clamp each prop's resulting speed, with `impulse = min(impulse, mass*14)` (at most 14 m/s).
3. Enable CCD on light props for 1 s after a whip (`body.enableCcd(true)`).

**Verify.**

- Spec: after the pg3 'held' release, fastestProp is between 6 and 15. A prop at the cable's midpoint moves toward the reel (its position delta has a negative dot product with (prop − anchor)) on both Playground and Lunch.

**Rules:** —

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The direction mismatch is real. game.ts:257 uses v=pos-anchor (away from the reel), while lunch-runtime.ts:201 uses v=anchor-p (toward it, as its comment at :198 says). Speed is real too: I measured fastestProp 53.77 m/s in the sprint-then-Q release (v1.mjs). With impulse=min(E*.22,45)*min(1,m/4+.25), a 0.05 kg paper gets about 2.5 N·s, which is about 50 m/s.

### R5-225

**R5-225 | P2 | global | fun | Throw and slingshot release have no body animation**

Found by: `characters#11` (P2 fun). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Q while carrying applies an impulse to the prop, and Q while holding the plug calls releasePlug. Neither tells the rig anything: PipState has no `throwing` or `released` field. Pip's arms just ease from the carry or haul pose back to idle while the crate flies off his head (characters-24, -18). The two chaos verbs that AGENTS 4 and 5 build the comedy on have no anticipation, follow-through or recoil. Even a 0.25 s overhead heave, or a stumble backwards when the overstretched cable is let go, would sell the physics. Hard landings already get a squash (game.ts:323), so the pattern exists.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:183` (throw = applyImpulse only)
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:9-14` (PipState has no throw/release state)
- [characters-24-throw-release.jpg](shots/characters-24-throw-release.jpg)
- [characters-18-after-slingshot-release.jpg](shots/characters-18-after-slingshot-release.jpg)
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:6-11`
- `src/game.ts:183`

**Fix.**

Add `throwAt:number` and `releaseAt:number` to PipState (set to this.time in game.ts:183 and in releasePlug). In pipRig.update, for 0.3 s after a throw: both arms swing from -2.6 (overhead) to -0.6 with the torso pitching forward .25, plus a small hop. For 0.4 s after a slingshot release with strain above .9: lean back -.35, take a backward step (body.position.z -.15), flail the arms out (lz/rz ±1.2) and use the O-mouth face from the expression finding. Optionally add a 60 ms hitstop on release (this.hitstop already exists).

**Verify.**

- Retake characters-24 and characters-18 with real-time capture (rt.mjs), 3 frames at 60 ms intervals after Q. The arms must be overhead or flailing in frame 1 and settling by frame 3.

**Rules:** AGENTS 4

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Code: the throw at src/game.ts:183 is only `this.held=undefined; p.body.applyImpulse(...)` plus a tone, and the Q-on-plug path calls releasePlug(). PipState (src/render/pipRig.ts:6-11) has no throw or release field, so the rig just eases back to idle. Hard landings do get a squash (src/game.ts:323), so the pattern exists. This is a missing animation, polish-level.

### R5-227

**R5-227 | P2 | global | fun | Pip can't emote: one fixed smile, mostly hidden under the hard-hat brim at the game camera**

Found by: `characters#3` (P2 fun). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Pip's face is a fixed set of GLB parts: two small ink eyes (7 cm tall), cheeks and a torus smile. The rig's only facial animation is a blink (eye scale y). Negative x tips the brim up and back for a model facing +z. The rest of the fix (extra mouth and brow parts toggled by strain, air, land and won, and a smaller brim overhang in create_assets.py:62) is fine. ### R5-228

Nothing ducks, stops, filters or changes the music bus on win, on fail, or while paused. togglePause (src/game.ts:191) only zeroes the strain hum. The win jingle and the Lunch groans therefore compete with the same jaunty loop, and the fail moment keeps upbeat swing music running under the 'sad' beat.

SONGS (audio.ts:6-10) defines only playground, meeting and lunch. setLevel falls back to playground (audio.ts:30), so the lobby, arcade, arcade-rush, garage, qfn, observatory and spectrum all play the Playground song.

- `src/render/audio.ts:25` musicBus gain fixed at .55

**Fix.**

1. Add `duck(level,secs)` on musicBus.gain using setTargetAtTime.

### R5-230

**R5-230 | P2 | global | fun | The startle is a 1-second blip with one pose: it faces Pip rather than the crash, leaves no aftermath, and never escalates**

Found by: `gap6-world-reacts#5` (P2 fun). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

`alarm()` sets npc.alarm=1 (src/game.ts:137), and it decays at 1/s (src/game.ts:423). The bubble pops in over 0.12 s and is gone after exactly 1 s. In every room I tested (playground, lobby, meeting, lunch, qfn, arcade), alarmed was 0 again at +3.5 s, and the coworker had returned to its exact rest pose (world-reacts-01-…-calm, -05-…-calm). The DR-04 timing passes (bubble within 0.5 s), but the reaction is thin. The startled blob turns toward Pip (`watch` → yaw to p, src/game.ts:424), not toward the bin that landed beside it. It doesn't hop, flinch away or glare, and there is no memory: throwing a second bin at the same coworker gives the same 1 s blip. With only one voice per 0.5 s across the whole room (src/game.ts:138), eight blobs startled by one plant make a single chirp. At the game camera, a 1 s bubble on one of 26 blobs is easy to miss while the player is watching the flying prop.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:137-138`
- `src/game.ts:423-430`
- [world-reacts-01-playground-throw-react.jpg](shots/world-reacts-01-playground-throw-react.jpg)
- [world-reacts-01-playground-throw-calm.jpg](shots/world-reacts-01-playground-throw-calm.jpg)
- [world-reacts-05-lunch-crowd-calm.jpg](shots/world-reacts-05-lunch-crowd-calm.jpg)
- `src/game.ts:454-459`

**Fix.**

Raise the alarm duration to 1.6 s. Store the impact point on the npc, look at it for the first 0.5 s, then turn and glare at Pip. Add an onset hop (+0.25 m over 0.15 s) and a 0.3 m lean away from the impact. Keep a per-npc `grudge` counter that decays over 20 s: at 2 or more hits, show a 'grumpy' mood face for 6 s, and at 3 or more, have the blob shuffle 1 m away from Pip. Play a second, lower voice for each extra 3 startled blobs. Optionally, add a 'Startle 5 coworkers' bonus to tie reactions to grading (DR-10).

**Verify.**

- Rerun throw.mjs for playground and meeting. At +0.5 s the screenshot shows the blob facing the impact; at +1.2 s the bubble is still visible; at +3.5 s a twice-hit blob shows the grumpy face.

**Rules:** DR-04, DR-10

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Confirmed in code. alarm sets npc.alarm=1 (src/game.ts:137), and it decays by render dt (src/game.ts:423), so it lasts 1 s of real time. watch turns the npc's yaw toward Pip's position p, not the impact (src/game.ts:424). There is one global voice per 0.5 s (src/game.ts:138) and no memory per npc.

### R5-234

**R5-234 | P2 | garage | fun | Polarity experiments at PULSE count as mistakes and cost the 'no tripped fuse' bonus; the time limit is about 19× the clean solve**

Found by: `garage-teach#15` (P2 fun). Batch: R-garage (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

PULSE is the 'look' tool, but a backwards diode or a reversed cap at PULSE does `mistakes++` (station.ts:219-220), counted as damage. With `limits.damage:1`, one curiosity flip still gets an A, but loses the bonus 'No failed test and no tripped fuse' (`garage-teach-48`: bonus 3 unlit after one experimental flip).

The polarity faults are the most truthful lessons here, and the bonus punishes discovering them (the arcade A7 pattern, DR-38/DR-02 spirit).

Meanwhile `limits.time:420` (station.ts:77) against a 22–45 s solve (`garage-teach-48` shows 0:22) means the time axis is always A (DR-07).

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:77`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:219-220`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:104`
- [garage-teach-48-result-card.jpg](shots/garage-teach-48-result-card.jpg)
- [verify-garage-teach-12-win.jpg](shots/verify-garage-teach-12-win.jpg) (mistakes 2 → B)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Don't set limits.time to 150 s from scripted game time. Time one or two real first-time runs (including the robot carry and reading the asks) and set the limit at about 1.5× the slowest clean run, likely 200–260 s. The rest of the fix (PULSE faults cost a small credit, not a mistake; rename bonus 3 to 'No failed test') is fine.

Reviewer's fix: - **Only TEST failures are mistakes.** Make PULSE shorts and vents cost a small credit (`spent+=.3`, 'blown fuse / scrap cap') instead of `mistakes++`.
- **Rename bonus 3** to 'No failed test' (station.ts:104).
- **Set `limits.time` to about 150 s** (roughly 2× a clean human run, including the robot carry). Re-tune once a human run is timed.

**Verify.**

- 1. Spec: flip the diode, PULSE, then finish clean. Mistakes = 0, the bonus lights, and the cost rises by 0.3. 2. The clean spec's time is within the new limit.

**Rules:** DR-02, DR-07, DR-38

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — station.ts:219-220 adds mistakes++ for a PULSE short or a vented cap, and bonus 3 (station.ts:104) requires mistakes===0. garage-teach-48 shows bonus 3 unlit after one curiosity flip. In my run, one PULSE short plus one failed TEST gave mistakes 2 and a B on that axis (verify-garage-teach-12). limits.time is 420 (station.ts:77).

### R5-235

**R5-235 | P2 | lobby | fun | Entering a door is an instant page reload, and coming back is a reset to spawn: no transition, no return payoff**

Found by: `lobby-play#5` (P2 fun). Batch: R-lobby (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Pressing E at a door calls location.href right away (src/hub/lobby.ts:123). It sets hud.dataset.leaving, but no CSS or code reads `data-leaving` (grep shows only this line), so Pip doesn't step into the corridor, the screen doesn't fade, and the job simply replaces the lobby about 1.4 s later (lobby-play-51 shows the Meeting already loaded). Going back through pause → Jobs reloads the lobby with Pip at the centre spawn (0,5.5), not at the door he left (lobby-play-53, player 0/5.5). A freshly earned medal or lit wing lamp is already there on load, with no lamp ignition, cheer or confetti. The hub's main reward moment, 'a wing lights up when repaired' (header comment at lobby.ts:1-3), never actually happens on screen. DR-11 asks for juicy, framed success moments.

**Evidence.**

- `src/hub/lobby.ts:1-3`
- `src/hub/lobby.ts:96-97`
- `src/hub/lobby.ts:123`
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:76`
- [lobby-play-51-entering-meeting-loading.jpg](shots/lobby-play-51-entering-meeting-loading.jpg)
- [lobby-play-53-back-in-lobby.jpg](shots/lobby-play-53-back-in-lobby.jpg)
- `src/game.ts:81`
- `src/ui/store.ts:20-21`

**Fix.**

In Lobby.enter: lock input and walk Pip 1.2 m into the doorway over 0.5 s (drive the player body toward door.at - wallNormal*1.2). Ramp portal uOpen to 1.5 and add a CSS fade on `body .hud[data-leaving]` (wing colour → black, 400 ms), then navigate. Before navigating, store sessionStorage 'circuit-crew:from'=level.id. In Lobby's constructor and game spawn, if 'from' is set, spawn Pip at that door's at, facing the room. If record() reported first/improved (store a 'circuit-crew:new-medal' flag in game-ui won()), play an ignition beat: the lamp scales 0→1.3→1 with hot() emissive, the glow fades in, a confetti burst comes from the door, nearby coworkers cheer (npc cheer path) and the medal plate flips in.

**Verify.**

- A script: enter the playground, finish it via the routes.spec path, press Jobs. The lobby starts with Pip at the playground door and the lamp-ignite burst is visible in a screenshot about 0.5 s in. Check a fade frame on the way in.

**Rules:** DR-11

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Grepping src for 'leaving' (TS and CSS) finds only the setter at src/hub/lobby.ts:123. Nothing reads data-leaving, so there is no fade or walk-in. The lobby always spawns at level.spawn (src/game.ts:81), and the store has no 'from' key (src/ui/store.ts:20-21 holds only the autostart flag). Lamps are built already lit at load (src/hub/lobby.ts:96-97), so the player never sees an ignition beat.

### R5-237

**R5-237 | P2 | meeting | fun | Backtracking: the strip-first order sends Pip across the same aisle five times on the clean route; most of the run is walking**

Found by: `meeting-play#12` (P2 fun). Batch: R-meeting (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The strip starts by the printer, 2 m from the reel, but must be set at the boardroom door, 21 m away. The cable can't be dragged while carrying it. So every route is: carry the strip 21 m east, walk back 22 m west, then drag the cable 25 m east again. The clean coupler route adds closet→cart→closet (2×13 m), or cart and back twice if the parts are carried separately as the spec does.
In the drive script (which auto-sprints whenever the target is more than 2.5 m away) the strip was placed at 9.6 s, I was back at the reel at 10.1 s, and the clean route finished at 39 s, of which roughly 120 m was traversal. At normal walking speed (4.2 m/s) that is about 29 s of pure walking in a 45–55 s job. Each leg passes the same desks, and nothing new happens on the return trip. It isn't a soft-lock, but it is the kind of dead time DR-09 targets ('no walk longer than 8 s passes nothing interactive'), and it makes the room feel like a fetch quest before the fun starts.

**Evidence.**

- `src/levels/meeting.ts:26` (strip at -8.6,-3.2 next to the reel)
- `tests/routes.spec.ts` placeStrip/backToReel
- [meeting-play-06-carry-aisle.jpg](shots/meeting-play-06-carry-aisle.jpg)
- [meeting-play-38-clean-route-survey.jpg](shots/meeting-play-38-clean-route-survey.jpg)
- s1/s3 logs: strip placed 9.6 s, back at reel 10.1 s, clean finish 39.3 s
- v1 log: 'strip placed true t 8.0' … 'won true t 29.8'
- `src/game.ts:318` (walk 4.2, sprint 6.8 m/s)

**Fix.**

Let the strip ride on the cable: with the strip held, pressing F next to the plug (or picking up the plug next to a dropped strip) plugs the reel into the strip, and Pip then carries the strip as the plug end. Setting it down within 2.6 m of the door completes both step 1 and step 2. That keeps the order (strip, then cable) and halves the walking. Alternatively, start the strip in the lounge (12.5, 4.2) under the lounge desk, so it is a 6 m detour at the far end, and reorder the card ('Bring the cable to the boardroom door', then 'The strip there is missing: find one'). If either is done, retune limits.time (see the grading finding).

**Verify.**

- Rerun s3.mjs with the new interaction and log the time at won: the clean route should drop by at least 8 s. Update tests/routes.spec.ts placeStrip/backToReel and the clean-route test to the new flow.

**Rules:** DR-09

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — meeting.ts:26 puts the strip at (-8.6, -3.2), and the target is (12.3, -2.25), 20.9 m apart. The anchor (-11.4, -7.8) is next to the strip, so every route goes strip east, walk back west, then drag the cable east. In my v1 run (auto-sprinting), the strip was placed at 8.0 s and the win came at 29.8 s, so most of the run is traversal.

### R5-238

**R5-238 | P2 | global | fun | Workshop practice offers no reason to use it: it's identical to normal play, only covers stations, and the picker leaks input**

Found by: `progression#10` (P2 fun). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The picker lists only the 5 station jobs (`levels.filter(l=>l.station&&!l.id.endsWith('-rush'))`, src/hub/lobby.ts:112), so the three cable floors, where the cable feel is learned, can't be practised. A practice run is the normal run with `record()` skipped (src/ui/game-ui.ts:208). Every rule, timer, mistake and grade is identical; there are no free parts, unlimited fuses or hints. Spelling: 'practise any station' on the arch and the picker versus 'Practice · not recorded' on the card (verb and noun are fine in British usage, but the page mixes them).

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Put the picker guard at the very top of the keydown listener, before `this.keys.add(e.code)` (src/game.ts:163), not at :166. Also clear `game.keys` when the picker opens. Otherwise a key already held when E is pressed keeps Pip walking.

Reviewer's fix: Make practice really different, behind `game.practice`:
- unlimited fuses with no mistake count (each station's `score()` returns `{mistakes:0,cost:0}`);
- every part bin unlocked, and a sub-job picker so the player can jump straight to cabinet 3;

Say it in the picker: 'No fuses blow, nothing is scored.' Hide the result card's grade in practice and show 'Practice done' instead. ### R5-240

**R5-240 | P2 | arcade, arcade-rush | clarity | Arcade: LED halo/bloom and a 400 px smoke ball cover the LED and the monitor exactly when the player must read why it failed**

Found by: `arcade-play#11` (P2 clarity), `gap2-quality2-retake#4` (P2 clarity), `arcade-rush-teach#8` (P2 visual-bug), `arcade-teach#9` (P2 visual-bug), `arcade-models#21` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*arcade-play* — **The LED halo and bloom, then a smoke ball, cover the monitor at exactly the moment the player needs to read it (Claw heat and pop).** Claw with the 220 Ω start, powered:
- The over-rated green LED's halo sprite and point light grow with `glowK` (`ledHalo.scale=.4+glowK*.8`, `ledLight.intensity=glowK*3`, station.ts:408). Under bloom this becomes a soft white disc about 450 px across. It washes out the left half of the meter (CURRENT, LIGHT, LED HEAT) and the chain pads (shot 28).
- 1.2 s later the block pops. A grey smoke burst of 8 particles plus the debris (station.ts:303) forms a solid ball that hides the monitor for about 1 s (shot 29), just as the toast explains the 441 mW.

This breaks DR-66 (glow sprites ≤ 1.5× source, never hide the part being taught) and DR-79 (effects never block more than 0.3 s; no solid smoke balls).

*gap2-quality2-retake* — **At quality 2 the Arcade LED halo floods the bench monitor (dark screen +75 luma) and the chain, exactly while the player reads LED HEAT.** arcade-play and arcade-teach report that the LED halo and bloom cover the monitor during the Claw heat. That was measured at q0, where the halo is a soft green disc over the LED and the monitor stays black. At quality 2 (03-arcade.mjs, claw heating 1.2 s after P, same frame as the q0 twin), bloom spreads the halo (opacity up to .95, station.ts:408) over the whole lower monitor. The LIGHT, LED HEAT and BLOCK HEAT bars and the 'NOT PLAYABLE / FUSE OK' row sit in a white haze, and the monitor bezel glows. On the board, the empty S and D chain slots, the LED and the ACROSS slot turn white. Measured: the monitor's mean luma is 111 at q2 against 36 at q0 (the dark screen lifts by 75 luma), and the bar-area std falls from 68 to 54. Chain/LED-region pixels above 230 are 35.1% at q2 and 7.8% at q0. After the pop, the monitor stays hazed (mean 60 at q2, 20 at q0). This is the moment the player must read LED HEAT and the current to understand 'too much current'. Verdict: the claim holds and gets worse at quality 2.

*arcade-rush-teach* — **LED-pop smoke is a giant grey ball that covers the LED, the meter and half the board.** When the LED pops, the smoke burst (10 'smoke' particles at the LED) shows from the bench camera as one huge translucent grey sphere, about 450 px across. It hides the LED being taught, the right half of the meter (light, heat, fuse readouts) and the ACROSS slot, right when the player needs to see what happened and read the toast. It reads as a rendering glitch rather than a puff.

*arcade-teach* — **Failure effects hide the taught part: a 400 px smoke ball covers the LED and the meter, and the overdriven LED's halo floods the chain.** The pop moments are the room's best 'show why' beats, but the effects cover what they should be showing.
- In arcade-teach-31-led-popped.jpg, the LED pop's smoke burst (station.ts:311, 10 'smoke' particles) makes a pale disc about 400 px wide over the LED, the right half of the board and two-thirds of the meter at the very moment the meter's numbers explain the failure.
- In arcade-teach-14-claw-popped.jpg, the block pop's smoke (station.ts:303) covers the whole meter screen.
- In arcade-teach-13-claw-hot-1_4s.jpg, the overdriven green LED's halo sprite (ledHalo, scale 0.4 + glowK·0.8, opacity up to 0.95, station.ts:408) washes the whole board green. The hot 220 Ω block, the part being taught (P = I²R), can hardly be seen under it, and the pre-pop smoke puffs (station.ts:420-421) drift over the meter.
- In arcade-teach-16/-30, the red halo floods the chain socket and the ACROSS slot.
DR-66 caps glow sprites at opacity ≤ 0.5 and 1.5× their source, and says they must never hide the part being taught. DR-79 says effects never block the taught part for more than 0.3 s.

*arcade-models* — **Block-pop smoke puff blankets the bench meter at the moment the player needs to read why it popped.** popBlock() (station.ts:303) emits 8 'smoke' particles at the chain position plus 8 debris. From the bench camera, shot -41 (1.6 s after POWER on the claw cabinet with the 220 Ω block) shows a large translucent grey disc about 500 px across covering the whole meter screen and the board. The toast underneath explains '441 mW into heat (P = I²R)'. By shot -42 (0.8 s later) it has cleared, so the meter is obscured for at least several hundred ms right when the explanation is shown. DR-79 says effects never block the taught part for more than 0.3 s and smoke must not stack into solid balls. The popped block also simply disappears from the pad with a small debris burst; nothing physically pops off the board (A6 not built).

**Fix.**

*From arcade-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The smoke-direction advice is backwards. The meter stands behind the board, at top-local z −0.56 (station.ts:37), so a −z drift pushes smoke toward the meter and keeps it between camera and meter. Instead, limit the pop to 3–4 puffs with low rise (vy about 0.3) and a short life (≤0.7 s). Cap the opacity at about 0.3 and the growth at ×1.8, and/or drift sideways (±x) away from the meter's centre. Halo: cap the scale at about 0.6 m (≤1.5× source, per DR-66) and the opacity at 0.5. ledLight already has distance 1.6 (station.ts:172); reduce its intensity cap rather than adding a new distance.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Cap `ledHalo` scale at 0.35 and opacity at 0.5. Set `ledHalo.material.depthTest=true` and render it before the meter (renderOrder −1).
2. Clamp `ledLight.intensity` at 1.2 and set `ledLight.distance` to 0.8 so it doesn't light the monitor.
3. For the white-hot over-rating cue, use dome colour flicker only.
4. In `popBlock`, emit smoke from the board level, drifting away from the camera (+z toward the meter is wrong; use −z velocity), with 4 particles at most and a 0.6 s fade. Delay the toast until the smoke has cleared to 30 % opacity.

*From gap2-quality2-retake:* In src/stations/arcade/station.ts:408, cap the halo opacity at .45 and its scale at .4+glowK·.4, and set ledLight to ≤1.5. Put the monitor's screen meshes on a no-bloom layer, or render the bench monitor as a DOM or unbloomed overlay, so bloom can't lift its blacks. Show 'over rating' with the LED HEAT bar and a red flicker on the dome, not a bigger halo.

*From arcade-rush-teach:* Use bench-scale smoke for station effects. Add a `scale` option to game.burst (or a 'wisp' kind) and call it from popLed/popBlock with 4 puffs of start radius ≤ 0.04 m, rising 0.3 m, opacity ≤ 0.45, fading within 0.8 s. Also offset them slightly away from the camera (−z board-local) so they rise behind the LED.

*From arcade-teach:* station.ts:408: clamp the halo to `opacity=Math.min(.5,glowK*.4)` and `scale=.3+Math.min(1.6,glowK)*.25` (at most about 0.7 m). Show the overdrive with a flickering dome and a pulsing rim ring instead.

For both pop bursts (lines 303 and 311), use 3–4 small smoke puffs, at most 0.08 m each, rising and drifting toward −z (away from the camera, behind the meter's lower edge). Fade each in 0.6 s.

At pop time, also freeze the meter frame for 1.5 s showing the fatal reading, e.g. 'LED: 62.5 mA = 3.1× rated → POPPED' in red. Then the cause stays readable after the smoke.

*From arcade-models:* In popBlock(), emit the smoke at the board position with smaller particles: count 4, start scale .15 growing to .35, lifetime .6 s, alpha .5→0. Drift them away from the camera (−z, toward the back of the bench) and up, not toward the meter. Add a physical pop: spawn the block mesh as a short-lived tumbling object, launched up 0.6 m with a spin, that lands beside the board and fades after 1.5 s. Keep the meter untouched.

### R5-242

**R5-242 | P2 | garage, observatory, qfn, spectrum | clarity | Bench labels and readout captions are 4–10 px cap height at 1440×900 (rule: 14 px)**

Found by: `garage-models#17` (P2 clarity), `observatory-play#12` (P2 visual-bug), `qfn-play#18` (P2 clarity), `spectrum-play#17` (P2 clarity), `spectrum-models#17` (P2 clarity). Batch: B6 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*garage-models* — **Bench labels and part tags are 7–8 px tall at 1440×900 bench view.** Measured in garage-models-54-bench-view:
- the dark-ink text rows of 'MOTOR' are 8 px tall and 'DIODE' (tray tag) 7 px;
- 'ACROSS MOTOR' text, inside its plate border, is about 8 px caps;
- NODE, SWITCH, CONTROLLER, GROUND: SHARED and the PULSE/TEST captions are the same.

DR-48 requires ≥14 px cap height. R3B M7 measured about 7 px. Little has changed, so this remains partly open. The labels are flat MeshBasic planes lying on the board at tilt -1.2 (station.ts sign(), :159), which foreshortens them further.

*observatory-play* — **Value tags and scope labels are 4–9 px; the tag covers the SHUNT sign; labels overlap.** The can tags carry the key teaching link between part value and corner frequency. The second line ('↓ 11 kHz', '↓ 3.4 kHz') renders at about 4–5 px cap height at 1440×900, the value line at about 8 px. The tag lies at -1.2 rad on the board, so it is foreshortened. The shunt can's tag is placed over the yellow 'SHUNT' slot sign, which then disappears (only a sliver shows). On the scope:
- the legend ('message noise filter'), the axis labels ('1 kHz', '10 kHz') and the corner labels are 7–9 px;
- two corner labels collide when the corners are close ('2.4 kHz' over '2.3 kHz' with a series C and a shunt C);
- the spectrum, which shows what the filter does, occupies only the bottom third, with bars 6–12 px wide.
Other overlaps:
- the rerouted 'clear' cable spline runs across the RECEIVER plate and jack (the R3A N9 complaint moved from ANTENNA to RECEIVER);
- in the 'past motor' position, the route lever's red knob sits over the '1.5 m' rack caption, which reads '1.5 r'.
Breaks DR-48 (text ≥ 14 px cap) and DR-70/DR-72 (no overlaps).

*qfn-play* — **Bench labels are too small: pin tags about 7 px, the EP line about 5 px, key letters about 10 px.** At 1440×900 the QFN pin tags (0.13×0.058 m plates, station.ts:158-159) render with about 7 px cap height. 'EP: not connected' (a 30 px font on a 512 px texture, station.ts:153) is about 5 px. The key letters on the pucks (R, L, V, C, ⏎) are about 10 px (qfn-play-15 crop, qfn-play-14). The net names are the core vocabulary of the puzzle (which pad is VDD), so they need to be readable without leaning in.

*spectrum-play* — **Bench key labels are about 10 px cap height, and the meter captions ('works', 'reliable') about 6 px.** R3B M7 said 6–7 px; the labels are better now but still under the 14 px minimum.
- **Band key plates** (RADIO, MICRO, THERMAL, NEAR IR, VISIBLE): about 10 px cap height in the 1440×900 bench view (2× crop 96).
- **Power keys:** '1 mW / 10 mW / 100 mW' about 9 px.
- **LINK screen:** the 'works' and 'reliable' tick captions about 6 px (crop 99), and the 'got …' line about 7 px.

Fixed since R3B: the GREEN detector label occlusion is gone, because the detector row was removed.

*spectrum-models* — **Bench view repeats values across monitor and side card; monitor microtext is below legibility.** In the bench view (55, 57) the left monitor shows the band, λ and f, and the right monitor shows 'LINK 31.0 dB, CLEAR LINK / BLOCKED: BRICK WALL'. The right-hand HUD card lists Pod, Band, Power, Path ('blocked: brick wall') and Link margin ('31.0 dB') again. Band, path and margin are each shown twice (DR-41), and the toast repeats λ and f a third time ('Radio 100 MHz: λ = 3 m, f = 100 MHz…'). The monitor sub-captions 'c = f × λ = 3×10⁸ m/s', 'FM radio · ribbon not to scale', 'works / reliable' and 'to the storeroom' are about 6–9 px cap height at 1440×900 (DR-48 wants ≥ 14 px). Model-wise the bench itself is rich and reads well (band keys, wave ribbon between posts, tilted map lectern, two housed screens, power keys, lever and send button).

### R5-243

**R5-243 | P2 | global, arcade-rush, meeting, lunch | clarity | Docs and code comments drift from the build (cut rooms, old lock rule, "absorbs the kick", 26 m reel, 4-second soak)**

Found by: `progression#16` (P2 clarity), `arcade-rush-teach#16` (P2 clarity), `meeting-teach#14` (P2 teaching), `lunch-teach#13` (P2 teaching). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*progression* — **Planning docs still describe cut rooms and an old lock rule.** docs/EXPANSION_PLAN.md marks the Via counter, `vias-rush`, Archive, Waterworks, Clockwork and Depot as 'Built', and says Rush is 'locked until the counter is done'. Those rooms were cut on 2026-10-30 (src/levels/index.ts:9 comment), and the only rush is Arcade Rush. PROGRESS.md:156 still says 'Via Rush stays locked until the Via Counter is finished.' Anyone reading the docs to reason about progression gets the wrong campaign.

*arcade-rush-teach* — **Naming and doc drift: 'Orders served', 'broken a new way', and the 4-second soak in the docs.** The result card says 'Orders served' (carried over from the cut Via Rush). The panel says 'N fixed' and the bonus says 'Eight cabinets or more'. The level tagline promises 'Every cabinet is broken a new way', but there are 5 fault templates, 14 % of starts already 'Work', and the fix set repeats (11 distinct answers). ### R5-244

**R5-244 | P2 | garage | clarity | Garage: the job robot is called "the cart" and is an identical copy of the decor robots beside it**

Found by: `garage-play#13` (P2 clarity), `gap7-snap-grab-target#7` (P2 clarity), `garage-models#2` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-garage (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*garage-play* — **Robot identity: the prompt calls it 'the cart', there's an identical teal decoy robot on the next pad, and a yellow cart near spawn also says 'Grab the cart'.** The job robot is spec kind 'cart' (src/levels/garage.ts:8), and NAMES maps cart→'cart' (src/ui/objectives.ts:58), so the prompt at the robot reads 'E Grab the cart' (shot 06) while the card says 'Carry the delivery robot'. The yellow mail cart at (−1, 6.6) right beside spawn (garage.ts:19) also prompts 'Grab the cart', which makes it the likeliest first grab for a new player. Two of the three charging pads hold decor robots (room.ts:85-87). The one at 4.4 is the same TEAL as the job robot and sits right next to it, but it's a fixed solid, so E only shrugs (shot 42). Only the marker tells them apart, and the marker is a 25 px unoutlined pale cone against a cream wall (crop 90). This breaks DR-50 (one name per thing), DR-17 (no false affordances that look like the job item) and DR-42 (the prompt names the current step's object).

*gap7-snap-grab-target* — **Garage pickup prompt calls the delivery robot 'the cart'.** The robot is a `cart` prop with a robot mesh. Next to it, the generic prompt says 'E Grab the cart' (NAMES.cart in src/ui/objectives.ts:58, used at :92), while the card says 'Carry the delivery robot onto the test stand' (src/stations/garage/station.ts:97). The station's own prompt only takes over once it is held ('Carry the robot', station.ts:456). Charging bay carts stand right beside it, so 'the cart' sends the player's eye to the wrong object at the moment of pickup, and the two texts break DR-50's one-name rule.

*garage-models* — **The job robot is an identical copy of the two decor robots beside it; only the marker says which one to carry.** The job robot (a cart prop, id 'robot', at (6.4, -5.2)) is drawn with robotMesh() in TEAL (station.ts:105). The decor robots at (4.4, -5.2) and (8.4, -5.2) use the same robotMesh, in TEAL and '#4aa3d8' (room.ts:87). All three:
- sit on identical glowing pads;
- have identical wall chargers;
- park nose-in toward the back wall.

The 4.4 m one is pixel-identical to the job robot (garage-models-10-robot-pad, -20-wheels-right, -22). Nothing on the model says 'faulty' or 'this one': no warning lamp, no open panel, no tag, no hazard stripe. A player who can't see the marker (it is a pale translucent cone, see the marker finding) has a one-in-three guess. The decor robots are solid colliders, so pressing E near them gives no prompt and no feedback. AGENTS 2 asks for 'play by doing': the world should show which robot is broken.

**Evidence.**

**Fix.**

*From garage-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Also exclude the robot from nearest() once onStand or driving, since it is then Fixed or kinematic and grabbing it does nothing useful.

Reviewer's fix: In objectives.ts promptFor, prefer a name by id: add `const ID_NAMES={robot:'delivery robot'}` and use it before NAMES[kind]. Or let the station supply the walking prompt when nearest().spec.id==='robot': 'E Pick up the delivery robot'.
Make the decor robots read as 'charging, not this one': give them a plugged-in cable from the wall charger and closed sleepy eyes (eyes material toon('#34424a')). Give the job robot a red '!' fault light or a blinking red antenna lamp at start.
Re-colour the spawn-side mail cart away from job yellow.

*From gap7-snap-grab-target:* In garage station.prompt(), add `if(grab===this.bot)return {key:'E',text:'Pick up the robot'}` before falling through (as spectrum does for the pod, spectrum/station.ts:435). More generally, let a prop's spec carry a display `name` that NAMES falls back from.

*From garage-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The eye and lamp materials are reassigned every frame in update() (station.ts:376), so the 'broken' blink must be folded into that line (for example `!this.onStand&&blink?hot('#ff5a4d',2):...`); a separate assignment would be overwritten. The rest of the fix (recolour or dim the decor robots, add a REPAIR tag) is fine.

Reviewer's fix: 1) Make the job robot visibly broken until it is fixed. In GarageBench.update, while !onStand:
   - blink the antenna lamp red (r.lamp.material = hot('#ff5a4d',2) at 1.5 Hz);
   - show '×' eyes (scale the eyes to a flat X, or swap the face material for a red-cross canvas);
   - emit a small spark every 2.5 s from the head (game.burst at root + (.3,.6,0), 'spark', 4);
   - hang a yellow/ink 'REPAIR' luggage tag on the antenna: rbox(.12,.08,.01) with a hazard texture, tied with a TubeGeometry string.
2) Recolour the decor robots so neither matches: for example '#6cc58a' and '#b392f0' bodies with CREAM cargo bins.
3) Turn the decor robots off: dim the eyes (toon('#34424a')) and show a full charge bar on their chargers, so they read as 'charged, parked, fine'.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

- *garage-models:* Hide the HUD via g.page CSS (.objective, .marker). In garage-models-10-robot-pad a first-time viewer should name the job robot from the model alone. Retake that shot and garage-models-01-start.

**Rules:** AGENTS 2, DR-17, DR-42, DR-45, DR-47, DR-50

I also found the same wrong name in two more places. (3/3 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-245

**R5-245 | P2 | global, lobby | clarity | Text polish: "Circuit Crew Hq", mixed practise/practice, a sentence on a sign, key letters inside step text**

Found by: `hud-ui#17` (P2 clarity), `lobby-models#19` (P2 clarity), `lobby-play#18` (P2 clarity). Batch: B6 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*hud-ui* — **Text polish: 'Circuit Crew Hq', mixed 'practise'/'practice', and key letters inside step text (DR-50, DR-39).** (1) The lobby pause header reads 'Circuit Crew Hq', because screens.ts title() lower-cases and re-capitalises every word (src/ui/screens.ts:22). (2) 'practise' appears on the arch sign, the prompt and the picker copy (src/hub/lobby.ts:103, :112), while 'Practice · not recorded', 'PRACTICE' and the ?practice URL use 'practice' (src/ui/game-ui.ts:216, src/ui/ui.css PRACTICE tag). That is L3, still open. (3) Every station step embeds the key: 'Step up to the service bench (E)', 'Sit at the garage bench (E)' and so on (src/stations/arcade/station.ts:110, garage:98, observatory:86, qfn:72, spectrum:87). The card then repeats what the pill says ('E Work at the bench'), and the card stops saying 'what, never how'. (4) The Garage stand moment says the same thing three times: card, the toast 'Sit at the bench to diagnose it.' and the pill 'E Work at the bench' (35 words).

*lobby-models* — **Workshop wording: 'practise'/'practice' still mixed, a sentence on a sign, and the job card and prompt stay live behind the picker (L3).** The Workshop shows the same noun spelt two ways:
- 'practise' in the sign 'practise any station' (src/hub/lobby.ts:103), the prompt 'Workshop: practise any station' (lobby.ts:132) and the picker copy 'Practise any station…' (lobby.ts:110);
- 'practice' in the URL flag, data-practice and the test (lobby.ts:111, tests/lobby.spec.ts:30).

That breaks DR-50. The world sign carries a phrase rather than a name (DR-49). With the picker open, the HUD job card and the prompt pill remain visible under the scrim (lobby-models-25), the L3 sub-item that was never claimed fixed. The two-line button titles are now left-aligned (fixed).

*lobby-play* — **'WORKSHOP: practise any station' lists only jobs 03–07, and 'station' is never explained.** The arch sign and prompt say 'practise any station' (src/hub/lobby.ts:103, :132), and the picker says 'Practise any station…' (l.113). It offers only the five bench jobs 03–07, filtered by l.station && !rush (l.112). A new player doesn't know the word 'station' as a game term (it isn't used on doors, the card or the board), and will wonder why Cable Playground, Big Meeting and Lunch, the jobs they have actually seen, are missing (lobby-play-18). The spelling is now consistent British usage, practise as the verb and Practice as the noun on the result tag, so the L3 spelling item is resolved. The noun is the problem.

### R5-246

**R5-246 | P2 | arcade, arcade-rush | clarity | Arcade bench controls break cross-room key meanings and key letters are missing on bins, lever and stamp**

Found by: `arcade-play#13` (P2 clarity), `arcade-rush-play#16` (P2 clarity). Batch: B2 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*arcade-play* — **Bench controls break cross-room key meanings and aren't labelled on the parts: E stands up, F flips, 1–4 aren't on the bins, and the POWER lever looks like an arcade joystick.** Key meanings change at the bench (DR-22):
- E (grab/use everywhere else) stands up (game.ts:164). A player pressing E on a hovered bin leaves the bench.
- F (plug everywhere else) flips the LED.

The parts don't show their keys:
- The bins show values, not their 1–4 keys. 1=47, 2=100, 3=220, 4=470 runs across the 2×2 layout (station.ts:194). The prompt "1–4 Take a block" doesn't say which is which.
- The pads show A/S/D and the ACROSS slot shows X, but the lever has no P and no POWER, and the ✓ stamp has no Enter (shot 13).
- In an arcade, the red ball-top lever on a mint box reads as a joystick, not a power switch.

Keyboard-only players have to guess or hover.

*arcade-rush-play* — **The bench shows key letters on the pads but not on the bins, the lever or the stamp.** The board prints A/S/D under the chain pads and X beside ACROSS. The four bins carry their Ω values but no 1–4 keycap, the POWER lever has no P, the SIGN OFF stamp has no Enter mark, and the LED has no F. On a 'hot', 'dim', 'across' or 'backwards' start the prompt skips straight to 'P Power on', so the player never sees the '1–4 Take a block' prompt. Learning the 12-key layout depends on hovering with the mouse. For a speed mode, keys need to be readable at a glance. R3A N3 recommended a shared `benchKey()` keycap; it isn't used here.

**Fix.**

*From arcade-play:* 1. In buildBins, add a small key chip on each bin rim (`sign(bg,String(k+1),…,.07)`, ink on lemon).
2. In buildPower:
   - replace the ball-top lever with a paddle rocker switch (rbox .14×.05×.22, tilting ±0.3) with an ON/OFF plate;
   - add a 'P' chip;
   - add an 'Enter' chip under the ✓ stamp.
3. In game.ts:164, make only Esc stand up. E at the bench should act on the hovered object (call `station.pointer` click on `hovered`), matching "E = use".

*From arcade-rush-play:* Add small cream keycap plates (`sign()` with a 0.06 m plate) to each bin rim ('1'…'4'), the lever base ('P'), the stamp rim ('⏎') and the LED rim ('F'). Use the same style as the A/S/D legends, at least 14 px cap height at 1440×900.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

- *arcade-rush-play:* Bench crop: each control shows its key. Measure cap height ≥ 14 px.

My bench shots show the bins labelled 47/100/220/470 with no 1–4 keys. The 2×2 layout runs 1=47 back-left, 2=100 back-right, 3=220 front-left, 4=470 front-right (station.ts:194). ### R5-247

**R5-247 | P2 | arcade-rush, qfn | clarity | Station toasts persist after standing up and describe arrangements that no longer exist**

Found by: `arcade-rush-play#15` (P2 clarity), `qfn-play#22` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*arcade-rush-play* — **Stale text: the card lags at the bench, and old toasts describe arrangements that no longer exist.** On sitting down, the job card keeps 'Step up to the service bench (E)' for about 0.8 s, while the prompt already says 'P Power on'. More importantly, toasts live at least 4 s and aren't cleared when the board changes. At '470 live', the chain is 470 Ω and in play test, but the toast still reads 'Nothing in the chain limits the current…', so the player reads a failure over a passing setup. ### R5-248

**R5-248 | P2 | meeting, global | clarity | "!" alarm bubbles draw through everything, pile up and stack over adjacent coworkers**

Found by: `characters#10` (P2 clarity), `gap6-world-reacts#6` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*characters* — **"!" bubbles draw through everything at 0.7 m and pile up over desks and near Pip.** Each alarm bubble is a 0.7 m sprite with depthTest:false and renderOrder 9, which overshoots to 0.91 m. One thrown chair startled 8 seated coworkers, and four or five big white discs immediately covered the desk cluster, a monitor and the space right beside Pip's helmet, drawn over the pillar and the desks in front of them (characters-90, -91). DR-04 wants the bubble visible, which it is. But stacked at this size they become the highest-contrast shapes in the frame, above Pip and the goal (DR-43), and with depthTest off one can sit on top of Pip whenever a startled blob is between Pip and the camera.

*gap6-world-reacts* — **Adjacent coworkers' '!' bubbles stack on top of each other.** Each bubble is a 0.7 m sprite at y 1.55 (+0.35 when seated), drawn with depthTest false at renderOrder 9 (src/game.ts:132). Boardroom chairs are 1.05 m apart (src/levels/meeting.ts:30), so from the game camera's pitch, one blob's bubble draws straight on top of the bubble of the blob behind it, and the two read as a column of '!' marks (world-reacts-26 crop of world-reacts-17). In the Meeting desk pods, eight bubbles from one plant throw form a dense band (world-reacts-03). The front bubbles also hide the startled faces of the blobs behind them, which are the actual reaction.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:132` (SpriteMaterial depthTest:false, scale .7, renderOrder 9)
- `src/game.ts:430` (pop scale up to 1.3×)
- [characters-90-meeting-seated-alarm.jpg](shots/characters-90-meeting-seated-alarm.jpg)
- [characters-91-meeting-seated-alarm-b.jpg](shots/characters-91-meeting-seated-alarm-b.jpg)
- `src/game.ts:132`
- `src/levels/meeting.ts:30`
- [world-reacts-17-meeting-glass-react.jpg](shots/world-reacts-17-meeting-glass-react.jpg)
- [world-reacts-26-crop-meeting-bubbles-stack.jpg](shots/world-reacts-26-crop-meeting-bubbles-stack.jpg)
- [world-reacts-03-meeting-throw-react.jpg](shots/world-reacts-03-meeting-throw-react.jpg)
- [verify-gap6-world-reacts-05-meet-glass-sprint.jpg](shots/verify-gap6-world-reacts-05-meet-glass-sprint.jpg) (two stacked bubble columns)

**Fix.**

*From characters:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep depthTest:false. Showing the '!' through desks and clutter is what DR-04 asks for, and turning depth testing on would hide bubbles behind monitors and pillars in a dense room. Shrink them instead (scale about .45, pop to 1.2×), cap the visible count at the 3 nearest the impact (the rest get sweat only), and fade any bubble whose projected position is within about 80 px of Pip's head projection.

Reviewer's fix: Set bubble scale .45 (pop to 1.2×) and turn depthTest back on, with a small depth offset (polygonOffset, or y +0.2) so it isn't hidden by its own blob. Limit visible bubbles to the 3 nearest the impact, and give the rest only the sweat drop. Fade bubbles whose screen position falls within 80 px of Pip's head, using opacity .35.

*From gap6-world-reacts:* Show the bubble only on the 3 blobs nearest the impact; the others get sweat and the startled face only. Offset each bubble sideways by ±0.22 m (screen-right, from the npc seed) and scale seated bubbles to 0.55. Alternatively, project the shown bubbles each frame and nudge any pair closer than 40 px.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *characters:* Retake characters-90 (s11.mjs). At most 3 bubbles, none overlapping Pip, and Pip plus the thrown chair still read first in a greyscale squint.
- *gap6-world-reacts:* Retake the Meeting glass throw (chaos.mjs meeting). In world-reacts-17 no two bubbles overlap, and the green and orange boardroom faces are visible.

**Rules:** DR-04, DR-43

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — In characters-90 four large white '!' discs cover the desk cluster and monitors, and one sits right next to Pip's helmet. They draw over the desks because the SpriteMaterial has depthTest:false and renderOrder 9 (src/game.ts:132), with a pop to 1.3× (line 430, scale .7*s). (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-249

**R5-249 | P2 | global | clarity | Mute and sound tile: the label never changes, the muted state is a faint glyph swap, and reduced-motion drops the result-card sound**

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#15` (P2 clarity), `gap8-meta-settings-errors#8` (P2 clarity). Batch: B2 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*gap4-juice-audio* — **Mute works and persists, but its label never changes, and reduced-motion silently drops the result-card sound.** Mute is solid. Clicking [data-ui=sound] set localStorage 'circuit-crew-muted'='1'. After a reload, aria-pressed was 'true' and the icon swapped (Sound constructor at src/render/audio.ts:14-17, syncSound at src/ui/game-ui.ts:142-143). The label stays 'Mute audio' in both states, though (src/ui/screens.ts:103, :158; syncSound doesn't update aria-label), so a screen reader announces 'Mute audio, pressed'.

Separately, the result-card thud sound is wrapped in `if(!reduced())` (game-ui.ts:219). Players who prefer reduced motion lose an audio cue, which is unrelated to motion.

*gap8-meta-settings-errors* — **The muted state of the Sound tile is shown only by a swapped glyph and a faint tint; the label still reads 'Sound'.** Mute works and persists. Clicking the pause tile set localStorage circuit-crew-muted='1' (src/render/audio.ts:18). The setting survived a page reload (aria-pressed true, #i-mute icon) and a trip to the lobby through 'Jobs'. The AudioContext master gain starts at 0 when muted (audio.ts:24). Observatory's own sound also checks a.muted (src/stations/observatory/station.ts:333). The only problem is legibility. The tile keeps the text 'Sound' in both states. syncSound (src/ui/game-ui.ts:142-143) only swaps the icon href and removes the green 'on' tint. In the 4-tile row, the difference is a small speaker glyph with or without an X. The lens tile next to it, by contrast, says 'View: Standard'.

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/audio.ts:14-17`
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:142-143`
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:219`
- `src/ui/screens.ts:103`
- `src/ui/screens.ts:158`
- juice-audio/playground.mjs log: 'muted after click 1 Mute audio', 'after reload {ls:1, pressed:true}'
- `src/render/audio.ts:15-18`
- [meta-settings-errors-50-pause-muted.jpg](shots/meta-settings-errors-50-pause-muted.jpg)
- [meta-settings-errors-51-pause-after-reload.jpg](shots/meta-settings-errors-51-pause-after-reload.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/meta-settings-errors/settings.mjs`

**Fix.**

*From gap4-juice-audio:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** With aria-pressed kept, the WAI-ARIA toggle pattern prefers a fixed label: 'Mute audio, pressed' is correct. Either keep aria-label fixed (then only the visible tile text should change) or drop aria-pressed and swap the label. Don't do both. The reduced-motion thud part stands.

Reviewer's fix: 1. In syncSound set `b.setAttribute('aria-label',muted?'Unmute audio':'Mute audio')`, and update the tile `&lt;span>` text to 'Sound off' when muted.
2. In game-ui.ts:219 play the thud regardless of reduced(), applying only the `.thud` CSS class conditionally.

*From gap8-meta-settings-errors:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The tile has two spans only when the label span is the first span. Use `b.querySelector('span:not(.key)')` or add a data-p="sound" span (like data-p="lens"), so the selector doesn't hit the wrong element.

Reviewer's fix: In syncSound, also set the label: `b.querySelector('span').textContent=muted?'Muted':'Sound'`. Give the muted tile a distinct style, such as a red-tinted background like `.tile.off`.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *gap4-juice-audio:* Re-run the mute section of juice-audio/playground.mjs. The label reads 'Unmute audio' after the click and after a reload. With emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}) the result drain still contains the Nlowpass thud.
- *gap8-meta-settings-errors:* Retake meta-settings-errors-50: the muted tile reads 'Muted' with a distinct colour, and the state survives a reload.

**Rules:** DR-47, DR-50

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — syncSound (game-ui.ts:142-143) updates aria-pressed, the class and the icon, but not aria-label. screens.ts:103 and :158 hard-code 'Mute audio', and the tile span reads 'Sound'. game-ui.ts:219 wraps the thud audio in if(!reduced()). (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-251

**R5-251 | P2 | lobby | clarity | Lobby bonus stars are never explained, two are the same check and the third is automatic**

Found by: `lobby-play#11` (P2 clarity), `progression#11` (P2 fun). Batch: B5 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*lobby-play* — **The hub's three bonus stars are never explained anywhere, and two of them are the same goal.** The lobby job card shows three grey stars (lobby-play-01). The code comment in objectives.ts says bonus wording lives 'on the pause and result screens'. The pause card doesn't list bonuses (lobby-play-27), and the hub never reaches a result screen, which is the only place bonuses render (src/ui/game-ui.ts:216-217). So the hub's goals are invisible. Also 'Light every wing' (this.doors.every(d=>d.done)) is identical to 'Finish every job', because door.done is just !!bestFor(id) (src/hub/lobby.ts:45, :47, :73). The third star is free with the first.

*progression* — **Two of the three lobby bonuses are the same check, and the third is automatic.** Lobby bonuses (src/hub/lobby.ts:44-47): 'Finish every job' is `jobs.every(l=>!!bestFor(l.id))`, and 'Light every wing' is `this.doors.every(d=>d.done)`, where `done=!!bestFor(level.id)` (lobby.ts:73). They are the same condition, so the hub's star row always lights its 1st and 3rd stars together. 'Earn an A on three jobs' is satisfied by almost any three clears (see the grading finding). The hub's job card therefore offers no real meta goal across the campaign, and 'Finish every job' also requires the optional Arcade Rush.

- 'Overheating Arcade' and 'Cable Playground': about 5-6 px (lobby-models-01, -43).

The hub's only job is choosing a door, and half the door names are below DR-48's 14 px. The row looks uneven, as if the signs were different sizes.

*lobby-models* — **The best-grade medal hangs half off the frame post, 18 cm in front of the wallpaper, and is about 12 px at the game camera.** The medal is signPlate(f, best.grade, 1.08, 2.12, .18, .34, …) (src/hub/lobby.ts:94):

- At the game camera it's a 10-12 px chip, and the grey 'B'/'C' variant on '#dfe3ea' melts into the cream wall (lobby-models-19). DR-47 and DR-48 call for a state readable at the game camera.

### R5-253

**R5-253 | P2 | observatory | clarity | Observatory: absurd readouts "S/N −180.0 dB" and "Tone level 0%" with TONE ● lit when the gust lays the whip flat**

Found by: `observatory-play#15` (P2 clarity), `observatory-teach#10` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-observatory (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*observatory-play* — **Absurd readouts: '−180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%' when the gust lays the whip flat.** At the start of job 3, a flat 3.1 cm whip gives an antenna factor of about 1e-37. The panel prints 'Signal/noise −180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%'; other rods print −160.2, −140.2 and −42 dB. These numbers are simulation artefacts (the 1e-6 floor in dB()). They mean nothing to a learner and look like a bug. The scope shows 'S/N -180.0 dB' as well. Breaks DR-31 (displayed numbers must be meaningful simulation values at the level taught).

*observatory-teach* — **Meaningless readings: 'S/N −180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%' with the TONE ● indicator lit, after the gust or with a 3.1 cm whip.** dB() clamps to 1e-9 (logic.ts:85). With the default 3.1 cm whip in job 3 the antenna factor is 0.000, so the scope and panel print 'S/N -180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%' (shot 13). That reads as a bug and teaches nothing about scale.
At the same time the scope's 'TONE ●' marker keeps blinking with the Morse key timing (station.ts:250, :255), as if a tone were arriving, while the trace shows only filtered noise. A learner sees 'tone on' plus 0 % tone and can't reconcile them.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/observatory/logic.ts:100-101` (exp(-r²) underflows)
- `src/stations/observatory/logic.ts:144` (dB(level/max(1e-6,noise)))
- `tools/observatory-play/01-clean.mjs` log 'log2 … snr:-180'
- [observatory-play-21-log2-gust.jpg](shots/observatory-play-21-log2-gust.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-play/01-logic.mjs` output f15
- `src/stations/observatory/logic.ts:85`
- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:250-255`
- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:270`
- [observatory-teach-13-job2-tier1-logged-gust.jpg](shots/observatory-teach-13-job2-tier1-logged-gust.jpg)
- [verify-observatory-teach-04-job3-start-r3.jpg](shots/verify-observatory-teach-04-job3-start-r3.jpg)
- [observatory-teach-32-job3-gust-0s.jpg](shots/observatory-teach-32-job3-gust-0s.jpg) (also −180 dB with TONE ●)

**Fix.**

*From observatory-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The fix (antenna factor floor of 0.01 plus 'no signal' when level < 0.05) is fine. Cite logic.ts:85 as the source of −180.

Reviewer's fix: Clamp the antenna factor to a floor of 0.01 (−40 dB) in antennaFactor() (logic.ts:101): `Math.max(.01, …)`. In the panel and scope, show 'no signal' when r.level < 0.05 instead of the S/N number (station.ts:270, :359).

*From observatory-teach:* Clamp the displayed S/N to '< −30 dB'. When r.level < 0.05, print 'no signal' in red instead of a number, on both the panel row and the scope line. Draw TONE ● only when on && r.tones[0].after > 0.1; otherwise 'TONE —'.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *observatory-play:* Unit test in logic.test.ts: read(beacon job, r3 flat).snr ≥ −40. Retake observatory-play-21: the panel reads 'no signal'.
- *observatory-teach:* Shot at job 3 start: the panel shows 'no signal', there is no −180, and TONE shows the dash.

**Rules:** DR-31, DR-47

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Shot 21 shows 'Signal/noise −180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%'. My logic sweep for job 3 with 10 mH + 1 µF gives r3 −180 (flat and upright), r17 −160.2 flat and −140.2 upright, r75 −7.8 flat and 12.2 upright, r150 −42/−22. One source detail is wrong: the −180 floor comes from dB()'s 1e-9 clamp (logic.ts:85; 20·log10(1e-9) = −180), not the 1e-6 noise floor at :144. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-257

**R5-257 | P2 | global | clarity | The strain thresholds are defined three times and disagree; the HUD meter, hose colour and prompt don't line up**

Found by: `cable#12` (P2 clarity). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

There are separate strain definitions that don't match:
- src/sim/cable.ts:83, `strainColor`: bands at 0.7, 0.85 and 0.97. It is unit-tested (cable.test.ts:8) and imported but unused by game.ts and lunch-runtime.ts.
- src/render/actors.ts:65, `STRAIN`: a ramp with stops at 0.55, 0.72, 0.86 and 1.0. This one actually colours the hose.
- objectives.ts:79 and game-ui.ts:200: the slingshot prompt and button at 0.97.
- game-ui.ts:186: the HUD bar scaled `strain/1.15`.
- audio.ts:46: the hum starting at 0.7.

On top of that, the hose colour along the length is `strain*(0.6 + 0.4u)` (game.ts:304). At strain 1.0 the reel end is still white and only the hand end is red, while the HUD bar is at 87%.

The player gets three slightly different 'how close am I' signals. The tested colour table isn't the one rendered.

**Evidence.**

- `src/sim/cable.ts:83`
- `src/sim/cable.test.ts:8`
- `src/render/actors.ts:65`
- `src/game.ts:304`
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:186`
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:200`
- `src/ui/objectives.ts:79`
- `src/render/audio.ts:46`
- [cable-21-pg-sling-taut-red.jpg](shots/cable-21-pg-sling-taut-red.jpg)
- `src/game.ts:24` and src/lunch-runtime.ts:6 (unused strainColor imports)

**Fix.**

1. Keep one table, `STRAIN_BANDS = {yellow:.72, orange:.86, red:1.0}`, in src/sim/cable.ts.
2. Build the actors.ts ramp from it and delete the unused `strainColor` imports.
3. Drive the HUD bar's colour stops from the same table, and scale the bar as `strain/1.0`, clamped, with a red 'over' overflow segment.
4. Show the prompt and button only on the stored charge (see the false-prompt finding).
5. Update cable.test.ts to test the rendered ramp.

**Verify.**

- Unit test: `strainAt(.72)` = yellow, `strainAt(.86)` = orange, `strainAt(1)` = red, and the HUD stop CSS variables match. Screenshot at strain 0.86: the HUD bar fill colour and the hand end of the hose are the same orange.

**Rules:** —

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — strainColor (cable.ts:83, bands .7/.85/.97) is imported at game.ts:24 and lunch-runtime.ts:6 but never called. A grep finds only the imports and cable.test.ts:8. The hose uses STRAIN (actors.ts:65, stops .55/.72/.86/1). The HUD bar is strain/1.15 (game-ui.ts:186), so it reads 87% at strain 1. The prompt and button use .97 (objectives.ts:79, game-ui.ts:200), and the hum starts at .7 (audio.ts:46).

### R5-260

**R5-260 | P2 | global | clarity | Cable-wrap knock spams 6–10 times a second while dragging or after a slingshot**

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#13` (P2 clarity). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

`knock()` fires whenever the cable's bend count changes, both when a wrap is added and when it is removed (src/game.ts:284). Bends flicker as the rope settles, so the hooked logs show long runs of knocks:
- Playground [slingshot aftermath]: 10 knocks in 1.5 s;
- Meeting [walk] carrying the extended reel: 9 knocks in one leg;
- [coupler F]: 5 knocks.

The knock was meant to say 'the cable caught a corner', a key routing cue (DR-46). As a constant patter it carries no information and masks the strain creak.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:284`
- `src/render/audio.ts:55`
- juice-audio/playground.mjs log [slingshot aftermath]
- juice-audio/meeting.mjs log [walk] after extension
- verify-gap4-juice-audio/meeting.mjs [walk] and [coupler F] drains

**Fix.**

1. Knock only when bends increase and the new bend is a different obstacle than the last one knocked.
2. Rate-limit to one knock per 0.3 s (store lastKnock time) and skip knocks while the rope speed is below a threshold.
3. Play the unwrap as a softer 'slip' (bandpass noise 1500 at .02) at most once per 0.5 s.

**Verify.**

- Re-run juice-audio/playground.mjs. The slingshot aftermath logs ≤ 3 knocks, and one wrap around a pillar still logs exactly one knock.

**Rules:** DR-46

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — game.ts:284 knocks on any change in bend count, in either direction. In my meeting run the [walk] leg after the extension had 9 knocks (t190/t285 + Nbandpass2400) and [coupler F] had 5.

### R5-261

**R5-261 | P2 | global | clarity | Placing any part on a bench plays the full 'plug seated' success chime, even a wrong part that will trip the fuse**

Found by: `gap4-juice-audio#9` (P2 clarity). Batch: B4 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

`plug()` (src/render/audio.ts:60) is the click-clack plus rising 880/1109/1319 arpeggio, the game's 'connection made' reward. The arcade plays it on every block placed in the chain or across the LED (arcade/station.ts:259, :264). The garage plays it on every part fitted to a slot (garage/station.ts:205). Logs: the arcade 'fix + fuse cools' and each cabinet drain carry 1–2 plug chimes. Garage 'fit diode, flip' carries one for a flipped diode about to cause a dead short.

So a reversed or across-the-LED part is greeted with the success chime. The chime is the most frequent positive cue in station rooms, which dilutes the real connection and success moments. Sound should never praise the action that's about to fail (DR-28, DR-38).

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/audio.ts:60`
- `src/stations/arcade/station.ts:259`
- `src/stations/arcade/station.ts:264`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:205`
- juice-audio/arcade.mjs and garage.mjs logs
- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:179` also uses a.plug() for knob slots
- verify-gap4-juice-audio/garage.mjs [fit diode, flip]

**Fix.**

Add `seat()`: two highpass clicks only (noise .02 at 3200/2600, vol .06), no bells. Use it in the bench slot handlers. Keep `plug()` for live cable connections and objects docking (robot on stand, tray to bench, Lunch ports).

**Verify.**

- Re-run arcade.mjs and garage.mjs. Slot actions log only the two Nhighpass clicks, with no 880/1109/1319 bells.

**Rules:** DR-28, DR-38

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — audio.ts:60 plug() is the click-clack plus 880/1109/1319 bells. It's called on slot placement at arcade:259/264, garage:205 and observatory:179. My garage [fit diode, flip] drain contains the full plug chime for the diode that then dead-shorts.

### R5-263

**R5-263 | P2 | lunch | clarity | Capacitor-cart dock prompt lags the real dock zone: 'Push the capacitor cart' shows while the cart is already inside the 2 m dock, and nothing in the world marks the dock**

Found by: `gap7-snap-grab-target#8` (P2 clarity). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Docking tests the cart's position, `distance(capPos,{x:12,z:-4.8})<2` (src/lunch-runtime.ts:232). The prompt tests Pip's position, `distance(pos,{x:12,z:-4.8})<2.2` (lunch-runtime.ts:182). Pushing the cart ahead, it was 1.28 m from the winch (well inside the dock) while Pip was at 2.56 m, and the pill still said 'E Push the capacitor cart'. Releasing there docked it. The lift's port ring is the dim 0.35 one (it only brightens while a cable is held) and is hidden behind the cart. So the player can't tell when to let go, and may push the cart into the winch or keep shoving. Only after release does the cart lead appear (shot 52).

**Evidence.**

- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:182,232,311-312`

- s7 log: ~2.2 capToWinch 1.28 pipToWinch 2.56 prompt 'Push the capacitor cart'; after E docked true
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:232` docked requires g.held!==capacitor, so the player must let go inside the zone without any cue

**Fix.**

Use the cart position in the prompt test (`distance(capacitor.body.translation(),LIFT)<2` → 'Park the cart by the winch'), and while the cart is held, draw the dock ring (r 2 m, dashed, job yellow) and a ghost of the cart lead to the winch socket.

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The code agrees. The prompt uses Pip's distance to (12,-4.8) <2.2 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:182), while docking uses the cart's distance <2 and requires that the cart not be held (src/lunch-runtime.ts:232). While pushing, the cart is ahead of Pip, so it enters the dock radius before the text changes. No dock ring is drawn for the cart. I did not rerun the push myself.

### R5-264

**R5-264 | P2 | global | clarity | The lens setting barely changes anything: Close, Standard and Wide differ by about 8–10% of view, and the bench ignores it**

Found by: `gap8-meta-settings-errors#4` (P2 clarity). Batch: B2 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The only camera setting is the pause tile 'View: Standard/Wide/Close' (src/ui/screens.ts:159; it cycles Standard → Wide → Close, src/game.ts:178). FOVS=[32,42,54] (src/render/lens.ts:5). lensScale (lens.ts:11) pulls the camera in to compensate, so the visible height at the focus point only scales by 1+(fov−30)/110: Close shows about 8% less than Standard and Wide about 10% more. Pip stays the same size on screen.
- **Floor:** with the view reset by C after each change, the three home views of the Playground (shots 52, 57, 58) look almost identical. None reaches the far wall, where the goal lamp is.
- **Bench:** the lens is exact on purpose (lens.ts:9-10), so the arcade bench is unchanged apart from the table corners touching the frame edge at Wide (shots 10, 11, 12).

There is no visible distortion and no cropped control at any setting, which is good, but the player gets no visible feedback from changing it. 'Close' also reads as 'camera closer', yet Pip isn't bigger. The default lens is 42°, while the rulebook's 'game camera FOV 30' convention and the lens.ts comment ('the 30° lens the zooms and bench views were tuned for') are stale.

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/lens.ts:5-11`
- `src/game.ts:178`
- `src/game.ts:58`
- `src/ui/screens.ts:159`
- [meta-settings-errors-52-playground-home.jpg](shots/meta-settings-errors-52-playground-home.jpg)
- [meta-settings-errors-57-playground-home-fov54-wide.jpg](shots/meta-settings-errors-57-playground-home-fov54-wide.jpg)
- [meta-settings-errors-58-playground-home-fov32-close.jpg](shots/meta-settings-errors-58-playground-home-fov32-close.jpg)
- [meta-settings-errors-01-meeting-fov42-standard.jpg](shots/meta-settings-errors-01-meeting-fov42-standard.jpg)
- [meta-settings-errors-10-arcade-bench-fov42-standard.jpg](shots/meta-settings-errors-10-arcade-bench-fov42-standard.jpg)
- [meta-settings-errors-11-arcade-bench-fov54-wide.jpg](shots/meta-settings-errors-11-arcade-bench-fov54-wide.jpg)
- [meta-settings-errors-12-arcade-bench-fov32-close.jpg](shots/meta-settings-errors-12-arcade-bench-fov32-close.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/meta-settings-errors/settings.mjs`
- `mockups/review5/tools/meta-settings-errors/lens.mjs`
- `src/render/lens.ts:2-4`
- `docs/PROGRESS.md:36`

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** One option makes the walking camera uncompensated. If chosen, check that Wide at the max zoom of 38 doesn't push into the survey's 44 framing and that the near-zoom Pip framing still holds. The safer option is the distance-multiplier variant.

Reviewer's fix: Make the setting mean something. Either:
- Turn it into a framing distance (multiply homeZoom by 0.8 / 1 / 1.25 and keep FOV 42). The labels 'Near / Standard / Far' then show visibly more room, and 'Far' can show the Playground goal.
- Or make the FOV choice not compensated (`lensScale` returns 1 for the walking camera), so Wide really shows about 30% more.

Also order the cycle Close → Standard → Wide. Update the rulebook's conventions table and the lens.ts comment to say the default is 42°.

**Verify.**

- Re-run mockups/review5/tools/meta-settings-errors/settings.mjs. The three home shots should differ clearly (for example, the Playground lamp at (7,−6) is in frame at the far setting), and the arcade bench shots are unchanged.

**Rules:** AGENTS 8, DR-21

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The math checks out. The visible height at the focus point is ∝ 2·dist·tan(fov/2) ∝ tan15°·(1+(fov−30)/110), which gives 1.018, 1.109 and 1.218 for 32°, 42° and 54°. Close is therefore −8% and Wide +10% against Standard, and the bench is exact (lens.ts:11). docs/PROGRESS.md:36 still says 'FOV 30' and the lens.ts comment references the 30° tuning, so that part is confirmed too.
