### R5-270

**R5-270 | P2 | garage | clarity | Job 3 prompt says '1–5 Change the parts' when the fix is the ground lever (G), not a part**

Found by: `garage-play#5` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-garage (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

After the job-3 PULSE captures a start-up brown-out, prompt() returns {key:'1–5', text:'Change the parts'} for any tier-0 verdict (station.ts:465). The fix in this job isn't a part: it's re-routing the controller's ground with the small blue-ball lever (key G), which is never named in any prompt unless the cursor happens to hover it (station.ts:447). So the key pill sends the player through the parts tray. The 1000 µF capacitor is the obvious-looking candidate, and it 'rides through part of it, but not enough' (spec line 'Job 3: a bulk capacitor ... but not enough'). That is a designed red herring, but the HUD actively pushes the player into it and gives no cue that the ground route is changeable. The lever is about 20 px at the bench camera and the 'GROUND: SHARED' plaque looks like a label, not a control (shot 24). Expected confusion: a cycle through all five parts and a failed TEST or two (each failed TEST is a mistake). This breaks DR-42 (the prompt points at the wrong thing) and DR-19 (the prompt isn't the real action). It also hurts DR-37: the ground route rule is hidden until stumbled on.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:465`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:447`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:149`
- [garage-play-24-job3-start-sag.jpg](shots/garage-play-24-job3-start-sag.jpg)
- [garage-play-25-job3-star.jpg](shots/garage-play-25-job3-star.jpg)
- [verify-garage-play-13-job3-after-pulse.jpg](shots/verify-garage-play-13-job3-after-pulse.jpg)
- verify log 'job3 pulse': prompt '1–5 Change the parts'

**Fix.**

In prompt(), pick the change hint from the verdict without naming the answer. For fault 'start', return {key:'1–5 · G', text:'Change the setup'}; keep '1–5' for the shutdown faults.
Make the lever read as a control:
- In buildBench, scale the lever ×1.8 and give it a yellow knob.
- After a 'start' capture, wiggle the lever (rotation.z ±0.15 for 0.6 s) the way the meeting coupler wobbles.
- Make the 'GROUND: SHARED' sign a hover target, so its hint shows G.
Also consider letting the player drag the controller's ground lead to the battery post physically (R4B redesign), which makes it a cable act (see the cable finding).

**Verify.**

- In a job-3 state after PULSE, read the .prompt-pill text: it must include 'G' or a non-parts wording. Retake garage-play-24: the lever is clearly visible and moves.

**Rules:** DR-19, DR-37, DR-42

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Reproduced. After the job-3 PULSE (start brown-out), the pill reads '1–5 Change the parts' (verify-13, log 'job3 pulse'), as station.ts:465 does for any tier-0 verdict. The claim of 'no cue that the ground route is changeable' is overstated.

Related (DR-41):
- the same number appears three times (scope readout, panel row and toast: '77 V' in `garage-teach-07`, '0.90 V' in `-22`);
- precision is inconsistent: the toast says '1.4 ms' (logic.ts:172 `ms()`) while the scope and panel say '1.37 ms' (`-19`).

Failing panel rows use class `no`, which CSS renders grey (ui.css:225), while passing rows are green. The failing value is the least salient.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:218`
- `src/stations/garage/station.ts:435-437`
- `src/stations/garage/logic.ts:172`
- `src/ui/ui.css:225`
- [garage-teach-23-j3-scope-start.jpg](shots/garage-teach-23-j3-scope-start.jpg)
- [garage-teach-26-j3-star.jpg](shots/garage-teach-26-j3-star.jpg)
- [garage-teach-19-j2-test-fail.jpg](shots/garage-teach-19-j2-test-fail.jpg)
- `src/ui/ui.css:225` (.bad red exists, unused by row())
- [verify-garage-teach-10-slowtest-t080.jpg](shots/verify-garage-teach-10-slowtest-t080.jpg) (toast 1.4 ms vs panel/scope 1.37 ms)

**Fix.**

- **station.ts:218:** for a job with a start problem (`job.id==='cargo'`), keep the scope on START, or split the screen into STOP top and START bottom, for every PULSE in that job.
- **Remove the numbers from the toast** (the scope is the single number source). Keep the toast as the cause sentence only.
- **Unify** `ms()` and `msText()` on two decimals.
- **station.ts:428:** use class `bad` (red) instead of `no` for failing rows.

**Verify.**

- Retake `garage-teach-26`: the START trace stays above the reset line. Each value appears once on screen. Failing rows are red.

**Rules:** DR-28, DR-31, DR-41, DR-50

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — station.ts:218 sets scopeMode to 'start' only for fault 'start'. After the star fix, garage-teach-26 shows the scope back on SWITCH NODE · STOP. The same value appears on the scope, the panel and the toast ('77 V' in garage-teach-07; '1.37 ms' on the scope and panel against '1.4 ms' in the toast in garage-teach-19/my verify-10), because ms() at logic.ts:172 uses 1 decimal at ≥1 ms. That breaks DR-41 and DR-50.

### R5-273

**R5-273 | P2 | lobby | clarity | The pause card in the hub shows a meaningless time/damage/cost tally, title-cases the name to 'Circuit Crew Hq', and has a 'Jobs' button that just reloads the lobby**

Found by: `lobby-play#12` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-lobby (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

After knocking a chair and a mug about, the lobby pause card shows 0:14, 2 damage, 30 cost (lobby-play-27). The hub is never graded, so these read as a score the player is losing. Damage is counted in the hub because the generic impact code runs there (src/game.ts:335). The header reads 'Circuit Crew Hq' because title() lowercases every word and re-capitalises the first letter (src/ui/screens.ts:22), and the same would hit any acronym such as QFN. The 'Jobs' button calls toJobs() → ?level=lobby (src/ui/game-ui.ts:76). In the lobby that reloads the same room and resets the toys, which reads as a broken button. This breaks DR-50 (one spelling per name) and DR-22 (buttons do what they say).

- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:76`
- `src/game.ts:335`
- [lobby-play-27-pause-menu.jpg](shots/lobby-play-27-pause-menu.jpg)
- `src/ui/screens.ts:157` (`&lt;button class="btn tile" data-ui="jobs-reload" …>`)
- `src/ui/game-ui.ts:70-72`

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Hide it with `body[data-hub] .pause-screen [data-ui="jobs-reload"]{display:none}`, and hide the stat cells that hold [data-p=time|damage|cost] the same way. body.dataset.hub is already set at src/ui/game-ui.ts:29. title(): keep words that are all caps and 3 letters or fewer as they are (HQ).

Reviewer's fix: screens.ts title(): keep tokens of 3 or fewer letters that are all caps in the source (HQ, QFN) as they are. In the pause markup, when body[data-hub], hide the time, damage and cost stats and the Jobs button (CSS `body[data-hub] .pause .stats, body[data-hub] [data-action=jobs-reload]{display:none}`), or relabel it 'Title'. Optionally turn hub breakage into a playful counter ('Mugs thrown: 2') instead of damage.

**Verify.**

- Retake lobby-play-27: the header reads 'Circuit Crew HQ', with no stats row and no Jobs button.

**Rules:** DR-22, DR-50

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — lobby-play-27 shows 'Circuit Crew Hq' with 0:14 / 2 / 30 stats. title() lowercases everything and then capitalises the first letter of each word (src/ui/screens.ts:22). toJobs() goes to ?level=lobby (src/ui/game-ui.ts:76), so in the hub the button just reloads the room. The QFN example is hypothetical: no level name currently contains QFN (that level is 'FABRICATION BAY'), so in practice only HQ is affected.

### R5-275

**R5-275 | P2 | lunch | clarity | A clean, careful run already shows '2 broken': placing the tray and pushing the capacitor cart count as damage**

Found by: `lunch-play#14` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-lunch (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

In the scripted clean run, damage went from 0 to 1 (cost +10) the moment the tray went onto the conveyor, and to 2 (cost +15) while pushing the capacitor cart to the winch. Both were logged at those steps.

The tray becomes kinematic and is teleported to (-0.5,1.18,-7) with setNextKinematicTranslation (src/lunch-runtime.ts:277-278). Rapier reports a large apparent velocity, and the next frame's speed drop trips the impact check (lastSpeed > 5.5 and drop > 3.5, src/game.ts:337), which marks the tray itself as broken. The pushed cart, driven by setLinvel ×12, bumps clutter at speed.

From the second step on, the HUD tally reads '1 broken' and then '2'. That tells a tidy player they broke something, which undermines the damage axis as feedback.

**Evidence.**

- `mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s2-clean.mjs` log: 'tray on belt … dmg 1 cost 10', 'at winch … dmg 2 cost 15'
- [lunch-play-c11-shelf-moved.jpg](shots/lunch-play-c11-shelf-moved.jpg) (tally 1 / 10)
- [lunch-play-c14-cap-docked.jpg](shots/lunch-play-c14-cap-docked.jpg) (tally 2 / 15)
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:277-278`
- `src/game.ts:337`
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v3-clean.mjs` log: 'tray on belt … dmg 1 cost 10', 'at winch … dmg 2 cost 15'
- [verify-lunch-play-c14-cap-docked.jpg](shots/verify-lunch-play-c14-cap-docked.jpg) (tally 2 / 15)

**Fix.**

(1) In the damage loop, skip props with spec.id, or with kinematic or fixed bodies.
(2) When placing the tray, call body.setTranslation (not setNext…) and set prop.lastSpeed = 0, damaged = true.
(3) Cap the pushed heavy prop's impulse transfer by setting damaged = true for clutter hit by a held heavy job item at under 6 m/s.

**Verify.**

- Rerun s2-clean.mjs. Expect damage 0 at 'tray on belt' and at 'cap docked'.

**Rules:** DR-02, DR-07

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — In my clean run, damage went 0→1 (cost 10) on 'tray on belt' and 1→2 (cost 15) at 'at winch' during the capacitor-cart push. The HUD tally reads 2 in c14. The root cause (a kinematic teleport tripping the impact check, src/lunch-runtime.ts:277-278, src/game.ts:335) is plausible, but I did not isolate which prop was marked damaged.

### R5-277

**R5-277 | P2 | lunch | clarity | The kitchen lamp's cord looks exactly like a thin job cable, is permanently plugged into the feed post, and stretches infinitely**

Found by: `lunch-teach#11` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-lunch (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

this.cord is a TubeGeometry from the post (-4,.4,-3.15) to wherever the portable lamp is, recomputed every frame with no length limit (src/lunch-runtime.ts:301-302). It uses colour '#ecE8dc' (:130), the same colour as the thin cables (:139). - It hides the post's real output wiring.
- Carrying the lamp anywhere (the doc's alternate 'carry the kitchen lamp into the storeroom', docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:44) drags an unlimited cord, which contradicts the room's own finite-cable rule.

**Evidence.**

- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:130`
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:139`

- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:319` (thin hose radius .075)

**Fix.**

Draw the lamp cord in the post's conduit grey (#7d8697), half the thickness, with a small fixed plug moulded into the post. Cap its length at about 6 m: if the lamp is carried beyond that, the cord pulls tight and the lamp drops, or the cord unplugs and the lamp goes dark. Alternatively make the lamp a normal cable load with its own socket.

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The cord is rebuilt every frame from the post to the lamp with no length cap (lunch-runtime.ts:301-302). Shot 04 shows a long cream line from the post across the kitchen. 'Looks exactly like a thin job cable' is overstated. The cord's radius is .025 against the thin hose's .075 (:302 vs :319), and its colour #ecE8dc matches the thin cable's plugs (:139), not the hose tint #ffe2a8 (:10).

### R5-281

**R5-281 | P2 | meeting | clarity | The projector's switch state is invisible; switched on early, the trip lands on the cable plug-in**

Found by: `meeting-teach#12` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-meeting (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The 'switch' is a 1.9 m radius around the projector on the table (game.ts:244, :217). It has no rocker and no standby LED. A press gives only a 6-spark burst and the prompt word changing ('Switch it on' or 'Switch it off', objectives.ts:77).

If the player switches on before plugging in, which the prompt allows ('Switch on (needs power first)'), the strip trips at the instant the cable goes in (run B, shot 21). The player will blame the cable or the plug, not the total load.

After the trip, nothing on the projector shows it is still switched on. Yet that latent 'on' is why a reset re-trips (shot 11).

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:217`
- `src/game.ts:244`
- `src/ui/objectives.ts:77`
- `src/levels/decor.ts:149`
- [meeting-teach-21-plugin-trips-at-once.jpg](shots/meeting-teach-21-plugin-trips-at-once.jpg)
- [meeting-teach-11-reset-while-overloaded.jpg](shots/meeting-teach-11-reset-while-overloaded.jpg)
- `src/game.ts:348`

**Fix.**

1. Add a rocker on the projector housing (decor.ts:149) that tilts with game.switchedOn.
2. Add an LED: amber when on but unpowered, green when running, off when off.
3. With the trip dwell from the first finding, a plug-in into an already-on projector hums for about 2 s first, so the needle is seen climbing past the line.

**Verify.**

- Zoom-9 projector shots in the off, on-unpowered and running states, readable without the HUD.

**Rules:** DR-28, DR-47

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The projector is an rbox plus a lens cylinder (decor.ts:149), with no rocker or LED. The switch toggles game.switchedOn with only a 6-spark burst and a tone (game.ts:217). Switched on before plug-in, closing the lead trips the strip on the next tick (game.ts:348 sets loads[0].enabled from switchedOn), as meeting-teach-21 shows: 'Reset the strip' right at plug-in.

The 'roof gust' story conflicts with the room: the real mast is on the receiver rack (room.ts:84-85), while the bench has its own whip. The player has two antennas, one inert, and can't tell which one the beacon reaches. Polarisation is meant to be 'found by accident' (R4A), but here it is just a state change with no visible cause.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:199`
- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:205`
- `src/stations/observatory/room.ts:84-85`

**Fix.**

Move the whip mount to the rack's mast top (the real roof antenna) and keep the bench rack as the spare-whip store, or say the bench mount is the 'roof feed'. Play the gust on the mast: tilt animation over 0.4 s, a few thin streak particles (the 'spark' style with a pale colour) instead of puffs, and a rattling sound. Lay the bench whip along x (sideways to the camera), not along z.

**Verify.**

- Shot at +0.1 s and +0.6 s after job 2's log: the whip is visibly tipping sideways; no white balls.

**Rules:** DR-37, DR-47, DR-79

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — gust() bursts 8 'dust' puffs at the bench mount (station.ts:205). observatory-teach-32 shows three large white spheres over the ANTENNA mount. The flattened whip rotates around z (station.ts:235), and at the bench camera it is hard to read as flat. The real mast stands on the rack (room.ts:84-85) and is inert, so there are two antennas. I did not retake the +0.6 s shot; I relied on the reviewer's 32 and 34.

### R5-284

**R5-284 | P2 | playground | clarity | The 'plugged in / live' cable tint is the same hex as the 70–85% strain warning**

Found by: `playground-teach#4` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-playground (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

game.ts:7 defines `const GOLD=new T.Color('#ffd451')`, the tint for a connected cable (game.ts:304, `tint:this.connected?GOLD:undefined`). sim/cable.ts:83 strainColor uses exactly '#ffd451' for strain 0.7–0.85, the first warning band of AGENTS rule 4's white→yellow→orange→red.

At the moment of plugging in, the cable jumps from orange (strain 0.91, shot 05) to uniform yellow (shot 06), although the strain is still 0.968 (logged at plug-in). The player sees 'the cable relaxed to yellow', when in fact it is nearly at its limit and is now 'live'.

This conflates two concepts the room should keep apart: mechanical strain, and electrical state. It also hides the strain lesson exactly when the cable is taut across the room. The rule set asks for the cable state to read without text (DR-46), and for one meaning per visual (DR-29 for dots, and the same spirit applies to tints).

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:7` (GOLD #ffd451)
- `src/sim/cable.ts:83` (strainColor 0.7–0.85 = #ffd451)
- `src/game.ts:304` (tint applied when connected)
- [playground-teach-05-at-socket.jpg](shots/playground-teach-05-at-socket.jpg)
- [playground-teach-06-plugged-switch-off.jpg](shots/playground-teach-06-plugged-switch-off.jpg)
- `src/render/actors.ts:65` (STRAIN ramp has #ffd451 at .72 — the ramp actually used by hoseGeometry)
- `src/game.ts:294` (strain drawn as .3 when plug not held)
- [verify-playground-teach-05-at-socket-before-F.jpg](shots/verify-playground-teach-05-at-socket-before-F.jpg)
- [verify-playground-teach-06-plugged.jpg](shots/verify-playground-teach-06-plugged.jpg)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Don't keep the plug's last strain after connection; that would paint a slack, seated cable orange or red. After plug-in, draw the normal relaxed ramp (strain .3, white), and show 'live' with a separate cue: a teal stripe or rim, with pulses only when current flows. Alternatively use a connected hue that STRAIN (actors.ts:65) never produces. The unit test should assert the connected tint is outside both STRAIN and strainColor.

Reviewer's fix: Give 'energised' its own channel, separate from strain:
- Keep strain colouring after connection, but have hoseGeometry stop at the strain colour from the plug's last strain, not tint.
- Show 'energised, no current' (plugged in, switch open) as a thin teal (#5ed6cc, the socket-ring colour) stripe or a soft emissive rim along the hose.
- Show 'current flowing' only by the two-lane pulses.

If a gold 'win' state is still wanted, use a clearly different hue (e.g. #f6b93b with a pulsing emissive) that strainColor never produces, and add a unit test asserting GOLD isn't in strainColor's palette.

**Verify.**

- Unit test in src/sim/cable.test.ts: strainColor outputs never equal the connected tint. Retake shots 05/06: after plug-in, the hose keeps its strain colour, gains a teal stripe, and shows no pulses until the switch closes.

**Rules:** DR-29, DR-46

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Same hex, confirmed: GOLD '#ffd451' (game.ts:7) is the connected tint (game.ts:304). The hose's own ramp STRAIN uses '#ffd451' at 0.72 (actors.ts:65), and so does strainColor at 0.7–0.85 (cable.ts:83). verify-05 shows the cable orange before plug-in; verify-06 shows it uniform gold afterwards. The claim that this hides a near-limit strain is wrong, though.

### R5-289

**R5-289 | P2 | qfn | clarity | Asks, the job card and a wall poster print the method ('two caps hug their pins', 'Use layer 2 and vias', 'cap beside the pins'), so the decoupling and layer-2 ideas are read, not discovered**

Found by: `qfn-teach#5` (P2 clarity). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The places that tell the player the answer: (a) Board 2's ask (logic.ts:86, shown in the bench panel at station.ts:416; shot qfn-teach-09): 'Each needs its own 100 nF cap hugging its VDD and GND pins.' (b) The job-card step (station.ts:73; card in qfn-teach-09): 'Board 2 · Decoupling: two caps hug their pins'. (c) A wall poster in the room (room.ts:60-61): 'SHORT LOOP / cap beside the pins (not across the board)'. (d) Board 3's ask (logic.ts:93): 'Use layer 2 and vias, and cool the exposed pad', and its card 'layer 2, vias, thermal pad'. Together they print the solution before the player meets the problem, so the board becomes 'follow the instruction', not 'apply the idea'. DR-39 wants goals to say *what* (an object and an outcome), not *how*. With the failure consequence missing (see the 'Works' finding above), reading the ask is the only way the player learns why caps go near pins. The teach line after shipping (logic.ts:87) is well worded and truthful ('supplies brief bursts of current (it is not a battery)'), but it repeats what the ask already said.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/qfn/logic.ts:86`
- `src/stations/qfn/logic.ts:93`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:73`
- `src/stations/qfn/room.ts:60-61`
- [qfn-teach-09-b1-ship-tier1.jpg](shots/qfn-teach-09-b1-ship-tier1.jpg)
- [qfn-teach-13-b3-start-chip-hot-unpowered.jpg](shots/qfn-teach-13-b3-start-chip-hot-unpowered.jpg)
- [qfn-teach-09-b1-ship-tier1.jpg](shots/qfn-teach-09-b1-ship-tier1.jpg) (card 'Board 2 · Decoupling: two caps hug their pins' and the panel ask)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Do the card text now. Change the bench asks only together with finding 3's bring-up test, so the failure teaches the method before the hint is removed.

Reviewer's fix: State the need, not the method. Board 2 ask: 'This MCU resets whenever its supply sags. Wire it so it stays up.' Card: 'Board 2 · Decoupling: keep the MCU from resetting'. Board 3 ask: 'Power passes through to J2, whose pins are flipped. Route it, and keep the LED driver under its temperature.' Card: 'Board 3 · Two layers: cross VIN and GND, keep it cool'. Keep the LAYER/VIA buttons lighting up on board 3 as the world's hint. Move the 'SHORT LOOP' poster's method line into the post-ship teach toast, or change the poster to a picture only (two loops, a small one and a big one, with a sad and a happy chip face) so it hints without the sentence. Pair this with the bring-up test so failure teaches the method.

**Verify.**

- Read every BOARDS[].ask and job.steps[].text: no 'hug', 'beside', 'use layer 2', 'vias'. Retake the qfn-teach-09 and -13 bench shots and count the words in the panel ask.

**Rules:** AGENTS 2, DR-26, DR-39, DR-40

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The strings are as cited: logic.ts:86 ('hugging its VDD and GND pins'), logic.ts:93 ('Use layer 2 and vias'), station.ts:73 card steps ('two caps hug their pins', 'layer 2, vias, thermal pad'), room.ts:60-61 poster. The card steps do name the method and tool, which breaks DR-39. Lowered to P2 for two reasons. The bench ask sits on the station's own panel, which is the place DR-40/DR-49 allow text.

### R5-292

**R5-292 | P2 | global, meeting, arcade, observatory, playground | overlap | Start-of-level interpenetrations: g.audit finds overlaps in 6 of 9 levels (51 in the Meeting; beanbags in paper, cabinets in boxes, monitors in paper)**

Found by: `props-gallery#7` (P2 overlap), `meeting-models#11` (P2 overlap), `arcade-models#16` (P2 overlap), `observatory-models#17` (P2 overlap), `playground-play#18` (P2 overlap). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*props-gallery* — **Start-of-level interpenetrations from hand-placed and recipe y and offset values (cabinet+box ×23, monitor+paper ×32, lounge paper inside a beanbag ×11, reel inside the mail cart).** Running `g.audit(.02)` on every level (`mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/probe2.mjs` and `probe3.mjs`) gives Meeting 51 overlaps, Arcade 6, Playground 3, QFN 3, Garage 2 and Observatory 1, against DR-70's target of zero. Root causes:

**Cabinet + box (18 in Meeting, 2 in Garage, 3 in QFN).**
- meeting.ts:21 puts a box at y 1.9 on a cabinet whose top is 1.625 (centre .825 + .8). The box bottom is then 1.6, sunk 2.5 cm.
- clutter.ts:47's `cabinets` recipe has the same y 1.9.

**Monitor + paper (32 in Meeting).** meeting.ts:16 places paper at x−.38, inside the 0.63 m monitor collider footprint (monitor at z±.17, bottom at y .96 vs paper at y .99).

**Beanbag + paper (lounge recipe; 3 Playground, 6 Arcade, 1 Observatory).** clutter.ts:38 puts the paper at (.1,.65), within the second beanbag's 0.45 half-width at (.55,.15).

**Mail cart + extension reel (1).** meeting.ts:27 puts the reel at y 1, 3 cm into the cart.

On the first physics steps the solver pushes these apart. Boxes jitter or pop off the cabinets, and paper squirts out from under monitors, producing start-of-level motion and possible damage-free noise.

*meeting-models* — **Start-state interpenetration: 51 audit hits (monitor/paper ×32, cabinet/box ×18, mail cart/reel), and every prop rests 2.5 cm below the visual floor.** `g.audit(.02)` at load reports 51 overlaps (mockups/review5/tools/meeting-models/audit.json). 32× monitor vs paper, depth .03: meeting.ts:16 puts a paper at desk x-.38, which is inside the monitor's full .63×.48×.17 collider (prefabs.ts:11) because the monitor's collider is a box down to the desk top, not its stand. 18× cabinet vs box, depth .02: the box is spawned at y 1.9 (meeting.ts:21), but the cabinet top is at 1.625 and the box half-height is .3, so it sits 2.5 cm inside. 1× mail-cart vs extension reel: reel y 1 (meeting.ts:27), reel half .35, cart top .675. At load, physics resolves all of these with small pops and jitter, and papers slide. Separately, the floor collider is `solid(this,l.width,.35,l.depth,0,-.2,0)`, whose top is at y -.025 (game.ts:117), while the visual floor plane is at y .002 (decor.ts:27) and the rugs at .006–.012 (decor.ts:120-123). Every prop settles 2.7 cm (3.7 cm on rugs) below what the player sees: the strip rests at y .045 for a .14-high body, and the mail cart at .2998 for a .65 body (snapshot in a.mjs). Chair casters (radius .035) and plant and bin bottoms are sunk by most of their radius. That breaks DR-71 (visual bottom within 1 cm of the surface it rests on) and DR-70 (zero overlaps at start).

*arcade-models* — **Clutter recipes overlap their own items (6 beanbag–paper interpenetrations at start), and 'lounge' is 37% of recipe draws, so identical beanbag+beanbag+plant triplets are copy-pasted across the floor.** g.audit(.02) at start reports 6 overlaps, all beanbag vs paper at 3 cm: beanbag @(-1.22,-5.58)/paper (-0.72,-5.13); (0.43,-3.88)/(-0.07,-4.33); (2.67,-4.54)/(2.17,-4.99); (4.4,0.39)/(3.9,-0.06); (-5.29,1.63)/(-5.74,2.13); (1.14,3.41)/(0.69,3.91). The cause is clutter.ts: the 'lounge' recipe (clutter.ts:38) puts a beanbag at (.55,.15) and paper at (.1,.65). Their centres are 0.67 m apart, while the beanbag's half-diagonal is 0.636 and the paper's is 0.19. Placement (clutter.ts:83) only tests a cluster against previously placed props, never its items against each other. DR-70 wants zero overlaps at .02. Separately, arcade.ts:155 lists recipes ['lounge','crates','cones','reading','lounge','bins','crates','lounge']: lounge is 3/8 (37.5%) of draws and 'reading' adds more beanbags, over DR-67's 25% cap. The survey (-02, -43) shows the same 'two beanbags + plant' arrangement repeated about 8 times with only a quarter-turn, which reads copy-pasted.

*observatory-models* — **Start-time audit: beanbag box collider overlaps paper by 3 cm (round prop on a square collider).** g.audit(.02) at start returns one overlap: beanbag @-5.94,-1.48 with paper @-5.44,-1.03, depth .03. The beanbag's physics shape is the .9×.9×.6 box from prefabs.ts:26, so a rotated cluster puts its invisible corner (reach .64 m) under nearby litter. DR-70 asks for zero overlaps at start, and DR-71 asks for round colliders on round props. g.audit(.005) also lists four desk/monitor contacts of .01, which are benign (the monitor rests on the desk).

*playground-play* — **Start layout interpenetrates: lounge beanbags overlap their paper.** g.audit(0.02) at start reports three overlaps of 0.03 m, all from the `lounge` recipe (src/levels/clutter.ts:38): beanbag @(-7.99,-1.52) with paper @(-8.44,-1.02), beanbag @(-1.33,1.73) with paper @(-0.88,1.23), and beanbag @(0.87,7.77) with paper @(0.37,7.32). The recipe offsets the paper only 0.65 m from a 0.9 m beanbag, and stacked or recipe-internal items skip the overlap test.

### R5-293

**R5-293 | P2 | global, arcade | overlap | Every prop gets a cuboid collider and models overhang it by up to 19 cm: round props rest on corners, reels and bins cannot roll**

Found by: `props-gallery#6` (P2 overlap), `gap5-toon-pipeline#5` (P2 overlap), `arcade-models#23` (P2 overlap). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*props-gallery* — **Every prop gets a cuboid collider: round props rest on invisible corners, reels and bins can't roll, and hollow furniture is a solid block.** `addProp` always creates `ColliderDesc.cuboid(size/2)` (game.ts:124), and `clearOfFixtures` uses `RAPIER.Cuboid` too (clutter.ts:67). That causes three problems.

**(a) Round props in box colliders.** Beanbag 0.9 m sack, plant pot, bin, mug, cone, reel and lamp base all sit in boxes. A tipped bin or plant rests on box corners that aren't there, and a reel, which begs to be rolled in a cable game, slides like a crate. This breaks R12.3/DR-71's "round props have round colliders".

**(b) Hollow furniture is solid.**
- The desk's 1.6×0.95×0.85 box fills the leg room. Chairs can't tuck in, and a thrown mug bounces off air at the desk edge.
- The ping-pong table's 2.6×0.9×1.5 box fills the space under the table.
- The mop bucket is 0.5 m tall inside a 1.5 m box, so a metre of invisible wall stands above it.
- The lamp's 0.65×1.5 box surrounds a thin pole.
- The wedge's full box makes its slope non-physical.

See the magenta wireframes in `props-gallery-10-sheet01`, `-07`, `-08` and `-09`.

**(c) Visual parts poke out of the collider by more than 3 cm** (R12.3), measured with `mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/measure.mjs`:

| Prop | Part | Outside the collider |
|---|---|---|
| cart | handle | +29.5 cm up, 14 cm out |
| coolbox | lid handle | +19 cm |
| printer | paper tray | 17 cm out of the front |
| ping-pong | net | +16 cm |
| whiteboard | feet | 15 cm each side |
| dolly, supply, capcart | handles | 14.2 cm |
| plug / coupler | prongs | 12 / 9 cm |
| chair | back | +10.4 cm |
| plant | foliage | 6.5 cm |
| splitter | outlets | 6 cm |

These parts clip through walls and through anything stacked on top. Going the other way, the printer top sits 6 cm below its collider and the lamp shade 8 cm below, so things set on them float.

*gap5-toon-pipeline* — **Models overhang their physics boxes by up to 19 cm, so props can sit inside each other at rest and g.audit can't see it.** prefabs.ts:9 says 'models below are drawn to fit inside it (the physics box)'. Measured, many don't (model w×h×d against collider size). Plug/coupler 0.42 vs 0.30 long: the pins stick 12 cm out of the collider, which is why the plug's prongs poke through the socket box. Splitter 0.62 vs 0.50 (inlet and outlet stubs). Mail cart 1.34 vs 1.20 wide and 0.945 vs 0.65 tall (the push bar). Coolbox 1.10 × 0.79 vs 1.00 × 0.60: the handle and lid rise 19 cm above the collider top. Supply cart 1.84 vs 1.70. Capcart 1.74 vs 1.60. Dolly 1.34 vs 1.20. Plant 0.70 vs 0.58 (leaves). Whiteboard depth 0.50 vs 0.20 (feet). Printer depth 0.92 vs 0.75. Desk height 1.15 vs 0.95 (clutter on top, which is acceptable). The cooler is the reverse: model 0.51 vs collider 0.60, so it stands 4.5 cm clear of anything touching it. Rapier collides the boxes, not the meshes, so at rest and after throws the overhangs interpenetrate other props and walls. For example, a prop stacked on a coolbox sinks into its handle, and carts parked side by side merge their bars. g.audit(0.02) works from colliders, so it reports these as clean (DR-70).

*arcade-models* — **Serviced cabinet base and body intrude 2–4 cm into the service bench; round props rest on box colliders.** buildCabinet() (station.ts:215) places the serviced cabinet at (t.x+OX-2.75, 0, t.z-.35) = (-2.95, 0, -2.8) with ry .38. Its body corner (local (.475,.4)) lands at world x -2.361 and the PLUM base corner at x -2.33. The bench body starts at x -2.35 (W 4.3 centred on -0.2) and the bench top overhang at -2.40. So the cabinet body pokes about 4 cm into the bench top and the base about 2 cm into the bench body, at z ≈ -2.6 (visible as the cabinet edge melting into the bench in shots -34, -72). Both are fixed bodies, so g.audit can't see it. Separately, every prop gets a cuboid collider (game.ts:124), including the round beanbag, plant, bin, lamp and cone. Tumbled round props therefore rest on invisible box corners (DR-71), and the beanbag's 0.9 m box makes neighbouring props float 1–3 cm off its curved sides.

*From props-gallery:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Rapier's `ColliderDesc.cylinder` is y-axis, so the reel needs `.setRotation()` with a quarter turn about x to put its axis on z. A chair collider change of .95 to 1.06 also shifts the spawn height (game.ts:121 uses size[1]/2), so re-run the layout and audit after it. Drop the plug from the overhang list unless 'plug' props get placed.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Add an optional `collider` field to `Prefab` (prefabs.ts:7): `{shape:'cyl'|'ball'|'compound',parts?:...}`.
2. In game.ts:124, build the matching shape:
   - **Cylinders:** `ColliderDesc.cylinder(h/2,r)` for bin (r .19), mug (.07), plant (pot r .26 plus a ball for the foliage), cone (.22), and reel (axis z, r .34, as a cylinder rotated by the collider's rotation).
   - **Round cuboid:** `ColliderDesc.roundCuboid` (radius .1) for the beanbag.
   - **Compound:** multiple colliders on the same body for the desk (top slab plus two leg panels), ping-pong (top plus 4 legs), mop (bucket cylinder r .27 h .5 plus a thin handle capsule), lamp (base cylinder plus pole capsule plus shade cylinder), wedge (`ColliderDesc.convexHull` of the 6 wedge vertices), chair (seat box plus back box plus base cylinder) and whiteboard (board plus two foot bars).
3. Shrink the visuals that poke out:
   - printer tray depth `d*.2`;
   - coolbox handle torus r .09, raised lid inside the box;
   - handles of cart, dolly, supply and capcart drawn at x `-w/2+.05` instead of `-w/2`;
   - chair prefab height .95 → 1.06.
4. Mirror the shapes in clutter's `clearOfFixtures`.

*From gap5-toon-pipeline:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Whitelist plug/coupler pins in the proposed unit test (they must protrude to enter sockets). If option (a) grows prefab sizes, addProp spawns at y = size[1]/2+.025 (game.ts:121), so taller colliders lift the models: the coolbox body would float about 9.5 cm unless the model is re-centred. Option (b), compound colliders, or re-centring the model inside the new box is required.

Reviewer's fix: Make the collider match the visual. Either (a) grow the prefab sizes to the measured model bounds where the overhang is solid body (coolbox h .79, cart [1.34,.95,.75], supply [1.84,…], capcart [1.74,…], dolly [1.34,…]), or (b) keep the box and add small compound colliders for the bars and pins in addProp (game.ts:124). Shrink the cooler collider to [.52,1.25,.52]. Add a unit test that asserts Box3(makeProp(k)) ⊆ prefab size + 2 cm for every kind except a whitelist (desk clutter, plant leaves).

*From arcade-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** If the cabinet moves, move the matching solid (station.ts:224) and the kid solid (station.ts:232) with it, since both are derived from t.x+OX-2.75. RAPIER's roundCylinder signature is (halfHeight, radius, borderRadius), so .25,.4,.05 gives the beanbag 0.6 m of height. Check the cone collider's centre offset against the mesh pivot.

Reviewer's fix: station.ts:215: move the cabinet to t.x+OX-2.85 (10 cm further left) or reduce ry to .3, and update the solid at :224. Better, add a fixed-vs-fixed check to audit() for station solids. game.ts:124: choose the collider by kind: beanbag → ColliderDesc.roundCylinder(.25,.4,.05); bin and plant → cylinder (half-height, radius .19/.26); cone → cone(.3,.25); lamp → a compound of a base cylinder plus a shade cylinder. Keep the masses.

### R5-297

**R5-297 | P2 | meeting | overlap | Interior walls stop thrown props in mid-air 1.25 m above their visible top**

Found by: `gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock#4` (P2 overlap). Batch: B1 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

interiorWall() draws a 1.35 m wall but gives it a 2.6 m collider (src/levels/decor.ts:44-49). The comment at decor.ts:20 says this keeps Pip from hopping walls. Thrown props also hit the invisible upper 1.25 m.

Three of my Meeting jump-throws aimed over the closet wall stopped dead in mid-air above the visible cap and dropped straight down to its foot (run output: landed at (−13.27, 0.10, −5.28) and (−12.27, 0.04, −4.92)). In stuck-softlock-09-1 the strip hangs in the air in front of Pip, above the low wall.

The same walls separate Lunch's kitchen, storeroom and lift room (src/levels/lunch.ts:33-39). An object bouncing off thin air reads as a bug. A slightly higher lob still clears the wall into the sealed closet (see the P0 findings), so the invisible extension neither looks right nor seals anything.

**Evidence.**

- `src/levels/decor.ts:20,44-49`
- [stuck-softlock-09-meeting-strip-jumpthrow-1.jpg](shots/stuck-softlock-09-meeting-strip-jumpthrow-1.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/stuck-softlock/meeting.mjs` runs ('throw 0 -> (-13.27,0.10,-5.28)', 'throw 1 -> (-12.27,0.04,-4.92)')
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock/wallhit2.mjs` output: frames 0-3 z -5.13…-5.16 at y 1.62→1.76, then falling to (-14.63,0.04,-5.05)
- [verify-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock-06-meeting-strip-stopped-above-wall.jpg](shots/verify-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock-06-meeting-strip-stopped-above-wall.jpg) (strip suspended above the wall cap)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Option (a) makes lobbing into sealed rooms easier, so it must ship together with the lids or doorways (index 0 and index 2). Otherwise it widens the soft-lock. In Rapier, set collision groups on both the upper-wall collider and the player capsule. Props default to 0xFFFF/0xFFFF, so the upper collider needs membership 0x0004 and filter 0x0002, and the player needs a filter that includes 0x0004.

Reviewer's fix: Pick one of these:
- (a) Use collision groups. Put the upper 1.25 m of interior-wall colliders in a group that only collides with the player capsule (Rapier setCollisionGroups, player group 0x0002). Then props fly over freely and Pip still can't hop. Pair this with lids over sealed rooms.
- (b) Make the visible wall match the collider: add a 1.25 m frosted-glass or mesh upper panel on interiorWall, so the room looks enclosed.

Option (b) also tells the player the closet is sealed.

**Verify.**

- Re-run meeting.mjs with zz −3.6/−3.0. Throws that clear the visible cap must follow a ballistic arc (no y drop at the wall plane). Take a frame at the moment of crossing.

**Rules:** —

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I reproduced it. A standing Q-throw from (-13.5,-4.26) toward the closet stopped at z≈-5.15, the wall plane, at y 1.62–1.76. That is above the 1.35 m visible cap. The strip then slid straight down to (-14.63,0.04,-5.05) at the foot of the wall. In my screenshot the strip hangs above the wall cap in front of the racks. decor.ts:44-49 confirms the visible h=1.35 against a solid collider of 2.6 at y 1.3.

The layout uses i%2 for the column, so the reading order zig-zags: the left column is 00, 02, 03R, 05, 07 and the right is 01, 03, 04, 06. labelTexture also shrinks each label to fit (src/render/labels.ts:9-10), so '03 Overheating Arcade' renders at about half the cap height of '01 Big Meeting'. At the game camera every row is under 8 px (lobby-models-01; DR-48).

### R5-307

**R5-307 | P2 | playground | overlap | Every dynamic prop rests about 2.7 cm below the visible floor (the floor collider top is at y −0.025)**

Found by: `playground-models#13` (P2 overlap). Batch: R-playground (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The floor collider is solid(this,w,.35,d,0,-.2,0), whose top is at y −0.025. The visible floor plane is drawn at y +0.002. Props settle on the collider, so every box, cone, bin, chair and beanbag sinks about 2.7 cm into the visible floor. The scene census shows boxes (h .6) centred at y .27, so their bottom is at −0.03, cone base plates at y 0.0 and beanbag base spheres reaching −0.036. Paper sheets (h .03) settle at y −0.01 to −0.02, so their top is only 3 mm above the floor or under it. That invites z-fighting and shimmer at distance, and some sheets vanish into the floor. Pip is offset by the controller and stands on the visible floor, so props look sunk next to Pip. The contact shadows land on the floor plane, not at the props' true base. Applies to every cable-floor level.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:117` (solid(this,l.width,.35,l.depth,0,-.2,0) → top −0.025)
- `src/levels/decor.ts:24-26` (floor plane at y+.002)

- snapshot pins y = 0.285 ×6
- Pip rests at y 0.77 (capsule bottom 0.0), avatar drawn at p.y−.78 (game.ts:414)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Raising the collider top to 0 also lifts Pip. Its capsule then rests at y .795 because of the controller offset of .025, and with game.ts:414 drawing the avatar at p.y−.78, Pip's boots would float about 1.5 cm above the floor (today they sit 1 cm into it). Change the avatar offset in game.ts:414 to p.y−.795, or derive it from the collider. Re-check the reel, socket and anchor heights, which are hard-coded to the visible floor.

Reviewer's fix: Change game.ts:117 to solid(this,l.width,.35,l.depth,0,-.175,0) so the collider top is at y 0.0, and keep the visible floor at y .002. Check that Pip's spawn y (.91) and the controller offset (.025) still ground Pip. Give paper a minimum resting top of y ≥ .01 (paper h .03 → .02 and a mass of .05 is fine).

**Verify.**

- Re-run scene.mjs. Box instances rest at y ≈ .30 and paper at ≥ .01. A zoom-9 two-frame diff over the litter shows no flicker. Re-run tests/layout.spec.ts.

Found by: `props-gallery#5` (P2 overlap). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Every sofa part is a centred rbox:

The back is a single 2.6×0.6 m red face with no trim (DR-62/DR-63, `props-gallery-10-sheet03` sofa back). At the game camera it reads as a red tub (`props-gallery-28-meeting-lounge-gamecam.jpg`).

- `src/levels/meeting.ts:29`

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Arithmetic on prefabs.ts:93-95 gives these lowest points: - seat: bottom+.125 (h .45 at bottom+.35); - arms: bottom+.275; - back: bottom+.45. Found by: `spectrum-models#13` (P2 overlap). Batch: R-spectrum (section 5).

On the last delivery, lightUp() (room.ts:148) adds a second set of boxes, box(13.5,.01,.1) at y .014 (spanning .009–.019). These intersect the base stripes and sit above the rug at .012, so the glowing strips draw over the dock rug. The stripes also run under the clutter crates along the front.

The green stripe (6.21–6.31) lies entirely under the rug and the magenta stripe straddles its edge, with 1 mm of separation. lightUp boxes at y .014 ±.005 (room.ts:148) cut through the base stripes and rise above the rug.

### R5-311

**R5-311 | P2 | arcade, garage, observatory, spectrum, qfn | visual-bug | Floating single-sided sign planes vanish from behind or hover off walls (Arcade STOREROOM, Garage TEST STAND, ROOF RECEIVER, Spectrum signs, QFN STOCK)**

Found by: `arcade-models#9` (P2 visual-bug), `arcade-play#17` (P2 visual-bug), `garage-models#12` (P2 visual-bug), `observatory-models#10` (P2 visual-bug), `spectrum-models#7` (P2 visual-bug), `qfn-models#20` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*arcade-models* — **REGRESSION / still open: the STOREROOM plaque floats in mid-air over the doorway and has no thickness, so it vanishes edge-on and from behind.** room.ts:115 creates `PlaneGeometry(1.5,.36)` at (-7.6, 2.1, 2.8) with rotation.y=0 and no backing, post or lintel. The doorway it labels is the gap between store-a's end (x -8.6) and store-b (x -6.55), so there is nothing under or behind it. From the default camera it hangs at head height in front of the west-wall cabinets (shots -14, -53). It hides the lower half of the PONG cabinet and is cut by the HUD (shot -01). Because it is a single-sided plane, orbiting 180° makes it disappear (shot -15). From the side it is an invisible sliver (shot -83: camera east of the storeroom, sign not visible at all). This breaks DR-72 (nothing floats), DR-49 (mounted signage only) and DR-63 (no open-backed planes). ART F8 reported it.

*arcade-play* — **STOREROOM plaque still floats in mid-air above the storeroom entrance (known DR-72, still open).** The plaque is a bare PlaneGeometry at (−7.6, 2.1, 2.8) with no mount (room.ts:115). The storeroom walls are only 1.35 m high, so it hangs 0.75 m above them in empty air. It reads clearly as floating at zoom 9 (shots 08, 09) and in the game camera (shots 61, 62, 72).

Orbited, it goes edge-on to a hairline (shot 03). It's also the first world label the player sees on the way to the tray.

*garage-models* — **TEST STAND sign is a single-sided plane: it vanishes from behind, leaving a bare post.** The TEST STAND sign is `new T.PlaneGeometry(1.2,.3)` with flat() (MeshBasic, FrontSide) on game.root at (STAND.x, .9, STAND.z-.9) = (0.7, .9, -5.35), tilted -.2 (room.ts:78). Its post is a separate box(.06,.8,.06) on the stand group at local (0, .4, -.85) (room.ts:79), so it ends at y .8, below the sign's centre, about 2 cm in front of the plane.

The sign has no backing board and no housing. Orbiting 180° shows the post with nothing on it (garage-models-13-test-stand-o180, -39). The front view shows a flat label floating above a thin stick. DR-63 requires signs to have housings, and DR-72 requires them to be mounted.

*observatory-models* — **ROOF RECEIVER plaque floats above the rack as a one-sided plane.** The plaque is a bare PlaneGeometry(.8,.2) with a flat (MeshBasic, FrontSide) texture at y 1.72, tilted -.3, at z RX.z+.16 (room.ts:86). The rack's brass top is at 1.55, so the sign's bottom edge (~1.62) hangs about 7 cm above it with no stand. It is a single plane with no housing, so it vanishes edge-on (shot 33) and from behind. It reads as a floating label, not a mounted sign. In the start view the bouncing objective marker sits right over it (shot 12: 'ROO…ER').

*spectrum-models* — **Floating, single-sided sign planes (TEA, POD DOCK, QUIET ROOM, HATCH, GLASS LAB); the QUIET ROOM sign is invisible from the approach side.** Every room sign is `standingSign()` (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:35-37): a bare PlaneGeometry with a MeshBasic texture, front side only, no housing and no post. (1) 'TEA' (room.ts:116) hangs in mid-air at y 1.5, z 5.2, 0.35 m in front of the counter's front face (z 5.16) and 0.55 m above its top, with no support (18, B0). (2) 'POD DOCK' (:133) is a 0.8 m plate standing on edge on the rug at y .35 with no foot, so it reads as a loose sheet leaning on nothing (13, 99c). (3) 'QUIET ROOM · SCREENED' (:106) faces +z, into the quiet room. The player approaches from the lab side (z < 1.5, route via 10.2,0.6), where the sign is back-face-culled and invisible (97); it is only readable from inside the room (23). (4) 'HATCH' and 'GLASS LAB' (:92-93) float 5 cm off the shutter face (shutter front at z1+.05, sign at z1+.10), against DR-72's 0.5–1 cm. When the hatch door slides up 0.62 m (station.ts:400), the door's front face reaches z −3.10, coplanar with the HATCH sign at y 1.75–1.89, which is a z-fight risk (66). DR-63: signs have housings, never open-backed planes.

*qfn-models* — **Wall signage: the STOCK sign is a bare plane floating 4 cm off the wall, and the posters' explanatory captions are illegible at the game camera.** **STOCK sign:** room.ts:56 puts a MeshBasic PlaneGeometry(1.1,.41) on kit.side at local z .2. The wallpaper's front face is at .16 (room.ts:26, box depth .02 at .15). The sign therefore hangs 4 cm in front of the wall with no thickness or backing. DR-72 wants 0.5–1 cm, mounted. At grazing orbits it reads as a floating card. The ink border is painted in the texture, not modelled.

**Posters** (room.ts:58-62): the 'QFN' and 'SHORT LOOP' posters carry sentence captions ('pin 1 · exposed pad', 'cap beside the pins (not across the board)') drawn at 22 px on a 256 px canvas onto a 0.72 m poster. That is about 8 px tall at zoom 9 and unreadable at the game camera (qfn-models-20, -23, -66). This is below DR-48's 14 px. They teach nothing as text and add visual noise.

The poster pictograms themselves (the pad pattern, the red/blue loop next to the chip) are good and should carry the idea without words.

**Fix.**

*From arcade-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The 'REGRESSION' label is wrong: this was never fixed. The fix is fine.

Reviewer's fix: Build a doorway frame: two posts rbox(.12,2.25,.3) in the CAP colour at (-8.55,1.125,2.6) and (-6.6,1.125,2.6), and a header beam rbox(2.07,.22,.32) at (-7.575,2.2,2.6), all as solid() so props collide. Mount the plaque on the beam's +z face at z 2.6+.165 as a 1.5×.3 rbox(…,.03) GRAPE board with the text plane 5 mm proud. Add a second text plane on the −z face (rotated π), so it reads from inside the storeroom. Lower the y to 2.2 to stay under the cutaway view.

*From arcade-play:* Mount the plaque on a frame. Put a plum `rbox(1.6,.46,.06)` on two DMETAL posts `box(.05,.8,.05)` standing on the `store-b` wall top at y 1.35–2.15, with the plane 0.01 m in front of the board. Or lay it on the storeroom wall face at y 1.1 and give it a back so it reads from both sides.

*From garage-models:* In room.ts:78-79 parent the sign to the stand group:
- a backing board rbox(1.28,.36,.05,.03) in toon(INK) at local (0, .92, -.9), rotation.x -.2;
- the plaque plane at local z offset +.03 in front of the board's face;
- a second plaque on the back face (rotation.y π) so it reads from both sides;
- extend the post to box(.06,.9,.06) at y .45 so it meets the board's bottom edge.

*From observatory-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** A minor tweak: at rack-local y 1.36 the backing (.22 tall) would overlap the top front panel (y 1.01–1.31) and touch the brass lid at 1.49. Use y≈1.40 with height .16, or mount it on the rack top with posts.

Reviewer's fix: Mount it on the rack's front face below the top: an INK backing box(.84,.22,.03) in the rack group at (0,1.36,.36), with the plaque plane at z .376 (0.5 cm off). Or put it on a small brass stand on the rack top: two posts box(.03,.1,.03) plus the backing box. Never leave a bare plane.

*From spectrum-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Two corrections. (a) POD DOCK is worse than described. It is centred at y .35 with height .176, so it floats about 26 cm above the floor rather than standing on the rug; the floor-decal fix is right. (b) QUIET ROOM is not invisible from the usual approach. The default camera sits at +z (yaw .14) and reads it correctly through the mesh, as 02-survey shows. It disappears only when the player orbits to the north side, so the real issue is that it is single-sided (DR-63), and it is not a readability blocker. For the hatch, moving the sign to z1+.056 is not enough while the door front is also at z1+.10. Put the door behind the frame (z1+.04) or the sign clearly in front of it (≥ z1+.11).

Reviewer's fix: Rewrite standingSign() to build a housed plaque: rbox(w+.06, h+.06, .04, .015) in the bg colour's darker shade, with the texture plane on BOTH faces at ±.021 (two planes, one rotated π), mounted 0.6 cm off the host surface. Mount each sign on something. TEA: on a 0.9 m DMETAL post (cyl .02) rising from the back of the counter at (2.4, 0.95→1.6, 4.6), or flat on the counter's front face at y .7, z 5.17. POD DOCK: lay it flat on the floor as a decal at y .013 (rotation.x = −π/2) at the dock's +z edge, like the PAD tags. QUIET ROOM: double-sided and hung from the top rail on two short chains (box .01×.12×.01), centred at y 2.05. HATCH/GLASS LAB: z = lb.z1 + .056. Put the HATCH sign at y 2.0 so the open hatch door (top at 1.87+.3) passes behind it, or move the hatch door to z1+.06 (behind the frame).

*From qfn-models:* **STOCK sign:** replace the plane with a plaque: an INK rbox(1.16,.47,.03) backing at z .175, plus the textured plane at z .192. Or set the plane to z .168 on a box(1.1,.41,.008) YEL board.

**Posters:** drop the caption sentences, or enlarge them to at least 40 px on the canvas and keep them to 2–3 words ('PIN 1', 'CAP CLOSE'). Make the loop poster's pictogram show 'short loop ✓ / long loop ✗' as two drawn mini-boards instead of words.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

### R5-312

**R5-312 | P2 | global, qfn, observatory, spectrum, garage | visual-bug | Clutter is parked against showpieces and intrudes into bench views (QFN machines, Observatory gallery, Spectrum ladder, Garage test stand)**

Found by: `camera-render#9` (P2 visual-bug), `qfn-models#1` (P2 overlap), `observatory-models#11` (P2 overlap), `spectrum-models#14` (P2 overlap), `garage-models#19` (P2 overlap). Batch: B3 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*camera-render* — **Clutter intrudes into bench views: the observatory floor lamp and box stack overlap the monitor area, and the garage box column fills the corner.** The clutter keep-out lanes don't cover the bench camera's frustum footprint behind and beside the table.

- Observatory: a floor lamp stands just behind the bench's right rear, with its shade beside the monitor and over the side card, and a stack of yellow and purple boxes crowds the antenna controls on the left (camera-render-ob-30-bench.jpg).
- Garage: a tall yellow box column and the red tool chest fill the top-left behind the monitor (camera-render-ga-30-bench.jpg).

It makes the bench, the one place the player has to read, visually noisy. This breaks DR-69 (detail only where it carries information) and DR-16's lane intent.

*qfn-models* — **Clutter is parked against the showpiece machines: a bookshelf blocks the pick-and-place, another bookshelf and a box block the oven windows, a cart sits under the crane.** The clutter generator only keeps the spawn-to-shelf-to-bench lane clear (qfn.ts:25, lanes r 1.05). It is free to drop clusters right in front of the back-wall machines. The prop dump (mockups/review5/tools/qfn-models/props.json) gives these positions:

- **Mint bookshelf at (−8.1, −5.09)**, 2 m wide, x −9.1..−7.1. It stands 0.3 m in front of the pick-and-place feeder reels (PnP front face z −5.85) and 0.18 m from the crane leg at x −9.4. It hides the left half of the PnP at the game camera and in every close-up (qfn-models-10, -24, -26, -76).
- **Kraft bookshelf at (0.65, −5.2)**, turned 90°, z −6.2..−4.2. It stands perpendicular to the reflow oven 10 cm from its front face and hides the oven's first window from the bench side (qfn-models-13, -67, -50).
- **Lone box at (2.71, −5.57)** (x 2.36..3.06). It sits 0.4 m in front of the oven, over its third window.
- **Lavender cart at (−5.97, −4.53)**, with a box on top, parked directly under the crane beam and trolley hook (qfn-models-25, -26).
- **Cabinet pair plus box (2.2 m tower) at (−1.48/−0.72, −4.34)**, right behind the bench. It fills the top-left of the bench camera frame on every board (qfn-models-37, -40, -42).

Why it matters:
- The machines are the room's identity and the 'story' backdrop. Burying them behind generic office furniture makes the room read as a storage office.
- It adds noise to the bench camera, which the room code explicitly tries to keep clean ('No lamps hang over the bench so the bench camera sees the whole board', room.ts:4).
- Design rules: DR-62/69 (detail where it carries information); DR-13 (when the oven gets a story beat, its target must not be hidden).

*observatory-models* — **Clutter fills the exhibit gallery: a desk pod against the RADIO panel, crates and lamps between the plinths; the safety note is hidden behind them.** The clutter lanes (observatory.ts:21) protect only the dome and the spawn-to-bench routes, so the 'pod', 'crates' and 'reading' recipes are free to fill the gallery strip, z -7.5 to -5. The audit lists a desk at (0.49,-6.97) with a monitor at (0.66,-6.97), jammed against the back wall under the RADIO and MICROWAVE panels. Its desk top at .95 m sits over the left end of the safety note, which is at y .9 (shots 20, 51). Purple and teal crates and a lamp-and-beanbag pair stand between the exhibit plinths (shots 21, 22, 64b). The plinths are .9 m tall with exhibits up to ~1.45 m, so they sit directly in front of the safety note band (y .73–1.07), and the dish covers 'safe: UV' (shot 20). The gallery stops reading as a curated exhibit wall and becomes a storeroom, and the plinth silhouettes merge with the crates.

*spectrum-models* — **Clutter desk pod parked in front of the roof-hatch ladder; the ladder leads nowhere.** The scene dump puts a clutter 'pod' desk (1.6×0.85) at (0.98, −6.82): it spans z −7.25…−6.40, with its monitor and chair in front. The roof-hatch ladder is at (0.9, −7.78) (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:129). The desk and chair stand directly in front of the ladder's foot, so the bottom rungs are hidden behind a monitor and the ladder can't plausibly be used (94, 36, 37). The ladder's rails are 2.9 m on a 3.0 m wall with no hatch, opening or ceiling detail at the top, and only the wall plaque 'ROOF HATCH ↑' explains it. It reads as a ladder leaning on a blank wall.

*garage-models* — **Clutter boxes the robot's test stand in: a yellow cabinet column and crates sit right behind the bench and stand.** The clutter lanes (garage.ts:32-33) protect the painted route and the carry path, but not the area around the stand's back and sides. The seeded clutter places:
- a 2.2 m cabinets cluster at (-1.6, -4.91), 0.7 m off the stand's -x edge, with a box stacked into its top (audit at 0.02: 'cabinet @-1.6,-4.91' vs 'box @-1.6,-4.91', depth .02);
- a teal crate just behind the stand's -z edge at about (0.6, -5.7);
- crate stacks behind the scope.

At the default camera the yellow column merges with the bench scope into one tall yellow-and-cream mass (garage-models-01, -14, -54). From behind, the stand is visually walled in (-39). The same 0.02 cabinet/box interpenetration also occurs at (-8.21, 3.21). It is the only audit result at 0.02, and zero at the 0.04 default.

- **Bench ring:** {points:[[-2.6,-2.2],[3.6,-2.2]], r:2.3}. That keeps the bench, its side table and the bench-camera frustum (z −4.5..0.1) clear.

If clutter.ts lanes are polylines only, also add an optional keep-out rect, `keep?:[x0,z0,x1,z1][]`, tested in the `ok` predicate at clutter.ts:69-76.

Re-seed if the prop count drops below about 110 after the extra keep-outs, and move the displaced clusters to the front half (z > 1.5) and the side walls.

*From spectrum-models:* Add a solid() footprint (or a clutter keep-out lane {points:[[.9,-7.6],[.9,-6.0]],r:.8}) in front of the ladder so clutter never lands there. Give the ladder a destination: a 0.9×0.9 m DMETAL hatch frame with a yellow-black hazard rim mounted on the top of the back wall at (0.9, 3.0, −7.9), its lid hinged open 30°, plus two wall brackets (box .1×.04×.12) holding the rails. Replace the 'ROOF HATCH ↑' plaque with a small arrow pictogram on the frame.

*From garage-models:* 1) garage.ts:32-33: add the lane {points:[[-2.8,-4.6],[2.8,-4.6]],r:1.4} (stand and bench back).
2) In clutter.ts:46, change the stacked box y in the `cabinets` recipe from 1.9 to 1.92, matching the cabinet's top trim (prefabs.ts:89 box h .04 at h/2-.02) plus the .3 half height, so stacked boxes rest instead of starting .02 inside.
3) Shrink the `cabinets` share of garage clusters (garage.ts:31 lists it once of 10, fine), but cap cabinet clusters to the outer 2.4 m band (fillBand logic) so 2.2 m columns never stand mid-floor.

### R5-313

**R5-313 | P2 | global, playground, lobby | visual-bug | Sprint and footstep dust are opaque outlined toon spheres up to 1.2 m: a sprint leaves a trail of snowballs / hollow ink rings**

Found by: `camera-render#10` (P2 visual-bug), `playground-models#15` (P2 visual-bug), `lobby-play#16` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B8 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*camera-render* — **Sprint dust is opaque, outlined toon spheres up to about 1.2 m wide, so a sprint leaves a trail of 'snowballs'.** 'dust' particles use `ico(1)` with `toon(color)`: opaque, lit and outlined. They grow to size×2.8, with the size up to 0.22 m radius (src/render/particles.ts:36, :50). Every sprint step spawns one (src/game.ts:328). Landings spawn 5 and shrugs 4 (src/game.ts:323, :231).

On screen they read as cream eggs or snowballs with dark ink outlines lying on the floor (camera-render-me-51b-crop-dust.jpg). Two big grey outlined balls sit in the Playground win frame (camera-render-pg-46-win-a.jpg). The particle code's own comment (particles.ts:13) says vapour must not read as snowballs, yet dust uses exactly that look. This breaks DR-79 and AGENTS 9 (restrained).

*playground-models* — **Sprint dust puffs are outlined toon spheres in floor colour, so they show as hollow ink rings.** Footstep and sprint dust uses toon('#e6dfd2') on an icosahedron. That material keeps the OutlineEffect hull, and its fill matches the floor, so every puff renders as a little blue-ink circle on the floor (crop -54). They trail Pip along every walk (shots -23, -30, -42, -43, -53) and look like stray wire rings or decals. DR-56 says effects are never outlined.

*lobby-play* — **Footstep dust leaves white pearl-like balls along Pip's path near the back wall.** After Pip walks along the back-wall doors, the floor behind him is dotted with white spheres, 10–25 px at the game camera (lobby-play-13, -14, -31: a trail of discs between the Lunch and Rush doors). They fade after a few seconds (none in lobby-play-38 after the settle). They are most likely the footstep dust puffs (src/game.ts:328, a 'dust' burst #e6dfd2 every step). On the warm plank floor they read as dropped pearls or snowballs, not dust: hard-edged, bright and round. This is the kind of particle stacking DR-79 targets.

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/particles.ts:36`
- `src/render/particles.ts:50`
- `src/game.ts:328`
- [camera-render-me-51b-crop-dust.jpg](shots/camera-render-me-51b-crop-dust.jpg)
- [camera-render-me-51-sprint-dust.jpg](shots/camera-render-me-51-sprint-dust.jpg)
- [camera-render-pg-46-win-a.jpg](shots/camera-render-pg-46-win-a.jpg)
- `src/render/particles.ts:35` (dust: mesh.material=toon(color))
- `src/render/particles.ts:50` (dust scale update)
- `src/game.ts:328` (footstep dust '#e6dfd2')
- [playground-models-54-crop-stray-ring.jpg](shots/playground-models-54-crop-stray-ring.jpg)
- [playground-models-42-drag-mid.jpg](shots/playground-models-42-drag-mid.jpg)
- `src/render/particles.ts:14,33` (the other effect materials disable outlines; dust does not)
- [lobby-play-31-rush-unlocked.jpg](shots/lobby-play-31-rush-unlocked.jpg)
- [lobby-play-14-at-qfn-side-door.jpg](shots/lobby-play-14-at-qfn-side-door.jpg)
- [lobby-play-13-locked-rush.jpg](shots/lobby-play-13-locked-rush.jpg)
- `src/game.ts:327` (dust only when pace>5.5)

- `src/render/particles.ts:35,50`

**Fix.**

*From camera-render:* Render dust like smoke: a per-puff MeshBasicMaterial (transparent, depthWrite false, outlineParameters.visible=false). Opacity goes 0.35 → 0 over its life. Cap the size at 0.12 m radius × 1.8 growth. Better still, use a flat ground-aligned soft disc (a radial-gradient alphaMap) at y 0.03.

*From playground-models:* In particles.ts:35, give dust a material with outlineParameters={visible:false}: a cached toon clone with userData.outlineParameters.visible=false, or a transparent MeshBasicMaterial that fades opacity like smoke (opacity .45·t). Tint it 10–15 luma darker than the floor so it reads as a scuff, not a void.

*From lobby-play:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Don't add 'emit only when not sprinting'. It is already sprint-only, so that change would remove the effect. Instead give 'dust' a transparent MeshBasicMaterial (opacity .45→0, floor-tinted, depthWrite false), the same pattern as 'smoke' (particles.ts:31-33), and flatten it on y. Verify in real time, not with ?manual advance: drop manual, or call render each frame, then sprint and screenshot.

Reviewer's fix: In the particle 'dust' kind (src/render particles), use a flattened (y .35), soft-edged sprite that grows 0.1→0.35 m while alpha fades 0.45→0 over 0.45 s, tinted toward the floor colour (multiply #d9ab6e). Emit every second step only when not sprinting.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *camera-render:* Retake camera-render-me-51 (a 0.9 s sprint at zoom 17). No outlined sphere is visible, and the puffs are gone 0.8 s after the sprint stops.
- *playground-models:* Run a 3 s sprint and take two zoom-9 shots. No ink-outlined circles on the floor. Retake playground-models-42.
- *lobby-play:* Walk the back wall, then advance(.3) and shot: no bright round discs. Any puffs are soft, low, and gone within 0.5 s.

**Rules:** AGENTS 9, DR-56, DR-79

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — src/render/particles.ts:36 builds dust as ico(1) with toon(color), so it is opaque, lit and goes through the OutlineEffect. camera-render-me-51b-crop-dust.jpg shows cream spheres with dark ink outlines on the floor, and pg-46-win-a.png shows big outlined grey balls. Sizing correction: update scales by (1+(1-t)*1.8)*min(1,3t) (particles.ts:50), which peaks at 2.2× when t=1/3, not 2.8×. (2/3 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-314

**R5-314 | P2 | meeting | visual-bug | Coffee and kettle steam are stacked hard-edged grey balls / 1.5 m ghost discs (M7 regression)**

Found by: `camera-render#11` (P2 visual-bug), `meeting-models#13` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B8 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*camera-render* — **REGRESSION (M7): coffee steam still reads as stacked hard-edged grey balls about 1.5 m wide.** Steam now uses unlit, unoutlined MeshBasic spheres that fade (src/render/particles.ts:31-34, :48-49). Each puff is a uniform-opacity disc with a hard silhouette: opacity up to 0.5 and scale up to size×3.4, about 0.75 m radius. One spawns every 450 ms (src/game.ts coffee burst).

Two or three overlapping puffs read as a stack of grey translucent snowballs above the black machine (camera-render-me-06b-crop-steam.jpg). At the front-left corner a huge pale disc floats over the filing cabinets (camera-render-me-11b-crop-steam.jpg). M7 asked for vapour, not snowballs. This breaks DR-79.

*meeting-models* — **Coffee and kettle steam puffs swell into 1.5 m translucent ghost discs that sit over the vending machine and the boardroom glass (M7 partly regressed).** Smoke particles are icosahedra of size .14–.22 that grow by ×(1+2.4·√age), reaching radius .48–.75 (a diameter of up to 1.5 m), at opacity up to .5·…≈.44 (particles.ts:31-33, :48-49). The coffee machine emits one every 450 ms (game.ts:444) and the kettle about 3/s while on (meeting-strip.ts:92), so 4–6 overlapping balls are alive at once. At the game camera they read as large pale ghost circles hovering in front of the vending machine and coffee corner (meeting-models-13, -14). By the boardroom door they read as a frosted disc over the glass and the table (-36, -41, -43). The steam no longer stacks into snowballs (QA 8 / M7 fixed that), but it now covers the very things the player is trying to read (the kettle's on state, the boardroom) for most of the time. That breaks DR-79 (smoke fades and never blocks) and the restrained-glow intent (AGENTS 9).

**Fix.**

*From camera-render:* Give the smoke material an alphaMap: a 64×64 canvas radial gradient, white centre to transparent edge, built once and shared. Reduce the peak opacity to 0.28 and the max growth to size×2.2 (about 0.45 m radius). Spawn every 700 ms with a sideways drift of ±0.15 m/s, so puffs separate rather than stack. A camera-facing Sprite with the same gradient works too.

*From meeting-models:* particles.ts smoke: size .06–.1, growth ×(1+1.4·√age) (max radius ≈ .24), peak opacity .3, life .9–1.3 s. Rise faster (velocity.y .9–1.3) so puffs leave the appliance silhouette. Add a per-source cap: the kettle emits at dt*1.5 and the coffee every 900 ms. Optionally use a soft camera-facing sprite (a radial texture like `glow`) instead of an ico mesh, so the puff has no hard disc edge.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *camera-render:* Retake camera-render-me-06 (meeting spawn, zoom 9, yaw toward the coffee corner) after 5 s idle. The steam reads as soft wisps with no visible disc edge (edge-luma step under 8), and no more than 2 puffs overlap.
- *meeting-models:* Retake b.mjs -13 and e.mjs -41 and -43. No puff larger than 0.5 m on screen at zoom 9, and the kettle and heater silhouettes stay fully readable in 10 consecutive frames (advance(.1) ×10 crops).

**Rules:** AGENTS 9, DR-79

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — src/render/particles.ts:31-34 and :48-49: the smoke is an unlit, unoutlined MeshBasic ico with uniform opacity, peaking at about 0.43, and grows to size×3.4 (up to about 0.75 m radius). The coffee machine spawns a puff every 450 ms (src/game.ts:443). camera-render-me-06b-crop-steam.jpg shows overlapping translucent grey discs with hard silhouettes above the machine. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-315

**R5-315 | P2 | lobby, observatory | visual-bug | Decor parented to game.root floats in mid-air when its wall cuts away (lobby blade signs and wing glows, observatory light rail)**

Found by: `lobby-models#1` (P2 visual-bug), `observatory-models#1` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*lobby-models* — **Blade signs and lit wing-lamp glows live on game.root, so they float in mid-air when the wall cuts away.** Shell walls fold to 0.9 m stubs when the camera swings behind them (src/game.ts:384-385). The doors are children of the folding upper group, so they vanish correctly (lobby-models-04).

Two things are not children of that group:
- the side-door blade signs, built with group(g.root, …) at src/hub/lobby.ts:82;
- the lit-lamp glow sprites, built with glow(g.root, …) at lobby.ts:97.

When the player orbits west (camera on the -x side) the left wall drops, but the 1.3 m grey blade bracket stays hanging at y 2.7-3.2 right in front of the camera (lobby-models-45: a large grey L-shaped pipe in the foreground, with its single-sided plate culled). The same applies to every lit wing glow once a job is done: the sprites keep floating at y 3.35 over a wall that is no longer there. That breaks DR-75 (cutaway must not leave artefacts) and DR-72 (nothing floats), and it appears on a common orbit in the hub.

*observatory-models* — **Gallery light rail and its 7 lamps float in mid-air when the back wall cuts away.** The brass light rail (box 9×.06×.1 at y 3.2, z -D+.4 = -7.6) is parented to decorRoot `r`. Its seven 'hot' lamp cylinders are parented to game.root (room.ts:94). The panels, banner and safety note it lights are parented to kit.back, which cuts away whenever the camera orbits behind the back wall. The rail stays put, so once the camera passes behind the back wall a 9 m brass bar with seven glowing pucks hangs across the room at 3.2 m with nothing holding it up, and the exhibits it should light have gone. It's the most noticeable artefact in the room at the game camera (shots 64 and 72). Even with the wall present, the rail has no brackets to the wall or ceiling. It is 0.4 m out from the wall with nothing joining them (shot 20). This breaks DR-72 (nothing floats) and DR-75 (cutaway must not leave odd remnants).

Keep the two pointLamps on game.root.

Add pendant shades to `game.occluders` (clone the material, transparent) so they fade over Pip.

### R5-318

**R5-318 | P2 | qfn | visual-bug | QFN: REGRESSION (R3A N7) — the reference J1 placement covers the board title plate**

Found by: `qfn-models#9` (P2 visual-bug), `qfn-play#11` (P2 overlap). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*qfn-models* — **REGRESSION (R3A N7): board 1's connector J1, placed on the near edge in the reference solution, covers the 'BOARD 1 · SENSOR BREAKOUT' title plate.** R3A N7 reported tall parts on the top row drawing over the board title. The fix moved the title and legend plates to the board's near margin, with the comment 'where no part standing on the board can draw over them' (station.ts:108-111, positioned at z = h/2 + .066 in loadBoard, station.ts:134).

The sensor board's intended route places J1 on the near (bottom) edge with its mouth out. The connector shroud group is offset −S*.5 − .07 toward the mouth (station.ts:162-166) and its end cap reaches further. So J1's dark shroud, pin tags and the yellow chevron sit on top of the left half of the title plate. In qfn-models-40, -42 and -80 the title reads 'SOR BREAKOUT'.

The plate is drawn at y −.033 under the board, so any part reaching the margin covers it. That is the same class of bug, moved to the other edge. It hides the board name during the most important moment (routing board 1). The panel also repeats the name, which is why the clutter matters little for teaching, but it looks broken.

*qfn-play* — **REGRESSION (R3A N7): the reference J1 placement covers the board title plate.** Review 3 N7 moved the title and legend plates onto the jig's near margin so parts on the top row couldn't cover them. Board 1's solution places the 3-pin header J1 on the near (bottom) edge at (3,8) rot 3 (logic.ts:310). Its shroud and name cap stick out 0.07–0.14 m past the edge, onto the plate at near = h/2+.066 (station.ts:134). The title then reads 'SOR BREAKOUT' for the rest of the board (qfn-play-20, -21, -22). Any player who puts a connector on the near edge, which is the natural place to put it, hits this.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:108-111`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:134`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:160-168` (connector shroud/cap offsets)
- [qfn-models-40-board1-placed.jpg](shots/qfn-models-40-board1-placed.jpg)
- [qfn-models-42-board1-check.jpg](shots/qfn-models-42-board1-check.jpg)
- [qfn-models-80-crop-board1-parts.jpg](shots/qfn-models-80-crop-board1-parts.jpg)
- [qfn-models-40-board1-placed.jpg](shots/qfn-models-40-board1-placed.jpg) (title reads 'SOR BREAKOUT', panel shows 'Sensor breakout')
- [qfn-play-20-b1-placed.jpg](shots/qfn-play-20-b1-placed.jpg)
- [qfn-play-22-b1-check.jpg](shots/qfn-play-22-b1-check.jpg)
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:110-111`
- `src/stations/qfn/logic.ts:310`

**Fix.**

*From qfn-models:* Move the title plate and legend outside the jig's reach. Pick one of these, in station.ts:110-111 and :134:
- Put them at z = h/2 + .26, beyond the jig rbox(w+.26) margin (connector shroud + cap reach about .22 m past the edge).
- Lay them on the bench mat's left and right of the board at x ∓(w/2 + .35), rotated so they read from the bench camera.

Alternatively, give the plates renderOrder 5 and depthTest false. This keeps them legible, but they would then draw over parts, so prefer moving them.

*From qfn-play:* Move the plates to near = h/2 + 0.24, past the connector shroud's reach of 0.07 + 0.15. Or move the board title to the jig's far edge, with the legend under the far-left corner. Alternatively give the plates renderOrder 5 and draw them over parts.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *qfn-models:* Run the reference solution (mockups/review5/tools/qfn-models/s5.mjs) and retake qfn-models-40/-42. 'BOARD 1 · SENSOR BREAKOUT' is fully legible with J1 on the near edge. Repeat for boards 2 and 3 with the connectors on every edge.
- *qfn-play:* Retake qfn-play-22. The full 'BOARD 1 · SENSOR BREAKOUT' is visible with J1 on the near edge.

**Rules:** DR-48, DR-49, DR-70

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — qfn-models-40 shows J1's shroud and cap lying over the left half of the title plate, which reads 'SOR BREAKOUT'. The plates are placed at z = h/2+.066 (station.ts:134), and the connector shroud is offset -S*.5-.07 toward the mouth (station.ts:162-166). So the R3A N7 fix moved the conflict to the other edge, a regression of that class of bug. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)
