Or, better, replace the cabinet head with a 'handheld kiosk': a low counter rbox(.9,1.0,.6) with the handheld lying on a tilted cradle at 30°, tethered by a coiled cable (TubeGeometry helix r .012, INK) to the counter.

**Verify.**

- Retake arcade-models-80 (side, low) and -21: the handheld touches its mount (a gap under 1 cm), and the cabinet screen is either visible or intentionally replaced.

**Rules:** DR-70, DR-72

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Rotating the handheld (room.ts:90: group at z .6, rotation.x -.2, depth .12) puts its back face at z ≈.45 at the top and ≈.64 at the bottom. The cabinet body front is at z .4 and the head front at about .30, so there is a 10–15 cm gap with no mount. Arcade-models-80 shows the gap from the side.

### R5-320

**R5-320 | P2 | arcade-rush | visual-bug | Back-wall cabinets light by index % 5 from the story jobs, and every rush sign-off stacks another glow and confetti burst on them**

Found by: `arcade-rush-play#18` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: R-arcade (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

`act('signoff')` calls `this.room?.light(this.index%5)`, and `light()` creates a new glow sprite (opacity 0.35) plus 16 confetti on the story cabinet k: PINBALL, RHYTHM, CLAW, HANDHELD, PRIZES. In Rush, the fixed cabinets are DANCE, RACER, SKEE and so on, so the wrong marquees light up. After five sign-offs every one is lit already, and each later sign-off stacks another glow sprite on the same marquee. A 32-cabinet run adds about 27 redundant additive sprites at the back wall. That breaks the restrained-glow rule over time and leaks objects. Visually at 12 cabinets it is still modest, but it grows without bound.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/arcade/station.ts:276` (room.light(index%5))
- `src/stations/arcade/room.ts:122-123` (new glow + confetti every call)
- [arcade-rush-play-72-backwall-after-12.jpg](shots/arcade-rush-play-72-backwall-after-12.jpg)
- [arcade-rush-play-23-after7-survey.jpg](shots/arcade-rush-play-23-after7-survey.jpg)
- `src/stations/arcade/room.ts:81-84` (lit[] built from the story JOBS titles)

**Fix.**

In `room.ts` `light(k)`, return early if `lit[k].done`, and set `done=true` the first time. In rush, light the back-wall cabinets as a progress meter instead: cabinet k lights at served = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, with its marquee retitled to the rush cabinet just fixed. Or add a 'FIXED' tally board on the back wall, a canvas plaque redrawn per sign-off.

**Verify.**

- After 32 sign-offs, count the sprites added by light(): there are 5. Survey shot: marquees show rush titles or a progress meaning.

**Rules:** DR-47, DR-66

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The code confirms it. Sign-off calls room.light(index%5) (station.ts:276). light() adds a new glow sprite (opacity 0.35) and a 16-piece confetti burst on every call with no guard (room.ts:122-123). lit[] holds the five story cabinets (PINBALL, RHYTHM, CLAW, HANDHELD, PRIZES) from room.ts:84, not the rush titles.

### R5-321

**R5-321 | P2 | global | visual-bug | The cable passes straight through the box or shelf Pip presses the plug against**

Found by: `cable#2` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

simulateCable drops any furniture obstacle whose padded AABB contains the plug position or the anchor (src/game.ts:279). The plug is simulated 0.65 m in front of Pip (game.ts:267). Walking up to a crate stack or bookshelf therefore puts the plug inside that prop's box, the prop is removed from the obstacle list, and the cable is routed and drawn straight through it. Any wraps on that prop also vanish, so the bend can jump.

- cable-124 (zoom 9, Playground): the hose and the held plug go into the middle of the crate stack beside Pip.
- cable-17 (socket orbit): the cable runs through the candy-block bookshelf next to the lamp.

This breaks DR-73 ('wraps around obstacles instead of clipping them'). It happens in the most-watched spot, right next to Pip, every time the player hugs furniture, which dense rooms (AGENTS 3) make constant.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:267`
- `src/game.ts:279`
- [cable-124-pg-cable-close-zoom9.jpg](shots/cable-124-pg-cable-close-zoom9.jpg)
- [cable-17-pg-at-socket-close-orbit.jpg](shots/cable-17-pg-at-socket-close-orbit.jpg)
- [cable-16-pg-at-socket-close.jpg](shots/cable-16-pg-at-socket-close.jpg)
- `src/game.ts:276-277` (AABB ignores the prop's height axis: rotation elements [4]/[6] missing)
- `src/levels/clutter.ts:42` (shelf recipe = bookshelf + box + bin)
- `src/props/prefabs.ts:10` (box mass 2 -> excluded at game.ts:273)
- `src/levels/playground.ts:9-11` (the crate stacks are boxes)
- [cable-17-pg-at-socket-close-orbit.jpg](shots/cable-17-pg-at-socket-close-orbit.jpg) (Pip faces away from the toppled shelf)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep the face-clamp idea for plugPosition. Separately, fix the AABB so tipped props keep their footprint. In simulateCable, compute hx=|e0|*w/2+|e4|*h/2+|e8|*d/2+.05 and hz=|e2|*w/2+|e6|*h/2+|e10|*d/2+.05 (the [w,h,d] from prefabs size). Retake cable-17 after knocking the bookshelf over: the hose must bend around it.

Reviewer's fix: Push the end out of the box instead of deleting the obstacle.

1. In simulateCable, for each furniture AABB that contains `plugPosition`, keep the obstacle. Clamp the rope end used for routing to the nearest face plus CORNER (0.12 m): move along the axis of smallest penetration.
2. Use the clamped point as `end` in `rope.update`, and keep `plugPosition` itself for snapping.
3. Do the same for the anchor (or simply never spawn clutter on the anchor).
4. Pull the plug's visual position back to the clamped point, so the glove doesn't sink into the crate.

**Verify.**

- Rerun mockups/review5/tools/cable/pg8.mjs (walk into the crate stack at (-2,4.6)) and check cable-124. The hose must bend around the crate's corner. Unit test in src/sim/cable.test.ts: an end inside an obstacle gives a route whose segments don't intersect that obstacle.

**Rules:** AGENTS 3, DR-73

**Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE — The code mechanism is real. game.ts:279 drops any furniture AABB that contains plugPosition, and the plug is 0.65 m ahead of Pip (game.ts:267), so pushing into a desk or bookshelf removes it as an obstacle and unwraps any bends on it. But the cited screenshots show other causes. cable-124: the crate stack is made of kind 'box' (playground.ts:11), mass 2 (prefabs.ts:10).

### R5-322

**R5-322 | P2 | global | visual-bug | Orbiting toward the open front, or spawning near it, frames large areas of void (up to 48% of the start frame)**

Found by: `camera-render#13` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B3 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Rooms have walls on two sides only; the front and right edges are 0.32 m lips (src/levels/decor.ts:66-69). The follow camera centres on Pip with no bounds clamp (src/game.ts:366-368; follow is 1 at the default station zoom of 18.5).

In start frames, the share of dark void pixels is:

| Room | Void share |
|---|---|
| observatory | 48% |
| spectrum | 44% |
| arcade | 32% |
| qfn | 28% |
| lobby | 11% |

In the observatory, the bottom 40% of the screen is empty navy while the receiver and bench are pushed off the top-right (camera-render-ob-01-start.jpg, camera-render-sp-01-start.jpg).

At zoom 9 facing the front, the room ends in a lip and an empty horizon, like a stage with no fourth wall (camera-render-pg-06-zoom9.jpg, camera-render-ar-06-zoom9.jpg). This is DR-75's known 'low lips facing the void'. The start-frame waste is new.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:366-368`
- `src/levels/decor.ts:66-69`
- [camera-render-ob-01-start.jpg](shots/camera-render-ob-01-start.jpg)
- [camera-render-sp-01-start.jpg](shots/camera-render-sp-01-start.jpg)
- [camera-render-pg-06-zoom9.jpg](shots/camera-render-pg-06-zoom9.jpg)
- [camera-render-ar-06-zoom9.jpg](shots/camera-render-ar-06-zoom9.jpg)
- python luma check on camera-render-ob/sp/ar-01-start.png: void about 0.36/0.36/0.14

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Clamp the follow target only while zoomed out (near<0.8), so close follow stays centred on Pip. Also keep Pip's projected position above the bottom action-bar band (NDC y > -0.55), or the clamp will park Pip under the key bar near the front edge. Front and right shellWalls depend on the cutaway fix in finding 0; with the current centre-dot test they would block the default camera.

Reviewer's fix: 1. Clamp the follow target. After computing `target`, clamp target.x to ±(W/2 − halfViewX + 1.5) and target.z to the depth range minus halfViewZ, where halfView ≈ distance × tan(fov/2) × aspect × 0.5. When the room is narrower than the view, centre the room instead.
2. Build front and right walls with shellWall() (normals [0,1] and [1,0]). Once the cutaway fix lands they will stub whenever the camera is outside them, so the default camera is unchanged, but a reverse orbit sees a closed room instead of the void.

**Verify.**

- Recompute the void fraction on camera-render-*-01-start (the python snippet in this review). Every room under 15%. Retake camera-render-pg-06 at zoom 9 facing the front: a wall stub or full wall is visible, not a horizon of void.

**Rules:** DR-75

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — camera-render-ob-01-start.jpg has the left third and bottom of the frame as empty navy, with the bench pushed to the top right. My own crude dark-blue pixel count gives about 36% void for the observatory, 36% for spectrum and 14% for the arcade, against the reviewer's 48/44/32%. The numbers depend on the threshold, but the effect is real for the observatory and spectrum.

### R5-323

**R5-323 | P2 | global | visual-bug | Occluder fade speed depends on frame rate: 0.22 s at 60 fps and 0.44 s at 30 fps, and depthWrite pops at 0.8**

Found by: `camera-render#6` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B3 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

src/game.ts:388 eases opacity with `lerp(opacity, target, .15)` once per rendered frame, ignoring dt. Reaching ≤0.25 from 1 needs about 13 frames: 0.22 s at 60 fps, and 0.44 s at 30 fps, the frame rate adaptQuality is meant to catch.

DR-12 asks for ≤0.2 s. At low frame rates Pip is hidden for almost half a second each time he walks behind a pillar.

`depthWrite` flips when opacity crosses 0.8, so mid-fade a wall switches from occluding props behind it to not occluding them in one frame. That is a visible pop of the props behind it (DR-78).

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:388`
- [camera-render-pg-41-pillar-fade-t0.jpg](shots/camera-render-pg-41-pillar-fade-t0.jpg)
- [camera-render-pg-42-pillar-fade-t1.jpg](shots/camera-render-pg-42-pillar-fade-t1.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-camera-render/v2.mjs` output: FADE {0.017:{frames:14,seconds:0.233},0.033:{frames:14,seconds:0.467}}

**Fix.**

Use `const k=1-Math.exp(-dt*18); material.opacity+= (target-material.opacity)*k;`. That reaches 0.25 in about 0.12 s at any frame rate.

Set depthWrite=false as soon as the target is the faded value. Restore depthWrite only when opacity returns above 0.98, so the pop happens while the mesh is almost opaque.

**Verify.**

- Unit-test updateCamera with dt=1/30: from opacity 1 with a hit, opacity ≤0.25 after 0.2 s of simulated frames. Visually, take two shots 0.1 s apart while walking behind the playground pillar. There is no frame where props behind the pillar flash in front of it.

**Rules:** DR-12, DR-78

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — src/game.ts:388 lerps by a fixed 0.15 per rendered frame, regardless of dt. Iterating the same formula from opacity 1 toward the 0.15 target takes 14 frames to reach 0.25: 0.233 s at 60 fps and 0.467 s at 30 fps. That misses DR-12's 0.2 s even at 60 fps. `depthWrite=opacity>.8` (the same line) flips in a single frame partway through the fade.

### R5-324

**R5-324 | P2 | global | visual-bug | Overstretch pull pose swings the plug over the shoulder into the helmet**

Found by: `characters#5` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

When strain passes about 0.85 (pull > .5), the right arm snaps to rotation.x = +2.45 rad. That swings the glove up and behind the shoulder, to about (0.39, 1.5, -0.32) m. The plug, about 0.25 m long, then sits against the side and back of the head, with the prongs into the brim (characters-16b). From the default rear camera it reads as a yellow box stuck on Pip's ear while the red cable drops vertically down his back (characters-16). The pose is meant to read as 'hauling over the shoulder', which is a good comedic idea, but the plug clips the helmet. The cable also ends at the head, so the strain gradient visually runs into Pip's skull. ART R10.3 / DR-65: never intersecting the head or helmet.

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/pipRig.ts:75` (rx=pull>.5?2.45:-1.1; rz -.35)
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:40` (hand anchor under right elbow)
- [characters-16-overstretch-pull-pose.jpg](shots/characters-16-overstretch-pull-pose.jpg)
- [characters-16b-crop-plug-vs-helmet.jpg](shots/characters-16b-crop-plug-vs-helmet.jpg)

**Fix.**

Change the haul pose to a two-handed tug-of-war lean. Right arm rx = -.6 (forward-down) with rz -.25, left arm lx = -.9 reaching for the cable, elbows -.6, and keep the torso lean -.32 (pipRig.ts:63) plus knees bent .3 for a dug-in stance. If the over-shoulder pose is kept, cap rx at 1.9, add rz = -.7 so the hand moves out to x ≈ .6, away from the brim (r .36), and rotate the plug so its prongs point back along the cable.

- Retake characters-16/16b/17 (s2.mjs). The plug's bounding box must not intersect a sphere of r 0.36 around (0,1.45,0) in Pip's local space. A crop must show a clear gap between the plug and the brim.

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Code: src/render/pipRig.ts:75 sets rx=2.45 once pull>.5, which is strain above 0.85, and the plug is attached to the hand under elbows[1] (line 40). In characters-16 and the 16b crop, the yellow plug sits against the side and back of the head with its prongs into the skull and brim. The red, strained cable drops straight down Pip's back from there. This breaks the 'never intersect the head' part of DR-65.

### R5-325

**R5-325 | P2 | global | visual-bug | Alarm pose squashes blobs flat while the sweat drop and "!" float detached above them**

Found by: `characters#9` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

When alarmed, the body is squashed to y 0.72 and xz 1.28 (`duck`), so a standing blob's head drops from 1.06 m to about 0.76 m. The sweat sprite stays at a fixed 1.02 m and the bubble at 1.55 m on the unsquashed group. The drop hangs about 0.26 m in the air above and beside the head, and the "!" floats about 0.8 m up (characters-48c: the purple blob is a flat dome with its startled eyes squeezed onto the top, and its sweat drop hangs in space). For seated blobs the squash turns them into a mound with eyes on the crown (characters-90). It reads as being stepped on, or as a macaron or bun shape (DR-52), rather than startled. Good Job's laughs come from coworkers recoiling or jumping. The startled mesh's raised arm nubs (rz -2.3) are also hidden by the squash.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:131` (sweat at fixed y (seated?.35:0)+1.02)
- `src/game.ts:132` (bubble at fixed y +1.55)
- `src/game.ts:426,429` (duck=.72; body.scale.set(2-duck,duck,2-duck))
- `src/render/actors.ts:31` (alarm arms rz -2.3)
- [characters-48-coffee-blobs-alarmed.jpg](shots/characters-48-coffee-blobs-alarmed.jpg)
- [characters-48c-crop-alarm-sweat-float.jpg](shots/characters-48c-crop-alarm-sweat-float.jpg)
- [characters-90-meeting-seated-alarm.jpg](shots/characters-90-meeting-seated-alarm.jpg)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Don't parent the sprites to npc.body. Body scale is non-uniform (1.28/.72/1.28, or the 1.15/.93 stretch), and a T.Sprite inherits its parent's world scale, so the drop and the '!' would be squashed and stretched with the body. Keep them on the group and set their y each frame from the body: `sweat.position.y=npc.body.position.y+(.55+.505)*npc.body.scale.y-.05`, and the bubble about 0.3 m above that.

Reviewer's fix: Replace the squash with a recoil hop in src/game.ts:426-429. Over the first 0.15 s of alarm, stretch (scale y 1.15, xz .93) and lift the body by `Math.sin(age*Math.PI/.3)*.25`. Then settle to a slight lean away from the impact: rotate body.x by .2 toward −(impact direction), which needs the alarm point stored on the npc. Parent the sweat and bubble sprites to `npc.body` (not `g`), or update them each frame to `npc.body.position.y+1.1*npc.body.scale.y`, so they ride on the head.

**Verify.**

- Retake characters-48/48c (s6.mjs) and characters-90 (s11.mjs). The sweat drop must touch the head silhouette, the "!" must sit 0.2–0.4 m above the head, and the blob must be taller during the first 0.3 s, not flatter.

**Rules:** DR-52

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Code: when alarmed, duck=.72 (src/game.ts:426) and body.scale=(1.28,.72,1.28) (line 429), which puts the head top at about .76 m for a standing blob. The sweat sprite sits at a fixed 1.02 m (line 131) and the bubble at 1.55 m (line 132), both on the unscaled group. Screenshots: in characters-48c the purple blob is a flat dome with its eyes on top and the sweat drop hanging well above it.

### R5-328

**R5-328 | P2 | lobby | visual-bug | Seen at a grazing angle, the open portal reads as a shallow orange closet, and the destination view vanishes**

From an orbit of about 35° (lobby-models-14), the ray mostly hits the corridor's side wall (uDepth 2.8, lobby.ts:86). ### R5-330

**R5-330 | P2 | observatory | visual-bug | Shared toon material mutated to DoubleSide by the dish exhibit**

Found by: `observatory-models#18` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: R-observatory (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

toon() caches materials by colour (toon.ts:34-44). room.ts:98 does `(bowl.material as T.Material).side=T.DoubleSide` on toon('#dfe3ea'). That same material is used for the mast crossbars (room.ts:84), every bench whip rod and spare rod (station.ts:141,144) and the series wire link, so all of them silently become double-sided. That doubles their fill and changes how the outline pass and AO treat them. room.ts:72 does the same to toon('#e9dcc0') (FrontSide, harmless today). The pattern is fragile: one prop's tweak changes many others in the instanced batches.

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/observatory/room.ts:98`
- `src/stations/observatory/room.ts:72`
- `src/render/toon.ts:33-44`
- `src/stations/observatory/station.ts:141,144`
- 01-room.mjs scene output: dfe3ea material sides [2] (one shared material, DoubleSide)

**Fix.**

Clone before mutating: `bowl.material=(bowl.material as T.Material).clone();(bowl.material as T.Material).side=T.DoubleSide;`. Or add a `side` field to ToonOptions and include it in the cache key in toon.ts:35.

**Verify.**

- In page.evaluate, traverse the scene and check that the whip rod meshes' material.side === FrontSide (0), and that only the dish uses DoubleSide.

**Rules:** DR-57

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — toon() caches by colour/emissive/map/opacity only (toon.ts:34-44), and room.ts:98 sets side=DoubleSide on the shared toon('#dfe3ea'). At runtime every mesh coloured #dfe3ea (mast crossbars room.ts:84, wire link station.ts:118, whip rod station.ts:141, spare rods station.ts:144, dish) shares one material with side=2 (DoubleSide).

### R5-332

**R5-332 | P2 | qfn | visual-bug | The ratsnest draws dashed lines to invisible parts before the crate arrives, and doesn't follow a part being dragged**

Found by: `qfn-play#12` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Before partsReady, syncParts hides every part except U1 (station.ts:183), but redraw() still builds the ratsnest from design.place. Dashed lines run from U1's pads to empty board cells (qfn-play-40), which looks broken. During a body drag, ghost() moves the part mesh to drag.to (station.ts:360), but the ratsnest and the pad rings are computed from the committed placement (station.ts:201), so the dashes keep pointing at the empty cell the part left (qfn-play-53). The live feedback that tells a player 'this placement shortens the route' is exactly what placement depends on, and it's missing while dragging.

**Evidence.**

- [qfn-play-40-bench-no-crate.jpg](shots/qfn-play-40-bench-no-crate.jpg)
- [qfn-play-53-drag-body.jpg](shots/qfn-play-53-drag-body.jpg)
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:183`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:201-204`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:360`
- [verify-qfn-play-02-bench-no-crate.jpg](shots/verify-qfn-play-02-bench-no-crate.jpg)
- [verify-qfn-play-11-mid-drag.jpg](shots/verify-qfn-play-11-mid-drag.jpg)

**Fix.**

In redraw(), when !partsReady, skip the ratsnest and the legend. During a drag, compute it with `ratsnest(b,{...d,place:{...d.place,[drag.id]:{at:drag.to,rot:d.place[drag.id].rot}}})` so the dashes stretch live as the part moves. Rate-limit it to cell changes, which ghost() already does.

**Verify.**

- Retake qfn-play-40 (no dashes) and qfn-play-53 (the dashes end at C1's ghost position).

**Rules:** DR-43, DR-47

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Both halves reproduced. Before the crate arrives, dashed lines run from U1 to empty cells (verify-qfn-play-02). During a body drag, C1's ghost sits near (3,5) while the red and blue dashes still end at its old cell (verify-qfn-play-11). redraw() uses the committed design.place (station.ts:201), and ghost() only moves the mesh (station.ts:360).

### R5-333

**R5-333 | P2 | qfn | visual-bug | New-board parts drop from 0.6–0.9 m and look like they're floating over the room; the ship toast describes the board that just left**

Found by: `qfn-play#20` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

On SHIP the next board loads in the same frame (station.ts:287), and dropIn() lifts every movable part to y 0.6–0.9 (station.ts:298). From the steep bench camera, parts at that height project far up the frame, over the background cabinets and bin (qfn-play-23: C1 and C2 at the top of the screen). Meanwhile the 25-word toast teaches the lesson of the board that has already gone ('Placement comes before routing…'), over a fresh scrambled board. The success moment is a cheer() burst plus an instant swap, with no beat to enjoy the finished board.

**Evidence.**

- [qfn-play-23-b1-shipped.jpg](shots/qfn-play-23-b1-shipped.jpg)
- [qfn-play-28-b2-shipped.jpg](shots/qfn-play-28-b2-shipped.jpg)
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:285-287`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:298`
- [verify-qfn-play-15-after-ship1.jpg](shots/verify-qfn-play-15-after-ship1.jpg)

**Fix.**

Hold the finished board for 1.6 s: the current bursts run and the board lifts and slides to the outbox stack. Show the teach line during that hold, then load the next board. Drop parts from 0.25 m, or slide them out of the crate on the side table.

**Verify.**

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — In verify-qfn-play-15, 0.3 s after shipping board 1, the new board's C1 and C2 hang at the top of the frame over the background cabinets and bin, which is the 0.6–0.9 m dropIn (station.ts:298). Board 1's teach toast is still showing over the new scrambled board, because the swap happens in the same frame (station.ts:287).

### R5-334

**R5-334 | P2 | spectrum | visual-bug | Toaster smoke is a flat white veil that washes out Pip and the tea coworker, hides its own toaster, and reads as a glow from low angles**

Found by: `spectrum-models#8` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: R-spectrum (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Fourteen billboard sprites (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:118-119, animated in station.ts:402-403) scale 0.8 → 2.7 m with opacity up to 0.5, colour #b4b8c6, depthWrite off. Near the tea corner they stack into a uniform translucent sheet. Standing at the counter turns Pip's yellow helmet near-white and veils the orange coworker and the whole counter (A8, 95, 96). The toaster (0.36×0.24×0.22 m) can't be seen as the source. From the default high camera the cloud reads as a grey smudge on the floor (02, 59). From low orbits it is a 2.5 m soft white column that looks like a lamp bloom, not burnt-toast smoke (07, 15, 17). DR-79 says smoke never stacks into a solid mass or blocks Pip. Mirror mark C and the tea-corner route (lane [.6,4.2]) both pass through it.

**Evidence.**

- [spectrum-models-A8-tea-coworker-z9.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-A8-tea-coworker-z9.jpg)
- [spectrum-models-95-toaster-close-high.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-95-toaster-close-high.jpg)
- [spectrum-models-17-tea-smoke.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-17-tea-smoke.jpg)
- [spectrum-models-07-orbit-low.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-07-orbit-low.jpg)
- [spectrum-models-B3-toaster-side-z9.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-B3-toaster-side-z9.jpg)
- `src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:118-119`
- `src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:402-403`
- `src/stations/spectrum/logic.ts` SMOKE={x:2.4,z:3.4,r:1.3}

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The smoke is a taught obstacle: logic.SMOKE (2.4, 3.4, r 1.3) attenuates NIR and visible light. The visual cloud must still cover that disc at beam height (y ≈ 1.25), or players will see beams dimmed by invisible smoke. Shrink and thin the individual puffs, but keep them spread over the SMOKE footprint, and fade them near Pip. Don't shrink the cloud as a whole to a 1.3 m column at the toaster.

Reviewer's fix: Make the smoke read as toon puffs from a visible source. Use 8 sprites, not 14. Scale 0.35 → 1.3 m (s = .35 + u*.95). Peak opacity .32, fading in over u < .15 and out from u > .6. Use a darker burnt grey '#8d8f9c' with a lighter core (TX.radial with a hard 0.55 stop for a cel edge). Start the puffs exactly at the toaster slots (2.1, 1.2, 4.85) rising 0.9 m before drifting toward SMOKE. Add a sprite-free zone: skip any puff whose screen-space footprint covers Pip (or set opacity *= .3 when within 1 m of the player). Make the toaster read: a slightly larger body rbox(.44,.28,.26), a side lever (box .04×.02×.06, INK), a coiled cord to the wall, and a faint hot-orange slot glow (hot('#ff8a3d',1.2) plane in each slot).

**Verify.**

- Retake A8, 95 and 17 (s9-yaws.mjs, s8-closeups.mjs). Pip's helmet keeps its yellow (median hue within 10° of #ffc94d in a helmet crop). The toaster and its slots are visible under the smoke, and the low-orbit shot shows distinct puffs rising from the toaster.

**Rules:** DR-12, DR-43, DR-79

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The code matches: 14 sprites, opacity .45, depthWrite off, colour #b4b8c6 (room.ts:118-119), animated at station.ts:403. A8 shows Pip's helmet washed near-white and the counter and coworker veiled. 07 shows a white column from the low orbit. DR-79 ('never block Pip') is broken.

### R5-336

**R5-336 | P2 | global, arcade, garage, observatory, spectrum, meeting, lobby, qfn, lunch | model-detail | Fixtures have big flat single-colour faces and bare, unfinished backs (cabinets, benches, racks, desks, scope, reception desk)**

Found by: `props-gallery#10` (P2 model-detail), `arcade-models#6` (P2 model-detail), `garage-models#15` (P2 model-detail), `observatory-models#9` (P2 model-detail), `spectrum-models#11` (P2 model-detail), `meeting-models#19` (P2 model-detail), `lobby-models#5` (P2 model-detail), `qfn-models#12` (P2 model-detail), `lunch-models#17` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*props-gallery* — **Large office props have bare single-colour backs: cabinet, printer, cooler, monitor and coffee machine.** DR-63 asks for a finished back because the camera orbits. From yaw 2.64 (`props-gallery-10-sheet*`, the back column):

| Prop | Back |
|---|---|
| cabinet | one 0.7×1.6 m grey face, 1.1 m², no seams (prefabs.ts:87-92) |
| printer | plain white box, with the INK top slab and nothing else |
| water cooler | plain cream body |
| monitor | an INK slab; a stand post shows but no rear housing bump or ports |
| coffee machine | plain black (prefabs.ts:108) |

Cabinets stand back to back in rows in the Meeting and in clutter (`cabinets` recipe), so these backs are often in view when orbiting. They read as cardboard stage flats.

*arcade-models* — **Arcade cabinets have blank backs and flat 1.5 m² sides, and the bench meter has a bare back: they read as pastel slabs from every angle except the front.** cabinet() (src/stations/arcade/room.ts:59-69) is a body rbox, a plinth, a tilted head box, a screen, a deck with 3 buttons, a coin door and a marquee, all on the front face. The back and the two sides are plain single-colour faces. Each side is 0.8 m × ~1.9 m ≈ 1.5 m², 3× the DR-62 limit of 0.5 m² untrimmed, and the back is 0.95 × 1.9 m. Since 3 cabinets stand against the east wall facing west and 3 against the west wall, orbiting even 90° shows a row of blank candy slabs: in shots -24 and -52 the right-wall cabinets from behind read as fridges or lockers, not arcade machines. The serviced cabinet (station.ts:216-220), described as 'back open, ribbon cable to the board' in the station.ts:212 comment, has a closed blank back too (shot -71). The bench meter (station.ts:184-187) is a pale pink board with a bare back (shot -34). DR-63 asks that every model has a finished back because the player orbits.

*garage-models* — **Big flat single-colour faces: bench cabinet front and back (4.3 m²), scope back (1.3 m²), tool-chest and cabinet backs.** DR-62 forbids visible flat single-colour faces larger than 0.5 m² without trim, panel lines or decals, and DR-63 requires finished backs because the player orbits.
- The bench cabinet is one cream rbox(4.3,1,1.25) (station.ts:116), with only two 3 cm vertical strips at x ±1.07 and a yellow kick stripe. Its 4.3 m² front and back faces are blank (garage-models-14-bench-front, -15-bench-front-o180, -54).
- The scope's back is a plain cream rbox(1.46,.92,.22) with a teal top (station.ts:170), reading as a crate from behind (garage-models-15, -78).
- The tool chest's back (1.3×1 m, red, room.ts:93) is blank (-17).
- The two side cabinets' backs at (10.2, -.6/.2) are bare pale slabs (-35, -21).
- The decor robots' backs show only cargo bin and teal. That is acceptable.

*observatory-models* — **Rack, dome exterior and scope cabinet have big blank faces and unfinished backs.** The receiver rack is an rbox of .9×1.5×.7 in NIGHT with three front panels, a dial each and 9 LED dots (room.ts:81-85). Its sides (1.05 m² each) and back (1.35 m²) are plain navy with no vents, handles, screws, cable entry or mast clamp (shots 33, 61). The mast pole just stands on the brass top. The outer dome shell, about 20 m², is uniform cream with no panel seams, ribs or hatch (shots 66b, 72, 65b). Seen from the gallery side, the scope cabinet's back (body rbox 1.6×1.0, station.ts:148) is a plain cream slab (shot 62b). All of these break DR-62 (no flat single-colour face over 0.5 m² without trim) and DR-63 (finished backs, because the player orbits).

*spectrum-models* — **Big flat single-colour fixture faces: dispatch desk, tea counter, exhibits counter and lab benches.** DR-62 allows no visible flat single-colour face over 0.5 m² without trim, a panel line or a decal. The dispatch desk body is rbox(4.4,1,1.3) cream (src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:111). Its front (4.4 m²) has only five 3.5 cm rainbow stripes near the floor, and its back and ends are blank (13, 14, A2). The tea counter is rbox(2.2,.9,.62) plain pink (room.ts:111): its 2 m² front is bare (18, B3). The exhibits counter is rbox(2.6,.9,.7) plain '#e9e2d4' (room.ts:122). The lab benches are rbox(2.4,.9,.8) plain white (room.ts:96). In this white hall these slabs merge with the floor and walls and read as untextured blockout boxes next to the detailed props. They are the room's main stations, so they need the most cues (≥ 6 per fixture).

*meeting-models* — **Fixture backs are unfinished from orbit: server racks, cabinets and the vending machine are plain slabs from behind.** The orbit is player-controlled, so DR-63 asks every model to have a finished back. The four server racks are plain `rbox(.8,2.3,.9)` in #3a3d55 with LEDs and a door only on their +z face (decor.ts:135-136). From the back-wall orbit (meeting-models-03, -06) and from above, they read as four black monoliths. The cabinets (prefabs.ts:87-92) have drawers and pulls only on +z, and from the back-wall orbit (-04) the 18-unit run is a featureless grey and kraft strip. The vending machine back is solid red (-52, -53; known F14). The load gauge back is a bare ink box (kit.ts:108; -29).

*lobby-models* — **Reception desk and board have bare backs, and the desk 'monitors' are plain ink cubes that read as speakers.** Reception is the lobby's only big fixture, but it has fewer than 6 cues and large flat faces. That fails DR-62 (stations and fixtures show at least 6 cues; no plain face over 0.5 m²) and DR-63 (finished backs, because the player orbits):
- The desk body rbox(4,1,1.1) has a 4 m² featureless cream back and two plain 1.1 m² ends (src/hub/lobby.ts:55; lobby-models-11, -33).
- The board's back is a 5.3 m² flat black slab (lobby-models-04, -11).
- The two 'screens' are rbox(.5,.35,.4) in INK at (±1.2, 1.25, -0.1) (lobby.ts:57). They have no bezel, no screen face and no stand, and from the front they read as two black speaker cubes (lobby-models-09, -12).
- There is no receptionist chair behind the desk, and no bell, phone, keyboard or papers, so the receptionist blob at (-1.4, 0.6) stands in front of the desk rather than behind it.

*qfn-models* — **The layout bench is a plain slab: blank front, sides and back; a flat 3.3×2.3 m mat; the side table top overlaps the bench top on a coplanar seam.** The bench (station.ts:85-93) is the room's main fixture. It is built from:
- a periwinkle rbox 3.9×0.84×2.3;
- a wood top box 4.05×0.08×2.45 and a darker edge strip;
- two blank lavender rbox .9×.5 front panels;
- a 3.3×2.26 plain lavender mat;
- a side table, rbox 1×0.84×1.4 with a wood top.

In qfn-models-30, -31 and -32 the front shows two blank panels, and the back and both 2.3×0.84 m ends are bare periwinkle. The bench breaks the ≥6 cue fixture rule and the 0.5 m² flat-face rule (DR-62), and the back is unfinished for orbiting (DR-63). In the bench view (qfn-models-37) about 55% of the frame is blank pale mat.

The side-table top box(1.08,.07,1.48) at x 2.55 spans x 2.01..3.09, and the bench top spans x −2.025..2.025. They overlap by 1.5 cm in x, with both top faces at exactly y 0.92 and the same colour #ecd3a6. That makes a coplanar overlap (DR-77 risk). The two read as one L-shaped top (qfn-models-32).

The shipped-board stack sits 5 mm above the side-table top (station.ts:296, y t.y + .02 with .03 thickness), which is acceptable.

*lunch-models* — **Kitchen set dressing is under-modelled: pots are bare cylinders and the oven's hood and back are large flat untrimmed slabs.** The four pots on the prep table (decor.ts:186) are plain cylinders cyl(.16,.14,.22) in red and grey. With no rims, handles or lids, they read as tin cans or cups (lunch-models-33, -59). The oven has good front cues: window, three knobs, bake gauge and socket. But from the side and back (lunch-models-31) the 2.6 × 1.7 m body and the 2.8 × 1.5 m hood top are uniform flat faces: no panel lines, vents, feet or back panel. The chimney is a plain cylinder going into the void above the wall line. The player orbits (AGENTS 8), and DR-62/63 require trimmed faces under 0.5 m² and finished backs. The baked-tray model is a red rbox with three squashed spheres (prefabs.ts:156), which reads as buns on a tray and is fine.

**Fix.**

*From props-gallery:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Prioritise the cabinet and printer backs, which are real DR-62 breaks, and clutter-placed cabinets. The monitor, cooler and coffee machine backs are lower-priority DR-63 polish.

Reviewer's fix: - **Cabinet:** 3 horizontal seam strips `box(w*.9,.015,.01)` in the dark shade on the back face at the drawer lines, plus a small cream inventory sticker `box(.12,.08,.01)`.
- **Printer:** a rear vent panel (a `rbox(w*.5,.18,.02)` in DMETAL) and an INK power-socket square; on the front, add a control panel strip `rbox(.25,.04,.1)` in INK with a `lit()` LED on top at the front-right.
- **Cooler:** an INK back vent grid (`box(.3,.4,.01)` decal) and a cord stub.
- **Monitor:** a rear housing bump `rbox(w*.5,h*.4,.04)` in INK at z `-.08`, and an off-white logo dot.

Keep these parts merged per kind so they batch.

*From arcade-models:* In cabinet(): (a) add T-molding: an INK or PLUM box(.025,1.9,.82) strip on each side's front edge and along the top of the body. (b) Add side art on each side: a flat decal plane (.62×1.1) using a small canvasTex per seed (a star burst or game logo in the cabinet's accent), offset 6 mm. (c) Add back detail: a recessed rear door rbox(.6,1.1,.02) in a darker body shade, two vent grilles (5 × box(.4,.02,.015) INK), a power cord tube from y .2 down to the floor (TubeGeometry r .015, INK). (d) Bevel the head into a slanted marquee hood, so the side silhouette has the classic stepped profile. For the serviced cabinet: actually open the back (omit the rear panel, add a dark interior box and a visible PCB plane in #2f7a5b with the ribbon cable emerging). For the meter: add a back housing rbox(1.5,.9,.06) in PLUM with 4 screw dots and a vent strip.

*From garage-models:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The bench desk is on g.decorRoot and gets merged by freeze(), which is fine for static doors and pulls; just keep them static.

Reviewer's fix: 1) Bench front (station.ts:116-117): add 4 cabinet doors rbox(.98,.78,.02,.03) in toon('#e6d6b6') at x -1.6/-.54/.54/1.6, y .5, z t.z+.63. Lab benches: a drawer bank on one end, reagent shelf uprights, and a blue edge band.

That includes the drop target sx in dropped() (station.ts:379-381), the shipped-board stack in stackShipped() (station.ts:296) and the side-table solid at station.ts:91. - **Front panels:** turn them into drawer stacks: 3 drawer fronts rbox(.85,.14,.03) each with an INK pull box(.18,.03,.03).

Keep everything below y t.y + .1, or behind z t.z − 1.0, so the bench camera (distance 5.6, pitch 1.02) still frames the board cleanly.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

### R5-337

**R5-337 | P2 | global, lunch, playground, qfn | model-detail | Pip's hard-hat ridge reads as a fin or cat ears, with grey plinth soles (DR-64 / F9 still open)**

Found by: `characters#6` (P2 model-detail), `lunch-models#18` (P2 model-detail), `playground-models#22` (P2 model-detail), `qfn-models#22` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*characters* — **REGRESSION-check DR-64 (ART F9) still open: plinth soles, a ridge that reads as a fin or ears, and arms that merge into a cape.** public/models/pip.glb hasn't changed since commit 1649a1e, and all three F9 artefacts are visible in the new 6-angle sheet:
- **Soles:** grey bevelled slabs (0.26 × 0.42 m) stick out past the round ink boots on every side. Pip stands on little skates or plinths (characters-09, all six angles; characters-60b; -21b).
- **Ridge:** the 0.48 m bevelled box on the dome pokes above the helmet at front and back. From behind and above it reads as a tab or 'ears' (characters-04 a180, characters-16b). At the game camera it looks like a crack down the helmet (characters-40b).
- **Arms:** the upper-arm ellipsoids (0.22 × 0.24 × 0.54 m, pivot ±.39) sit flush against the 0.68 m-wide torso. Their tops bulge up beside the chin like shoulder pads or wings in the front view (characters-01, -40b), and from behind the arms and torso form one wide blue mass (characters-04, -83, -85).

Pip is on screen 100% of the time, so these read as modelling errors.

*lunch-models* — **Pip still shows the helmet ridge 'fin' and grey plinth soles from side and back (DR-64).** At zoom 9 in Lunch's power room (lunch-models-50b: front-top, side and back crops), Pip's hard hat has a raised ridge or fin on the crown that reads as a little ear or blade from the side and back. Each boot sits on a flat grey rectangular plate that sticks out beyond the boot outline. Both are exactly what DR-64 lists as 'no cat-ear helmet ridge, no plinth soles'. They read as model errors at the close camera, which players use constantly for plugging. (Pip is shared by all rooms; it is logged here because it is visible in every Lunch close-up, e.g. lunch-models-53, -57, -97.)

*playground-models* — **Pip's hard-hat ridge ends stick out of the flattened dome as two 'cat ears' (F9 still open).** The helmet is a flattened sphere (scale z .17) with a straight 0.48 m ridge box laid on top at z 1.72. The dome curves away beneath the ridge's ends, so the front and back ends stand up as two bumps. From behind or three-quarter views they read as cat ears (crops -57, -60). Pip is in every shot of the tutorial, so this is the first silhouette a player learns.

*qfn-models* — **Pip's hard-hat ridge still reads as a 'cat ear' in close and side views in this room.** In side and three-quarter zoom-9 views in the Fab Bay, the hard hat's raised ridge and front lamp form a pointed lobe that reads as an ear:
- qfn-models-68-oven-shelf-o200-p-150: two pointed bumps at the top of the hat;
- qfn-models-83-crop-rack;
- qfn-models-14.

DR-64 explicitly bans the 'cat ear' helmet ridge. Pip is the same model in every room (tools/create_assets.py:60, 'Hard hat: dome, brim, ridge, lamp'), so this is a re-check of a known issue, and it is still present. It is visible here because the QFN bench forces many close side angles.

### R5-338

**R5-338 | P2 | meeting, global, lunch, lobby | model-detail | Vending machine, water cooler, printer and ping-pong table miss their identifying cues (slab with sticker grid, pedestal with a can; the "printer stand" does not exist)**

Found by: `props-gallery#9` (P2 model-detail), `props-gallery#11` (P2 model-detail), `lunch-models#16` (P2 model-detail), `lobby-models#11` (P2 model-detail), `meeting-models#21` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The back and sides are flat red faces of up to 2×1 m, against DR-62's 0.5 m² limit (`props-gallery-25-meeting-vending-back-o700.jpg`, `props-gallery-10-sheet07`). The re-check item "Lunch vending machine faces +z" passes: it is decor (`decor.ts`), and the window faces the camera in `props-gallery-52b-lunch-survey.jpg`.

*props-gallery* — **Water cooler, printer and ping-pong table miss their identifying cues at the game camera.** DR-62 wants 2–4 cues per prop.

*lunch-models* — **Still open: the vending machine is a slab with a sticker grid, the water cooler is a box with a can on it, and the supply-cart gauge is a bare board from behind.** These were reported in research-art F14/F15 and are re-checked here.

DR-62 says a fixture should show at least 6 cues and no flat face over 0.5 m² without trim.

The two INK outlet cylinders on the end face read as a pair of eyes (lunch-models-99b, -72), so the cart reads like a face, which competes with the blobs.

*lobby-models* — **The water cooler reads as a white pedestal with a can: no taps, bottle neck, drip tray or cups.** The cooler prefab (src/props/prefabs.ts:129) is a rbox body (0.51 × 0.94 × 0.51) plus a flat-topped translucent cylinder (r .2, .375 tall). Close up it looks like a bin or a pedestal (lobby-models-27, -29).

*meeting-models* — **The printer is a three-part white box, and the 'printer stand' the job card names doesn't exist (the strip lies on the carpet 1.8 m away).** The printer prefab is an rbox, a dark top recess and a paper tray (prefabs.ts:118). **R5-339 | P2 | global, observatory, qfn | model-detail | Bookshelves are tinted accent colours and filled with uniform saturated candy-block books that poke above the frame**

Found by: `props-gallery#8` (P2 model-detail), `observatory-models#16` (P2 art-style), `qfn-models#13` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B9 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*props-gallery* — **Bookshelf books are still uniform candy bricks, saturated and poking above the frame.** This confirms RESEARCH_ART F10 is still open. Each shelf holds 7 identical `box(.14,.34,d*.7)` books, 14 cm thick (about 3× a real book), in full `CHAIRC`-style saturated colours (prefabs.ts:52, :123-125). The top row reaches y .97 against a frame top of .9, so the books stick 7 cm out of the frame and the collider. There is no back panel or top. The gallery (`props-gallery-10-sheet06`) and the Meeting lounge (`props-gallery-29c-meeting-lounge-close-low-o500.jpg`) show crayon or brick blocks, the most saturated thing in frame, competing with the cable (DR-53). The R7 cues are missing: 10–14 thin spines of varied height, one leaning, one gap, desaturated colours. The colour wrap formula itself is fixed; no undefined colours appear (re-check item).

*observatory-models* — **Bookshelves are tinted the room's accent purple and filled with uniform, fully saturated candy-block books.** The bookshelf board colour comes from the level's clutter colours ('#4a4380', '#9b7bf0' and so on, observatory.ts:21; shelf recipe clutter.ts:42 → color:pick(r,c)), so shelves are violet. Every book is the same box(.14,.34,d*.7) in saturated primaries (prefabs.ts:123-125), so the shelves read as rows of red, blue, green and yellow candy blocks, not star atlases (shots 31, 30, 02). That breaks DR-51: books are desaturated, and a level may tint accents but never the family. They are also the most saturated objects in the room, which competes with the job items. The colour-wrap fix (books cycling correctly) still holds: no wrap artefact was seen.

*qfn-models* — **Bookshelf prefab (3 here) is an open frame of fat rounded 'candy-bar' books with no back or sides, mint shelves, and is off-theme in a fab bay.** The bookshelf prefab (prefabs.ts:123-125) is:
- 4 METAL posts;
- 3 coloured shelf boards;
- 7 identical box(.14,.34,d*.7) 'books' per shelf in full saturated CHAIRC colours.

It has no back panel, no side panels and no variation in height or width. Through the kit's rounding, the books read as soap or candy bars (qfn-models-65-bookshelf-mid, -66 at o700, -10, -24).

Because the frame is open, the books show through from both sides, so free-standing in mid-floor (it sits at (−3.62, 3.88) on the spawn side) it reads as a crayon display. The 'shelf' recipe colours the boards from the level palette, giving mint #7fe6c6 boards (DR-51 'no teal shelves').

It is also the most saturated, busiest object in several frames (qfn-models-04-orbit180, -65), so it competes with the job crate (DR-69). Research-art flagged the same prefab (`prefabs.ts:123-125`, 'teal shelf' in research-art-24-qfn-close), and it is still open.

### R5-340

**R5-340 | P2 | arcade | model-detail | Arcade: the serviced cabinet's ribbon cable stops in mid-air on the bench as a loose purple stub, short of the board**

Found by: `arcade-models#13` (P2 model-detail), `arcade-play#20` (P2 visual-bug). Batch: R-arcade (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*arcade-models* — **The serviced cabinet's ribbon cable stops in mid-air on the bench as a loose purple stub that reads as a pen, never reaching the channel board.** station.ts:222-223 builds the ribbon cable as a TubeGeometry from local (.35,.9,-.2) to (1.8,1.05,.5) in the cabinet group, which sits at (-2.95,0,-2.8) with ry .38. Its end is at about world (-1.09, 1.05, -3.0), lying on the bench top 1.1 m from the channel board (board centre at about (-0.08,1.08,-2.29)), and it ends in an open tube. In every bench-view shot (-36…-42, -78) a lilac 'crayon' lies on the bench behind the bins, connected to nothing (crop -36b). The station's premise is 'the broken cabinet's LED channel is opened up on the bench' (station.ts:1-3). The one physical link that shows the board IS the cabinet's circuit is broken, which hurts teaching (the player doesn't see that the board is inside the machine) and is a visible modelling error at the most-viewed camera.

*arcade-play* — **The serviced cabinet's ribbon cable ends on the bench top short of the board, so the link between cabinet and channel board isn't shown.** The GRAPE tube from the serviced cabinet (station.ts:222-223) ends at cabinet-local (1.8,1.05,0.5). In world space that is about (−1.09,1.05,−3.0), behind the bins and about 0.5 m from the board's SUPPLY terminal at about (−0.98,−2.49).

Compute the end point in world space as this.top.localToWorld(BOARD.x+SUPX-.1, .06, BOARD.z) and convert it into cabinet-local with c.worldToLocal. Use 5 control points: rising out of the cabinet back, a sag to y .99 on the bench top, then onto the board. Model it as a flat ribbon (ExtrudeGeometry of a .08×.01 rect along the curve, or a scaled tube with scale.z=.2) in GRAPE with 3 thin coloured stripe tubes. When live, run Lunch-style `Pulses` along it (current flowing), which also gives the room a visible cable (DR-05/DR-46).

### R5-341

**R5-341 | P2 | lunch | model-detail | Wedge and cable bridge are unbevelled knife-edge extrusions with no ink outline and no functional cues**

Found by: `gap5-toon-pipeline#2` (P2 model-detail), `props-gallery#12` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*gap5-toon-pipeline* — **Wedge and bridge are unbevelled knife-edge extrusions with no ink outline, and the wedge is the first job item in Lunch.** The doorstop wedge (prefabs.ts, case 'wedge': ExtrudeGeometry with bevelEnabled:false) and the leak bridge (case 'bridge': same) are the only unbevelled prop bodies. My geometry audit flags both as UNBEVELLED (wedge 0.80×0.35×0.50, bridge 1.80×0.20×1.00). At zoom 9 the wedge reads as a flat yellow sheet ending in a razor tip. Its silhouette has almost no dark outline. Only the vertical back face and the rubber ribs are inked. The cause is that ExtrudeGeometry is non-indexed with flat per-face normals, so OutlineEffect's inverted hull splits at every hard edge and leaves gaps along the slope and tip. The wedge is the target of Lunch step 1 ('Wedge the kitchen door open…'), so the first item the player is asked to grab is the one with no outline and no form. It also breaks the 'chunky and soft' style. RESEARCH_ART R5.2 already prescribed the fix, but it was never built.

*props-gallery* — **Cable bridge and doorstop wedge are sharp, bare yellow extrusions with no functional cues.** Both are job items in Lunch Rush, built with `ExtrudeGeometry({bevelEnabled:false})` (prefabs.ts:143-145 and :177-182). This is the known R5.2 / DR-58 break, still open.

The **bridge** is a 1.8×1.0 m flat-shaded yellow trapezoid with a black top strip (`props-gallery-10-sheet08`). It has no cable channels on its underside or ends, no ramp ribs and no hazard stripes. Nothing says "cables pass under me safely", which is the concept it stands in for (the water short in Lunch, DR-33/DR-37). Its 24-triangle mesh renders as hard flat facets, unlike every other rounded prop.

The **wedge** ribs are fine, but its edges are razor sharp and it lacks the ink stripes of the job-item language (DR-45) (`props-gallery-32-pip-scale-handhelds.jpg`).

**Evidence.**

- `src/props/prefabs.ts:136-137` (bridge, bevelEnabled:false)
- `src/props/prefabs.ts:163-167` (wedge, bevelEnabled:false)
- [toon-pipeline-11-lunch-wedge-bridge-zoom9.jpg](shots/toon-pipeline-11-lunch-wedge-bridge-zoom9.jpg)
- [toon-pipeline-11b-crop-wedge.jpg](shots/toon-pipeline-11b-crop-wedge.jpg)
- [toon-pipeline-12-lunch-wedge-orbit-zoom9.jpg](shots/toon-pipeline-12-lunch-wedge-orbit-zoom9.jpg)
- `mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/scale.json` (wedge, bridge: UNBEVELLED extrude)
- `src/props/prefabs.ts:144` (bridge), :178 (wedge): bevelEnabled:false
- [verify-gap5-toon-pipeline-01-lunch-wedge-orbit-left.jpg](shots/verify-gap5-toon-pipeline-01-lunch-wedge-orbit-left.jpg) (wedge near (530,580): no ink silhouette, yellow on wood)
- `src/props/prefabs.ts:143-145`
- `src/props/prefabs.ts:177-182`
- [props-gallery-10-sheet08-bridge-mop-tray.jpg](shots/props-gallery-10-sheet08-bridge-mop-tray.jpg)
- [props-gallery-10-sheet11-plug-wedge-beanbag.jpg](shots/props-gallery-10-sheet11-plug-wedge-beanbag.jpg)
- [props-gallery-32-pip-scale-handhelds.jpg](shots/props-gallery-32-pip-scale-handhelds.jpg)
- [props-gallery-52b-lunch-survey.jpg](shots/props-gallery-52b-lunch-survey.jpg)

**Fix.**

*From gap5-toon-pipeline:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Don't use mergeVertices + computeVertexNormals across the whole extrude. ExtrudeGeometry caps are triangulated only from outline vertices, so smoothed border normals would tilt the shading of the entire flat face. Instead, enable the bevel (bevelThickness/bevelSize .02–.03, bevelSegments 2–3) and run BufferGeometryUtils.toCreasedNormals(geo, Math.PI/4 or so). Bevel faces then shade smoothly while cap and slope faces stay flat. Also consider a darker wedge colour or a contrasting stripe, since #ffc94d on the Lunch wood floor is low contrast.

Reviewer's fix: In both kindGeometry builders, use {depth:d-.04, bevelEnabled:true, bevelThickness:.02, bevelSize:.02, bevelSegments:2} and inset the shape by .02. Then call e=mergeVertices(e) (BufferGeometryUtils) followed by e.computeVertexNormals() so normals are smooth across the bevels and the outline hull stays closed. Round the wedge tip: start the shape at (−w/2, .025) instead of a zero-height point.

*From props-gallery:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** With ExtrudeGeometry the bevel grows the shape outward by bevelSize, and grows the depth by bevelThickness on both caps. To keep the collider size, inset the shape by bevelSize (.02) and also set `depth: d - 2*bevelThickness` (d−.04). Then translate z by −(d−.04)/2 −.02 rather than −d/2.

Reviewer's fix: **Both:** set `bevelEnabled:true, bevelSize:.02, bevelThickness:.02, bevelSegments:2` and shrink the shape by .02 so the size is kept.

**Bridge:**
- 3 INK channel grooves: dark `box(.1,.06,d*1.01)` set into the underside at x −.4, 0, .4, visible at both ends as arch cut-outs (`decal` of three dark semicircles on each end face);
- 5 rib strips across each slope;
- swap the black top strip for a `stripes('#ffc629','#2b2d42')` decal band.

**Wedge:** a `stripes()` decal on the tall back face.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *gap5-toon-pipeline:* Re-run node mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/scale.mjs: no UNBEVELLED entries. Retake toon-pipeline-11/12 at zoom 9: the wedge should show a continuous ink silhouette and a lit chamfer on the slope edge.
- *props-gallery:* Run `shoot.mjs` with `only=bridge,wedge` at yaw -.5 and 2.64, and retake the Lunch survey `props-gallery-52b`. The bridge's channels read at zoom 9, and lit chamfers show on every edge.

**Rules:** AGENTS 9, DR-33, DR-37, DR-45, DR-56, DR-58, DR-62

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Both builders use ExtrudeGeometry with bevelEnabled:false. The cited line numbers are wrong: the bridge is at src/props/prefabs.ts:144 and the wedge at :178, not 136-137/163-167. The visual symptom is real. (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

### R5-343

**R5-343 | P2 | lunch, global | model-detail | Capacitor cart, power strip and reel lack the electrical cues that make them read as what they teach (cart reads as paint cans, no inlet)**

Found by: `lunch-models#15` (P2 model-detail), `props-gallery#15` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*lunch-models* — **Capacitor cart reads as paint cans next to a black box, and has no visible inlet socket for the lead the player must plug into it.** The capacitor cart is the 'aha' object of the room: the lift's feed plugs into it, and it supplies the start-up kick. Its model is four plain blue cylinders with grey caps on a cart deck, plus an INK rbox (.36 × .5 × .85) with a thin green light strip. In lunch-models-90 and -91 (storeroom lit) the cylinders read as paint or chemical drums, and the ink block reads as a dark hole, because its 0.85 × 0.5 m face is untrimmed. Nothing says 'capacitor': no sleeve stripe with − marks, no top vent cross and no terminals. The model has no socket plate either. The inlet port 'cap' is just a floating cyan ring at the cart's position + 0.75 m (lunch-runtime.ts:54), so the player plugs a cable into thin air on the deck. Every other inlet (oven, fridge, post, winch, conveyor motor) has a socketPlate().

*props-gallery* — **Capacitor cart, power strip and reel lack the electrical cues that make them read as what they teach.** Three props that carry the taught concepts are generic.

**capcart** (prefabs.ts:169-172): four plain blue cylinders with grey caps plus an INK box. They read as paint tins or gas bottles (`props-gallery-10-sheet10`). Real electrolytic capacitors show a sleeve with a minus stripe and +/− terminals on top. That is the one visual hint that these store charge and that polarity matters.

**strip** (prefabs.ts:138): the Meeting power strip is an orange bar with 4 sockets and a red switch, but no lead or plug tail. Its 5 A breaker, the load-budget concept, has no visible reset button or rating label, only the red cylinder.

**reel** (prefabs.ts:100 / kit.ts:115-119): a plain white drum with no wound-cable texture and no plug parked on the flange, so it reads as an empty spool.

Per DR-47 the state should be shown on the device itself, and per DR-62 each device needs ≥ 2–4 cues.

### R5-349

**R5-349 | P2 | global | model-detail | Sprint makes the feet skate about 50% and the steps get slower than walking; slow hauling also slides**

Found by: `characters#2` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The rig ties step phase to distance so that planted feet don't skate (pipRig.ts:49-52), but the stride formula only matches at normal walking speed. From the code's own numbers (leg about 0.56–0.59 m, swingAmp = .32 + .26·amount + .12·run, cycle = 4·.56·sin(swingAmp)·(1 + run·1.1)):
- Walk, 4.2 m/s: 6.8 steps/s, step 0.61 m, foot travels back 0.65 m per stance. Matched.
- Sprint, 6.8 m/s (Shift): the ×2.1 'flight' factor makes each step 1.52 m, but a leg swinging ±0.70 rad only sweeps 0.76 m. There is no real flight phase: runBob is ±3.5 cm and the feet stay down. So every planted foot slides forward about 0.76 m (50%). The cadence also drops from 6.8 to 4.5 steps/s at the moment the player presses sprint.
- Slow movement, about 2 m/s (heavy carry, thick cable at 0.65×, rope pull): the hip angle is scaled by `amount` (line 68) but the cycle length isn't. About 46% slip.

Sprinting is the slingshot verb (overstretch, then Q) and the chaos route in Meeting. Pip gliding with slower legs reads as ice-skating, not a frantic dash. The sprint strip (characters-32, real time) shows long, slow scissor poses with both boots near the floor. The earlier gait work (tools/gallery/gait.*) only validated walking.

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/pipRig.ts:51` (swingAmp, cycle with *(1+run*1.1))
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:52` (phase += dt*spd*2π/cycle)
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:58-59` (runBob only ±.035; no airborne flight)
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:68` (hip uses swingAmp*amount, cycle uses unscaled swingAmp)
- `src/game.ts:318` (sprint 6.8 vs walk 4.2; carry and thick-cable slowdowns)
- [characters-32-sprint-side-strip.jpg](shots/characters-32-sprint-side-strip.jpg)
- [characters-31-walk-side-strip.jpg](shots/characters-31-walk-side-strip.jpg)
- computed: walk 6.8 steps/s slip -5%; sprint 4.5 steps/s slip +50%; 2 m/s slip +46%
- `src/render/pipRig.ts:51-52,56-58,68`
- `src/game.ts:318` (speed 6.8 sprint / 4.2 walk; carry and thick-cable divisors)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Dropping the (1+run*1.1) term and using the amplitude actually applied (swingAmp*amount) is right for sprinting. Applied as written at low speed, it gives cycle≈0.5 m at 2 m/s, which is about 8 steps/s of tiny scurrying steps. Scale the amplitude more gently so stride and cadence share the speed change, for example `amp=swingAmp*Math.sqrt(amount)` used for both the hip (line 68) and the cycle. Keep Math.max(.4,cycle) and the cap Math.min(cycle,1.6).

Reviewer's fix: In pipRig.ts: compute the cycle from the amplitude actually used, `const amp=swingAmp*amount; cycle=4*.56*Math.sin(Math.max(.15,amp))` with no `(1+run*1.1)` term. Then let the cadence rise with speed (for example, cap the stride at 0.8 m per step and let frequency take the rest: `cycle=Math.min(cycle,1.6)`), so the sprint becomes about 8.5 steps/s with a bigger forward lean (already +.16) and a longer arm pump. If a flight phase is wanted, raise the body by `run*.08*Math.abs(sin)` and lift both knees during the flight half, so the 'extra' distance happens in the air. Keep walking as it is.

**Verify.**

- Add a tools/debug/gait-slip.mjs (or extend tools/debug/gait.mjs) that steps the rig at 60 Hz for v = 2, 4.2, 6.8 and records the world x of the lower boot while it is in contact. Slip must be under 10% of step length at every speed, and sprint cadence must be at least walk cadence. Retake characters-32 with rt.mjs (s4.mjs).

**Rules:** —

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Reran the numbers from src/render/pipRig.ts:48-52,68. Walk at 4.2 m/s (amount 1, run 0): swingAmp .58, cycle 1.23 m, 6.8 steps/s, 0.61 m step against a 0.64 m stance sweep, so it matches. Sprint at 6.8 m/s (run 1): swingAmp .70, cycle 3.03 m including the ×2.1 term, 4.5 steps/s, 1.52 m step against about 0.75 m of sweep, so about 50% slip with no airborne phase (runBob ±.035, line 56).

### R5-351

**R5-351 | P2 | global | model-detail | Big rounded boxes are bevelled at 2.5–4.4% of their size (2 cm cap), so cabinets, vending, printers and crates read as sharp slabs**

Found by: `gap5-toon-pipeline#3` (P2 model-detail). Batch: B8 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

rbox() (kit.ts:17) caps the top and bottom edge bevel at Math.min(.02, h*.2, w*.15, d*.15), and box() (kit.ts:26) caps its radius at .025. DR-58 asks for ≥6% of the smallest dimension. Measured on the makeProp() models (bevel ÷ smallest dimension): printer 2.0 cm / 0.75 m = 2.7%, vending 2.5%, supply cart 2.5%, cabinet 3.0%, crate 3.3%, coffee machine 3.6%, cooler 3.9%, coolbox 4.2%, sofa 4.4%, capcart 5.6%. The vertical corners do get the r argument, but the horizontal top edges, which catch the light from the high camera, stay at 2 cm. At zoom 9 the crate and cabinet tops show a thin hard line rather than a lit chamfer. Because the extrude normals are flat (non-indexed), the 3-segment bevel also renders faceted. These are the largest, most repeated props (the Meeting has a wall of 1.6 m cabinets), so they set the style.

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/kit.ts:15-23`
- `src/render/kit.ts:26`
- `mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/scale.json` (extrude-bevel entries)
- [toon-pipeline-13-playground-crates-zoom9.jpg](shots/toon-pipeline-13-playground-crates-zoom9.jpg)
- [toon-pipeline-15-meeting-gamecam.jpg](shots/toon-pipeline-15-meeting-gamecam.jpg)
- `src/render/kit.ts:17` and :25 (box is line 25, not 26)
- mockups/review5/RULES.md DR-58 'Check' (known fail on crates)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The bevel formula change is fine. Don't do 'mergeVertices and computeVertexNormals in rbox'. The extrude caps have only outline vertices, so smoothed normals at the cap border would tilt the whole top-face shading. ExtrudeGeometry is also non-indexed with UVs that differ per face, so mergeVertices won't merge without deleting uv first. Use BufferGeometryUtils.toCreasedNormals(g, ~0.6 rad) instead, which smooths across bevel segments and keeps the caps flat.

Reviewer's fix: kit.ts:17: bevel=Math.min(Math.max(.015, Math.min(w,h,d)*.07), .06, h*.3, w*.2, d*.2). kit.ts:26: radius Math.min(.06, m*.1), with segments 3. Then mergeVertices and computeVertexNormals in rbox so the bevel shades smoothly. Templates are cached by key, so the draw-call cost stays the same.

**Verify.**

- Re-run node mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/scale.mjs: no extrude-bevel or rbox entry below 6% where the smallest dimension is > 0.25 m. Retake toon-pipeline-13 at zoom 9: crate and cabinet top edges should show a lit chamfer band of at least 3 px.

**Rules:** DR-58

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — kit.ts:17 caps the top/bottom bevel at Math.min(.02, h*.2, w*.15, d*.15). kit.ts:25 (box) caps the radius at Math.min(.025, m*.2). Crate: rbox(.7,.6,.7,.04), top bevel 2 cm = 3.3% of 0.6 m, below DR-58's 6%. RULES.md DR-58 already lists the 2.5 cm cap as a known fail on crates, so this isn't new, but it is unfixed.

The runtime swap `x.hot.material=on?hot(...):toon(...)` (meeting-strip.ts:91) then acts on a detached mesh. The 'on' state shows only through the additive halo sprite, not a lit grille or base (compare -28 off and -41/-42 on: the heater changes only under the halo). **Fix.**

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Code-verified. Both hotParts are meshes in groups under game.decorRoot (meeting-strip.ts:34,38,44). freeze(decorRoot) at game.ts:105 merges and removes them (kit.ts:83), so the swap `x.hot.material=…` (meeting-strip.ts:91) acts on detached meshes, and the grille and base never light on their own. ### R5-359

**R5-359 | P2 | observatory | model-detail | Motor reads as a red cable reel, not a noisy motor**

buildMotor (station.ts:167-169) is a red cylinder of r .2 × .42 with two ink end discs of r .21 and four cream fan blades outside one end, on a grey plate. ### R5-360

**R5-360 | P2 | playground | model-detail | The spool's remaining length can't be read at the game camera; the reel has no stand and sinks into its base**

Found by: `playground-models#11` (P2 model-detail). Batch: R-playground (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The spool was added so players can read the cable left (P4). But the anchor reel's axis runs along world z (cyl 'z'), and the default camera looks almost straight down −z (yaw 0.14). The player therefore sees the front flange disc face-on, and the white wound cable is hidden behind it except for a thin sliver above the rim. Start crop -56 and after-payout crop -55 differ only by that sliver, about 40 px of reel at default zoom.
The model is also unfinished:
- The flanges (r .336, centre y .35, so the bottom is at y .014) sink about 6.6 cm into the 0.06 m INK base plate (top at y .08).
- The drum and axle float with no A-frame or cradle holding them.
- There is no crank or cable guide where the lead leaves.
As the 'star' prop next to spawn, it reads as a yellow cotton reel on a tile.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:90-91` (anchor group at y .35; flanges cyl(.336,.336,.056,24,'z'); base box(.5,.06,.5) at y -.3)
- `src/game.ts:292` (spool scale)
- `src/game.ts:58` (yaw=.14 default)
- [playground-models-56-crop-spool-start.jpg](shots/playground-models-56-crop-spool-start.jpg)
- [playground-models-55-crop-spool-after.jpg](shots/playground-models-55-crop-spool-after.jpg)
- [playground-models-12-close-reel-back.jpg](shots/playground-models-12-close-reel-back.jpg)
- [verify-playground-models-12-hold-plug-side.jpg](shots/verify-playground-models-12-hold-plug-side.jpg) (reel side view: no stand, flange on the plate)
- [verify-playground-models-07-crop-start-plug.jpg](shots/verify-playground-models-07-crop-start-plug.jpg)

**Fix.**

Turn the anchor group 90° (group.rotation.y=Math.PI/2) so the drum's side faces the default camera and the winding thickness reads directly. Raise the axle to y .44 so the flanges clear the plate. Add two A-frame legs per side (box(.05,.5,.05) ±0.3 rad), joined at the axle hubs, on a rounded base rbox(.7,.05,.5,.03). Add a crank handle (cyl + knob) on one hub and a cable guide ring (Torus .06) where the lead exits. Optional: paint 3 bands on the drum (green, yellow, red) that the winding covers in turn, so 'nearly empty' reads as red.

**Verify.**

- Crop the reel at the default camera at start and after walking to (5.8,-5.5) (d.mjs). The visible winding thickness differs by at least 10 px at 1440×900. In a zoom-9 orbit, no flange intersects the base.

**Rules:** DR-46, DR-62, DR-70

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — In game.ts:90-91 the anchor group sits at y .35, the flanges are cyl r .336 along z (bottom at y .014), and the INK base box(.5,.06,.5) is at local y -.3 (world .02-.08). The flanges therefore sink about 6.6 cm into the plate, with no frame, crank or guide. The default yaw .14 looks along −z at the flange face.

### R5-361

**R5-361 | P2 | playground | model-detail | The cable is a 20 cm fire hose as thick as the plug, and pale when slack**

Found by: `playground-models#14` (P2 model-detail). Batch: R-playground (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

hoseGeometry radius .1 makes the cable 20 cm across, roughly the plug's own diameter (coupler cyl r .11–.13). A real lead is about 1 cm (DR-59 allows 1.2–1.5× for gameplay, and 'chunky' toon style allows more), but at 20 cm:
- the plug doesn't read as a plug head on a lead;
- the reel would hold barely 1 m of it;
- the cable swallows Pip's forearm when held;
- it reads as a vacuum hose or pool noodle at zoom 9 (shots -41, -44).
When slack (strain ≈ 0) it is cream-white, at luma 219 on a 206-luma floor (13 luma of contrast). The outline does all the separation, and the most important object in the room is the least saturated thing near Pip until it is strained.

**Evidence.**

- `src/game.ts:304` (hoseGeometry radius .1)
- `src/props/prefabs.ts:101-102` (coupler r .11/.13)
- `src/render/actors.ts:78` (hoseMaterial white, vertex-coloured by strain)
- [playground-models-41-hold-plug-close-side.jpg](shots/playground-models-41-hold-plug-close-side.jpg) (cable 219 vs floor 206 luma)
- [playground-models-44-drag-at-socket-close.jpg](shots/playground-models-44-drag-at-socket-close.jpg)
- [playground-models-42-drag-mid.jpg](shots/playground-models-42-drag-mid.jpg)
- [verify-playground-models-12-hold-plug-side.jpg](shots/verify-playground-models-12-hold-plug-side.jpg) (cable 227 vs floor 203 luma)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Don't jump straight to .055. At zoom 38 a 5.5 cm cable may drop under DR-59's 8 px minimum and lose its role as the room's main object (AGENTS: the cable is the star). Try .07–.075, check the width in px at zoom 38 and zoom 9, and keep the tracer-stripe idea for slack contrast.

Reviewer's fix: Set the hose radius to .055 (game.ts:304) and the Pulses capsule radius to .055 (actors.ts:82). Give the coupler a strain-relief collar cyl(.07,.09,.08) where the lead enters, so the plug stays clearly bigger than the cord. Keep strain white per AGENTS 4, but darken the rest tone to '#e9e2d0' and add a thin ink 'tracer' stripe along the cable (a second vertex-colour band), so a slack cable reads on pale floors. That also helps once the floor value drops (DR-54).

**Verify.**

- Retake playground-models-41 and -44. Cable diameter is under 60% of the plug head's diameter, and at strain 0 the cable/floor luma difference is ≥ 25 in a crop.

**Rules:** AGENTS 4, DR-46, DR-53, DR-54, DR-59

**Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE — In code, game.ts:304 sets the hose radius to .1 (20 cm diameter), close to the coupler's r .11-.13 (prefabs.ts:102). My side view shows the hose about as thick as Pip's forearm and plug. The luma claim is weaker than stated: I measured slack cable 227 against floor 203 (24 luma), not 13. Whether 20 cm is 'too thick' is a style judgment: the cable is the hero object and must read at zoom 38.

### R5-363

**R5-363 | P2 | qfn | model-detail | The three signature fab machines don't read as fab machines: the pick-and-place looks like a yellow gate over a table, the reflow oven like a lavender sideboard, the AOI like a photocopier**

Found by: `qfn-models#0` (P2 model-detail). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The Fabrication Bay's identity rests on three back-wall fixtures, and none of them passes the squint test (DR-61). Each also misses the detail floor of at least 6 cues per fixture (DR-62).

(1) **Pick-and-place, room.ts:29-34.**
- It is a cream rbox 2.8×0.9×1.7 with a periwinkle lip and a green bed carrying three miniBoards.
- Two flat yellow side posts (rbox .16×.9×1.5) and a yellow Y-beam sit over it, with a white 30 cm cube 'head' on a 2 cm nozzle.
- The glass hood is a 2.7×0.95×1.55 rbox at opacity .2 with no frame, so it is effectively invisible.
- The seven feeder reels hang off the front face with no feeder bank or slots.
- At the game camera (qfn-models-01-start, -05-orbit270) the strongest shape is the overhead crane in front of it: a yellow arch with black hazard dashes. The PnP reads as 'a table under a yellow doorway'. From behind (qfn-models-76) it reads as a yellow-framed tray.

(2) **Reflow oven, room.ts:40-44.**
- It is a 4.2×1.05×1.15 periwinkle slab with a darker lip.
- Four 0.7×0.26 orange windows stand only 5 mm proud (z −6.31 against a front face at −6.325).
- A blank white 0.5×0.3 tab stands on the top front edge, and a dark tray at each end holds a miniBoard.
- In qfn-models-13, -67 and -68 it reads as a kitchen counter or reception sideboard. There is no tunnel mouth, no visible belt, no heat-zone segmentation, no exhaust stacks or vents, and no controller screen. Its 4.4 m² front face carries only four small rectangles, which breaks DR-62's 0.5 m² flat-face rule.

(3) **AOI box, room.ts:46-48.**
- It is a cream rbox 1.5×1.3×1.1 with a lavender top box and a pale glass strip.
- A bare monitor sits sunk into the top (see the overlap finding).
- In qfn-models-15, -16 and -82 it reads as a photocopier or fridge. There is no camera head, no inspection light ring, no board inside, and no stack light.

All three have plain cream or lavender backs and sides (DR-63) and big blank faces. For the player, the room never says 'factory that makes boards', so the bench puzzle's payoff (boards going into production) has no visual home. R4A already noted that after the crate the room contributes nothing.

**Evidence.**

**Fix.**

In src/stations/qfn/room.ts, split each machine into its own builder: pickAndPlace(), reflowOven(), aoiStation().

**Pick-and-place:**
- Give the hood a toon INK frame: 4 vertical rbox .05 posts plus a top rim of rbox .05 bars around 2.7×1.55. Keep the glass panes at opacity .25.
- Add a feeder bank: a dark DMETAL rbox 2.6×.35×.25 at local z .95, y .55, with 7 slot dividers (box .02×.3×.25). Seat the reels in the slots at z 1.0 so they no longer sink into the body.
- Add a conveyor rail through the machine at y .95: two DMETAL rails box 3.4×.04×.04 at z ±.25, sticking out .3 m each end.
- Add a stack light on the right post: 3 stacked cylinders r .05, green/amber/red (hot), with green lit.
- Add a 0.35×0.25 HMI screen on a short arm at the front-right corner (MeshBasic TX.screen('chart')).
- Make the head a rounded 2-tone carriage, rbox .3×.2×.3 plus a nozzle cluster of 3 cylinders.

**Reflow oven:**
- Model a tunnel: 4 zones as separate rbox 1.0×1.05×1.15 blocks with 2 cm INK gaps between them, so it reads as a segmented tunnel.
- Add a visible mesh belt: a DMETAL box 5.2×.03×.6 at y .82 running through the open mouths at both ends. Add the mouths as INK insets box .02×.3×.65 on each end face.
- Add 2 exhaust stacks: cylinders r .1, h .5 on top.
- Replace the white tab with a framed controller screen: rbox .5×.3×.08 INK frame plus a MeshBasic canvas showing a temperature-profile curve.
- Make the windows inset 1 cm with a frame: box .74×.3×.03 INK, then the hot pane at +.02.

**AOI:**
- Add a camera gantry inside the glass: a box .9×.05×.05 bar with a cylinder r .06 camera and a hot ring-light torus r .08.
- Put a green miniBoard on the internal bed so it shows through the window.
- Add a 3-lamp stack light and a keyboard shelf (rbox .6×.03×.25 at y .95 on the front).

On every machine, add a back panel with vent slats (6 thin INK boxes) and a mains cable stub to the wall, so 180° orbits read finished.

**Verify.**

- Retake qfn-models-01-start, -10-pnp, -13-oven, -15-aoi, -76-pnp-front-bookshelf with the same capture scripts (mockups/review5/tools/qfn-models/s1.mjs, s2.mjs, s6.mjs). A first-look viewer should name 'pick-and-place / reflow oven / inspection machine' from the norim start shot (s6.mjs -70). Count cues per fixture: at least 6 each.

**Rules:** DR-61, DR-62, DR-63

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — I checked the geometry at room.ts:29-48 and it matches the finding: the hood is at opacity .2 with no frame, the oven is a periwinkle slab with four small windows and a white tab, and the AOI is a cream box with a lavender top box and a bare monitor. In the screenshots (qfn-models-13, -15, -82, my verify-qfn-models-02-survey) the oven reads as a sideboard and the AOI as a copier. Two parts are overstated.
