### R5-365

**R5-365 | P2 | qfn | model-detail | Bench part models: locked connector end caps are plain job yellow (the code comment says striped), and in the layer-2 x-ray the pin tags float at full opacity over a 28% chip**

Found by: `qfn-models#21` (P2 model-detail). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The bench's part models are mostly good:
- the dark QFN body with a printed name, pin-1 dot and coloured pin tags;
- SMD pads in net colours;
- 2-pin parts with net-coloured end caps;
- through-hole ring pads with drill holes;
- connector shrouds with a mouth chevron;
- the hot-chip colour lerp and glow (qfn-models-47) read clearly.

Two polish issues:

(1) **Locked connector end caps** (station.ts:166) use toon(p.locked ? '#ffc629' : '#3a3d55'), and the comment says '(striped when the enclosure fixes it)'. No stripes are drawn, so J1 and J2 on board 3 have flat job-yellow caps (qfn-models-81-crop-board3-parts). The 'fixed by enclosure' meaning isn't shown, and the colour borrows the job-item language.

(2) **Layer-2 x-ray:** with layer 2 active, the QFN body drops to opacity .28 and its top text to .3 (station.ts:213-214), but the pin tags (renderOrder 2 plates) stay at full opacity. They hover over a ghost chip (qfn-models-48, -81).

Also, the QFN body is a featureless slab from the side: there are no leads or solder fillet hints, which R4A noted as a teaching gap ('nothing about the QFN package itself').

**Evidence.**

- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:149-156` (QFN body/tags)
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:166` (locked cap colour)
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:212-214` (x-ray opacity)
- [qfn-models-47-board3-hot-chip.jpg](shots/qfn-models-47-board3-hot-chip.jpg)
- [qfn-models-48-board3-layer2-xray.jpg](shots/qfn-models-48-board3-layer2-xray.jpg)
- [qfn-models-81-crop-board3-parts.jpg](shots/qfn-models-81-crop-board3-parts.jpg)
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:216-217` (actual x-ray opacity lines)

**Fix.**

**Locked caps:** give them a canvas texture with INK diagonal stripes on a PERI or grey base, plus a small padlock glyph on the top plate. Using the striped language for 'fixed' is fine if the base isn't job yellow.

**X-ray tags:** when the body becomes see-through, set each pin tag's material opacity to .45 (station.ts:212-214). Alternatively, lift the tags to the pad edge outside the body.

**Package detail:** add 12 tiny metal lead tabs, box(.03,.012,.02) DMETAL, at the body edge over each perimeter pad, so the package reads as a QFN with leads under its edge.

**Verify.**

- Bench zoom crop on board 3 (s5.mjs, shots -47/-48/-49): the caps are striped and not yellow, the tags are faded in L2 view, and the lead tabs are visible.

**Rules:** DR-45, DR-62

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — station.ts:166 colours locked caps '#ffc629' and draws no stripes, even though the comment says 'striped'. qfn-models-81 shows plain yellow J1 and J2 caps. The x-ray code is at station.ts:216-217, not 212-214: it sets body opacity .28 and top .3 but leaves the pin tag plates (renderOrder 2, line 156) untouched. qfn-models-48 and -81 show full-opacity VIN, GND and ISET tags over the ghosted chip.

### R5-366

**R5-366 | P2 | qfn | model-detail | The parts crate is the generic shipping carton recoloured, is named 'crate' like every other box, and the grab cue lands on a junk box**

Found by: `qfn-models#4` (P2 model-detail). Batch: R-qfn (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The room's only job item is spec {kind:'box', id:'parts', color:'#ffc629'} (qfn.ts:6). It uses the same 0.7×0.6×0.7 carton builder as the other 34 boxes (prefabs.ts:56-61): tape strip, flap seam, white label. It has no stripes, no handles, no visible contents and no parts icon.

- **Silhouette:** at the game camera it is indistinguishable from the clutter cartons. Colour is the only cue, and that colour is shared (see the yellow finding).
- **Name:** NAMES maps every box to 'crate' (objectives.ts:57). - **After delivery:** the crate snaps onto the side table as the same closed box (qfn-models-35, -50). Nothing on the crate shows that the parts left it (DR-47). The parts just appear on the board.

This is the only physical act in the job, and the model gives it no character. Good Job's job items read at a glance by their shape.

- `src/levels/qfn.ts:6`
- `src/props/prefabs.ts:56-61` (box builder)
- `src/ui/objectives.ts:57` (NAMES box:'crate')

- `src/ui/objectives.ts:83` (prompt text built from NAMES[kind])
- [qfn-models-74-stock-sign-edge.jpg](shots/qfn-models-74-stock-sign-edge.jpg) (tape square + marker on crate)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Drop the game.ts:192 grab-preference change, because it already exists (reach() at game.ts:193). Keep the tote prefab and the empty-after-delivery idea. For naming, have objectives.ts:83 use an id-aware name (spec.id==='parts' gives 'parts crate'), and rename the generic box to 'box'. Make sure the step text, prompt and result card all use the same noun.

Reviewer's fix: **New prefab** in src/props/prefabs.ts: add a kind 'tote' (size .75×.45×.55, mass 2) as an ESD parts tote.
- Open-top rbox shell: 4 walls of .03 thickness plus a floor, in #ffc629.
- Two INK ink-stripe bands (box w×.05×d+.01 at y ±.12) and recessed hand-holds (INK rbox .16×.05×.02 on both short ends).
- Contents visible from above: 3 mini tape reels (kit.reel s .25, flanges PERI and white), a green miniBoard stack and 2 ESD-pink bags (rbox .2×.04×.15 '#f5a3c0').
- A front label with a chip glyph decal.

**Level and names:**
- Use it for {kind:'tote', id:'parts'} in qfn.ts:6.
- Add NAMES tote:'parts tote', or name it from spec.id: 'parts crate' for id 'parts'. Keep box:'box' so junk never says 'crate'.

**Delivery** (station.ts:379-384): hide the contents meshes (or tween them down into the tote), so the empty tote shows the parts have moved to the board.

**Grab preference** (game.ts:192): when the current step's at() is an id'd item within 0.4 m of the nearest junk reach, prefer it (DR-18).

**Verify.**

- Retake qfn-models-20-stock and -71 from (−7.6, 3.8): the prompt reads 'Grab the parts crate' and the cue brackets are on the tote. Retake qfn-models-01-start: the tote is recognisable by shape with the colour desaturated (greyscale squint). Retake qfn-models-35: the tote is empty after delivery.

**Rules:** DR-17, DR-18, DR-45, DR-47, DR-50, DR-61

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Three parts hold up. The job item is the same carton builder recoloured (qfn.ts:6, prefabs.ts:56-61). NAMES maps every box to 'crate' (objectives.ts:57,83), so junk boxes also prompt 'Grab the crate' (DR-50). And dropped() just pins the same closed box on the side table (station.ts:379-384). The DR-18 part is refuted. game.ts:192-193 already prefers job items: reach() subtracts 2 m for anything with an id.

### R5-372

**R5-372 | P2 | global | art-style | The new rim light has no measurable effect and misses Pip, the cable and every coworker (glossyToon overwrites it; toon().clone() drops it)**

Found by: `gap5-toon-pipeline#1` (P2 art-style), `camera-render#14` (P2 art-style). Batch: B8 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

*gap5-toon-pipeline* — **The new rim light misses Pip, the cable and every coworker: glossyToon() overwrites it and toon().clone() silently drops it.** The cool rim (toon.ts:20-31, WIP in 3631876) is meant to 'separate props from pale floors'. It is installed only through toon()'s onBeforeCompile and customProgramCacheKey 'toonRim' (toon.ts:39). Two paths lose it. (1) glossyToon() (actors.ts:9-18) builds its own MeshToonMaterial with a different onBeforeCompile and never calls rimShader. So Pip's helmet, mitts and boots (game.ts:155), the cable hose (actors.ts:78), the garage robot and the lamp shades get no rim. (2) Material.clone() does not copy onBeforeCompile or customProgramCacheKey; I confirmed in-page that toon(c).clone().onBeforeCompile !== toon(c).onBeforeCompile. Every cloned toon therefore renders without the rim. That covers all coworker blobs (shared vertex-colour clone, actors.ts:60 and kit.ts:95), occluder walls and pillars (decor.ts:47, :55), plain decor (decor.ts:19), confetti (particles.ts:17), every QFN part (qfn/station.ts:42), spectrum walls (spectrum/room.ts:21) and the lunch reset buttons (lunch-runtime.ts:60). Census of toon materials with no rim per level: lobby 9, playground 11, meeting 47 (28 of them blob white), lunch 52, arcade 20, garage 9, qfn 168, observatory 9, spectrum 16, plus 18–29 glossy meshes per level. The result is the opposite of DR-43: background clutter gets the separating edge, while the three shapes that must stand out most (Pip, the cable and the coworkers who react to chaos) don't. Next to each other, rimmed and unrimmed objects of the same colour also shade differently.

*camera-render* — **The new rim light has no measurable effect: rim on and ?norim differ by 0.44 mean luma.** The rim term is `rimColor*edge*up*rimStrength*diffuseColor` with rimStrength 0.22, edge = smoothstep(.62,.92,1−N·V) and up = smoothstep(-.2,.6,N.y) (src/render/toon.ts:20-31). Comparing zoom-9 garage frames with and without ?norim: mean absolute luma difference 0.44/255, only 3,415 px differ by more than 10 (mostly animation), and Pip's median luma (180) and darkest 2% (54) are identical (camera-render-garage-64-zoom9-rim.jpg vs -norim.png).

The stated goal, separating props from pale floors (DR-54 asks for at least 25 luma), is not met. Meanwhile the rim forces one custom shader variant onto every toon material. Commit 3631876 marks it 'WIP, verifying'; this is the verification result.

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/toon.ts:20-45`
- `src/render/actors.ts:9-18`
- `src/render/actors.ts:60`
- `src/render/actors.ts:78`
- `src/render/kit.ts:95`
- `src/levels/decor.ts:19`
- `src/levels/decor.ts:47`
- `src/levels/decor.ts:55`
- `src/stations/qfn/station.ts:42`
- `src/render/particles.ts:17`
- `mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/materials.json` (types: 'toon(no rim/clone)' / 'glossyToon' per level)
- `mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/ramp.mjs` output cloneHasRim:false
- `mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap5-toon-pipeline/v1.mjs` output: clone.same=false, clone key 'onBeforeCompile() {}', glossySrc(rim)=false, census {rim:62, glossy:5, noRim:6 incl '#ffffff(vc)'}
- node_modules/three/src/materials/Material.js:1119-1199 (copy() omits onBeforeCompile/customProgramCacheKey)
- `src/game.ts:111` (fade wall/occluder toon(color).clone(), also rimless)
- `src/game.ts:155` (Pip hat/gloves/boots → glossyToon)
- `src/render/toon.ts:20-31`
- [camera-render-garage-64-zoom9-rim.jpg](shots/camera-render-garage-64-zoom9-rim.jpg)
- [camera-render-garage-64-zoom9-norim.jpg](shots/camera-render-garage-64-zoom9-norim.jpg)
- python diff: mean 0.432, >10: 2398 px
- `src/render/toon.ts:21-31`

**Fix.**

*From gap5-toon-pipeline:* **Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The fix works. One addition: the per-instance customProgramCacheKey in toonClone must stay 'toonRim' only if the injected shader is identical. For glossy, the key must include both rim and spec ('glossyToonRim'+spec+size), as proposed. Also respect noRim in glossyToon (skip rimShader when ?norim) so the comparison flag still works.

Reviewer's fix: Export rimShader from toon.ts. In glossyToon (actors.ts:12), call rimShader(s) first, then apply the spec replace, which chains on the same '#include &lt;opaque_fragment>' anchor (inject the rim before the spec mix), and make the cache key 'glossyToonRim'+spec+size. Add a helper in toon.ts, toonClone(m) => {const c=m.clone(); c.onBeforeCompile=m.onBeforeCompile; c.customProgramCacheKey=m.customProgramCacheKey; return c;}. Use it at actors.ts:60, kit.ts:95, decor.ts:19/47/55, particles.ts:17, qfn/station.ts:42, spectrum/room.ts:21 and lunch-runtime.ts:60. Big flat wall faces may stay rimless on purpose (DR-56 excludes them), but blobs, the cable and Pip must have it. Keep ?norim working.

*From camera-render:* Either drop the rim (delete rimShader and customProgramCacheKey) or make it do its job. To make it work:
- Set rimStrength to 0.55.
- Widen edge to smoothstep(.45,.85,…).
- Use `up` only to suppress downward faces: smoothstep(-.4,.2,N.y).
- Add the rim to the colour without multiplying by diffuseColor, so dark props also get a light edge.

Then check the rim at grazing silhouettes against pale floors.

*Merged entry:* apply one fix for the shared root cause and check it against every room and reviewer listed above; where reviewers proposed different fixes, prefer the verifier-corrected one, then the lead (first) reviewer's.

**Verify.**

- *gap5-toon-pipeline:* Re-run node mockups/review5/tools/toon-pipeline/materials.mjs. The 'toon(no rim/clone)' counts should drop to walls and plain decor only (no #ffffff blob entries, no QFN part colours), and glossy materials should report the rim cache key. Compare zoom-9 crops of Pip and a blob with and without ?norim: a cool edge should appear on Pip's helmet and the blob's top.
- *camera-render:* Diff ?norim against the default at the same zoom-9 garage view. The mean luma difference on prop silhouettes over the floor must be at least 8 (crop 1-px outline bands). Then check DR-54: props differ from the floor under them by at least 25 luma.

**Rules:** AGENTS 9, DR-43, DR-54, DR-56, DR-57

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — Reproduced in-page (mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap5-toon-pipeline/v1.mjs). toon(c).clone() has onBeforeCompile !== the original's, and its customProgramCacheKey falls back to the prototype default ('onBeforeCompile() {}') instead of 'toonRim'. Material.copy in three r186 (Material.js:1119-1199) copies userData but not onBeforeCompile. glossyToon's onBeforeCompile source contains no rim code (actors.ts:12-17). (2/2 merged findings CONFIRMED.)

**R5-373 | P2 | arcade | art-style | Lighting is over budget: 6 point lights at start (+1 on lightUp) and a neon glow sprite that grows to 8 m**

Found by: `arcade-models#19` (P2 art-style). Batch: R-arcade (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

A scene traverse (s2.mjs, scene.json) finds 6 PointLights at start: the bench lamp (0,2.7,-1.8, i 5); pink (-6.4,2.4,-5.4) and cyan (6.2,2.4,-5.4), both i 4; lilac (8.4,2.2,1.2) i 3.5; storeroom (-8.6,2.4,5.4) i 3; and the bench LED light (station.ts:172), which sits at 0 intensity until lit. lightUp() (room.ts:124) adds a 7th (i 8, distance 9). The neon glow sprite is 5 m at opacity .18 (room.ts:100) and lightUp adds an 8 m sprite at .3 (room.ts:124) over a 4.6 m sign, 1.7× its source, against the ≤1.5× rule. In the win frames (-73, -74) the back wall washes pink. Each extra point light also multiplies the toon shader cost on ~650 toon meshes.

Keep 3 room lights: the bench warm lamp, one pink at (-4,2.4,-5.4) with distance 8, and one cyan at (5,2.4,-3) with distance 8. Fold the lilac and storeroom lamps into lampPool decals plus emissive cabinet screens. Make the bench LED's PointLight the 4th and only dynamic light. Found by: `cable#8` (P2 art-style). Batch: B7 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

The hose's rest colour is #f5f1dc (src/render/actors.ts:65, STRAIN), and a dropped or slack cable is drawn at strain 0.3 (game.ts:294).

On the Playground concrete (#d8cdb8, decor.ts:84), PIL samples on cable-122 give:
- the lit top of the cable: luma 232, saturation 0.09;
- the floor next to it: luma 191–212, saturation 0.17;
- the cable's shaded side: luma 185, the same as the floor.

So for most of a run the cable is the least saturated object near Pip and reads mainly through its outline (cable-10, cable-40, cable-122/123). DR-53 says the cable should be the most saturated thing near Pip.

In Lunch, the yellow strain band (#ffd451) on the honey wood floor nearly disappears (cable-130). The thin leads (radius 0.075, #ece8dc) are pale hairlines at the game camera (cable-134; LR5 still partly open).

Strain reads well from orange up (cable-12, cable-21, cable-64), so this is polish for the rest and yellow states.

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/actors.ts:65`
- `src/game.ts:294`
- `src/levels/decor.ts:84`
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:139`

- `src/render/actors.ts:78`
- `src/lunch-runtime.ts:315` (bands only for rating>3)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Two parts of the fix are technically wrong. (1) glossyToon's `size` (actors.ts:9-12, hoseMaterial at actors.ts:78) is the specular-highlight edge (uniform specEdge), not the outline weight. Changing .982 to .975 only resizes the highlight. To thicken the hose outline, set the OutlineEffect parameters on the hose material (material.userData.outlineParameters={thickness:~0.006}), the same mechanism game.ts:95 uses to hide outlines. (2) Don't add ink bands to the thin Lunch leads. In Lunch, bands are the signifier of the thick 10 A cable (bands: cable.rating>3, lunch-runtime.ts:315), and striping thin leads would blur the rating lesson. Use the contact-shadow ribbon and the larger radius instead.

Reviewer's fix: Keep the white → yellow → orange → red ramp (AGENTS 4), but give the jacket an ink identity.

1. Pass `bands:true` with a thin stripe for the hero cable: a 0.05 m ink band every 0.6 m, using hoseGeometry's band code with a smaller duty cycle.
2. Raise the outline weight on the hose: the material `size` from 0.982 to about 0.975.
3. Add a soft contact-shadow decal under the hose: a dark ribbon 0.3 m wide at 20% opacity.
4. For Lunch, darken the yellow stop to #ffc21a, or outline-tint it on wood floors.
5. Raise thin-lead radius to 0.085, as the Good Job hose readability suggests.

In cable-123 the cream hose reads mostly through its dark outline and shading against the beige floor. In cable-130 the yellow thin lead on honey wood is low contrast but still readable up close.

### R5-375

**R5-375 | P2 | global | art-style | Pip's outline is thin and light: luma about 106, 1–2 px, even at zoom 9**

Found by: `characters#13` (P2 art-style). Batch: B10 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

Sampled across the helmet and arm edges in the zoom-9 front shot (Pip about 300 px tall), the outline pixel is rgb(101,104,135), luma 106, and only 1–2 px wide. DR-56 asks for ink of luma 70 or less at 2–3 px. At the game camera (characters-40b), Pip's silhouette against the blue-grey meeting carpet relies on the yellow helmet and ring, because the outline barely separates the blue overalls (luma 132, hue 195°) from the floor (luma 158). The same applies to the blobs, which share the outline pass. The concept's chunky toon look depends on a dark contour around the hero.

**Evidence.**

- `src/render/toon.ts:77` (outline defaultColor [.13,.135,.2], thickness .0036)

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** The colour values are wrong. The outline is not tone-mapped: [.13,.135,.2] linear shows as about (101,104,135), which is plain linear-to-sRGB. So [.07,.075,.12] would show as about rgb(74,77,97), luma about 78, which still fails. To reach the target rgb(52,54,76) (#34364c, luma ≤70), set defaultColor to about [.035,.037,.072] at src/render/toon.ts:77. Raising defaultThickness from .0036 to about .0055, with the hero override userData.outlineParameters={thickness:.007} on Pip's materials, is fine.

Reviewer's fix: In src/render/toon.ts:77, set the outline colour to [.07,.075,.12] (about #12131f in linear, which displays near rgb(52,54,76) after ACES and sRGB) and thickness .0055. Give Pip's materials their own `userData.outlineParameters={thickness:.007}` (set when traversing the GLB in game.ts:156), so the hero gets the heaviest line.

### R5-376

**R5-376 | P2 | global | art-style | Neither toon ramp shows 3 bands: a white sphere spans only 13–25 luma, and from the game camera the lit side uses only the top of the ramp**

Found by: `gap5-toon-pipeline#0` (P2 art-style). Batch: B8 (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

AGENTS 9 and DR-55 ask for a readable 3-step ramp. I measured it, and neither ramp gets close. I put a toon('#f4efe6') sphere (r 0.45 m) next to Pip at zoom 9 and sampled luma along its highest-contrast diameter. Default soft ramp: 13 luma range seen from the front (229→217), one plateau covering 93%. Seen from the side across the terminator: 25 range, 2 plateaus (65%/18%). ?hardcel: 18 range from the front, 1 plateau; 19 from the side, 2 plateaus (229/218, 46%/34%). ?hardcel&norim gives the same. Real props are just as flat. Crate faces measure top 172, front 155, side 152; the lobby cooler measures front 223, side 211, top 205 (soft) or 225/214 (hardcel). Three causes stack. (1) three.js samples the gradient at u = dotNL*0.5+0.5, so every surface facing the sun only reads the top half of the ramp. With the soft ramp (toon.ts:13: 92,96,120,168,196,226,246,255 with LinearFilter), that half is a smooth 196→255 gradient, not bands. With hardcel [90,185,255] it is 2 bands, and the dark band only appears where dotNL < −1/3. (2) The sun sits at (−11,21,13) (toon.ts:80), up and in front, on the camera's side, so the faces that would be in shadow point away from the camera at every default orbit. (3) Hemi 0.68–0.76 and ambient 0.12 (toon.ts:79, MOODS) lift the remaining shadow band, and ACES at exposure 1.02 crushes pale albedos into the shoulder. The comment at toon.ts:10-11 says the soft ramp gives 'three readable bands'. It does not: it is continuous shading. For the player, every pale prop reads as a flat cut-out with an outline and no form. Pip, the cooler, crates and white props merge with the pale floors (DR-54 asks props to sit ≥25 luma off the floor). The cel look the art direction promises never appears, with or without ?hardcel.

**Evidence.**

**Fix.**

**Verifier correction (takes precedence over the reviewer's fix where they differ):** Keep steps 1, 2 and 5. In the remap, mention that the fill/rim directional lights should either skip the ramp (add them as plain Lambert in RE_Direct, or lower them to about 0.2) or be removed in favour of hemi only. Otherwise three summed ramps still blur the bands. Moving the sun (step 4) also moves every shadow, so the change needs re-checking against DR-70/71 grounding shots and the shadow camera bounds (toon.ts:82).

Reviewer's fix: Make the ramp span the lit hemisphere and leave a visible terminator. (1) In toon() and glossyToon(), use onBeforeCompile to replace the toon gradient lookup (#include &lt;lights_toon_pars_fragment> / getGradientIrradiance) with coord = vec2(clamp(dotNL,0.,1.), 0.). The whole ramp then maps to the faces the camera sees. (2) Make the default a real 3-band ramp: bands [105,185,255] with NearestFilter, or the soft variant [105,105,185,185,255,255] with LinearFilter so only the edges blend. Bands then switch near dotNL 0.33 and 0.66. (3) Drop hemi from about .7 to .45 and ambient from .12 to .06 (toon.ts:79 and the MOODS hemi values) so the shadow band is about 45–55% of lit. (4) Move the key light further to the side, e.g. sun.position (−18,21,2), so the terminator crosses the camera-facing half of props. (5) Fix the comment at toon.ts:10-11. Either way the product owner must sign off on one ramp (DR-55).

Expect 3 plateaus each ≥15% of the diameter and ≥40 luma between the lit and shadow plateaus on the #f4efe6 sphere, at both the front and the side orbit. Also re-crop the playground crates: top, front and side faces should differ by ≥25 luma.

**Rules:** AGENTS 9, DR-43, DR-54, DR-55

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — The mechanism is confirmed in code. three r186 gradientmap_pars_fragment uses coord = dotNL*0.5+0.5 (node_modules/three/src/renderers/shaders/ShaderChunk/gradientmap_pars_fragment.glsl.js), so lit faces only sample texels 4–7 of the soft ramp (196,226,246,255) with LinearFilter (src/render/toon.ts:13-15), which is a continuous gradient rather than bands.

### R5-378

**R5-378 | P2 | spectrum | art-style | Brick texture squashed on narrow wall faces; wall caps and the STOREROOM sign stay opaque when the brick wall fades**

Found by: `spectrum-models#10` (P2 art-style). Batch: R-spectrum (section 5).

**What is wrong.**

(1) Each brick slab gets one cloned texture with repeat (len/1.3, 1.6) (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:62) applied to every face of a box(). The 0.3 m end faces and edge returns therefore get the same horizontal repeat as the full-length face. At the storeroom's corner returns and the lab side wall, bricks come out as thin vertical slivers (34 right edge, 14 left edge). (2) The brick slabs are faded occluders (slab() pushes them into game.occluders, room.ts:39-43). The cream cap box (:70), the brown pier caps (:69) and the 'STOREROOM' sign (:71) are separate meshes that never fade. When Pip walks behind the storeroom front wall, the faded bricks show a hard cream cap bar, two brown blocks and the sign floating at full opacity over him (33). DR-78 asks for no outline ghost and no popping in front of a half-faded mesh. (3) In 14 the same wall does not fade at all while it hides Pip's body from a camera over the storeroom; only his head shows above it.

**Evidence.**

- [spectrum-models-34-store-wooden-door-inside.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-34-store-wooden-door-inside.jpg)
- [spectrum-models-14-desk-back.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-14-desk-back.jpg)
- [spectrum-models-33-store-shelves.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-33-store-shelves.jpg)
- `src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:39-43`
- `src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:62`
- `src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:69-71`
- [spectrum-models-61-carry-mirror-zoom9-side.jpg](shots/spectrum-models-61-carry-mirror-zoom9-side.jpg) (lab side wall, room.ts:77, hides Pip's body unfaded)
- `src/game.ts:387-388` (single occlusion ray)

**Fix.**

(1) Build brick walls as a box with per-face UVs scaled to world size: after creating box(w,h,d), rewrite the uv attribute so each face's u = face width / 1.3 and v = face height / 1.3 (a small helper worldUV(geo) in src/render/kit.ts), and set repeat to (1,1). Alternatively cap the end faces with a 0.3 m plain mortar trim box. (2) Parent the cap, pier caps and sign to the faded slab mesh, or register them in a fade group (game.occluders entries that share opacity with their wall: e.g. slab returns the mesh, and `fadeWith(mesh, ...children)`). Their materials need transparent:true. (3) For DR-12, add the chest and head rays (p.y+.9, p.y+1.5) to the occlusion test in src/game.ts:386-388 so a 2.1 m wall between the camera and Pip's torso fades.

**Verify.**

- Zoom-9 shots at the storeroom corners show bricks with the same aspect on long and short faces. Rerun s3-back.mjs shot 33: cap, caps and sign fade together with the bricks. Retake 14: Pip's torso is visible through a faded wall.

**Rules:** DR-12, DR-68, DR-78

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED — (1) room.ts:62 sets repeat (len/1.3, 1.6) on one texture shared by every box face, and the 0.3 m return faces show squashed vertical brick slivers (34, right pier). (2) slab() pushes only the slab mesh into game.occluders (room.ts:41). The cap (:70), pier caps (:69) and STOREROOM sign (:71) are separate, unfaded meshes, and in 33 they sit at full opacity over a faded wall with Pip behind it.

## 5. Suggested execution order

Batches are ordered so that P0 work lands first and so that each batch touches one area of code; inside a batch, do the entries in ID order. After every batch run `npm.cmd test` (Vitest) and `npx.cmd playwright test` (all `tests/*.spec.ts`) and the capture scripts named under "Verification". Where an entry says "new spec", add it to `tests/` next to the room's existing spec, reusing `tests/navigation.ts`. The `R-<room>` batches hold the room-specific entries that were not part of a cross-cutting batch; they can be done in any order after B1–B6, and in parallel by different sessions because they touch different `src/stations/<room>/` or `src/levels/<room>.ts` files.

### B1. P0 and soft-locks: phone benches, stuck items, respawn

6 entries (2 P0, 1 P1, 3 P2). Files: `src/ui/ui.css` (bench layout ~208-258), `src/game.ts` (bench camera fit ~366-372, respawn ~339-342), `src/stations/*/station.ts` (bench cameras and touch targets), `src/levels/meeting.ts`, `src/levels/decor.ts` (closet walls), `src/lunch-runtime.ts` (storeroom items).

Entries: R5-001, R5-002, R5-011, R5-166, R5-297, R5-326.

Verification: new `tests/phone-bench.spec.ts` that sets a 390×844 touch viewport and finishes QFN, Spectrum, Arcade, Garage and Observatory by taps only; new `tests/respawn.spec.ts` that throws each Meeting/Lunch job item into the closet/storeroom and expects it back within 6 s with a puff (DR-15/25); retake `hud-ui` phone shots and `gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock` shots.

## 6. Open questions for the product owner

1. **Cable in station rooms (AGENTS 4 / DR-05).** The cable is absent in 6 of 9 doors (R5-079). Should every station get a physical cable act (a bench lead to drag and plug, the Observatory receiver cable, the Garage ground cable), or does the product owner accept cable-free stations? The fix for R5-079 and several fun findings depends on this.
2. **Overall grade = best of three (AGENTS 6).** With best-of-three, any finish earns an A unless every axis is tight (R5-078). Keep best-of-three and tune per-room limits hard, or change the overall formula (e.g. median)? And should Arcade Rush require a minimum number of orders before any grade?
3. **Phone / touch support.** R5-001 is filed P0 because the build shows touch UI and a mobile layout. If phones are not a target, it drops to P2 and R5-016 (touch camera) can be closed.
4. **Gamepad at benches.** The HUD shows pad glyphs but no pad input reaches any bench (R5-015). Is gamepad a supported input for the full game?
5. **Restart key.** Should R stay as instant restart on the floor (with a confirm or a hold), or move to the pause menu only (R5-004)?
6. **Live meters vs. predict-before-test (DR-31/38).** Arcade, Spectrum and Observatory show the live result while the player sweeps values, so brute force is free (R5-028, R5-048). Is it acceptable to hide the live reading until a commit (TEST / SEND / power-on) and count wrong commits, or should sweeping stay free?
7. **Job yellow exclusivity (DR-45).** Fixing R5-101 recolours mugs, crates, cabinets, carts, books and one trainee across every room. Confirm that no decor may use the job yellows.
8. **Scale of gameplay parts (DR-59).** Plugs, strips, reels and mugs are 2–4× real size (R5-342). Is oversizing intended for readability (then relax DR-59), or should they come down to 1.2–1.5×?
9. **Curriculum order (DR-27).** The progression reviewer suggests Playground → Meeting → Arcade → Lunch → Garage → Observatory → QFN → Spectrum (R5-069). Reordering changes the lobby, locks and the "next job" chain. Approve, or keep the current order?
10. **Meeting's tidy route is a daisy chain** (wall → reel → coupler → reel → strip), which real safety guidance forbids (R5-203). Keep it as the lesson, or redesign the tidy route?
11. **Lunch idle failure.** The fridge spoils the job at 2:00 from second 0 (R5-091). AGENTS 5 says only a concept mistake can fail a job; is a pure timer that fails an exploring player allowed?
12. **Bench text budget (DR-40).** Does the 25-word budget include the bench side panel and monitor, or only the floor HUD? The text-load entry (R5-102) assumes the side panel counts.

## Appendix — refuted findings

These were raised by a reviewer and refuted by the adversarial verifier. They are not in the fix list.

- **REGRESSION (partial) L6: R on the pause card instantly reloads the job, and Tab on the result card drops focus to &lt;body>** (`gap3-recheck-list#2`, P2) — I reproduced the behaviour, but it is not the bug described. (a) R on the pause card is a deliberate, labelled shortcut. The pause card's Restart button carries a visible 'R' keycap (src/ui/screens.ts:156). src/ui/game-ui.ts:119 explicitly sets flagAutostart for R when the screen is 'pause' so that the reload goes straight back into play. A menu button's own labelled shortcut is not a 'game key acting while a menu is open' under DR-22. My run: pause → R → screen 'play', mark false, as designed. (b) Tab on the result card wraps normally: from Next job (the last button) it goes to BODY, then restart → jobs-reload → nextjob.
- **Required doorstop (or any job item) thrown behind the conveyor is lost for good, so the job can't be finished without a restart** (`lunch-play#0`, P2) — I reproduced the throw: from (2.83,-5.25) the doorstop came to rest at (-0.24,0.15,-8.91), walking toward it stalls at z -6.20, and 10 s later it has not moved. All of that matches. But it is not lost. The conveyor collider is only 1.1 m tall (solid 8.5×0.3×0.9 at y 0.95, src/lunch-runtime.ts:95), and Pip's jump clears about 1.36 m (vertical 7, gravity 18, src/game.ts:181,320). One Space+W from (0.02,-6.11) carried Pip over the belt to (-0.76,-9.50). There the prompt read 'E Grab the doorstop' with the marker above it, E picked it up, and Space+S jumped him back to (0.19,-3.97). It is not a soft-lock and no restart is needed.
- **The cable slingshot is unreachable in Lunch and there is nothing to fling** (`lunch-play#4`, P2) — The slingshot is reachable. I took thin-2 at spawn and walked the route a lift or conveyor feed actually takes: corridor → kitchen door → (3,-2.6) → (7.3,-1.2) → the gap at (9.2,-1) → (14,-6) → the lift-room corner. Strain climbed to 1.028, about 0.84 m past length, so energy ≈ 42 > 1 (src/sim/cable.ts:71). The pull caps it, as designed. On Q, fastestProp was 8.22 m/s and damage went 0→2, so clutter along the cable was flung and broke. The reviewer's test only stretched the cable straight along the corridor, where 30 m does not reach the east wall from cart A. Two points stand: no NPC was alarmed in that corner (alarmed 0), and there is no dedicated fling target like the Playground pins.
- **The thermal IR link has no background, though everything at room temperature (and the hot toaster sitting in the beam) glows at 10 µm** (`spectrum-teach#12`, P2) — The key factual premise is wrong. The toaster isn't 'in the beam'. It sits at about (2.1, 4.85) (tea group 2.4,4.85 with toaster at −0.3; room.ts:111-112). The thermal ray TX→quiet pad passes at z≈3.03 at that x, about 1.8 m away, just clipping the smoke cloud edge (closest approach 0.27 m from SMOKE centre). The physics claim is also overstated. Long-wave IR free-space links are a real research and engineering use, chosen precisely because 8 to 14 µm passes smoke and fog. Room-temperature background is a mostly constant (DC) level that a modulated link rejects, so leaving it out is a fair simplification at the level taught, not a falsehood under AGENTS 10.
